target: But if you find anyone who has your gods, that person shall not live. In the presence of our relatives, see for yourself whether there is anything of yours here with me; and if so, take it.” Now Jacob did not know that Rachel had stolen the gods.

source: Chuin Laban Jacob pon in'a alutnin, Leah pon in'a, chule asohnu teni pon in'a alutnin; ahin aman hiho chu amupon ahi. Chujouvin ama Leah pon in'a konin apotdoh in, Rachel pon in'a aluttan ahi.
target: So Laban went into Jacob’s tent and into Leah’s tent and into the tent of the two female servants, but he found nothing. After he came out of Leah’s tent, he entered Rachel’s tent.

source: Tun Rachel'in milim hochu analan, sangongsao pho lah-a chun akoijin, achunga chun atouvin ahi. Chuin Laban'in pon insung jouse chu amailen, ahivangin amupon ahi.
target: Now Rachel had taken the household gods and put them inside her camel’s saddle and was sitting on them. Laban searched through everything in the tent but found nothing.

source: Chuin amanun apa henga, namasanga kakipatdoh theilou jeh hin, ka Pakaiyin nopmo sahihbeh hen; ajehchu numei hina ngai chu kachunga auma ahi, ati. Chuin aman ahol len, ahin limho chu amujou pon ahi.
target: Rachel said to her father, “Don’t be angry, my lord, that I cannot stand up in your presence; I’m having my period.” So he searched but could not find the household gods.

source: Chuin Jacob alunghangin, Laban chu ahousen; chule Jacob'in adonbutnin, Laban henga, Kasuhkhel ipi ham? Kachonsetna ipi hija, Lungsa tah-a neihin nung del jengham?
target: Jacob was angry and took Laban to task. “What is my crime?” he asked Laban. “How have I wronged you that you hunt me down?

source: Kathil jouse namaichai soh helin, na insung thil ipi namu em? Eini kahlah thuhi atan theina dingun, hikoma hin kasopite le nasopite anga podoh-in.
target: Now that you have searched through all my goods, what have you found that belongs to your household? Put it here in front of your relatives and mine, and let them judge between the two of us.

source: Hiche kum somni jenhi nakoma kaumtan, nakelngoipi hole nakelpi hon anou anei chavai khapouvin, chule nakelngoi hon lah-a achal hojong kanekhapoi.
target: “I have been with you for twenty years now. Your sheep and goats have not miscarried, nor have I eaten rams from your flocks.

source: Gamsa loitel ho jong nahenga kahinlhut khapon; keima tah-in amang chu kamo poh-in; suna kigumang hihen, jana kigumang hijongle, hichu keima neidit sah-in ahi.
target: I did not bring you animals torn by wild beasts; I bore the loss myself. And you demanded payment from me for whatever was stolen by day or night.

source: Hiti hin kaumin; sun teng nisatnin, chule janteng dapmin eisugim lheh jengjin, chule ihjong ka-ihmuji pon ahi.
target: This was my situation: The heat consumed me in the daytime and the cold at night, and sleep fled from my eyes.

source: Chuti chun kum somni na in'a kahung umin; nachanu teni lonan kum som le kum li nangma kana jenin, chule naganchaho lona-in nangma kumgup kajenin; chuleh nangman katoh man chu somveijen neikhel peh-in ahi.
target: It was like this for the twenty years I was in your household. I worked for you fourteen years for your two daughters and six years for your flocks, and you changed my wages ten times.

source: Kapa Pathen, Abraham Pathen, chule Isaac gina chu kakoma umlou hile, thonlouva tu-a jong hi khutgoh keova neisol mang teiding ahi. Pathen'in kahesohna le kakhutna katoh gimna chu amua, janhi janna chu napho ahitai, ati.
target: If the God of my father, the God of Abraham and the Fear of Isaac, had not been with me, you would surely have sent me away empty-handed. But God has seen my hardship and the toil of my hands, and last night he rebuked you.”

source: Chuin Laban'in adonbutnin, Jacob henga, Hiche chanute hohi keima chanute ahin, hiche chate hi keima chate ahiuvin, hiche gancha ho jonghi keima gancha ho ahiuvin, chule namu jouse hi keima-a ahi. Ahin tuni hin hiche kachanu te chung le, ahinnu achateu chunga hin ipi kabolthei dingham? ati.
target: Laban answered Jacob, “The women are my daughters, the children are my children, and the flocks are my flocks. All you see is mine. Yet what can I do today about these daughters of mine, or about the children they have borne?

source: Hijeh chun tun hungin, nangma le keiman kitepna khat sem hite; hichu nangma le keima kah-a hettohsahna hihen, ati.
target: Come now, let’s make a covenant, you and I, and let it serve as a witness between us.”

source: Chuin Jacob'in song khat alan, khommin aphuttan ahi.
target: So Jacob took a stone and set it up as a pillar.

source: Chuin Jacob'in asopite henga, song lhoh khomun, ati. Chuin amahon song alhoh khomun, alhuh-in aseuvin, chule songlhuh chunga chun an aneuvin ahi.
target: He said to his relatives, “Gather some stones.” So they took stones and piled them in a heap, and they ate there by the heap.

source: Chuin Laban'in hichu Jegar-Sahadutha asah-in; ahivangin Jacob'in hichu Gilead asah-in ahi.
target: Laban called it Jegar Sahadutha, and Jacob called it Galeed.

source: Chuin Laban'in, Tunikhoa hi hiche kisekhom hohi nangle keima kikah-a hettohsahna ahitai, ati. Hijeh chun hiche min chun Gilead akisahtan;
target: Laban said, “This heap is a witness between you and me today.” That is why it was called Galeed.

source: Chule Mizpah jong akisah-in ahi; ajehchu Laban'in, Eini khat le khat ikikhen tengleh, Pakaiyin nangle kei eivetup jing lhonhen.
target: It was also called Mizpah, because he said, “May the Lord keep watch between you and me when we are away from each other.

source: Nangman kachanu te hi nasuh genthei ja, ahilouleh kachanu te tailou jidang naneija ahile, koimacha eini koma aumhih nai; ven, Pathen chu nangle kei kah-a ahetoh ahi, atin ahi.
target: If you mistreat my daughters or if you take any wives besides my daughters, even though no one is with us, remember that God is a witness between you and me.”

source: Chuin Laban'in Jacob henga, Hiche song kisekhom hi venlang, nangma le keima kah-a hiche song kaphu jong hi ven.
target: Laban also said to Jacob, “Here is this heap, and here is this pillar I have set up between you and me.

source: Suhset nadinga keiman hiche songlhuh le song kiphut khela nangma henglam kahinkhel louding, chuleh nangman jong hiche songlhuh le songkiphut khela keima henglam nahin khellouna dingin, hiche songlhuh hi hettohsah hihen, chule song kiphut hi hettohsah hihen.
target: This heap is a witness, and this pillar is a witness, that I will not go past this heap to your side to harm you and that you will not go past this heap and pillar to my side to harm me.

source: Abraham Pathen, Nahor Pathen, chule apatehou Pathen chun ikah hona thu tanhen, ati. Chuin apa Isaac ginna-a chun Jacob akihah seltan ahi.
target: May the God of Abraham and the God of Nahor, the God of their father, judge between us.” So Jacob took an oath in the name of the Fear of his father Isaac.

source: Chujouvin Jacob'in molsang chunga chun ganlhaina atoh-in, asopite chu changlhah nedingin akouvin ahi. Chuin amahon changlhah aneuvin, molsang chunga chun ageh khovah taovin ahi.
target: He offered a sacrifice there in the hill country and invited his relatives to a meal. After they had eaten, they spent the night there.

source: Chuin jingpi matah-in Laban athouvin, achapate le achanute achopmin, chule phatthei aboh-in ahi. Chuin Laban akipatnin agam lama akiletan ahi.
target: Early the next morning Laban kissed his grandchildren and his daughters and blessed them. Then he left and returned home.

source: Chuin Jacob achepeh-in ahile, Pathen vantil ten ana kitopiuvin ahi.
target: Jacob also went on his way, and the angels of God met him.

source: Chuin Jacob'in amaho chu amu phat nin, Hiche hi Pathen ngahmun ahi, ati. Chuin aman chuche munchu Mahanaim asahtai.
target: When Jacob saw them, he said, “This is the camp of God!” So he named that place Mahanaim.

source: Chuin Jacob'in Edom gamkai sunga Seir gama a-upa Esau henga chun, amasanga sottol ho asolin ahi.
target: Jacob sent messengers ahead of him to his brother Esau in the land of Seir, the country of Edom.

source: Chuin aman amaho chu thu apen, ahenguva, Hitia hi nanghon ka pakai Esau henga nasei dingu ahi; nasohpa Jacob'in hitin aseije, keima Laban koma kagathamin, chumuna chun tugeihin kaume.
target: He instructed them: “This is what you are to say to my lord Esau: ‘Your servant Jacob says, I have been staying with Laban and have remained there till now.

source: Chule keiman bongchal ho, sangan ho, kelngoi ho, soh pasal ho, chule soh numei ho kaneijin; chule namit mu-a hi lungsetna kamu theina dinga ka pakai hetsah dinga kahinsol ahi, tin gaseijun, ati.
target: I have cattle and donkeys, sheep and goats, male and female servants. Now I am sending this message to my lord, that I may find favor in your eyes.’ ”

source: Chuin sottol hochu Jacob henga ahung kileuvin, ajah-a, Na-upa Esau heng kaga phaovin, chujongle ama nangma toh kimuto dingin mi jali toh kilhonin ahunge, atiuve.
target: When the messengers returned to Jacob, they said, “We went to your brother Esau, and now he is coming to meet you, and four hundred men are with him.”

source: Chuphatnin Jacob hatah-in akichan chule alung gimlhehtan ahi. Chuin aman aum khompi miho, kelngoihon, bonghon, chule sangongsao ho chu loinin ahom khenin;
target: In great fear and distress Jacob divided the people who were with him into two groups, and the flocks and herds and camels as well.

source: Chule aman, Esau chu loikhat koma ahunga, atha tah-a ahijongle, adalhah loikhat chu hoidoh theijinte, atin ahi.
target: He thought, “If Esau comes and attacks one group, the group that is left may escape.”

source: Chuin Jacob'in, Vo kapa Abraham Pathen, chule Kapa Isaac Pathen, nagam lam le nasopite henglama kiletan, keiman nangma bolpha nange tia kahenga seija Pakai;
target: Then Jacob prayed, “O God of my father Abraham, God of my father Isaac, Lord , you who said to me, ‘Go back to your country and your relatives, and I will make you prosper,’

source: Nangman nasoh chunga namusah hepina jouse le thutah jouse lah-a hi aneopen changdinga kilom kahipoi; ajehchu hiche Jordan hi ka tenggol sehtoh hung galkai ja kahin, tunvang loini hel kahung hitai.
target: I am unworthy of all the kindness and faithfulness you have shown your servant. I had only my staff when I crossed this Jordan, but now I have become two camps.

source: Katao ahi, ka-upa khutna kon, Esau khut ngeija konin neihuh-in: ajehchu ajole ama hungintin, nunao chapang ho pumin eihung that get nunte, ti kakichan ahi.
target: Save me, I pray, from the hand of my brother Esau, for I am afraid he will come and attack me, and also the mothers with their children.

source: Chule nangman, Tahbeh-in keima nabol phang ting, chule nachilhahte atambehseh jeh-a simjoulou twikhanglen kama neldi jat banga kasem ding nahi, tin naseijin ahi, ati.
target: But you have said, ‘I will surely make you prosper and will make your descendants like the sand of the sea, which cannot be counted.’ ”

source: Chuin ama chuche jan chun chukoma chun agehtan; chule akhutna um aneiho lah-a konin a-upa Esau thilpeh-a pehding aladoh-in;
target: He spent the night there, and from what he had with him he selected a gift for his brother Esau:

source: Kelpi jani le kelchal somni, kelngoipi jani le kelngoichal somni,
target: two hundred female goats and twenty male goats, two hundred ewes and twenty rams,

source: Anoi kilhoh lai sangongsao somthum le anoute, bongpi somli le bongchal som, sanganpi somni le sangan chal som akhendoh-in ahi.
target: thirty female camels with their young, forty cows and ten bulls, and twenty female donkeys and ten male donkeys.

source: Chuin aman hiche ho chu loitum cheh-in asoh ho khutna apedoh-in, chuin asoh ho henga, Kamasanga ana chepeh unlang, gancha loitum cheh kikah-a chun mun ong umsahcheh-un, ati.
target: He put them in the care of his servants, each herd by itself, and said to his servants, “Go ahead of me, and keep some space between the herds.”

source: Chuin aman amasapen chu thu apen ahenga, ka-upa Esau'in nakimupia, nahenga, Koija nahim, hoija cheding nahim? Chule namasanga um hiche hohi koija ham? tia nadoh tengle;
target: He instructed the one in the lead: “When my brother Esau meets you and asks, ‘Who do you belong to, and where are you going, and who owns all these animals in front of you?’

source: Nangman, Hiche hohi nasoh Jacob'a ahiuvin, ka pakaiyu Esau dinga thilpeh-a ahinthot ahi; chule Ven, amajong kanunguva ahunge, tia nasei dingu ahi, ati.
target: then you are to say, ‘They belong to your servant Jacob. They are a gift sent to my lord Esau, and he is coming behind us.’ ”

source: Chuin aman chutobang machun anina, athumna, chule gancha hon loitum juiho henga chun, Esau namu tengule chutobangma cheh-a chu nasei dingu ahi, tin thu apei.
target: He also instructed the second, the third and all the others who followed the herds: “You are to say the same thing to Esau when you meet him.

source: Chule nanghon chuche chungchon chun, Ven, nasoh Jacob jong kanunguva khun ahunge, nati dingu ahi, tin ahilcheh in ahi. Ajehchu aman, Kamasanga kisol thilpeh hin keiman alung sudamthei khat ning ting, chujouteng le amai mu nange; ijem atile aman eisangkhat nante, atin ahi.
target: And be sure to say, ‘Your servant Jacob is coming behind us.’ ” For he thought, “I will pacify him with these gifts I am sending on ahead; later, when I see him, perhaps he will receive me.”

source: Chuti chun thilpeh ho chu amasanga asol masan; amatah vangchu chuche jan chun mihon lah-a chun agehtan ahi.
target: So Jacob’s gifts went on ahead of him, but he himself spent the night in the camp.

source: Chuin chuche jan chun ama athouvin, a-inneipi teni, asoh numei teni, chule achapate somlekhat chu akipuijin, Jabbok vadung agalkai taovin ahi.
target: That night Jacob got up and took his two wives, his two female servants and his eleven sons and crossed the ford of the Jabbok.

source: Chuin aman amaho chu apuijin, vadunga chun asol galkaijin, chule anei chengse jong agalkaisah tai.
target: After he had sent them across the stream, he sent over all his possessions.

source: Chuin Jacob achang seh-in aumtan; chuin mikhatnin amachu khovahlhah masangsen akibotpin ahi.
target: So Jacob was left alone, and a man wrestled with him till daybreak.

source: Chuin amapa chun Jacob athatlel ding amuphatnin, apheipi gu kisuhtona akhoipeh in ahile, akibotlhon phatnin Jacob pheipigu kisuhtona chu akikhentan ahi.
target: When the man saw that he could not overpower him, he touched the socket of Jacob’s hip so that his hip was wrenched as he wrestled with the man.

source: Chuin aman, Neichesah tan, ajehchu khovahlha ding ahitai, ati. Chuin aman, Phatthei neiboh louleh lhaponge ati.
target: Then the man said, “Let me go, for it is daybreak.” But Jacob replied, “I will not let you go unless you bless me.”

source: Chuin aman ahenga, Namin ipiham? ati. Hichun aman, Jacob kahi, ati.
target: The man asked him, “What is your name?” “Jacob,” he answered.

source: Chuin aman, Namin Jacob kiti louding, Israel joh nakiti ding ahitai: ajehchu nangma Pathen toh mihem toh nakibonin najoutai, ati.
target: Then the man said, “Your name will no longer be Jacob, but Israel, because you have struggled with God and with humans and have overcome.”

source: Chuin Jacob'in amachu adongin, Katao ahi, namin neisepeh-in, tin angehtan ahi. Chuin aman ipidinga kamin neidoh ham? ati. Chuin chua chun amachu phatthei aboh tan ahi.
target: Jacob said, “Please tell me your name.” But he replied, “Why do you ask my name?” Then he blessed him there.

source: Chuin Jacob'in chuche munchu Peniel asahtai: ajehchu keiman Pathen chu kimaito-in kamun, chule kahinkho hing hoijin aume, ati.
target: So Jacob called the place Peniel, saying, “It is because I saw God face to face, and yet my life was spared.”

source: Chuin aman Penuel agalkaijin nisa achunga ahung sohtan, chule ama apheipi jehchun akibaipeh-in ahi.
target: The sun rose above him as he passed Peniel, and he was limping because of his hip.

source: Chuti ahijeh chun tuni geihin Israel chaten pheipi gu kisuhtona thajung achomho, pheipi homa umho chu anengai pouve. Ajehchu aman Jacob pheija thagui chomho chu akhoipeh ahi.
target: Therefore to this day the Israelites do not eat the tendon attached to the socket of the hip, because the socket of Jacob’s hip was touched near the tendon.

source: Chuin Jacob akhodah-in agahven ahile, veuvin, Esau mi jali toh kilhonin ahungin ahi. Hijeh chun aman achate chu Leah le Rachel chule sohnu teni henga ahomkhen tan ahi.
target: Jacob looked up and there was Esau, coming with his four hundred men; so he divided the children among Leah, Rachel and the two female servants.

source: Chuin aman sohnu teni le achateu chu amasa penin akoijin, chuin Leah le achate chu abana, chule Rachel le Joseph chu anunung penin akoijin ahi.
target: He put the female servants and their children in front, Leah and her children next, and Rachel and Joseph in the rear.

source: Chule ama amasanguva achen, a-upa kom aphah kahsen, tolla sagivei aboh khupmin.
target: He himself went on ahead and bowed down to the ground seven times as he approached his brother.

source: Chuin ama kimupi ding chun Esau ahung lhaijelin, apomin, chuin angong koijin achopmin; chuin amani akaplhon tai.
target: But Esau ran to meet Jacob and embraced him; he threw his arms around his neck and kissed him. And they wept.

source: Chuin ama akhodah-in ahile, numei ho le chapang ho chu amun, Nalhonpi hohi koi hiuvam? ati. Chuin aman, Pathen'in lungset tah-a nasoh apeh chapang ho chu ahiuve, ati.
target: Then Esau looked up and saw the women and children. “Who are these with you?” he asked. Jacob answered, “They are the children God has graciously given your servant.”

source: Chujouvin sohnu teni chu achateu toh ahung naijun, amani le achateu chu aboh khupmun ahi.
target: Then the female servants and their children approached and bowed down.

source: Chuin Leah jong chu achate toh ahung naijun aboh khupmun ahi. Chujouvin Joseph le Rachel ahungnai lhonin, abohkhup lhonin ahi.
target: Next, Leah and her children came and bowed down. Last of all came Joseph and Rachel, and they too bowed down.

source: Chuin aman, Gancha hon kakitopi ho jouse chu ipi nangaitona ham? ati. Chuin aman, Hiho chu ka Pakai mitmu-a lungsetna kachan nadinga ahi, ati.
target: Esau asked, “What’s the meaning of all these flocks and herds I met?” “To find favor in your eyes, my lord,” he said.

source: Chuin Esau'in, Kanao, keiman kagotkhop kaneinai; nangman nanei chu nangma din kikoijin, ati.
target: But Esau said, “I already have plenty, my brother. Keep what you have for yourself.”

source: Chuin Jacob'in, Ahipoi, nahenga katao ahi, tu-a hi namitmu-a lungsetna changa kahile, kakhut na konin kathilpeh hi kisanin. Ajehchu namai kamu hi Pathen mai kamu toh abang jengin, nangma kachunga nakipah-in ahi.
target: “No, please!” said Jacob. “If I have found favor in your eyes, accept this gift from me. For to see your face is like seeing the face of God, now that you have received me favorably.

source: Nahenga hinkichoi vangbohna hi kisanin, tia katao ahi; ajehchu Pathen'in eilungsetnin, kagotkhop jong kaneinai, ati. Chuin aman amachu angeh khoh-in ahile, akilah tai.
target: Please accept the present that was brought to you, for God has been gracious to me and I have all I need.” And because Jacob insisted, Esau accepted it.

source: Chuin Esau'in aseijin, Ilamjotnu jong jomu hitin, chetao hite, chule keima namasanguva lamkai jinge, ati.
target: Then Esau said, “Let us be on our way; I’ll accompany you.”

source: Chuin aman ahenga, Chapang hohi neocha cha ahiuvin, chule kelngoi hon kakoma umho jonghi anoukai ahiuve ti ka pakaiyin nahei; chule nikhat jengcha jong kahoi valleh ganchahon jouse hi thigam diu ahi.
target: But Jacob said to him, “My lord knows that the children are tender and that I must care for the ewes and cows that are nursing their young. If they are driven hard just one day, all the animals will die.

source: Katao ahi, ka Pakai, nasoh masanga anache masatan; keiman Seir munna ka Pakai heng kahung lhun masangsen, kamasanga um gancha ho le chapang ho kalson dungjui jin hung taovinge.
target: So let my lord go on ahead of his servant, while I move along slowly at the pace of the flocks and herds before me and the pace of the children, until I come to my lord in Seir.”

source: Chuin Esau'in, Tun keiman kalhonpi mi phabep nangma dalhahpeh inge, ati. Chuin aman, Ipi ngaikhoh ding ham? Ka pakai mitmun lungsetna neimusah tan, ahi.
target: Esau said, “Then let me leave some of my men with you.” “But why do that?” Jacob asked. “Just let me find favor in the eyes of my lord.”

source: Chuti chun Esau chuche nichun Seir lam jonin akiletai.
target: So that day Esau started on his way back to Seir.

source: Chuin Jacob Succoth lama achen, ama dingin in khat asan, chule ganchahon dingin buh asahpeh-in ahi. Hijeh chun chukom munchu Succoth akisah tai.
target: Jacob, however, went to Sukkoth, where he built a place for himself and made shelters for his livestock. That is why the place is called Sukkoth.

source: Chuin Jacob Padan Aram-a konin Canaan gama Shechem khopi Shalem chu ahung lhung tan; chule aman khopi maija chun apon in asongin ahi.
target: After Jacob came from Paddan Aram, he arrived safely at the city of Shechem in Canaan and camped within sight of the city.

source: Chuin aman Shechem pa Hamor chate khutna konin gam behkhat dangka jakhat-in acho-in, hia chun apon in asongin ahi.
target: For a hundred pieces of silver, he bought from the sons of Hamor, the father of Shechem, the plot of ground where he pitched his tent.

source: Chuin aman chukoma chun maicham khat asemin, hichu El-Elohe-Israel asahtai.
target: There he set up an altar and called it El Elohe Israel.

source: Chuin Leah'in Jacob ahinpeh achanu Dinah chu chuche gam chanute ve dingin agapotdoh-in ahi.
target: Now Dinah, the daughter Leah had borne to Jacob, went out to visit the women of the land.

source: Chuin Hiv mi Hamor chapa Shechem, chuche gam leng chapa chun amanu amuphatnin, apuijin, aluppin, asubohtan ahi.
target: When Shechem son of Hamor the Hivite, the ruler of that area, saw her, he took her and raped her.

source: Chuin alungthim chu Jacob chanu Dinah chunga chun aumtan, chule aman nungahnu chu angailutan, amanu chu kamdam awnemin ahoupitan ahi.
target: His heart was drawn to Dinah daughter of Jacob; he loved the young woman and spoke tenderly to her.

source: Chuin Shechem'in apa Hamor akihoupin, Hiche nungah nu khu kajidin neipui peh-in, ati.
target: And Shechem said to his father Hamor, “Get me this girl as my wife.”

source: Chuin Jacob'in achanu Dinah Shechem'in asuhboh chu ahetai. Tun achapate gamlah-a aganchate toh uma ahiuvin, chule amaho ahung lhunkah seuchun, Jacob'in alung adejingin ahi.
target: When Jacob heard that his daughter Dinah had been defiled, his sons were in the fields with his livestock; so he did nothing about it until they came home.

source: Chuin Shechem pa Hamor chu Jacob toh kihou dingin ahung potdoh-in ahi.
target: Then Shechem’s father Hamor went out to talk with Jacob.

source: Chuin Jacob chapate chun hichu ajah phatnun, gamlah-a konin ahung lhung taove. Chule aman Jacob chanu aluppia, Israel lah-a ngolhoi tah-a achona, bollou hel ding thil abol jehchun, pasal ho chu alung phamo uvin, alunghang lheh jeng taovin ahi.
target: Meanwhile, Jacob’s sons had come in from the fields as soon as they heard what had happened. They were shocked and furious, because Shechem had done an outrageous thing in Israel by sleeping with Jacob’s daughter—a thing that should not be done.

source: Chuin Hamor'in amaho chu akihoupin, Kachapa Shechem lungin nachanu alha ngaitai. Amanu hi ajidingin petaovin, tia katao ahi.
target: But Hamor said to them, “My son Shechem has his heart set on your daughter. Please give her to him as his wife.

source: Chule keihotoh kichengto uhitin, nachanu teo keiho neipeuvin lang, chule keiho chanute nangho din kilah uvin.
target: Intermarry with us; give us your daughters and take our daughters for yourselves.

source: Chule nangho keiho lah-a chenguvin natin, chule gamchu namasanguva umding ahi. Nangho chengunlang, hia chun kiveijun, chule nanghon gou kikholun, ati.
target: You can settle among us; the land is open to you. Live in it, trade in it, and acquire property in it.”

source: Chuin Shechem'in numeinu pa le asopite henga chun, Namit muva lungsetna neimusah-un, chule kahenga nasei chanu pengkate.
target: Then Shechem said to Dinah’s father and brothers, “Let me find favor in your eyes, and I will give you whatever you ask.

source: Man le thilpeh neiha ngeh behseh hih-un, kahenga nasei dungjuijun penge. Ahinla nungah chu jidingin neipeuvin, ati.
target: Make the price for the bride and the gift I am to bring as great as you like, and I’ll pay whatever you ask me. Only give me the young woman as my wife.”

source: Chuin asopinu Dinah chu asuhboh jehchun, Jacob chapate chun Shechem le apa Hamor chu dohan adonbut uvin;
target: Because their sister Dinah had been defiled, Jacob’s sons replied deceitfully as they spoke to Shechem and his father Hamor.

source: Chuin amahon amani henga, Kasopinu cheptan lou khat henga pehdoh ding, hitobang thil hi keihon kabolthei pouve; ijeh inem itile hichu keiho dinga kisuhjum na ahi.
target: They said to them, “We can’t do such a thing; we can’t give our sister to a man who is not circumcised. That would be a disgrace to us.

source: Ahin hiche hi nabol ule vang kanop dingu ahi: nalah uva pasal jousen chep atanuva, keiho banga hi naum uva ahile;
target: We will enter into an agreement with you on one condition only: that you become like us by circumcising all your males.

source: Chuteng le kachanuteu nangho peuvingting, chule nachanuteu keihon kakipui diu, chuleh nangho toh kachengkhom uva, namkhat ihung hidiu ahi.
target: Then we will give you our daughters and take your daughters for ourselves. We’ll settle among you and become one people with you.

source: Ahinla kathuseiju nangailou uva, chep natan lou vangule; kachanu kakipui uva, kache diu ahitai, tin adonbutnuve.
target: But if you will not agree to be circumcised, we’ll take our sister and go.”

source: Chuin athuseiju chun Hamor le Hamor chapa Shechem chu alung lhaisah lhontan ahi.
target: Their proposal seemed good to Hamor and his son Shechem.

source: Chuin Jacob chanu adeijeh-in gollhangpa chun chuche thilbol ding chu ageisang sahpon ahi. Chule amachu apa insung jouse lah-a ja-um pentah hija ahi.
target: The young man, who was the most honored of all his father’s family, lost no time in doing what they said, because he was delighted with Jacob’s daughter.

source: Chuin Hamor le achapa Shechem chu akhopiu kotpibul lah ahung lhonin, akhopiu miho chutoh akihouvun, ajah uvah,
target: So Hamor and his son Shechem went to the gate of their city to speak to the men of their city.

source: Khuche miho khu eihotoh kicham tah-in aumuve; hijeh chun hiche gama khun chengu henlang, kiveiju hen; ajehchu veuvin, gam khu amaho dingin alen khopnai; achanuteu ji dingin kipuiju hitin, chule eiho chanute amaho peuhite.
target: “These men are friendly toward us,” they said. “Let them live in our land and trade in it; the land has plenty of room for them. We can marry their daughters and they can marry ours.

source: Namkhat ihung hina dingule eihoto achenkhomna dinguva, eihon hiche bouhi ibolu ngai ahi: Hichu amaho cheptan banga, eiho lah-a pasal jousen chep atan cheh ding hi ahi.
target: But the men will agree to live with us as one people only on the condition that our males be circumcised, as they themselves are.

source: Chutile aganchahou, anei agouhou, chule asa jouseu khu eihoa hisoh keilou ding ham? Athuseiju ngaipou pouvu hite, chutile amaho ilah uva hungcheng taovinte, atilhone.
target: Won’t their livestock, their property and all their other animals become ours? So let us agree to their terms, and they will settle among us.”

source: Chuin akhopi kotpi phunga hungpotdoh jouse chun Hamor leh achapa Shechem thu ajoptaovin; chuin akhopiu kotpi phunga hunglut jouse pasal tapou achep atanpeh taovin ahi.
target: All the men who went out of the city gate agreed with Hamor and his son Shechem, and every male in the city was circumcised.

source: Chuin anithum chanin ahitin ahi, amaho anat laitah-un, Jacob chapate lah-a ni, Dinah sopiteni, Simeon le Levi chun achemjam cheh akilah lhonin, khopi chu hangtah-in anokhum lhonin, pasal jouse athatgam lhontan ahi.
target: Three days later, while all of them were still in pain, two of Jacob’s sons, Simeon and Levi, Dinah’s brothers, took their swords and attacked the unsuspecting city, killing every male.

source: Chuin amanin Hamor le achapa Shechem chu chemjam hemin athatlhonin, chuin Shechem in'a konin Dinah chu apuidoh lhonin, achemang lhontai.
target: They put Hamor and his son Shechem to the sword and took Dinah from Shechem’s house and left.

source: Jacob chapate chun thilong chunga chun lam ajotnun, asopinu asuhboh jeh-u chun, akhopiu chu achomun ahi.
target: The sons of Jacob came upon the dead bodies and looted the city where their sister had been defiled.

source: Amahon akelngoi hou, abongchal hou, asangan hou, chule khopi sungle gamlah-a umjouse chu akilah taovin ahi.
target: They seized their flocks and herds and donkeys and everything else of theirs in the city and out in the fields.

source: Chule agou jouseu, achasen hou jouse, ajite hou jouse chu sohchangin akaijun, chule insunga um jouse chu achomun ahi.
target: They carried off all their wealth and all their women and children, taking as plunder everything in the houses.

source: Chuin Jacob in Simeon le Levi henga, Nangnin hiche gama cheng Canaan mite leh Perizz mite lah-a hin hotnin neiumsah lhonin, neisugim lheh lhontai; keima lhomcha kahijeh-in, amaho eidoudin hung kikhom khom untin, keima eitha diu; keima le ka-insung mite hi suhmanga kaum dingu ahi, ati.
target: Then Jacob said to Simeon and Levi, “You have brought trouble on me by making me obnoxious to the Canaanites and Perizzites, the people living in this land. We are few in number, and if they join forces against me and attack me, I and my household will be destroyed.”

source: Chuin amahon, Kasopinu chu aman mijong banga abolding ham? atiuve.
target: But they replied, “Should he have treated our sister like a prostitute?”

source: Chuin Pathen'in Jacob henga, Kipat doh-in, Bethel'a chetou vinlang, chua chun gachengin; chule na-upa Esau'a kona najam mang laija nahenga hung kilah Pathen dingin chua chun maicham khat semin, ati.
target: Then God said to Jacob, “Go up to Bethel and settle there, and build an altar there to God, who appeared to you when you were fleeing from your brother Esau.”

source: Chujouvin Jacob'in a-insung mite le aumpiho jouse henga chun, Nalah uva gamdang Pathen umho chu koidoh-un, kisuthengun, chule navonu kikhelun,
target: So Jacob said to his household and to all who were with him, “Get rid of the foreign gods you have with you, and purify yourselves and change your clothes.

source: Chule eiho kipatnu hitin, Bethel'a chetouvu hite; chua chu kahesoh laija eina donbutna, kachena lam chana eiumpi jinga Pathen dingin maicham khat kasem ding ahi, ati.
target: Then come, let us go up to Bethel, where I will build an altar to God, who answered me in the day of my distress and who has been with me wherever I have gone.”

source: Chuin amahon akhutnuva um gamdang pathen jouse le abiluva bilba jouse Jacob apetaovin; chuin Jacob'in hiho chu Shechem koma gangpi phung noija chun aselin ahi.
target: So they gave Jacob all the foreign gods they had and the rings in their ears, and Jacob buried them under the oak at Shechem.

source: Chuin amaho acheuvin ahile, aveluva um khopi ho jouse chunga chun Pathen'a kona tijatna achutan, chule amahon Jacob chapate chu anungdel tapouvin ahi.
target: Then they set out, and the terror of God fell on the towns all around them so that no one pursued them.

source: Chutichun Jacob chu ama le aumpi miho jouse chutoh Canaan gama Luz, hichu Bethel ahin, ahunglhung taove.
target: Jacob and all the people with him came to Luz (that is, Bethel) in the land of Canaan.

source: Chuin aman chukoma chun maicham khat asemin, hichu El-Bethel asahtai. Ajehchu a-upa-a kona ajammang laija chumuna chu Pathen ahenga hung kilah-a ahi.
target: There he built an altar, and he called the place El Bethel, because it was there that God revealed himself to him when he was fleeing from his brother.

source: Ahin Rebekah jennu Deborah athitan, chule amanu chu Bethel mun'a gangpi phung noija chun akivuitan ahi. Chule chuche minchu Allon-bacuth akisah tai.
target: Now Deborah, Rebekah’s nurse, died and was buried under the oak outside Bethel. So it was named Allon Bakuth.

source: Chuin Padan-Aram'a kona ahung potdoh chun, Pathen Jacob henga ahung kilah kitnin, amachu phatthei aboh-in ahi.
target: After Jacob returned from Paddan Aram, God appeared to him again and blessed him.

source: Chuin Pathen'in ama henga, Namin hi Jacob ahin: namin hi Jacob kiti kit lou ding, amavang namin Israel kiti joding ahitai, ati. Chuin aman amin chu Israel asahtai.
target: God said to him, “Your name is Jacob, but you will no longer be called Jacob; your name will be Israel.” So he named him Israel.

source: Chuin Pathen'in ahenga, Keimahi hat chungnung Pathen kahi, chi tamtah lhah inlang, hapunin pungin; nampikhat chule nam chom chom loijong nanga konin hung doh intin, chule lengho jong nanga kona hung pengdoh dingu ahi.
target: And God said to him, “I am God Almighty; be fruitful and increase in number. A nation and a community of nations will come from you, and kings will be among your descendants.

source: Chule Abraham le Isaac henga kanapeh gamchu nangma pengting, chule nangma nungsanga nachilhahte jong hiche gamhi kapeh ding ahi, ati.
target: The land I gave to Abraham and Isaac I also give to you, and I will give this land to your descendants after you.”

source: Chuin akihoulimpi na mun'a chun Pathen ama-a konin akaltou tai.
target: Then God went up from him at the place where he had talked with him.

source: Chuin akihoulimpi na mun'a chun Jacob'in khompi khat, songkhompi chu aphutnin; hiche chunga chun donding thilpeh alheilhan, chuin aman chuche chunga chun thao asungin ahi.
target: Jacob set up a stone pillar at the place where God had talked with him, and he poured out a drink offering on it; he also poured oil on it.

source: Chuin Jacob'in Pathen'in ahoulim pina mun chu Bethel asah tai.
target: Jacob called the place where God had talked with him Bethel.

source: Chuin amaho Bethel'a konin achetauvun, chuin Ephrath lhunna ding chu phabep aum nalaijin ahi. Chuin Rachel naosonat nin anatan, nasatah-in athohgim tan ahi.
target: Then they moved on from Bethel. While they were still some distance from Ephrath, Rachel began to give birth and had great difficulty.

source: Chuin ahitin ahi, amanu athohgim behseh phatnin, nao domnu chun ahenga, Kicha hih-in, nangman hiche chapa jonghi naneiding ahi, ati.
target: And as she was having great difficulty in childbirth, the midwife said to her, “Don’t despair, for you have another son.”

source: Chuin ahitin ahi, alha achedoh to lhonin, (ajehchu amanu thia ahitai) amanun amin Ben-oni asah-in ahi. Ahivangin apan Benjamin asah-in ahi.
target: As she breathed her last—for she was dying—she named her son Ben-Oni. But his father named him Benjamin.

source: Chuin Rachel athitan, Bethlehem kiti Ephrath jotna lampia chun avuitaovin ahi.
target: So Rachel died and was buried on the way to Ephrath (that is, Bethlehem).

source: Chuin Jacob'in alhan chunga chun songkhom aphutnin; hichu tuni geihin Rachel lhansongphu akiti jingin ahi.
target: Over her tomb Jacob set up a pillar, and to this day that pillar marks Rachel’s tomb.

source: Chuin Israel achepeh-in, Edar insang kala chun apon in chu asongin ahi.
target: Israel moved on again and pitched his tent beyond Migdal Eder.

source: Chuin ahitin ahi, Israel chuche gama achenlai chun Reuben achen, apa thaikemnu Bilhah chu aga luppitan; chuin Israel'in hichu ahetan ahi. Tun Jacob chapate chu somleni ahiuve.
target: While Israel was living in that region, Reuben went in and slept with his father’s concubine Bilhah, and Israel heard of it. Jacob had twelve sons:

source: Leah chapate chu, Jacob chapa masapen Reuben, Simeon, Levi, Judah, Issachar chule Zebulun ahiuve.
target: The sons of Leah: Reuben the firstborn of Jacob, Simeon, Levi, Judah, Issachar and Zebulun.

source: Rachel chapate chu, Joseph le Benjamin ahilhone.
target: The sons of Rachel: Joseph and Benjamin.

source: Chule Rachel sohnu Bilhah chapate chu, Dan le Naphtali ahilhone.
target: The sons of Rachel’s servant Bilhah: Dan and Naphtali.

source: Chule Leah sohnu Zilpah chapate chu, Gad le Asher ahilhone. Hichenghi Jacob chapate Padan-Aram gama pengho chu ahiuve.
target: The sons of Leah’s servant Zilpah: Gad and Asher. These were the sons of Jacob, who were born to him in Paddan Aram.

source: Chuin Jacob Arba khopi, hichu Hebron ahin, Abraham le Isaac pemna mun Mamre'a chun apa Isaac kom ahunglhun tan ahi.
target: Jacob came home to his father Isaac in Mamre, near Kiriath Arba (that is, Hebron), where Abraham and Isaac had stayed.

source: Chule Isaac damsung chu kum jakhat le kum somget ahi.
target: Isaac lived a hundred and eighty years.

source: Chuin Isaac'in alhagao alhan, upatah le teh bongsetnin athitan, amite toh gopkhomin aumtan ahi. Chuin achapa teni Esau le Jacob chun avuilhon tan ahi.
target: Then he breathed his last and died and was gathered to his people, old and full of years. And his sons Esau and Jacob buried him.

source: Tun hichengho hi Edom kiti, Esau chilhah teho chu ahiuve.
target: This is the account of the family line of Esau (that is, Edom).

source: Esau'in Canaan chanute jin akipuijin, amaho chu: Hit mi Elon chanu Adah, chule Hiv mi Zibeon chanu, Anah chanu Aholibamah,
target: Esau took his wives from the women of Canaan: Adah daughter of Elon the Hittite, and Oholibamah daughter of Anah and granddaughter of Zibeon the Hivite—

source: Chule Nebojoth sopinu, Ishmael chanu Bashemath ahiuve.
target: also Basemath daughter of Ishmael and sister of Nebaioth.

source: Chuin Adah'in Esau Eliphaz ahinpeh-in, chule Bashemath'in Reuel ahingin ahi.
target: Adah bore Eliphaz to Esau, Basemath bore Reuel,

source: Chuin Aholibamah'in Jeush, Jaalam chule Korah ahingin ahi. Hichenghi Esau chapate Canaan gama pengho chu ahiuve.
target: and Oholibamah bore Jeush, Jalam and Korah. These were the sons of Esau, who were born to him in Canaan.

source: Chuin Esau'in a-inneipite, achapate, achanute, chule a-insung mite jouse, aganchaho leh agamsa jouse, chule Canaan gama alamdoh aneijouse akitolin, anaopa Jacob'a konin gamchoma achemang tai.
target: Esau took his wives and sons and daughters and all the members of his household, as well as his livestock and all his other animals and all the goods he had acquired in Canaan, and moved to a land some distance from his brother Jacob.

source: Ajehchu amaho munkhatna achenkhom nadiuvin aneiho chu atambehseh tan, chule agancha hou jehchun apemnao gamchun adol tapouvin ahi.
target: Their possessions were too great for them to remain together; the land where they were staying could not support them both because of their livestock.

source: Chutichun Esau Seir molsanga achengtan ahi. Esau chu Edom ahi.
target: So Esau (that is, Edom) settled in the hill country of Seir.

source: Chule hichenghi Seir molsang mun'a Edom mite pa Esau chilhahte chu ahiuvin;
target: This is the account of the family line of Esau the father of the Edomites in the hill country of Seir.

source: Hichenghi Esau chapate minho chu ahi; Esau inneipi Adah chapa Eliphaz, Esau inneipi Bashemath chapa Reuel ahilhone.
target: These are the names of Esau’s sons: Eliphaz, the son of Esau’s wife Adah, and Reuel, the son of Esau’s wife Basemath.

source: Chule Eliphaz chapate chu Teman, Omar, Zepho, Gatam chule Kenaz ahiuve.
target: The sons of Eliphaz: Teman, Omar, Zepho, Gatam and Kenaz.

source: Chule Timna chu Esau chapa Eliphaz thaikemnu ahin; amanun Eliphaz dingin Amalek ahinpeh-in ahi. Hichenghi Esau inneipi Adah chapate ahiuve.
target: Esau’s son Eliphaz also had a concubine named Timna, who bore him Amalek. These were grandsons of Esau’s wife Adah.

source: Chule hichenghi Reuel chapate ahiuve; Nahath, Zerah, Shammah chule Mizzah ahiuve. Hichenghi Esau inneipi Bashemath chapate ahiuve.
target: The sons of Reuel: Nahath, Zerah, Shammah and Mizzah. These were grandsons of Esau’s wife Basemath.

source: Chule hichenghi Zibeon chanu, Anah chanu, Esau inneipi Aholibamah chapate ahiuve. Amanun Esau chu Jeush, Jaalam chule Korah ahinpeh-in ahi.
target: The sons of Esau’s wife Oholibamah daughter of Anah and granddaughter of Zibeon, whom she bore to Esau: Jeush, Jalam and Korah.

source: Hichenghi Esau chapate lah-a apipu ho chu ahiuve: Esau chapa masapen Eliphaz chapate chu, pipu Teman, pipu Omar, pipu Zepho, pipu Kenaz,
target: These were the chiefs among Esau’s descendants: The sons of Eliphaz the firstborn of Esau: Chiefs Teman, Omar, Zepho, Kenaz,

source: Pipu Korah, pipu Gatam, chule pipu Amalek ahiuve. Hicheng hi Edom gama Eliphaz'a kona pengdoh pipu hochu ahiuvin, hichenghi Adah chapate ahiuve.
target: Korah, Gatam and Amalek. These were the chiefs descended from Eliphaz in Edom; they were grandsons of Adah.

source: Hichenghi Esau chapa Reuel chapate ahiuve: Pipu Nahath, pipu Zerah, pipu Shammah, chule pipu Mizzah ahiuve. Hichenghi Edom gama Reuel'a kona pengdoh pipuho chu ahiuvin; hichenghi Esau inneipi Bashemath chapate ahiuve.
target: The sons of Esau’s son Reuel: Chiefs Nahath, Zerah, Shammah and Mizzah. These were the chiefs descended from Reuel in Edom; they were grandsons of Esau’s wife Basemath.

source: Chule hicheng hi Esau inneipi Aholibamah chapate chu ahiuve: Pipu Jeush, pipu Jaalam, pipu Korah ahiuve. Hicheng ho hi Anah chanu, Esau inneipi Aholibama'a kona pengdoh pipu hochu ahiuve.
target: The sons of Esau’s wife Oholibamah: Chiefs Jeush, Jalam and Korah. These were the chiefs descended from Esau’s wife Oholibamah daughter of Anah.

source: Hichenghi Edon kiti Esau chapate ahiuvin, chule hichenghi apipuhou chu ahiuve.
target: These were the sons of Esau (that is, Edom), and these were their chiefs.

source: Hichenghi chuche gama cheng, Hor mi Seir chapate ahiuve: Lotan, Shobal, Zibeon, Anah,
target: These were the sons of Seir the Horite, who were living in the region: Lotan, Shobal, Zibeon, Anah,

source: Dishon, Ezer, chule Dishan ahiuve. Hichengho hi Edom gama Seir chapate, Hor mite pipuho chu ahiuve.
target: Dishon, Ezer and Dishan. These sons of Seir in Edom were Horite chiefs.

source: Chule Lotan chapate chu Hori le Heman ahilhonin; chuleh Lotan sopinu chu Timna ahi.
target: The sons of Lotan: Hori and Homam. Timna was Lotan’s sister.

source: Chule Shobal chapate chu hicheho ahiuve: Alvan, Manahath, Ebal, Shepho, chule Onam ahiuve.
target: The sons of Shobal: Alvan, Manahath, Ebal, Shepho and Onam.

source: Chule hichenghi Zibeon chate chu ahiuve; Ajah chule Anah ahilhone. Hiche Anah hi ahi apa Zibeon sanganho gamthipma achinna-a sanganpi ho mudohpa chu.
target: The sons of Zibeon: Aiah and Anah. This is the Anah who discovered the hot springs in the desert while he was grazing the donkeys of his father Zibeon.

source: Chule Anah chate chu hichenghi ahiuve; Dishon le, Anah chanu Aholibamah ahilhone.
target: The children of Anah: Dishon and Oholibamah daughter of Anah.

source: Chule hichenghi Dishon chate chu ahiuve; Hemdan, Eshban, Ithran, chule Cheran ahiuve.
target: The sons of Dishon: Hemdan, Eshban, Ithran and Keran.

source: Ezer chate chu hichenghi ahiuve; Bilhan, Zaavan, chule Akan ahiuve.
target: The sons of Ezer: Bilhan, Zaavan and Akan.

source: Dishan chate chu hichenghi ahiuve; Uz le, Aran ahilhone.
target: The sons of Dishan: Uz and Aran.

source: Hicheng hi Hor mite-a kona hungpeng doh pipu hochu ahiuve: Pipu Lotan, pipu Shobal, pipu Zibeon, pipu Anah,
target: These were the Horite chiefs: Lotan, Shobal, Zibeon, Anah,

source: Pipu Dishon, pipu Ezer, chule pipu Dishan ahiuve. Hichengho hi Seir gama pipu holah-a Hor mite hung dohna pipuho chu ahiuve.
target: Dishon, Ezer and Dishan. These were the Horite chiefs, according to their divisions, in the land of Seir.

source: Chule hichengho hi Israel chate chunga koimacha ana lengchan masanga, Edom gama analeng changa lengho chu ahiuve.
target: These were the kings who reigned in Edom before any Israelite king reigned:

source: Beor chapa Bela chu Edom'ah ana leng changin; chule akhopi min chu Dinhabah anahi.
target: Bela son of Beor became king of Edom. His city was named Dinhabah.

source: Chuin Bela chu athitan, Bozra gama Zerah chapa, Jobab chu akhelin analeng changin ahi.
target: When Bela died, Jobab son of Zerah from Bozrah succeeded him as king.

source: Chuin Jobab chu athitan, Temani gama Husham chu amakhelin analeng changin ahi.
target: When Jobab died, Husham from the land of the Temanites succeeded him as king.

source: Chuin Husham chu athitan, Moab gamlah-a Midian thatpa Bedad chapa Hadad chu ama khelin aleng changin ahi. Chule akhopi min chu Avith ahi.
target: When Husham died, Hadad son of Bedad, who defeated Midian in the country of Moab, succeeded him as king. His city was named Avith.

source: Chuin Hadad chu athitan, Mashrekah mi Samlah chu akhelin analeng change.
target: When Hadad died, Samlah from Masrekah succeeded him as king.

source: Chuin Samlah athitan, luipi panga Rehoboth kho-a Shaul chu ama khelin analeng changin ahi.
target: When Samlah died, Shaul from Rehoboth on the river succeeded him as king.

source: Chuin Shaul chu athitan, Achbor chapa Baal-hanan chu ama khelin analeng changin ahi.
target: When Shaul died, Baal-Hanan son of Akbor succeeded him as king.

source: Chuin Akchbor chapa Baal-hanan chu athitan, ama khelin Hadar analeng change. Chuleh akhopi min chu Pau ahin; chule a-inneipi chu Matred chanu, Mezahab chanu Mehetabel ahi.
target: When Baal-Hanan son of Akbor died, Hadad succeeded him as king. His city was named Pau, and his wife’s name was Mehetabel daughter of Matred, the daughter of Me-Zahab.

source: Hichengho hi a-insung dungjuiju, achennao munho dungjuile, aminu dungjuija Esau'a kon hungdoh pipu hochu ahiuve; Pipu Timnah, pipu Alvah, pipu Jetheth,
target: These were the chiefs descended from Esau, by name, according to their clans and regions: Timna, Alvah, Jetheth,

source: Pipu Aholibamah, pipu Elah, pipu Pinon,
target: Oholibamah, Elah, Pinon,

source: Pipu Kenaz, pipu Teman, pipu Mibzar,
target: Kenaz, Teman, Mibzar,

source: Pipu Magdiel, chule pipu Iram ahiuve. Hichengho hi agoulona gama achennao dungjuija Edom pipuho chu ahiuve. Amachu Edom mite pa Esau ahi.
target: Magdiel and Iram. These were the chiefs of Edom, according to their settlements in the land they occupied. This is the family line of Esau, the father of the Edomites.

source: Chuin Jacob apa kholjina gam, Canaan gama chun achengtan ahi.
target: Jacob lived in the land where his father had stayed, the land of Canaan.

source: Hichenghi Jacob achilhah ho chu ahiuve. Joseph chu kum som le kum sagi alhinin, asopite toh ganchahon achingun; chule chapang chu apa inneipi teni Bilhah chapate le Zilpah chapate toh aumin ahi. Chuin Joseph'in agitlounau thuthang chu apa henga alhutjin ahi.
target: This is the account of Jacob’s family line. Joseph, a young man of seventeen, was tending the flocks with his brothers, the sons of Bilhah and the sons of Zilpah, his father’s wives, and he brought their father a bad report about them.

source: Tun Israel'in Joseph chu atehnunga ahin achapa ahijeh chun, achapa dang jouse sangin angailun ahi. Chuin aman amachu sangkhol chol jemchom choma pol asempeh-in ahi.
target: Now Israel loved Joseph more than any of his other sons, because he had been born to him in his old age; and he made an ornate robe for him.

source: Chuin amachu asopiho jouse sangin apauvin angailujoi ti a-ute chun amuphatnun, amahon amachu aho taovin, kam ngeijin ahouthei tapouvin ahi.
target: When his brothers saw that their father loved him more than any of them, they hated him and could not speak a kind word to him.

source: Chuin Joseph'in mang aneijin, hichu asopite henga aseipeh-in ahi. Chuin amahon amachu anahot locheh taovin ahi.
target: Joseph had a dream, and when he told it to his brothers, they hated him all the more.

source: Chuin aman ahenguva, Katao ahi, keiman kamangmat hiche mang hi ngaitemun,
target: He said to them, “Listen to this dream I had:

source: Ajehchu veuvin, eihon louva changphal inakanun, chule veuvin, keima changphal chu ahung kipatdoh-in, adingjang petnin; chuin veuvin, nangho changphal hochu ahung ding kimvelun, keima changphal chu chibai aboh-un ahi, ati.
target: We were binding sheaves of grain out in the field when suddenly my sheaf rose and stood upright, while your sheaves gathered around mine and bowed down to it.”

source: Chuin a-ute chun ahenga, Nangma kachunguva nalengchan mongding ham? Ahilouleh nangma kachunguva vaihoma napan mongding ham? atiuve. Chuin amahon amachu ahotbecheh jeng taovin ahi.
target: His brothers said to him, “Do you intend to reign over us? Will you actually rule us?” And they hated him all the more because of his dream and what he had said.

source: Chuin aman mang chomkhat amat kitnin, chule hichu a-ute henga ahilin, ajah uvah, Veuvin keiman mang khat kanei kitnin ahi; chule veuvin, nisa, lhathah chule ahsi somlekhat nin chibai eina boh-e, ati.
target: Then he had another dream, and he told it to his brothers. “Listen,” he said, “I had another dream, and this time the sun and moon and eleven stars were bowing down to me.”

source: Chuin aman hichu apa leh a-ute aseipehtan ahi. Chuin apan amachu aphoh-in, ajah-a, Namang neihi ipi mang ham? Keima le nanu chule nasopite hi nangma henga tolla bohkhupma chibai boh dinga kahung mong diuham? ati.
target: When he told his father as well as his brothers, his father rebuked him and said, “What is this dream you had? Will your mother and I and your brothers actually come and bow down to the ground before you?”

source: Chuin a-uten amachu amitthip taovin; ahin apa vangin thu kiseichu aching jingin ahi.
target: His brothers were jealous of him, but his father kept the matter in mind.

source: Chuin a-ute chu apao ganchahon vah dingin Shechem'a achetauvin ahi.
target: Now his brothers had gone to graze their father’s flocks near Shechem,

source: Chuin Israel'in Joseph henga, Na-uten gancha hon Shechem'a avah-u hilouham? Hungin, keiman nangma amaho henga solinge, ati. Chuin aman ahenga, Hikoma ka ume, ati.
target: and Israel said to Joseph, “As you know, your brothers are grazing the flocks near Shechem. Come, I am going to send you to them.” “Very well,” he replied.

source: Chuin aman ahenga, Katao ahi, chenlang na-ute ho dam naovem, chule ganchahon jong dam naovem gavenlang, chule kahenga thu hinpo kitnin, ati. Chutichun aman amachu Hebron phaichama konin asolin, chuin ama Shechem aga lhungtai.
target: So he said to him, “Go and see if all is well with your brothers and with the flocks, and bring word back to me.” Then he sent him off from the Valley of Hebron. When Joseph arrived at Shechem,

source: Chuin mi koiham khatnin amachu amun, chule veuvin, ama gamlah-a avahlen ahi. Chuin mipa chun ahenga, Ipi nahol ham? tin adongin ahi.
target: a man found him wandering around in the fields and asked him, “What are you looking for?”

source: Chuin aman, ka-ute kahol ahi. Nahenga katao ahi, hoija aganchahon nu avah-um neisei peh-in, ati.
target: He replied, “I’m looking for my brothers. Can you tell me where they are grazing their flocks?”

source: Chuin mipa chun, Amaho hia konin achetauve; ajehchu amahon Dothan'a cheohite atiu kajai, ati. Chuin Joseph'in a-ute chu anungdelin, Dothan'a chun agamutan ahi.
target: “They have moved on from here,” the man answered. “I heard them say, ‘Let’s go to Dothan.’ ” So Joseph went after his brothers and found them near Dothan.

source: Chuin amahon amachu gamlatah-a agahmu phatnun, amaho lam ahungnai masangin, amahon ama tha ding thu ana kihousom taove.
target: But they saw him in the distance, and before he reached them, they plotted to kill him.

source: Chuin khatnin khat henga aseijin, Veuvin, mang neipa chu ahunge.
target: “Here comes that dreamer!” they said to each other.

source: Hijeh chun tun hunguvin, amahi thatnu hitin, kokhuh khat touva seplutnu hitin, chule eihon, Gamsa hang khat touvin atha ahitai tiu hite: chule amang chu ipi ahungso ivet dingu ahi, akitiuve.
target: “Come now, let’s kill him and throw him into one of these cisterns and say that a ferocious animal devoured him. Then we’ll see what comes of his dreams.”

source: Chuin Reuben'in hichu ajan, akhut nuva konchun ahuhdoh-in; chule, Eihon amahi that pou hite, atin ahi.
target: When Reuben heard this, he tried to rescue him from their hands. “Let’s not take his life,” he said.

source: Chuin Reuben'in akhutnuva kona chudoh-a, apa henga anungsolpeh theina dingin, ajah uva, Thisan sohih beh-un, amavang gamthip laija hiche kokhuh-a khun galeh lutnuvin lang achunga vang khut lhahih-un ati.
target: “Don’t shed any blood. Throw him into this cistern here in the wilderness, but don’t lay a hand on him.” Reuben said this to rescue him from them and take him back to his father.

source: Chuin ahitin ahi, Joseph chu a-ute heng ahung lhun phatnin, amahon Joseph'in aki-ah sangkhol chol, ajemchom choma pol chu asutlhah peh-un;
target: So when Joseph came to his brothers, they stripped him of his robe—the ornate robe he was wearing—

source: Chule amahon amachu apuijun, kokhuh sunga alehlut taove. Hiche kokhuh chu akeo ahin, asunga twi umlou ahi.
target: and they took him and threw him into the cistern. The cistern was empty; there was no water in it.

source: Chuin amaho an nedingin atou taovin ahi. Chuin amaho akhodah-un ahile, veuvin, Ishmael honkhat Gilead gama kona asangongsao houtoh thil namtui, thingnailou, chule Myrrh hinpo-a, Egypt gama posuh dinga cheho chu amuvin ahi.
target: As they sat down to eat their meal, they looked up and saw a caravan of Ishmaelites coming from Gilead. Their camels were loaded with spices, balm and myrrh, and they were on their way to take them down to Egypt.

source: Chuin Judah'in asopite henga, Eihon inaopao ithaova, athisan isouva ipi phachom ding ham?
target: Judah said to his brothers, “What will we gain if we kill our brother and cover up his blood?

source: Hungun, Ishmael mite henga johdoh-u hitin, achunga ikhutnu lhapouhite; ajehchu ama inaopao ahin, itahsa mongu ahibouve, ati. Chuin asopiten athu angai taovin ahi.
target: Come, let’s sell him to the Ishmaelites and not lay our hands on him; after all, he is our brother, our own flesh and blood.” His brothers agreed.

source: Chuin Midian sumkol veiho chun ahinho pauvin ahile, amahon Joseph chu kokhuh-a konin akaidoh-un, Ishmael miho henga chun dangka somni dingin ajoh taovin ahi. Chuin amahon Joseph chu Egypt gama apuitaove.
target: So when the Midianite merchants came by, his brothers pulled Joseph up out of the cistern and sold him for twenty shekels of silver to the Ishmaelites, who took him to Egypt.

source: Chuin Reuben kokhuh-a ahung kitnin ahile; veuvin, Joseph chu kokhuh-a ana umtapon; aman apon asattel jengin ahi.
target: When Reuben returned to the cistern and saw that Joseph was not there, he tore his clothes.

source: Chuin ama asopite henga ahung kilen, ahenguva, Chapang chu aumtapoi; keima hi hoilama chetang katem? ati.
target: He went back to his brothers and said, “The boy isn’t there! Where can I turn now?”

source: Chuin amahon Joseph sangkhol chol chu alauvin, kelcha khat athatnun, athisan lah-a chun sangkhol chol chu adeuvin ahi.
target: Then they got Joseph’s robe, slaughtered a goat and dipped the robe in the blood.

source: Chuin amahon sangkhol chol jemchom choma kisem chu apau athotnun, chule amahon ahenga ahin choijun, ajah-a, Hichehi keihon kamu-u ahi: nachapa sangkhol chol ahi ahilou nahet em? atiuve.
target: They took the ornate robe back to their father and said, “We found this. Examine it to see whether it is your son’s robe.”

source: Chuin aman hichu ahetan, Hichehi kachapa sangkhol chol ahi; gamsa hangin anehjou hiding hitahi; Joseph hi thonlouva ahal hala asatel hitahi, ati.
target: He recognized it and said, “It is my son’s robe! Some ferocious animal has devoured him. Joseph has surely been torn to pieces.”

source: Chuin Jacob'in aponsil ho asat telin, akonga khaodip pon akichenin, nitampi achapa pul adouvin ahi.
target: Then Jacob tore his clothes, put on sackcloth and mourned for his son many days.

source: Chuin achapate jouse le achanute jouse ama lhamon dingin akipatnun; ahivangin ama lhamon ding anompon; Ajehchu chu keima lhankhuh-a lunghem puma kachapa henga cheding kahi, ati. Chutichun apa chu ama dingin akap akapmin ahi.
target: All his sons and daughters came to comfort him, but he refused to be comforted. “No,” he said, “I will continue to mourn until I join my son in the grave.” So his father wept for him.

source: Chuin Midian mihon amachu Egypt gama Pharoah noija pipu, ngahtup ho lah-a lamkai Potipher henga ajoh taovin ahi.
target: Meanwhile, the Midianites sold Joseph in Egypt to Potiphar, one of Pharaoh’s officials, the captain of the guard.

source: Chuin hiche laichun ahitin ahi, Judah chu asopite lah-a konin achesuh-in, Adulam mikhat amin Hirah chu agabeltan ahi
target: At that time, Judah left his brothers and went down to stay with a man of Adullam named Hirah.

source: Chuin hia chun Judah chun amin Shua kiti Canaan mikhat chanu amutan; chule aman amanu chu akichenpin, ahenga aluttan ahi.
target: There Judah met the daughter of a Canaanite man named Shua. He married her and made love to her;

source: Chuin amanun nao avopmin, chapa khat ahingin; chule aman amin Er asah-in ahi.
target: she became pregnant and gave birth to a son, who was named Er.

source: Chuin amanun nao avoppai kitnin, chapa khat ahingin; aman amin Onan asah-in ahi.
target: She conceived again and gave birth to a son and named him Onan.

source: Chuin amanun nao avopkitnin, chapa khat ahingin; amin Shelah asah-in ahi. Amanun ama ahinna chun amapa Cherib'a aumin ahi.
target: She gave birth to still another son and named him Shelah. It was at Kezib that she gave birth to him.

source: Chuin Judah'in achapa masa Er ding chun ji apuipeh-in, amin Tamar ahi.
target: Judah got a wife for Er, his firstborn, and her name was Tamar.

source: Chuin Judah cha masapen Er chu Pakai mitmun akhang gilou lheh-in ahile, Pakaiyin amachu athat tan ahi.
target: But Er, Judah’s firstborn, was wicked in the Lord ’s sight; so the Lord put him to death.

source: Chuin Judah'in Onan henga, Na-upa inneipi henga galutnin lang, amachu kichenpin, chule na-upa dingin chi khaipeh-in, ati.
target: Then Judah said to Onan, “Sleep with your brother’s wife and fulfill your duty to her as a brother-in-law to raise up offspring for your brother.”

source: Chuin Onan'in achikhai chu ama-a ahilouding chu ahen; chuin ahitin ahi, ama a-upa inneipi henga alut phatnin, a-upa dinga chi akhai pehlouna din, tolla alhi lhajin ahi.
target: But Onan knew that the child would not be his; so whenever he slept with his brother’s wife, he spilled his semen on the ground to keep from providing offspring for his brother.

source: Chuin athilbol chun Pakai alung lhaitapon; hijeh chun amajong athattan ahi.
target: What he did was wicked in the Lord ’s sight; so the Lord put him to death also.

source: Chujouvin Judah'in amounu Tamar henga, Kachapa Shelah ahung khandoh kahsen, napa in'a meithaijin ana umtan, ati. Ajehchu aman, Ama jonghi a-uteni bangin thiget inte ati ahi. Chuin Tamar achen, apa in'a agachengtan ahi.
target: Judah then said to his daughter-in-law Tamar, “Live as a widow in your father’s household until my son Shelah grows up.” For he thought, “He may die too, just like his brothers.” So Tamar went to live in her father’s household.

source: Chuin phat chomkhat jouvin Shua chanu Judah inneipi chu athitan ahi; chuin Judah chu lhep lung mongin aumtan, ama le agolpa Adullam mi Hira chu Timnah'a kelngoimul vouho henga agachetou lhonin ahi.
target: After a long time Judah’s wife, the daughter of Shua, died. When Judah had recovered from his grief, he went up to Timnah, to the men who were shearing his sheep, and his friend Hirah the Adullamite went with him.

source: Chuin Tamar henga chun, Ven natehpu akelngoi mul voudingin Timnah'a achetouve, tin aseipeh-un ahi.
target: When Tamar was told, “Your father-in-law is on his way to Timnah to shear his sheep,”

source: Chuin aman ameithai vonho ahohlhan, pon lukhuh akikhuh in, akitomchah-in, Timnah jotna lampi mun onglai khatna atouvin ahi; ajehchu Shelah chu kikhan lhitna ahitan, akichenpi dinga apehlou chu amanun ahet ahi.
target: she took off her widow’s clothes, covered herself with a veil to disguise herself, and then sat down at the entrance to Enaim, which is on the road to Timnah. For she saw that, though Shelah had now grown up, she had not been given to him as his wife.

source: Judah'in amanu chu amuphatnin, amai akhujeh chun noti hinte tin angaiton ahi.
target: When Judah saw her, he thought she was a prostitute, for she had covered her face.

source: Chuin ama lampama amanu henglama chun akiheijin, ajah-a, Katao ahi, hungin, keima nahenga hunglut inge, ati (Ajehchu aman amounu ahilam chu ahetlou ahi.) Chuin amanun, Kahenga nahunglut dinga ahile, ipi neipeh ding ham, ati.
target: Not realizing that she was his daughter-in-law, he went over to her by the roadside and said, “Come now, let me sleep with you.” “And what will you give me to sleep with you?” she asked.

source: Chuin aman, Keiman ganhon lah-a konin kelnou khat hinthot nange, ati. Chuin amanun, Nangman hichu nahinthot masanga, kitepna khat neipeh ding hinam? ati.
target: “I’ll send you a young goat from my flock,” he said. “Will you give me something as a pledge until you send it?” she asked.

source: Chuin aman, Ipi kitepna kapeh ding ham? ati. Chuin amanun, Na mahor, na chao, chule nakhutna um natenggol chu neipen, ati. Chuin aman hichu amanu apen, chule amanu henga aluttan, chule amanun amapa-a konin nao avoptan ahi.
target: He said, “What pledge should I give you?” “Your seal and its cord, and the staff in your hand,” she answered. So he gave them to her and slept with her, and she became pregnant by him.

source: Chuin amanu akipatdoh-in, achemangin, aponkhu chu ahohlhan, chule ameithai von chu akivon kittan ahi.
target: After she left, she took off her veil and put on her widow’s clothes again.

source: Chuin Judah chun numeinu khutna kona akitepna thilho ladingin, agolpa Adullam mi khutna chun kelnou khat chu athotnin ahi. Ahinla aman amanu chu amujou tapon ahi.
target: Meanwhile Judah sent the young goat by his friend the Adullamite in order to get his pledge back from the woman, but he did not find her.

source: Chuin aman chuche munna miho chu adongin, Lam pama mun ong laija notinu chu hoija umtam? ati. Chuin amahon, Hiche mun'a noti koima aumpoi, atiuve.
target: He asked the men who lived there, “Where is the shrine prostitute who was beside the road at Enaim?” “There hasn’t been any shrine prostitute here,” they said.

source: Chuin ama Judah henga ahung kilen, ajah-a, Amanu chu kaga mujoupoi; chule chuche mun'a mihon jong, Hiche mun'a koima noti aumpoi, atiuve, tin aseijin ahi.
target: So he went back to Judah and said, “I didn’t find her. Besides, the men who lived there said, ‘There hasn’t been any shrine prostitute here.’ ”

source: Chuin Judah'in thil chu amanu changden tahen, achuti loule kijumso get hite;ven, hiche kelnou hi kathotnin, amanula nagamu joupoi, ati.
target: Then Judah said, “Let her keep what she has, or we will become a laughingstock. After all, I did send her this young goat, but you didn’t find her.”

source: Chuin ahitin ahi, lha thum jouvin, Judah henga, Namounu Tamar noti'n apangin, chukal valin jong, ven, ajon na-a konin nao avoptai, tin aseipeh-un ahi. Chuin Judah'in, Amanu chu hinpui doh-un, chule kihal lihhen, ati.
target: About three months later Judah was told, “Your daughter-in-law Tamar is guilty of prostitution, and as a result she is now pregnant.” Judah said, “Bring her out and have her burned to death!”

source: Chuin amanu ahinpuidoh phatnun, Hiche thilho neipa-a kona hi naovopma kahi, tin atehpu henga chun thu agathot tan ahi. Chuin amanun, Katao ahi, hiche mahor, chao, chule tenggol hi koija ham? vechenin, ati.
target: As she was being brought out, she sent a message to her father-in-law. “I am pregnant by the man who owns these,” she said. And she added, “See if you recognize whose seal and cord and staff these are.”

source: Chuin Judah'in chuche thilho chu ama-a ahi chu ahetan, Amanu keisangin achonphajon ahi; ajehchu kachapa Shelah amanu dinga kapehlou jeh ahi, ati. Chuin amanu chu akal akitimatpi kittapon ahi.
target: Judah recognized them and said, “She is more righteous than I, since I wouldn’t give her to my son Shelah.” And he did not sleep with her again.

source: Chuin amanu naosonat phat ahunglhin phatnin ahitin ahi, veuvin, naobu sunga chun apengkop ding ni anaumin ahi.
target: When the time came for her to give birth, there were twin boys in her womb.

source: Chule ahitin ahi, amanu anaovin ahinheh phatnin, khatnin akhut ahinsoh doh-in ahile, naodom nun, Hichehi ahung sohdoh masajo ahi tin akhut chu alan, pat sandup abupeh-in ahi.
target: As she was giving birth, one of them put out his hand; so the midwife took a scarlet thread and tied it on his wrist and said, “This one came out first.”

source: Chuin ahitin ahi, aman akhut aloilut kit phatnin, veuvin asopipa ahungdohtan ahi. Chuin amanun, Iti nahin phut vang ham? hiche phutkeh nahi nachunga umhen, ati: hijeh chun amin Pharez asah taove.
target: But when he drew back his hand, his brother came out, and she said, “So this is how you have broken out!” And he was named Perez.

source: Chuin chuche jouchun akhutna pat sandup kibua asopipa chu ahung pengtan ahi. Chuin amin Zarah asah taovin ahi.
target: Then his brother, who had the scarlet thread on his wrist, came out. And he was named Zerah.

source: Chuin Joseph chu Egypt gama apuisuh-un; chule Pharoah noija pipu khat, ngahtup loilah-a lamkai Egypt mi Potipher chun hinpui suh-a Ishmael miho khutna konin achotan ahi.
target: Now Joseph had been taken down to Egypt. Potiphar, an Egyptian who was one of Pharaoh’s officials, the captain of the guard, bought him from the Ishmaelites who had taken him there.

source: Chuin Pakaiyin Joseph chu aumpin, amachu milolhing tah ahung hita; chule apu Egypt mipa in'a chun aumin ahi.
target: The Lord was with Joseph so that he prospered, and he lived in the house of his Egyptian master.

source: Chuin Pakaiyin ama aumpia, atoh jouse chu Pakaiyin akhut na alolhinsah chu apupa chun amutai.
target: When his master saw that the Lord was with him and that the Lord gave him success in everything he did,

source: Chuin Joseph apu mitmun lungsetna achangtan, amachu ajen letan ahi. Chuin ama insung vetup ding chun akoijin, aneijouse chu akhutna akoitan ahi.
target: Joseph found favor in his eyes and became his attendant. Potiphar put him in charge of his household, and he entrusted to his care everything he owned.

source: Chuin ahitin ahi, a-insung le anei jouse chunga avetup dinga akoi nikho-a pat chun Pakaiyin Joseph jal-in Egypt mipa insung chu phatthei aboh tan; chule Pakai phatthei bohchu a-insung alouma chule aneijouse chunga chun aumtan ahi.
target: From the time he put him in charge of his household and of all that he owned, the Lord blessed the household of the Egyptian because of Joseph. The blessing of the Lord was on everything Potiphar had, both in the house and in the field.

source: Chuin aman aneijouse Joseph khutna akoisohtan, chule anehding an tailou ahetding dol thiljong ahetapon ahi. Chule Joseph chu migong hoitah le melhoitah ahi.
target: So Potiphar left everything he had in Joseph’s care; with Joseph in charge, he did not concern himself with anything except the food he ate. Now Joseph was well-built and handsome,

source: Chuin hiche nungchun ahitin ahi, apu inneipi chun Joseph chu deichat mitnin avetan, chule amanun Neiluppin, atin ahi.
target: and after a while his master’s wife took notice of Joseph and said, “Come to bed with me!”

source: Ahivangin ama anompon, apu inneipi henga chun, Vetan kapun hiche insunga hi kakhutna ipipi um ahi ahepon, chule aman aneijouse kakhutna akoi ahitai.
target: But he refused. “With me in charge,” he told her, “my master does not concern himself with anything in the house; everything he owns he has entrusted to my care.

source: Hiche insunga hi keima sanga lenjo koima aumpon; chujongle nangma a-inneipi nahi jeh-in nangma tailou hiche insunga aman keima khutna apehdoh lou imacha umlou ahi. Chuti ahile keiman hitobang khangitlouna lentah hi iti kabola, Pathen douna-a kachonset thei ding ham? ati.
target: No one is greater in this house than I am. My master has withheld nothing from me except you, because you are his wife. How then could I do such a wicked thing and sin against God?”

source: Chuin ahitin ahi, amanun Joseph luppi ding ahiloule aumpi dinga niseh-a aseivangin, aman amanu chu lungna changin angai pehpon ahi.
target: And though she spoke to Joseph day after day, he refused to go to bed with her or even be with her.

source: Chuin chuche laiphat chun ahitin ahi, Joseph chu insunga kinbol dingin agalutnin ahile, insunga chun koimacha aumpon ahi.
target: One day he went into the house to attend to his duties, and none of the household servants was inside.

source: Chuin amanun, Neiluppin, atin amachu aponsilin amanin ahi. Chuin aman aponsil chu amanu khutna chun adalhan, ajamin, insunga kon chun apotdoh tan ahi.
target: She caught him by his cloak and said, “Come to bed with me!” But he left his cloak in her hand and ran out of the house.

source: Chuin ahitin ahi, amanun akhutna apon adalhan, insunga konin ajamdoh tai, ti ahet phatnin,
target: When she saw that he had left his cloak in her hand and had run out of the house,

source: Amanun a-insunga miho chu akouvin, ajah uvah, Vetaovin eiho jum sahdin aman Hebrew mikhat ihenguva ahin puilutnin; eiluppi dingin amapa kahenga ahung lutnin, chuin keima hapenin kapeng jah jengin ahi.
target: she called her household servants. “Look,” she said to them, “this Hebrew has been brought to us to make sport of us! He came in here to sleep with me, but I screamed.

source: Chuin ahitin ahi, Aman aw sangtah-a kapenjah jengchu ahet phatnin, aponsil kakoma adalhan ajamin, insunga konin ajamdoh tan ahi, ati.
target: When he heard me scream for help, he left his cloak beside me and ran out of the house.”

source: Chuin amanun a-pakaipa in ahunglhun kahsen, aponsil chu akoma akoi jingin ahi.
target: She kept his cloak beside her until his master came home.

source: Chuin amanun chuche thu mama chu ahenga aseijin, Ihenguva nahin puilut Hebrew mi sohpa chu eisujum dingin kahenga ahung lutnin ahi.
target: Then she told him this story: “That Hebrew slave you brought us came to me to make sport of me.

source: Chuin ahitin ahi, aw sangtah-a kapenjah phatnin, aman aponsil kakoma adalhan, ajamdoh tai, ati.
target: But as soon as I screamed for help, he left his cloak beside me and ran out of the house.”

source: Chuin ahitin ahi, Joseph pakaipa chun a-inneipin ahenga, Nasohpan hitihin eibole, tia aseichu ajah phatnin, alunghan akoujah jengin ahi.
target: When his master heard the story his wife told him, saying, “This is how your slave treated me,” he burned with anger.

source: Chuin a-pakaipa chun Joseph chu akaijin, lengte soh changho kihenna mun songkul'a chun akoitan; chule ama songkul'a chun aumtan ahi.
target: Joseph’s master took him and put him in prison, the place where the king’s prisoners were confined. But while Joseph was there in the prison,

source: Ahivangin Pakaiyin Joseph aumpin, hepina amusah-in, chule songkul ngahpa mitmu-a lungsetna achansahtan ahi.
target: the Lord was with him; he showed him kindness and granted him favor in the eyes of the prison warden.

source: Chuin songkul ngahpa chun songkul'a um sohchangho jouse chu Joseph khutna achinsahtan; chule chumuna kibol jouse chu, Joseph mopohna ahitai.
target: So the warden put Joseph in charge of all those held in the prison, and he was made responsible for all that was done there.

source: Pakaiyin aumpi jeh le atoh tapou chu Pakaiyin alolhinsah jeh-in, akhut noija thil umpou pou chu songkul ngahpan adonkhoh tapon ahi.
target: The warden paid no attention to anything under Joseph’s care, because the Lord was with Joseph and gave him success in whatever he did.

source: Chuin chucheng thil jouse nungin ahitin ahi, Egypt lengpa jukhon dompa le changlhah sempa chun a-pakaiyu, Egypt lengpa chu alung phatmosah lhontan ahi.
target: Some time later, the cupbearer and the baker of the king of Egypt offended their master, the king of Egypt.

source: Chuin Pharoah noija pipu teni, jukhon dom pipu le changlhah sem pipu chunga alunghang tan ahi.
target: Pharaoh was angry with his two officials, the chief cupbearer and the chief baker,

source: Chuin aman Joseph kihenna songkul ngah ho lamkaipa in, kihenna mun'a chun amani chu akhumtai.
target: and put them in custody in the house of the captain of the guard, in the same prison where Joseph was confined.

source: Chuin ngahtup ho lamkaipa chun amani vetup dingin Joseph chu akoijin, chule aman amani chu ajenletan ahi. Chule kihenna munna chun amani phat chomkhat a-umlhontan ahi.
target: The captain of the guard assigned them to Joseph, and he attended them. After they had been in custody for some time,

source: Chuin songkul'a um Egypt lengpa jukhon dompa le changlhah kangpa mang amat lhonin, anilhona jan khatna aneicheh lhon ahin, chule anilhonin aledohna to amangmat tha cheh lhonin ahi.
target: each of the two men—the cupbearer and the baker of the king of Egypt, who were being held in prison—had a dream the same night, and each dream had a meaning of its own.

source: Chuin Joseph chu jingkah-in amani henga ahungin, amani chu aven ahile, veuvin amani anguichet jeng lhonin ahi.
target: When Joseph came to them the next morning, he saw that they were dejected.

source: Chuin aman a-pakaipa indan khatna aumpi Pharaoh vaipo teni chu adongin, Ibola nangni tunia hi hiti nguichet jeng nahi lhonham? ati.
target: So he asked Pharaoh’s officials who were in custody with him in his master’s house, “Why do you look so sad today?”

source: Chuin amanin ahengah, Keinin mang kamat lhonin, ahinla hichu aledohding koima aumpoi, atilhone. Chuin Joseph'in amani hengah, Aledoh nachu Pathen'a um hilouham? Kahenga neiseipeh lhonin tia katao ahi, ati.
target: “We both had dreams,” they answered, “but there is no one to interpret them.” Then Joseph said to them, “Do not interpretations belong to God? Tell me your dreams.”

source: Chuin juhai dom pipu chun amang chu ahilin, ajah-a, Kamangin, veuvin, kamasanga lengpigui khat anaumin;
target: So the chief cupbearer told Joseph his dream. He said to him, “In my dream I saw a vine in front of me,

source: Chule lengpiguija chun abah thum aumin; chule hichu amum hung kisem bangin aumin, apah ho ahung sohdoh-in, chule apahboh hochun lengpiga minho chu ahinsodoh tan ahi.
target: and on the vine were three branches. As soon as it budded, it blossomed, and its clusters ripened into grapes.

source: Chuin Pharaoh khon chu kakhutna hin anaumin; chule keiman lengpiga chu kanalan, Pharaoh khonsunga kana mehlhan, chuin keiman khon chu Pharaoh khutna kanapen ahi, ati.
target: Pharaoh’s cup was in my hand, and I took the grapes, squeezed them into Pharaoh’s cup and put the cup in his hand.”

source: Chuin Joseph'in ahenga, Hiche hi aledohna chu ahi: Abah thum hochu nithum ahi.
target: “This is what it means,” Joseph said to him. “The three branches are three days.

source: Nithum sunga Pharaoh'in nangma nalhadoh-a, natoh mun'a napansah kitding ahi. Chule masanga nangma ajukhon doma napan laija banga, Pharaoh khonchu akhutna napeh kitding ahi.
target: Within three days Pharaoh will lift up your head and restore you to your position, and you will put Pharaoh’s cup in his hand, just as you used to do when you were his cupbearer.

source: Ahin nangma dinga thil aphatsoh phatle keima neihin geldoh inlang, kachunga hin lungsetna neihin musah-in, chule Pharaoh henga kaumchan hinseijin lang, hiche in'a konhin neihung puidoh teijin.
target: But when all goes well with you, remember me and show me kindness; mention me to Pharaoh and get me out of this prison.

source: Ajehchu tahbeh-a keima hi Hebrew mite gamsunga kona eikigudoh ahin; chule hikom jenga jong hi hiche gimbolna mun'a eikikhum nathei khopma ima katohset umlou ahi, ati.
target: I was forcibly carried off from the land of the Hebrews, and even here I have done nothing to deserve being put in a dungeon.”

source: Chuin changlhah sem pipu chun aledohna chu aphalam ahi ti amuphatnin, Joseph henga, Keiman jong mangkhat kana matnin, chule veuvin, changlhah lothum kalu chunga kathopton ahi.
target: When the chief baker saw that Joseph had given a favorable interpretation, he said to Joseph, “I too had a dream: On my head were three baskets of bread.

source: Chuin achung nungpen lo-a chun Pharaoh dinga kihon nehthei namkim aumin; chuin kalu chunga lo-a konchun vachaten hichu aneuvin ahi, ati.
target: In the top basket were all kinds of baked goods for Pharaoh, but the birds were eating them out of the basket on my head.”

source: Chuin Joseph'in adonbutnin, ahenga, Hiche hi aledoh nachu ahi: Lo thum chu nithum ahin;
target: “This is what it means,” Joseph said. “The three baskets are three days.

source: Nithum sunga Pharaoh'in nangma nalhadoh-a thingchunga nakhai ding; chule vachaten nasa anehdiu ahi, ati.
target: Within three days Pharaoh will lift off your head and impale your body on a pole. And the birds will eat away your flesh.”

source: Chuin nithum chanin ahitin ahi, hichu Pharaoh pen nikho ahin, aman asohte jouse din golvah abolin ahi. Chuin aman jukhon dom pipu le changlhah sem pipu chu asohte lah-a apuidoh tan ahi.
target: Now the third day was Pharaoh’s birthday, and he gave a feast for all his officials. He lifted up the heads of the chief cupbearer and the chief baker in the presence of his officials:

source: Chuin aman jukhon dom pipu chu ajukhon dopna mun'a apansah kitnin; chuin aman khon chu Pharaoh khutna apekit tan ahi.
target: He restored the chief cupbearer to his position, so that he once again put the cup into Pharaoh’s hand—

source: Ahivangin aman changlhah sem pipu chu Joseph'in aheng lhona aledoh bangchun, akhailih tan ahi.
target: but he impaled the chief baker, just as Joseph had said to them in his interpretation.

source: Ahinla jukhon dom pipu chun Joseph ageldoh tapon, amachu asumiltan ahi.
target: The chief cupbearer, however, did not remember Joseph; he forgot him.

source: Chuin ahitin ahi, kumni kichaina lamin Pharaoh'in mang aneijin; chule veuvin, ama vadung panga ana dingin ahi.
target: When two full years had passed, Pharaoh had a dream: He was standing by the Nile,

source: Chuin veuvin, bongpi sagi hoitah cheh le thaochet cheh vadunga konin ahung doh-un; hampa lah-a chun alhaovin ahi.
target: when out of the river there came up seven cows, sleek and fat, and they grazed among the reeds.

source: Chuin veuvin, bongpi dang sagi melse tah le gongtah tah vadunga kon mama chun ahungdoh kitnun; vadung pam twi china-a chun bongpi dangho koma adingun ahi.
