target: After them, seven other cows, ugly and gaunt, came up out of the Nile and stood beside those on the riverbank.

source: Chuin bongpi melse tah le gongtah tah ho chun, bongpi hoitah le thaotah tah hochu anejou hel taovin ahi. Chuin Pharaoh ahung khangdoh tan ahi.
target: And the cows that were ugly and gaunt ate up the seven sleek, fat cows. Then Pharaoh woke up.

source: Chuin Pharaoh a-ihmulhu kitnin, anivei channa-in mang aneikit: chule veuvin, changkung khat nahin changvui sagi lentah le phatah ahung doh-in ahi.
target: He fell asleep again and had a second dream: Seven heads of grain, healthy and good, were growing on a single stalk.

source: Chuin chuche jouchun, veuvin, solam huijin asem gopsa changvui geositset sagi ahungdoh-in ahi.
target: After them, seven other heads of grain sprouted—thin and scorched by the east wind.

source: Chuin geositset sagi chun changvui lentah le phatah sagiho chu avallhumtan ahi. Chuin Pharaoh ahung khangin ahile, veuvin, hichu amang anahi.
target: The thin heads of grain swallowed up the seven healthy, full heads. Then Pharaoh woke up; it had been a dream.

source: Chuin ahitin ahi, jingkah ahung hi phatnin ama alungkham lheh jengtan, chuin aman mi asolin, Egypt gama mitphel doithem jouse le miching jouse akoutan ahi. Chuin Pharaoh'in amaho henga amang chu aseijin; ahivangin Pharaoh henga chun hiche ledohthei koimacha aumtapon ahi.
target: In the morning his mind was troubled, so he sent for all the magicians and wise men of Egypt. Pharaoh told them his dreams, but no one could interpret them for him.

source: Chujouvin jukhon dom pipu chun Pharaoh henga, Tunin kathemona khat kagel doh-e:
target: Then the chief cupbearer said to Pharaoh, “Today I am reminded of my shortcomings.

source: Pharaoh chu asohte ni chunga alung hana, keima le changlhah sem pipu chu ngahtup ho lamkai in'a songkul'a akoi laijin,
target: Pharaoh was once angry with his servants, and he imprisoned me and the chief baker in the house of the captain of the guard.

source: Keima le ama chun jan khat mang kanei gel lhonin; keinin atumcheh-in aledohna um mang kanei gel lhonin ahi.
target: Each of us had a dream the same night, and each dream had a meaning of its own.

source: Chuin chukoma chun ngahtup lama lamkaipa sohpa Hebrew khangdong khat keini toh aumkhomin ahi; chuin amachu kaseipeh lhonin ahile, aman kamanglhon chu aledoh-in; kamanglhon dungjui chun aledohna chu eiseipeh gel lhonin ahi.
target: Now a young Hebrew was there with us, a servant of the captain of the guard. We told him our dreams, and he interpreted them for us, giving each man the interpretation of his dream.

source: Chuin ahitin ahi, aman kaheng lhona aledoh bang chun, chutichun ahung guilhungin; aman keima katoh na mun'a eipansah kitnin, chule amavang chu akhailih tan ahi, ati.
target: And things turned out exactly as he interpreted them to us: I was restored to my position, and the other man was impaled.”

source: Chujouvin Pharaoh'in Joseph koudingin mi asolin, chuin amahon songkul'a konin gangtah-in ahin puidoh-un ahi. Chuin ama akivou ngimin, aponsil akikhelin, Pharaoh henga chun ahunglut tan ahi.
target: So Pharaoh sent for Joseph, and he was quickly brought from the dungeon. When he had shaved and changed his clothes, he came before Pharaoh.

source: Chuin Pharaoh'in Joseph henga, Keiman mangkhat kaneijin, hichu aledohthei ja koimacha aumtapoi. Chule keiman nangma chungchang thu, nangman mang ledohthem theina naneije ti mi seinan kajan ahi, ati.
target: Pharaoh said to Joseph, “I had a dream, and no one can interpret it. But I have heard it said of you that when you hear a dream you can interpret it.”

source: Chuin Joseph'in Pharaoh chu adonbutnin, ahenga, Hichu keima-a uma ahipoi; Pathen joh-in lungmon umtah donbutna chu Pharaoh apehding ahi, ati.
target: “I cannot do it,” Joseph replied to Pharaoh, “but God will give Pharaoh the answer he desires.”

source: Chuin Pharaoh'in Joseph henga, Kamangin, veovin, keima vadung panga kana dingin ahi.
target: Then Pharaoh said to Joseph, “In my dream I was standing on the bank of the Nile,

source: Chuin, veovin, bongpi sagi thaotah le hoitahcheh vadunga konin ahungdoh-un; hamhing lah-a chun alhaovin ahi.
target: when out of the river there came up seven cows, fat and sleek, and they grazed among the reeds.

source: Chule veovin, bongpi sagi dang phamotah le melsetah chule gongtah tah, chutobang tah-a melse Egypt gam jouse-a jong kanamukhah louhel chu anunguva chun ahungdoh-un ahi.
target: After them, seven other cows came up—scrawny and very ugly and lean. I had never seen such ugly cows in all the land of Egypt.

source: Chuin bongpi gongtah le melsetah hochun bongpi sagi thaotah tah masaho chu anejouhel taovin ahi.
target: The lean, ugly cows ate up the seven fat cows that came up first.

source: Chuin hiho chu anehjouhel vangun, anehjouvu chu hetdoh thei ahidehpoi; ajehchu amaho chu atila bang chun amelse jing jenguvin ahi. Chuti chun keima kahung khangdohtai.
target: But even after they ate them, no one could tell that they had done so; they looked just as ugly as before. Then I woke up.

source: Chuin keiman kamangin, veuvin, changkung khatna changvui sagi dimset set le phatah tah ahungdoh kamun ahi.
target: “In my dream I saw seven heads of grain, full and good, growing on a single stalk.

source: Chuin veuvin, hiho nunga chun changvui sagi asisa le gaositset chule solam huijin asemgopsa ahungsoh kitnin ahi.
target: After them, seven other heads sprouted—withered and thin and scorched by the east wind.

source: Chuin changvui geositset hochun changvui phatah tah sagiho chu avaljouhel tan ahi. Chule keiman hichu mitphel doithemho henga kaseijin; ahivangin eihilchen thei koimacha aumpon ahi, ati.
target: The thin heads of grain swallowed up the seven good heads. I told this to the magicians, but none of them could explain it to me.”

source: Chuin Joseph'in Pharaoh henga, Pharaoh manghi thakhat ahi, Pathen'in athil hinbol dingho chu Pharaoh henga amusah ahi, ati.
target: Then Joseph said to Pharaoh, “The dreams of Pharaoh are one and the same. God has revealed to Pharaoh what he is about to do.

source: Bongpi phatah sagiho chu kum sagi ahin; chule changvui pha sagi chu kum sagima ahi. Mang chu thakhat ahi.
target: The seven good cows are seven years, and the seven good heads of grain are seven years; it is one and the same dream.

source: Chule anunga bongpi gongtahle melsetah sagi hungsoh doh hochu kum sagi ahin; chule changvui sagi asikeu, solam huijin asemgopsa chu kum sagi kel lhah ding ahi.
target: The seven lean, ugly cows that came up afterward are seven years, and so are the seven worthless heads of grain scorched by the east wind: They are seven years of famine.

source: Keiman Pharaoh henga kaseisa chu hiche thilhi ahi. Pathen'in athil hinbolding chu Pharaoh amusah ahi.
target: “It is just as I said to Pharaoh: God has shown Pharaoh what he is about to do.

source: Veovin, Egypt gam pumpi-a hi kum sagi neh nasatah-a ninglhingsetna hung lhung ding ahi.
target: Seven years of great abundance are coming throughout the land of Egypt,

source: Chule hiche jou chule kum sagi kel lhah hung lhungding; chule Egypt gama neh ning lhinna kum jouse chu suhmila hung umding; chule kel lhah chun gam chu anehchai ding;
target: but seven years of famine will follow them. Then all the abundance in Egypt will be forgotten, and the famine will ravage the land.

source: Chule kel hung lhunding jeh-a chu ninglhinna chu gamsunga hetphah louhela umding ahi; ajeh chu hichu nasalheh ding ahi.
target: The abundance in the land will not be remembered, because the famine that follows it will be so severe.

source: Chule Pharaoh'in mang nivei nanei kopna jehchu hichehi ahi: Pathen'in thilchu asuhdet ahitan; chule hichu Pathen'in chomlouva aguilhunsah ding jeh ahi.
target: The reason the dream was given to Pharaoh in two forms is that the matter has been firmly decided by God, and God will do it soon.

source: Hijeh chun tun Pharaoh'in lungelthem le miching khat holdoh henlang, amachu Egypt gam chunga vaipon tungdoh hen.
target: “And now let Pharaoh look for a discerning and wise man and put him in charge of the land of Egypt.

source: Hijeh chun Pharaoh'in tun hichehi bolhen, chule gamsunga hin vaipoho lhengdoh henlang, amaho chun neh ninglhinna kum sagi sungchun Egypt gama nehsoh hopnga-a hopkhat lakhom uhen.
target: Let Pharaoh appoint commissioners over the land to take a fifth of the harvest of Egypt during the seven years of abundance.

source: Chule amahon ahung lhung ding kum phaho sunga chang jouse chu khom khomu henlang, changho chu Pharaoh khutnoija kholuhen, chule amahon khopiho-a chun chang kholuhen.
target: They should collect all the food of these good years that are coming and store up the grain under the authority of Pharaoh, to be kept in the cities for food.

source: Chule keljeh-a gamhi amanthah louna dinga, Egypt gama hung chuding kelhah kum sagi sunga dinga kigina-a, chang chu hiche gama dinga hi kholkhom ding ahi, ati.
target: This food should be held in reserve for the country, to be used during the seven years of famine that will come upon Egypt, so that the country may not be ruined by the famine.”

source: Chuin hiche thuchu Pharaoh leh asohte mitmun aphalheh jengin ahi.
target: The plan seemed good to Pharaoh and to all his officials.

source: Chuin Pharaoh'in asohte henga, Ama tobanga Pathen Lhagao asunga aumna mihem hi imu joumong diu hinam? ati.
target: So Pharaoh asked them, “Can we find anyone like this man, one in whom is the spirit of God?”

source: Chuin Pharaoh'in Joseph henga, Pathen'in hicheho jousehi nangma namusah jeh hin, nangma banga lungelthem le miching dang aumpoi.
target: Then Pharaoh said to Joseph, “Since God has made all this known to you, there is no one so discerning and wise as you.

source: Nangma ka-insung chunga vaipo-a napanding, chule nangma thupeh dungjuija kamite hi kivaipo diu ahi; Laltouna chungchanga hibou keima nangma sanga lenjo kahiding ahi, ati.
target: You shall be in charge of my palace, and all my people are to submit to your orders. Only with respect to the throne will I be greater than you.”

source: Chuin Pharaoh'in Joseph henga, Ven, keiman nangma Egypt gam jouse chunga vaipo-a katun nahitai, ati.
target: So Pharaoh said to Joseph, “I hereby put you in charge of the whole land of Egypt.”

source: Chuin Pharaoh'in akhutna konin khutjem chu aladoh-in, Joseph khutna abupeh-in, chule tupat ponsil hoitah-in ajemin, sana ngong'o angonga a-o peh-in;
target: Then Pharaoh took his signet ring from his finger and put it on Joseph’s finger. He dressed him in robes of fine linen and put a gold chain around his neck.

source: Chule amachu akangtalai nei nilhina-a chun atousah-in; chule amasanga, Dilsuvin, tin asamun ahi. Chutichun aman Egypt gam pumpi chunga vaipon atungtan ahi.
target: He had him ride in a chariot as his second-in-command, and people shouted before him, “Make way!” Thus he put him in charge of the whole land of Egypt.

source: Chuin Pharaoh'in Joseph henga, Keimahi Pharaoh kahin, chule nangma thulouvin Egypt gam pumpi-a hin koimachan akhut hile akeng hileh lamthei ponte, ati.
target: Then Pharaoh said to Joseph, “I am Pharaoh, but without your word no one will lift hand or foot in all Egypt.”

source: Chuin Pharaoh'in Joseph min chu Zaphnath-Paaneah asah in; On thempu Potiphera chanu Asenath chu aji dingin apen ahi. Chuin Joseph'in Egypt gam jouse agachonle tan ahi.
target: Pharaoh gave Joseph the name Zaphenath-Paneah and gave him Asenath daughter of Potiphera, priest of On, to be his wife. And Joseph went throughout the land of Egypt.

source: Joseph Egypt lengpa Pharaoh angsunga adin chun kum somthum alhingtan ahi. Chuin Joseph Pharaoh henga konin apotnin, Egypt gam pumpi agachonsoh tan ahi.
target: Joseph was thirty years old when he entered the service of Pharaoh king of Egypt. And Joseph went out from Pharaoh’s presence and traveled throughout Egypt.

source: Chuin kum sagi neh ninglhin sung chun leijin nengtah-in an asosah-in ahi.
target: During the seven years of abundance the land produced plentifully.

source: Chuin aman Egypt gamsunga kum sagi sungin chang jouse akhom khomin, khopi ho-a chun akholin ahi. Chule akimvela louho-a kona changho chu khopitina chun akhol khomin ahi.
target: Joseph collected all the food produced in those seven years of abundance in Egypt and stored it in the cities. In each city he put the food grown in the fields surrounding it.

source: Chuin Joseph'in chang chu twikhanglen'a neldi jat banghela tamin akhomin, simjouhoi ahitahlou jeh in, asimjong abang heltan ahi.
target: Joseph stored up huge quantities of grain, like the sand of the sea; it was so much that he stopped keeping records because it was beyond measure.

source: Chuin kel lhah kum ahunglhun masangin Joseph'in chapa ni aneijin, hichu On thempu Potiphera chanu Asenath'in ahinpeh ahi.
target: Before the years of famine came, two sons were born to Joseph by Asenath daughter of Potiphera, priest of On.

source: Chuin Joseph'in apeng masa chu Manasseh asah-in ahi. Ajehchu Pathen'in kahahsatna jouse le kapa insung jouse eisuhmil sahtai, ati.
target: Joseph named his firstborn Manasseh and said, “It is because God has made me forget all my trouble and all my father’s household.”

source: Chuin ani lhinna chu amin Ephraim asahtai. Ajehchu Pathen'in kathoh gimna gamahin eipunsahtai, ati.
target: The second son he named Ephraim and said, “It is because God has made me fruitful in the land of my suffering.”

source: Chuin Egypt gama neh lhinna kum sagi chu ahung kichaitai.
target: The seven years of abundance in Egypt came to an end,

source: Chule Joseph'in aseibangin kellhah kum sagi chu ahung lhungtan; ahivangin Egypt gam pumpi-a chun neh aumin ahi.
target: and the seven years of famine began, just as Joseph had said. There was famine in all the other lands, but in the whole land of Egypt there was food.

source: Chuin Egypt gam jouse-a kel ahunglhah phatnin, miho chu Pharaoh lengpa henga neh thumin ahung tao taovin ahi. Chuin Pharaoh'in Egypt mite jouse henga chun, Joseph koma cheovin, aman naheng uva aseichu bolun, atitai.
target: When all Egypt began to feel the famine, the people cried to Pharaoh for food. Then Pharaoh told all the Egyptians, “Go to Joseph and do what he tells you.”

source: Chule kel chu leiset pumpi chunga alhatan ahi. Chuin Joseph'in chang kikhol khomna in jouse chu ahong doh-in, Egypt mite henga chun ajoh in; chule kel chu Egypt gama chun akhohlheh jengin ahi.
target: When the famine had spread over the whole country, Joseph opened all the storehouses and sold grain to the Egyptians, for the famine was severe throughout Egypt.

source: Chuin kel chu gam jouse-a alhah nasat behset jeh in, gam jouse-a mihemte Egypt gama Joseph henga chun chang cho dingin ahungun ahi.
target: And all the world came to Egypt to buy grain from Joseph, because the famine was severe everywhere.

source: Tun Jacob'in Egypt gama chang aume, ti amuphat nin, Jacob'in achapate henga, Ipi dinga nakimoh vetto jengu ham? ati.
target: When Jacob learned that there was grain in Egypt, he said to his sons, “Why do you just keep looking at each other?”

source: Chuin aman, Veuvin, Egypt gama chang aume, ti kajai; thilouva ihindoh theina diuvin chua chun gachesuh unlang, eiho dingin chang gacho taovin, ati.
target: He continued, “I have heard that there is grain in Egypt. Go down there and buy some for us, so that we may live and not die.”

source: Chuin Joseph sopi somho chu Egypt gama chang cho dingin achesuh taove.
target: Then ten of Joseph’s brothers went down to buy grain from Egypt.

source: Ahin Joseph naopa Benjamin vang chu Jacob'in asopiho chutoh asolthapoi; ajehchu aman, Ijemtin toset khat achunga chukhante, atin ahi.
target: But Jacob did not send Benjamin, Joseph’s brother, with the others, because he was afraid that harm might come to him.

source: Chuin Israel chapate chu adang ahungho chutoh lhonin chang cho dingin ahungtaove. Ajehchu Canaan gama chun kel alhatan ahi.
target: So Israel’s sons were among those who went to buy grain, for there was famine in the land of Canaan also.

source: Chule Joseph chu chuche gama chu gamvaipo-a panga ahitan, chule ama chuche gam mijouse henga chu chang joh-a panga ahitai. Chuin Joseph sopite chu ahungun, chule a-angsunga tolla chun aboh khupmun ahi.
target: Now Joseph was the governor of the land, the person who sold grain to all its people. So when Joseph’s brothers arrived, they bowed down to him with their faces to the ground.

source: Chuin Joseph'in asopite chu amun, chule amaho chu ahen; ahivangin aman amaho chu ahetlou bangin abolin, i-sah loutah-in ahouvin; chuin aman amaho henga, Hoija kona hung nahiuvem? ati. Chuin amahon, Canaan gama kona chang cho dinga hunga kahiuve, atiuvin ahi.
target: As soon as Joseph saw his brothers, he recognized them, but he pretended to be a stranger and spoke harshly to them. “Where do you come from?” he asked. “From the land of Canaan,” they replied, “to buy food.”

source: Chule Joseph'in asopite chu ahenan, ahivangin amahon amachu ahepouve.
target: Although Joseph recognized his brothers, they did not recognize him.

source: Chuin Joseph'in amaho chungchang thua mang anamat chu ageldoh-in, chuin ahenguva, Nangho hi gam velhi nahiuve, gam agohkeova aumhi velhi dinga hung nahiuve, ati.
target: Then he remembered his dreams about them and said to them, “You are spies! You have come to see where our land is unprotected.”

source: Chuin amahon ahenga, Ahipoi, ka pakai, nasohte hi changcho dinga bou hunga kahi bouvui, atiuve.
target: “No, my lord,” they answered. “Your servants have come to buy food.

source: Keiho kabon chaovin mikhat chapate kahiuve; mi kitah kahiuvin, nasohte gamvelhi kahipouve.
target: We are all the sons of one man. Your servants are honest men, not spies.”

source: Chuin aman amaho henga, Ahipoi, hiche agoh keova aum hi velhi dinga hunga nahiuve, ati.
target: “No!” he said to them. “You have come to see where our land is unprotected.”

source: Chuin amahon, Nasohte hi sopi somleni kahiuvin, Canaan gama mikhat chapate kahiuve; chule vetan, alhumpen chu tupet hin kapau toh aumin, khatvang aumtapoi, atiuve.
target: But they replied, “Your servants were twelve brothers, the sons of one man, who lives in the land of Canaan. The youngest is now with our father, and one is no more.”

source: Chuin Joseph'in ahenguva, Gamvelhi nahiuve, katichu nahiuve.
target: Joseph said to them, “It is just as I told you: You are spies!

source: Hichea hi nangho kipatep ding nahiuve: Nasopi pao alhumpen chu hikoma hi ahung louleh, Pharaoh mina kahahsel nahiuve, nangho hikoma kona hi napotdoh loudingu ahi.
target: And this is how you will be tested: As surely as Pharaoh lives, you will not leave this place unless your youngest brother comes here.

source: Nangho-a thutah aum aumlou nathusei uva kona photchet ahina dingin, nalah uva mikhat solunlang nanaopao chu hinpuihen, nangho vang songkul'a naum dingu ahi. Achuti louleh Pharaoh mina kahahsel nahiuve, nangho hi gam velhi nahi mongui, atitai.
target: Send one of your number to get your brother; the rest of you will be kept in prison, so that your words may be tested to see if you are telling the truth. If you are not, then as surely as Pharaoh lives, you are spies!”

source: Chuin aman amaho chu abonchauvin thakhatnin nithum ahentan ahi.
target: And he put them all in custody for three days.

source: Chuin Joseph'in anithum chanin ahenguvah, Hichehi bolun lang hinnan neijun; ajehchu keiman Pathen kaginge, ati.
target: On the third day, Joseph said to them, “Do this and you will live, for I fear God:

source: Nangho hi mikitah nahiuleh, na-uchahou lah-a khatpen hitihin songkul'a umden hen: Nangho adangse na-in sunguva kelthohho ding chang kipoh unlang chetaovin.
target: If you are honest men, let one of your brothers stay here in prison, while the rest of you go and take grain back for your starving households.

source: Ahin nanao-u alhumpen chu kahenga hinpuijun; hitichun nathusei houchu photchetnin umintin, nangho nathiloudiu ahi, ati. Chuin amahon chutichun aboltauve.
target: But you must bring your youngest brother to me, so that your words may be verified and that you may not die.” This they proceeded to do.

source: Chuin amaho khatnin khat henga, Tahbeh-in eiho inaopao thudol, aman eiho eingeh tun tun pettah uva alungsung hesoh je kimu khel khela, ingaipeh louvu chu ithemo lheh-ui, Hiche jeh-a chu hiche gentheina hi ichunguva chua ahitai, atiuve.
target: They said to one another, “Surely we are being punished because of our brother. We saw how distressed he was when he pleaded with us for his life, but we would not listen; that’s why this distress has come on us.”

source: Chuin Reuben'in amaho chu adonbutnin, Chapang chunga chun chonset bolhih-un tia kaseipehsa nahilouvu ham? Ahin nanghon kathusei nangai pouve; hiche jeh-a chu veuvin, athisan phu chu kingeh-a ahitai, ati.
target: Reuben replied, “Didn’t I tell you not to sin against the boy? But you wouldn’t listen! Now we must give an accounting for his blood.”

source: Chule akah uva Pao le aum jehchun, Joseph'in amaho thusei ahet chu amahon ahepouve.
target: They did not realize that Joseph could understand them, since he was using an interpreter.

source: Chuin ama amaho-a konin akihei mangin, akaptai; chuin ama ahenguva ahung kitnin, amaho chutoh akihouvin, chuin Simeon chu ahenguva konin akaijin, chuin amitmuva chun akantai.
target: He turned away from them and began to weep, but then came back and spoke to them again. He had Simeon taken from them and bound before their eyes.

source: Chujouvin Joseph'in adipmu chu chang sundimpeh dingle asum cheh-u chu adipcheh uva lekhum pehcheh dingin, chule lampi-a aneh dingu an agonpeh dingun thu apetan; chutichun amaho ding chun abolpeh tan ahi.
target: Joseph gave orders to fill their bags with grain, to put each man’s silver back in his sack, and to give them provisions for their journey. After this was done for them,

source: Chuin achang houchu asangan hou apohsah-un, akipatdoh taove.
target: they loaded their grain on their donkeys and left.

source: Chuin alah uva khatnin agenau inna asangan an pedinga adipchu agah honleh, asumchu amutai; ajehchu, veovin, hichu adip kama chun ana umin ahi.
target: At the place where they stopped for the night one of them opened his sack to get feed for his donkey, and he saw his silver in the mouth of his sack.

source: Chuin aman asopite henga, Kasum ana kilekoi kit tai; Chule veuvin, kadipsung ahin ana ume, ati. Chuin amaho alungling laovun, akicha gamtaovin, Pathen'in ichunguva abolhi ipi ahitadem? akitiuvin ahi.
target: “My silver has been returned,” he said to his brothers. “Here it is in my sack.” Their hearts sank and they turned to each other trembling and said, “What is this that God has done to us?”

source: Chuin amaho Canaan gama apau Jacob heng ahung lhung taovin, chule achunguva thusoh jouse chu ama chu ahilun; ahenga hitin aseijun ahi,
target: When they came to their father Jacob in the land of Canaan, they told him all that had happened to them. They said,

source: Mipa, agam pakaipa chun huham tah-in eina houvun, chuche gam velhi danin einalaovin ahi.
target: “The man who is lord over the land spoke harshly to us and treated us as though we were spying on the land.

source: Chuin keihon ahenga, Keiho mikitah tah te kahiuvin; gam velhi kahipouve,
target: But we said to him, ‘We are honest men; we are not spies.

source: Keiho sopi somleni kahiuvin, pakhat hinbou kahiuve; khatpa aumtapoi, alhumpen vang tupetnin Canaan gama kapau toh aume, katiuvin ahi.
target: We were twelve brothers, sons of one father. One is no more, and the youngest is now with our father in Canaan.’

source: Chuin chuche mipa, agam pakaipa chun kahenguva, Hichea hin nangho milungdih nahiu chu hethei jinge; nasopiteu lah-a khat kahenga dalhao vin, chule na-in sunguva kelthoh ho dingin chang kipoh unlang chetaovin.
target: “Then the man who is lord over the land said to us, ‘This is how I will know whether you are honest men: Leave one of your brothers here with me, and take food for your starving households and go.

source: Chule nanao-u alhumpen chu kahenga hinpuijun: chutengle nangho gam velhi nahipouvin, ahin mikitah tah te nahiuve tichu heng kate. Chuteng nasopi pao lhadohpeh ungting, chule hiche gamahi nakivei dingu ahi, eitiuve, atiuvin ahi.
target: But bring your youngest brother to me so I will know that you are not spies but honest men. Then I will give your brother back to you, and you can trade in the land.’ ”

source: Chuin amahon adip mu alheilhah phatnun, ahitin ahi, veuvin, amitakip sum chun chu adip cheh-a ana umtan ahi. Chuin amaho leh apau chun asumchun hou amuphat nun, akicha lheh taovin ahi.
target: As they were emptying their sacks, there in each man’s sack was his pouch of silver! When they and their father saw the money pouches, they were frightened.

source: Chuin apau Jacob chun ahenguva, Nangho hin kachate neichan sah-u ahitai; Joseph aumtapon, Simeon jong aumtapon, chule nanghon Benjamin jong puimang nagouve. Hicheng thil jousehin eilhunkhum ahitai, ati.
target: Their father Jacob said to them, “You have deprived me of my children. Joseph is no more and Simeon is no more, and now you want to take Benjamin. Everything is against me!”

source: Chuin Reuben'in apa henga, Keiman amachu nakoma kahin puilutkit louleh kachapa teni hi that jengin; amachu kakhutna neipedoh-in, keiman ama chu nahenga hinle puikit nange, ati.
target: Then Reuben said to his father, “You may put both of my sons to death if I do not bring him back to you. Entrust him to my care, and I will bring him back.”

source: Chuin aman, Kachapa hi nangho toh kilhona chesuh louhel ding ahi; ajehchu a-upa thia ahitan, ama changsehbou uma ahitai. Nachenao lamdunga achungah toset chutale, kasam kangsa hi lhankhuh-a lunghem puma napuisuh dingu ahi, ati.
target: But Jacob said, “My son will not go down there with you; his brother is dead and he is the only one left. If harm comes to him on the journey you are taking, you will bring my gray head down to the grave in sorrow.”

source: Chuin hiche gama chun kel alha nasalheh jengtan ahi.
target: Now the famine was still severe in the land.

source: Chuin ahitin ahi, amahon Egypt gama kona ahinpoh-u chang chu anehjou phatnun, apauvin ahenguva, Chekitnun lang eihodin chang phabep gachouvin ati.
target: So when they had eaten all the grain they had brought from Egypt, their father said to them, “Go back and buy us a little more food.”

source: Chuin Judah'in ahenga, Mipa chun, Nanaopao chu nahin kilhonpi lou uleh kamai namu louhel dingu ahi, tin nasatah-in eigih-un ahi.
target: But Judah said to him, “The man warned us solemnly, ‘You will not see my face again unless your brother is with you.’

source: Nangman kanaopao hi keihotoh lhondinga nasolding vangle, keiho chesuh ungting, chang gachohpeh unge.
target: If you will send our brother along with us, we will go down and buy food for you.

source: Ahin amachu nasol louding vangleh, keiho chesuh pouvinge. Ajehchu mipa chun kahenguva, Nanaopao chu nahin kilhonpi lou uleh, kamai namu louheldiu ahi, ati ahi, tin aseije.
target: But if you will not send him, we will not go down, because the man said to us, ‘You will not see my face again unless your brother is with you.’ ”

source: Chuin Israel'in, Ipidinga naokhat nanei nah laiju thu chu mipa chu nahin seipehkhel kheluva, hitobanga phalou tah-a hi neibolu ham? ati.
target: Israel asked, “Why did you bring this trouble on me by telling the man you had another brother?”

source: Chuin amahon, Mipa chun, napau damna laijam? Sopidang naneijum? tin keiho thudol le insung thudol eidoh doh jeng jeh uva, hiche akam chengho dungjuija chu ama kaseipeh-u ahi. Nanaopao hinpui suh-un, ati ding chu keihon ija kahet diu ham? atiuve.
target: They replied, “The man questioned us closely about ourselves and our family. ‘Is your father still living?’ he asked us. ‘Do you have another brother?’ We simply answered his questions. How were we to know he would say, ‘Bring your brother down here’?”

source: Chuin Judah'in apa Israel henga, Keiho le nangma, chule chapang sen hohi thilouva ahintheina diuvin chapang chu keimatoh neilhon sah-in.
target: Then Judah said to Israel his father, “Send the boy along with me and we will go at once, so that we and you and our children may live and not die.

source: Keima ama dingin kitung-ing kating, keima khut ngeija amachu ngeh-in: keiman ama nahenga kahin lepui louva, namasanga hi kadinsahkit louva ahileh mona chu kumkhon pojeng ing kate.
target: I myself will guarantee his safety; you can hold me personally responsible for him. If I do not bring him back to you and set him here before you, I will bear the blame before you all my life.

source: Ajehchu keiho khongaisot louva hileuveng, tu-a hi nivei kile kitding kahiu ahitai, ati.
target: As it is, if we had not delayed, we could have gone and returned twice.”

source: Chuin apau Israel'in ahenguva, Tun hichu hiding mong ahi tah le, hiche hi bolun; nadip uva hichegam thingga phapen phabepho, thingnailou phabep, khoiju phabep, thilnamtui, myrrh, beleilut, chule jonmot posuh unlang, chule mipa chu thilpeh-in peuvin.
target: Then their father Israel said to them, “If it must be, then do this: Put some of the best products of the land in your bags and take them down to the man as a gift—a little balm and a little honey, some spices and myrrh, some pistachio nuts and almonds.

source: Chule nakhut un dangka ajatnia tamin kenbeuvin, chule nadip uva dangka nahinlepoh kitnu jongchu kiken kitnuvin, mukhel jong hithei ahi.
target: Take double the amount of silver with you, for you must return the silver that was put back into the mouths of your sacks. Perhaps it was a mistake.

source: Nanaopao jong chu kipuijun, kipat doh-un lang, chuche mipa henga chun chekit taovin.
target: Take your brother also and go back to the man at once.

source: Chule amapan nasopipa le Benjamin ahinlhadoh kit nadin, imajouse bolthei hat chungnung Pathen'in mipa masanga chun lungsetna napeu hen. Kachate chu kachantah jong leh kachan himaitante, ati.
target: And may God Almighty grant you mercy before the man so that he will let your other brother and Benjamin come back with you. As for me, if I am bereaved, I am bereaved.”

source: Chuin miho chun thilpeh chu apouvin, dangka jatni apoh beuvin, chule Benjamin jong akipuijun; akipatnun, Egypt gama achesuh-un, Joseph anga chun ading kit taove.
target: So the men took the gifts and double the amount of silver, and Benjamin also. They hurried down to Egypt and presented themselves to Joseph.

source: Chuin Joseph'in Benjamin chu amaho chutoh amuphatnin, a-insung vetuppa henga, Hiche miho hi in'a puijin, sa thatnin lang, gotsan koijin; ajehchu miho khun sun le keima toh ankong a-umkhom dingu ahi, ati.
target: When Joseph saw Benjamin with them, he said to the steward of his house, “Take these men to my house, slaughter an animal and prepare a meal; they are to eat with me at noon.”

source: Chuin mipa chun Joseph thupeh bangchun abolin; miho chu Joseph in'a apuilut tan ahi.
target: The man did as Joseph told him and took the men to Joseph’s house.

source: Chuin Joseph in'a apuilut jehchun, miho chu akicha taovin; chule amahon iche masah uva idipmuva dangka ana kikoijeh-a chu ichunguva agomkom ahola, ichunguva chua, eiho le isangan hou hi soh-a neiding eigotnuva eipuilutnu ahi, akitiuve.
target: Now the men were frightened when they were taken to his house. They thought, “We were brought here because of the silver that was put back into our sacks the first time. He wants to attack us and overpower us and seize us as slaves and take our donkeys.”

source: Chuin amahon Joseph insung vetuppa chu ahin naijun, kotkhah bula chun amachu akihoulim piuvin,
target: So they went up to Joseph’s steward and spoke to him at the entrance to the house.

source: Chule amahon, Vo hepu, kahung masah chungu chun keiho chang choding monga hunga kahiuve.
target: “We beg your pardon, our lord,” they said, “we came down here the first time to buy food.

source: Chuin ahitin ahi, keiho jinlhun in kalhun phatnun, kadipmuchu kahongun ahile, ka dangka cheh uchu kadipkam cheh uva chun ana umtan, ka dangkao chu agih lhingsetnin ana umtan ahi. Chule keihon hichu kahinpo kitnun ahi.
target: But at the place where we stopped for the night we opened our sacks and each of us found his silver—the exact weight—in the mouth of his sack. So we have brought it back with us.

source: Chule chang choh nading dangka jong kahinpouvin, ahi. Kadip sunguva kadangkau chu kon anakoiham Kahepouve, atiuve.
target: We have also brought additional silver with us to buy food. We don’t know who put our silver in our sacks.”

source: Chuin aman, Lungmong tah-in umun, kicha hih-un; na Pathen'u chule napau Pathen chun nangho dinga nadip uva gou nakoipeh-u ahi; keiman nangho dangka kamunai, ati. Chuin Simeon chu ahenguva ahinpui doh-in ahi.
target: “It’s all right,” he said. “Don’t be afraid. Your God, the God of your father, has given you treasure in your sacks; I received your silver.” Then he brought Simeon out to them.

source: Chuin mipa chun amaho chu Joseph in'a apuilutnin, chuin amaho chu twi apen, amahon akengu akisilun; chule aman asangongsao hou jong an apen ahi.
target: The steward took the men into Joseph’s house, gave them water to wash their feet and provided fodder for their donkeys.

source: Chuin amahon chua changlhah anehdiu chu ajataovin, sunna Joseph ahung tengle peh ding chun thilpeh hochu agongtup mun ahi.
target: They prepared their gifts for Joseph’s arrival at noon, because they had heard that they were to eat there.

source: Chuin Joseph in'a ahung phatnin, akhutnuva um thilpeh chu insunga ahin choilutnun, chuin amaho tolla aboh khupmun, ama chu chibai aboh-un ahi.
target: When Joseph came home, they presented to him the gifts they had brought into the house, and they bowed down before him to the ground.

source: Chuin aman amaho umchan chu adongin, Nanghon aumchan naseiju napau tehse chu damnam? amachu hing nalaijam? ati.
target: He asked them how they were, and then he said, “How is your aged father you told me about? Is he still living?”

source: Chuin amahon adonbut un, Nasohpa kapau chu adampet ahin, chule ahing nalainai, atiuve. Chuin amaho akunun, chibai abohkitnun ahi.
target: They replied, “Your servant our father is still alive and well.” And they bowed down, prostrating themselves before him.

source: Chuin ama akhodah-in ahile, anaopa Benjamin, anu chapa chu amun; hichun aman, Hiche hi nanao-u alhumpen, aumchan kahenga naseipao chu ham? ati. Chuin aman, Kachapa, Pathen'in nalungset hen, ati.
target: As he looked about and saw his brother Benjamin, his own mother’s son, he asked, “Is this your youngest brother, the one you told me about?” And he said, “God be gracious to you, my son.”

source: Chuin Joseph'in anaopa chu alung ase behseh-in, kikin notah-in kana ding mun aholtan; Chuin ama a-indan sunga alutnin, chua chun agakaptan ahi.
target: Deeply moved at the sight of his brother, Joseph hurried out and looked for a place to weep. He went into his private room and wept there.

source: Chuin aman amai akiphetnin, apotdoh kitnin, chuin ama akikham nahnah-in, Ankong semun, ati.
target: After he had washed his face, he came out and, controlling himself, said, “Serve the food.”

source: Chuin amahon amading atumin, chule amahoding atumin, chule amatoh neh khompi Egypt miho ding chun atumin asemtaove. Ajehchu Egypt miho chun Hebrew miho toh an aneh khom ngailouvu ahi; ajehchu Egypt mite dinga hichu thet umtah ahi.
target: They served him by himself, the brothers by themselves, and the Egyptians who ate with him by themselves, because Egyptians could not eat with Hebrews, for that is detestable to Egyptians.

source: Chuin amaho apeng masapen chu a-upat hina dungjuijin, chule alhumpen chu achapan dungjuijin Joseph anga chun atousah taovin ahi. Chuin amaho chun kidang asalheh jengun ahi.
target: The men had been seated before him in the order of their ages, from the firstborn to the youngest; and they looked at each other in astonishment.

source: Chuin ama-a konchun chanho chu alan ahenguva chun ahomin; ahin Benjamin chan chu amaho khat chan sangin chan nga in atamjon ahi. Chuin amahon adonun, amato akipahkhom taovin ahi.
target: When portions were served to them from Joseph’s table, Benjamin’s portion was five times as much as anyone else’s. So they feasted and drank freely with him.

source: Chuin aman a-insung vetuppa chu thu apen, ajah-a, Amahon ajo chanuva apoh diuvin adip-u khu chang sundim peh-in, chule adangka cheh-u chu adip kamuva koipeh cheh-in.
target: Now Joseph gave these instructions to the steward of his house: “Fill the men’s sacks with as much food as they can carry, and put each man’s silver in the mouth of his sack.

source: Chule kakhon, kadangka khon chu alhumpenpa dipkama achang man dangka chutoh koithan, ati. Chuin aman Joseph'in aseibang chun aboltan ahi.
target: Then put my cup, the silver one, in the mouth of the youngest one’s sack, along with the silver for his grain.” And he did as Joseph said.

source: Chuin jing kho ahungvah vah-in, miho chu asangan hou toh asoldoh taove.
target: As morning dawned, the men were sent on their way with their donkeys.

source: Chuin amaho khopi-a kona achedoh uva gamlatah agei masangun, Joseph'in neichingpa henga chun, Kipat in lang miho chu delin, chule nangman amaho chu naphah tengle, ahenguva, Ipi dinga phatna chu setna-a nalethuh uham?
target: They had not gone far from the city when Joseph said to his steward, “Go after those men at once, and when you catch up with them, say to them, ‘Why have you repaid good with evil?

source: Hichea hi ka pakai pan adonji hilou hija, chule tahbeh-a hichehi agaochan naji chu hilouham? Hiche nabolu hi nangho nasuhkhelu ahitai, tin ahenguva gaseijin, ati.
target: Isn’t this the cup my master drinks from and also uses for divination? This is a wicked thing you have done.’ ”

source: Chuin aman amaho chu adelpha tan, chule hiche thu mama chu ahenguva aseitan ahi.
target: When he caught up with them, he repeated these words to them.

source: Chuin amahon ahenga, Ipi dinga ka pakaiyin hitobang thuhi naseiham? Nasohten chutobang aboldiu chu Pathen'in jada jenghen.
target: But they said to him, “Why does my lord say such things? Far be it from your servants to do anything like that!

source: Vetan, kadip kamuva kamudoh-u dangka chu Canaan gama konin nahenga kahinlepoh kitnuve; achutile napakai pa in'a kona sana le dangka keihon iti kaguh diu ham?
target: We even brought back to you from the land of Canaan the silver we found inside the mouths of our sacks. So why would we steal silver or gold from your master’s house?

source: Nasohte lah-a hin koihile namuna penpen chu, ama chu thijeng hen, chule keiho jeng jong ka pakai soh-in um jenguvinge, atiuve.
target: If any of your servants is found to have it, he will die; and the rest of us will become my lord’s slaves.”

source: Chuin aman, Tun nasei bangu chu himaihen: hiche kimuna penpa chu kasoh himai ding ahin; chule adangho vang themo chanda jenghen ati.
target: “Very well, then,” he said, “let it be as you say. Whoever is found to have it will become my slave; the rest of you will be free from blame.”

source: Chujouvin amaho amitakipmin adipmu chu gangtah-in tolla akoilhauvin, amitakip chun adip cheh uchu ahong taovin ahi.
target: Each of them quickly lowered his sack to the ground and opened it.

source: Chuin aman alenpena apanin, alhumpen geijin akholtan ahile, khon chu Benjamin dipma chun amudohtan ahi.
target: Then the steward proceeded to search, beginning with the oldest and ending with the youngest. And the cup was found in Benjamin’s sack.

source: Chutah-in amahon avonhou chu asattelun, chule amitakip chun apotnu asangnu apohsah kitnun, khopi lama akilekit taove.
target: At this, they tore their clothes. Then they all loaded their donkeys and returned to the city.

source: Chuin Judah le asopite chu Joseph'in ahung lhung taove; ajehchu ama chua chu umnalai ahi. Chuin amaho a-angsunga chun tolla abohkhup taove.
target: Joseph was still in the house when Judah and his brothers came in, and they threw themselves to the ground before him.

source: Chuin Joseph'in amaho henga, Hiche nathilbol uhi ipi nabolnao hitam? Keitobang mihin phun asan theije ti nahet lou uham? ati.
target: Joseph said to them, “What is this you have done? Don’t you know that a man like me can find things out by divination?”

source: Chuin Judah'in ka pakai henga ipi kaseidingu hitam? keihon ipi seitaoving em? Ahilouleh keiho le keihon iti kaki seitheng diu hitam? Pathen'in nasohte khangitlouna hi amudoh ahitai. Vetan, keiho hi ka pakai sohte kahiu ahitai, keiho le khon kimudoh napa jonghi, ati.
target: “What can we say to my lord?” Judah replied. “What can we say? How can we prove our innocence? God has uncovered your servants’ guilt. We are now my lord’s slaves—we ourselves and the one who was found to have the cup.”

source: Chuin aman, chutobanga kaboldiu chu Pathen jahda hihen. Ahin khon akhutna kimudohna pa bouchu kasoh hiding ahin; nangho vang, lungmong tah-in kipat un lang napau henga chetaovin, ati.
target: But Joseph said, “Far be it from me to do such a thing! Only the man who was found to have the cup will become my slave. The rest of you, go back to your father in peace.”

source: Chuin Judah'in akom ahin naijin, Vo ka pakai, nahenga katao ahi, nasoh hin ka pakai nahenga thucheng khat seijing ting, chule nalunghanna chu nasoh chunga hinkou dohsah hih-in; ajehchu nangma Pharaoh masap nahi.
target: Then Judah went up to him and said: “Pardon your servant, my lord, let me speak a word to my lord. Do not be angry with your servant, though you are equal to Pharaoh himself.

source: Ka pakaiyin nasohte henga, Nanghon pa ahiloule nasopiu nanei nalai uvem? tin neina dongun;
target: My lord asked his servants, ‘Do you have a father or a brother?’

source: Chuin keihon ka pakai henga, Kapau tehse khat le ateh nunga ahin chapang sopi khat kaneijuve; chule a-upa vang athitan, chule anu chate lah-a amabou uma ahitan, apan amachu angailu lheh-e, kanatiuve.
target: And we answered, ‘We have an aged father, and there is a young son born to him in his old age. His brother is dead, and he is the only one of his mother’s sons left, and his father loves him.’

source: Chuin nangman nasohte henga, Amachu kamitna kamunadin kahenga hinpui suh-un natin, ahi.
target: “Then you said to your servants, ‘Bring him down to me so I can see him for myself.’

source: Chuin keihon ka pakai henga, Chapang chun apa dalhathei ponte, ajehchu aman apa dalha taleh, apa thijeng ding ahi, kanatiuve.
target: And we said to my lord, ‘The boy cannot leave his father; if he leaves him, his father will die.’

source: Chuin nangman nasohte henga, Nanao lhumpenu chu nang hotoh lhona ahungsuh louva ahile, nanghon kamai namukit loudiu ahi, nati.
target: But you told your servants, ‘Unless your youngest brother comes down with you, you will not see my face again.’

source: Chuin nasoh kapau henga kakiletou kitphatnun ahitin ahi, Keihon ka pakai thusei jouse chu kaseipeh-un ahi.
target: When we went back to your servant my father, we told him what my lord had said.

source: Chuin kapau vin, Chekitnun lang eihoding chang phabep gachokitnun atin ahi.
target: “Then our father said, ‘Go back and buy a little more food.’

source: Chuin keihon, Keiho chesuhthei pouvinge, kanaopao alhumpen chutoh neilhonsah dinguleh keiho kachesuh dingu ahi: ajehchu kanaopao alhumpen chutoh kalhon lou uleh, mipa maichu kamu kitthei loudiu ahi, kanatiuve.
target: But we said, ‘We cannot go down. Only if our youngest brother is with us will we go. We cannot see the man’s face unless our youngest brother is with us.’

source: Chuin nasoh kapau chun kahenguva, Ka-inneipin chapa ni eihinpeh nanghon naheuve.
target: “Your servant my father said to us, ‘You know that my wife bore me two sons.

source: Chuin khatpa chun eidalhatan, chule keiman thonlouva ahal hala kimaltel hitante, kanatin; chule keiman amachu chuche-a patchun kamutapon ahi.
target: One of them went away from me, and I said, “He has surely been torn to pieces.” And I have not seen him since.

source: Chule nanghon ama jonghi keija konin puidoh unlang, achunga toset chutale, nanghon kasam kangsahi lunghem puma lhankhuh-a napuilut dingu ahi, atin ahi.
target: If you take this one from me too and harm comes to him, you will bring my gray head down to the grave in misery.’

source: Hijeh chun tun, keima hi nasoh kapau kom kalhunteng, chapang chu keihotoh umtahih leh, ahinkho chu chapangpa hinkho toh kikan khom ahijeh chun,
target: “So now, if the boy is not with us when I go back to your servant my father, and if my father, whose life is closely bound up with the boy’s life,

source: Hung hitiding ahi, aman chapang chu keihotoh kalhonkhom louvu chu amuteng, thitei ding ahitai. Chule nasohte hin, nasoh kapau sam kangsa chu lunghem puma lhankhuh-a kapuilut dingu ahi.
target: sees that the boy isn’t there, he will die. Your servants will bring the gray head of our father down to the grave in sorrow.

source: Ajehchu nasoh hi kapau henga chapang dinga hungkitung kahin, ahenga, Nahenga kahin lepuikit louleh, kapa henga kumkhon themona pong kate, kanati ahi.
target: Your servant guaranteed the boy’s safety to my father. I said, ‘If I do not bring him back to you, I will bear the blame before you, my father, all my life!’

source: Hijeh chun tun, nahenga katao ahi, chapang khelchun keimahi ka pakai dingin nasoh-in umingting, chule chapanghi asopite toh chetaohen.
target: “Now then, please let your servant remain here as my lord’s slave in place of the boy, and let the boy return with his brothers.

source: Ajehchu chapang chu kalhonpi louleh, kapa koma iti kakiletou thei ding ham? Ajehchu kapa chunga hung chuding setna chu muget inge, ati.
target: How can I go back to my father if the boy is not with me? No! Do not let me see the misery that would come on my father.”

source: Chujouvin Joseph akoma dingho angsunga chun ama le ama akikhamtang joutapon; chuin aman, Mijouse kakoma konin potdoh sah-un, tin asamtan ahi. Chuin Joseph ama le ama asopite henga akiphondoh chun, koimacha akoma aumpon ahi.
target: Then Joseph could no longer control himself before all his attendants, and he cried out, “Have everyone leave my presence!” So there was no one with Joseph when he made himself known to his brothers.

source: Chuin ama hatah-in akaptan; chule Egypt mite le Pharaoh insung mite chun ajauvin ahi.
target: And he wept so loudly that the Egyptians heard him, and Pharaoh’s household heard about it.

source: Chuin Joseph'in asopite henga, keima Joseph kahi; kapa dam nalai nam? ati. Chuin asopite chun amachu adonbut thei pouvin; ajehchu amasanga chu lungdong gamu ahitai.
target: Joseph said to his brothers, “I am Joseph! Is my father still living?” But his brothers were not able to answer him, because they were terrified at his presence.

source: Chuin Joseph'in asopite henga, Katao ahi, kakom hinaijun ati. Chuin amahon ahin naijun ahi. Chuin aman keima nanaopao Joseph, Egypt gama najohdoh pao chu kahi.
target: Then Joseph said to his brothers, “Come close to me.” When they had done so, he said, “I am your brother Joseph, the one you sold into Egypt!

source: Hijeh chun tun nanghon hikoma neinajoh jeh-uchun lungkham hih-un, ahilouleh nangho le nangho kilunghan hih un; ajehchu Pathen'in hinkho venbitna aumna dinga nangho masanga einasol ahi.
target: And now, do not be distressed and do not be angry with yourselves for selling me here, because it was to save lives that God sent me ahead of you.

source: Ajehchu hiche kumni sunghin hiche gamahin kel alhatai: chule kumnga aum nalaijin, hiche sunga hi lou tuh le chang-at himhim umlou ding ahi.
target: For two years now there has been famine in the land, and for the next five years there will be no plowing and reaping.

source: Chule leichunga hi nachilhah teo hongbit dingle, lhatdohna loupitah-a nahinkhou hoidoh sah dinga Pathen'in nama sang uva einasol ahi.
target: But God sent me ahead of you to preserve for you a remnant on earth and to save your lives by a great deliverance.

source: Hijeh chun tun hikoma einasola chu nangho nahipouvin, Pathen joh ahibouve. Chule aman Pharaoh pa le a-insung jouse pakai ding, chule Egypt gam pumpi-a vaihom dingin eisemtan ahi.
target: “So then, it was not you who sent me here, but God. He made me father to Pharaoh, lord of his entire household and ruler of all Egypt.

source: Kino uvin, kapa koma cheovin lang, ahenga, Nachapa Joseph'in, Pathen'in Egypt gam pumpi-a pakaiyin eitung tai; kahenga hin hungsuh-in, hung geisang hih-in.
target: Now hurry back to my father and say to him, ‘This is what your son Joseph says: God has made me lord of all Egypt. Come down to me; don’t delay.

source: Chule nangma Goshen gama nachen ding, nangma le nachate, chateho, nakelngoi hon, nabonghon, chule nanei chengse puma keima kom naija naum ding ahi.
target: You shall live in the region of Goshen and be near me—you, your children and grandchildren, your flocks and herds, and all you have.

source: Chule keiman nangma chua chun vah-ing kate; ajehchu kumnga kel lhanalai ding ahi; achuti loule nangma le na-insung mite, chule nanei chengse vaichat na-a chugetnun nate, tin aseije gatiuvin.
target: I will provide for you there, because five years of famine are still to come. Otherwise you and your household and all who belong to you will become destitute.’

source: Chule, veuvin, keiman kakamtah-a naheng uva kasei ahi ti namit tah-u le kanao Benjamin mittah-in amutai.
target: “You can see for yourselves, and so can my brother Benjamin, that it is really I who am speaking to you.

source: Chule Egypt gama kaloupina jouse le nathil mu jouseu hi kapa naseipeh dingu; chule nanghon gangtah-a kapa chu hilama nahin puisuh diu ahi, ati.
target: Tell my father about all the honor accorded me in Egypt and about everything you have seen. And bring my father down here quickly.”

source: Chuin aman anau Benjamin chu angong koijin, akaptan; chule Benjamin'in jong angong koijin akaptan ahi.
target: Then he threw his arms around his brother Benjamin and wept, and Benjamin embraced him, weeping.

source: Chuche chung chon chun asopite jouse chu achopmin, akakhumin ahi. Chujou chun asopite chun ama akihou limpi taovin ahi.
target: And he kissed all his brothers and wept over them. Afterward his brothers talked with him.

source: Chuin Joseph sopite ahunguve, ti thuthang chu Pharaoh'in ajah phatnin, Pharaoh le asohte chu akipah lheh-un ahi.
target: When the news reached Pharaoh’s palace that Joseph’s brothers had come, Pharaoh and all his officials were pleased.

source: Chuin Pharaoh'in Joseph henga, Nasopite henga hitin seijin, Nanghon hitin bolun: nanghon nasangan houchu chang pohsah unlang, cheovin, Canaan gama kileuvin;
target: Pharaoh said to Joseph, “Tell your brothers, ‘Do this: Load your animals and return to the land of Canaan,

source: Chule napau le na-insung miho hinpui junlang, kahenga hunguvin; keiman nangho Egypt gam phapen chu kapeh uva, chule nanghon chuche gamphapen ga chu naneh dingu ahi.
target: and bring your father and your families back to me. I will give you the best of the land of Egypt and you can enjoy the fat of the land.’

source: Tun nangma thu kapeh nahin, hichehi bolun: nachasenhou dingle, na-inneipite diuvin, Egypt gama konin kangtalai ho kilah-un, chule napau hinpuijun lang, hunguvin.
target: “You are also directed to tell them, ‘Do this: Take some carts from Egypt for your children and your wives, and get your father and come.

source: Chujongleh nathilkeo hou gelkhoh hih-un; ajehchu Egypt gam pumpi-a aphapen chu nangho-a ahi, tin aseijin ahi.
target: Never mind about your belongings, because the best of all Egypt will be yours.’ ”

source: Chuin Israel chaten chutichun aboltauvin; chule Pharaoh kamsoh dungjuijin, Joseph'in amaho chu kangtalai ho apen, lampi-a aneh dingu an jong apen ahi.
target: So the sons of Israel did this. Joseph gave them carts, as Pharaoh had commanded, and he also gave them provisions for their journey.

source: Aman aboncha diuvin kikhelna ding ponsil apesoh keijin; ahin aman Benjamin vang chu dangka jathum le kikhelna ponsil to nga apen ahi.
target: To each of them he gave new clothing, but to Benjamin he gave three hundred shekels of silver and five sets of clothes.

source: Chuin aman apa henga hiche hohi athotnin ahi; Egypt gam thilphaho sangan som poh dimset le,lamjotna-a apan aneh ding chang, changlhah chule nehding sanganpi poh som dimset athotnin ahi.
target: And this is what he sent to his father: ten donkeys loaded with the best things of Egypt, and ten female donkeys loaded with grain and bread and other provisions for his journey.

source: Chutichun aman asopite chu asoltan, chule amaho akipatdoh taove. Chuin aman ahenguva, Lampia nakiboipa louna dingun kichih theijun, ati.
target: Then he sent his brothers away, and as they were leaving he said to them, “Don’t quarrel on the way!”

source: Chuin amaho Egypt gama konin achetouvun, Canaan gama apau Jacob heng ahung lhung taove,
target: So they went up out of Egypt and came to their father Jacob in the land of Canaan.

source: Chuin amahon ahenga, Joseph chu ahing nalaijin, chule Egypt gam pumpi-a gamvaipon apange, atiuve. Chuin Jacob lungphut akhongaijin ahi; ajehchu amaho chu atahsan lou ahi.
target: They told him, “Joseph is still alive! In fact, he is ruler of all Egypt.” Jacob was stunned; he did not believe them.

source: Chuin amahon Joseph'in ahenguva aseithu jouse chu aseipeh taovin ahi. Chuin ama akitolna dinga Joseph'in ahinthot kangtalai ho chu amuphatnin, apau Jacob lungthim ahung haldoh kittan ahi.
target: But when they told him everything Joseph had said to them, and when he saw the carts Joseph had sent to carry him back, the spirit of their father Jacob revived.

source: Chuin Israel'in, Aphaset tai; kachapa Joseph adam nalaije. Kathi-kah in cheng ting amachu gamunge, ati.
target: And Israel said, “I’m convinced! My son Joseph is still alive. I will go and see him before I die.”

source: Chuin Israel anei chengsetoh akipatnin, Beersheba ahung lhungin, chuin apa Isaac Pathen henga chun kilhaina gantha ho atoh-in ahi.
target: So Israel set out with all that was his, and when he reached Beersheba, he offered sacrifices to the God of his father Isaac.

source: Chuin jana mu aneina-a Pathen'in Israel chu ahin houvin, ajah-a, Jacob, Jacob, atin ahi. Chuin aman, hikoma kaume, ati.
target: And God spoke to Israel in a vision at night and said, “Jacob! Jacob!” “Here I am,” he replied.

source: Chuin aman keimahi Pathen, napa Pathen chu kahi; Egypt gama chesuhding kicha hih-in: ajehchu chukoma chu keiman nangma nam lentah-a kasemding nahi.
target: “I am God, the God of your father,” he said. “Do not be afraid to go down to Egypt, for I will make you into a great nation there.

source: Keiman nangma Egypt gamah kilhonsuh pingting, chule nangma kahin lepuikit teiding nahi; chule Joseph'in akhut tah-a namit ahin sinsah ding ahi.
target: I will go down to Egypt with you, and I will surely bring you back again. And Joseph’s own hand will close your eyes.”

source: Chuin Jacob Beersheba'a konin akipatdoh tai. Chuin Israel chapate chun apau Jacob chu achasen hou, chule a-inneipi teochu Pharaoh'in ama kitol nadinga ahinsol kangtalai ho-a chun atousah taovin ahi.
target: Then Jacob left Beersheba, and Israel’s sons took their father Jacob and their children and their wives in the carts that Pharaoh had sent to transport him.

source: Chuin Jacob le achilhahte chun Canaan gama alamdoh-u aganchahou leh athilkeu hou chu akipoh-un, Egypt gam ahung lhung taovin ahi.
target: So Jacob and all his offspring went to Egypt, taking with them their livestock and the possessions they had acquired in Canaan.

source: Achapate le atupate, Achanute le atunute, chule achilhahte chengse akipuijin, Egypt gam alutpitan ahi.
target: Jacob brought with him to Egypt his sons and grandsons and his daughters and granddaughters—all his offspring.

source: Chule hicheng hi Egypt gama lut, Israel chate, Jacob le achapate minho chu ahiuve; Reuben, Jacob chapa lenpen ahi.
target: These are the names of the sons of Israel (Jacob and his descendants) who went to Egypt: Reuben the firstborn of Jacob.

source: Chule Reuben chapate chu; Hanoch, Phallu, Hezron, chule Carmi ahiuve.
target: The sons of Reuben: Hanok, Pallu, Hezron and Karmi.

source: Chule Simeon chapate chu; Jemuel, Jamin, Ohad, Jachin, Johar, chule Canaan numei khat chapa Shaul ahiuve.
target: The sons of Simeon: Jemuel, Jamin, Ohad, Jakin, Zohar and Shaul the son of a Canaanite woman.

source: Chule Levi chapate chu; Gershom, Kohath chule Merari ahiuve.
target: The sons of Levi: Gershon, Kohath and Merari.

source: Chule Judah chapate chu; Er, Onan, Shelah, Pharez chule Zerah ahiuvin; ahivangin Er le Onan chu Canaan gama athilhontan ahi. Chule Pharez chapate chu Hezron le Hamul ahilhone.
target: The sons of Judah: Er, Onan, Shelah, Perez and Zerah (but Er and Onan had died in the land of Canaan). The sons of Perez: Hezron and Hamul.

source: Chule Issachar chapate chu; Tolla, Phuvah, Job, chule Shimron ahiuve.
target: The sons of Issachar: Tola, Puah, Jashub and Shimron.

source: Chule Zebulun chapate chu; Serad, Elon, chule Jahleel ahiuve.
target: The sons of Zebulun: Sered, Elon and Jahleel.

source: Hichenghi Leah chapate, achanu Dinah toh Padan-Aram gama Jacob ahinpehho chu ahiuve. Achapate le achanute agomin somthum le thum ahiuve.
target: These were the sons Leah bore to Jacob in Paddan Aram, besides his daughter Dinah. These sons and daughters of his were thirty-three in all.

source: Chule Gad chapate chu; Ziphion chule Haggi, Shuni, Ezphon, Eri, Arodi, chule Areli ahiuve.
target: The sons of Gad: Zephon, Haggi, Shuni, Ezbon, Eri, Arodi and Areli.

source: Chule Asher chapate chu; Jimnah, Ishuah, Ishui, Beriah, chule asopinu Sarah toh ahiuve. Chule Beriah chapateni chu Heber, Malchiel ahilhone.
target: The sons of Asher: Imnah, Ishvah, Ishvi and Beriah. Their sister was Serah. The sons of Beriah: Heber and Malkiel.

source: Hichenghi Laban'in achanu Leah dinga apeh Zilpah chapate ahiuvin, hicheng ho hi amanun Jacob ahinpeh ahi; agoma mi somlegup ahiuve.
target: These were the children born to Jacob by Zilpah, whom Laban had given to his daughter Leah—sixteen in all.

source: Jacob inneipi Rachel chapate chu; Joseph le Benjamin ahilhone.
target: The sons of Jacob’s wife Rachel: Joseph and Benjamin.

source: Chuin Joseph chun Egypt gama achapa Manasseh le Ephraim ahingin, hichu On kho-a thempu, Potiphera chanu Asenath'in ahinpeh ahi.
target: In Egypt, Manasseh and Ephraim were born to Joseph by Asenath daughter of Potiphera, priest of On.

source: Chule Benjamin chapate chu; Belah, Becher, Ashbel, Gera, Naaman, Ehi, Rosh, Muppim, Huppim chule Ard ahiuve.
target: The sons of Benjamin: Bela, Beker, Ashbel, Gera, Naaman, Ehi, Rosh, Muppim, Huppim and Ard.

source: Hicheng hi Rachel'in Jacob dinga ahinpeh chapateho chu ahiuvin, abonchauvin mi somleli ahiuve.
target: These were the sons of Rachel who were born to Jacob—fourteen in all.

source: Chule Dan chapa chu; Hushim ahi.
target: The son of Dan: Hushim.

source: Chule Naphtali chapate chu; Jahzeel, Guni, Jezer, chule Shillem ahiuve.
target: The sons of Naphtali: Jahziel, Guni, Jezer and Shillem.

source: Hichengho hi Laban'in achanu Rachel dinga apeh Bilhah chapate chu ahiuvin, amanun hicheng hohi Jacob ahinpeh ahi; abonchauvin mi sagi ahiuve.
target: These were the sons born to Jacob by Bilhah, whom Laban had given to his daughter Rachel—seven in all.

source: Jacob achapate inneipi teho tilouvin, Egypt gama Jacob toh lhonlut, ataiguija kondoh ho chu abonchauva mi somgup le gup ahiuve.
target: All those who went to Egypt with Jacob—those who were his direct descendants, not counting his sons’ wives—numbered sixty-six persons.

source: Chule Egypt gama penga Joseph chapa chu mini ahilhonin, Egypt gama pemlut insung mite jouse chu somsagi hiuve.
target: With the two sons who had been born to Joseph in Egypt, the members of Jacob’s family, which went to Egypt, were seventy in all.

source: Chuin Jacob'in Goshen gam lampi chu gahetoh dingin, Judah chu Joseph henga asolmasan; chuin amaho Goshen gam ahung lhung taovin ahi.
target: Now Jacob sent Judah ahead of him to Joseph to get directions to Goshen. When they arrived in the region of Goshen,

source: Chuin Joseph'in akangtalai akigotnin, Goshen gama apa Israel kimutopi dingin achetoutan, chuin ama le ama ahenga akiphongin ahi; chuin amachu angong koijin, angongkoi pumin sot thimtah akaptan ahi.
target: Joseph had his chariot made ready and went to Goshen to meet his father Israel. As soon as Joseph appeared before him, he threw his arms around his father and wept for a long time.

source: Chuin Israel'in Joseph henga, Tunvang dama nana umma, namai kamukit tahjeh-in, thi jong leng khoh kasatapoi, ati.
target: Israel said to Joseph, “Now I am ready to die, since I have seen for myself that you are still alive.”

source: Chuin Joseph'in asopite le apa insung mite ho henga, Keima chetou vingting, Pharaoh kimuping ting, chule ahenga, Canaan gama cheng kasopite le kapa insungmite ho kaheng ahung lhung taove;
target: Then Joseph said to his brothers and to his father’s household, “I will go up and speak to Pharaoh and will say to him, ‘My brothers and my father’s household, who were living in the land of Canaan, have come to me.

source: Chule amaho natoh chu ganchavah ahin, chule kelngoi ching mi ahiuve; chule amahon akelngoihon uleh agancha honnu, chule anei jouseu ahinposoh keijun ahi, tin gasei ing kate.
target: The men are shepherds; they tend livestock, and they have brought along their flocks and herds and everything they own.’

source: Chule hung hiti ding ahi, Pharaoh'in nangho nakou uva, ipi natong mi nahiuvem? tia ahin dohteng leh,
target: When Pharaoh calls you in and asks, ‘What is your occupation?’

source: Goshen gama nachen theina dinguva, nanghon, Nasohte hi kachapan nuva pat tuni geijahi keiho le kapateho ganchavah mi kahiuve, nati dingu, ahi. Ajehchu kelngoiching tapou chu Egypt mite dinga thet umtah ahi, tin aseije.
target: you should answer, ‘Your servants have tended livestock from our boyhood on, just as our fathers did.’ Then you will be allowed to settle in the region of Goshen, for all shepherds are detestable to the Egyptians.”

source: Chujouvin Joseph chu ahungin Pharaoh henga, Kapa le kasopite ho akelngoi hon nutoh, agancha hon nutoh, chule anei chengseutoh Canaan gama konin ahunguvin; chule, vetan, amaho Goshen gama aumuve, ati.
target: Joseph went and told Pharaoh, “My father and brothers, with their flocks and herds and everything they own, have come from the land of Canaan and are now in Goshen.”

source: Chuin aman asopite lah-a konin mi nga apuijin, Pharaoh henga, aphongdoh-in ahi.
target: He chose five of his brothers and presented them before Pharaoh.

source: Chuin Pharaoh'in asopite henga chun, Nangho ipi natong mi nahiuvem? ati. Chuin amahon Pharaoh henga, Nasohte hi, keiho le kapu kapateu jong kelngoi ching mi kahiuve, atiuve.
target: Pharaoh asked the brothers, “What is your occupation?” “Your servants are shepherds,” they replied to Pharaoh, “just as our fathers were.”

source: Hicheng chungchon chun amahon Pharaoh henga, Hiche gama pemdinga hunga kahiuve; ajehchu Canaan gam kel akhoh behset jeh-in, nasohte kelngoihon nehding hampa aumtapoi: hijeh chun tun nasohte hi Goshen Gama neichen sah-un, tia nahenga kataovu ahi, atiuve.
target: They also said to him, “We have come to live here for a while, because the famine is severe in Canaan and your servants’ flocks have no pasture. So now, please let your servants settle in Goshen.”

source: Chuin Pharaoh'in Joseph henga, Napa le nasopite nahenga ahunguvin;
target: Pharaoh said to Joseph, “Your father and your brothers have come to you,

source: Chule Egypt gam hi namasanga aume; napa le nasopite hi gampha pentah-a chensah in; Goshen gama chun chenguhen. Chule alah uva mi natong theitah nahet le, kagancha ho chunga thuneidin koijin, ati.
target: and the land of Egypt is before you; settle your father and your brothers in the best part of the land. Let them live in Goshen. And if you know of any among them with special ability, put them in charge of my own livestock.”

source: Chuin Joseph'in apa Jacob ahin puilutnin, Pharaoh anga adinsah-in ahi. Chuin Jacob'in Pharaoh chu phatthei aboh-in ahi.
target: Then Joseph brought his father Jacob in and presented him before Pharaoh. After Jacob blessed Pharaoh,

source: Chuin Pharaoh'in Jacob henga, Kum ijat nahitah em? ati.
target: Pharaoh asked him, “How old are you?”

source: Chuin Jacob'in Pharaoh henga, Kahinkho kakholjinna nikho hohi kum jakhat le kum somthum ahitai. Kadamsung kumhi lhomcha le hahsatah ahin, kapu kapate hinkho kholjin laisung kum ho jong aphajoupoi, atin ahi.
target: And Jacob said to Pharaoh, “The years of my pilgrimage are a hundred and thirty. My years have been few and difficult, and they do not equal the years of the pilgrimage of my fathers.”

source: Chuin Jacob'in Pharaoh phatthei aboh-in, Pharaoh angsunga konin achedohtan ahi.
target: Then Jacob blessed Pharaoh and went out from his presence.

source: Chuin Joseph'in apa le asopite chu achensah-in, Pharaoh thupeh dungjuijin Egypt gamsunga, Rameses gam sunga mun phapen chu alodiuvin apetan ahi.
target: So Joseph settled his father and his brothers in Egypt and gave them property in the best part of the land, the district of Rameses, as Pharaoh directed.

source: Chuin Joseph'in apa le asopite, chule apa insung mite jouse chu a-inko pumpiuvin changlhah in avahtan ahi.
target: Joseph also provided his father and his brothers and all his father’s household with food, according to the number of their children.

source: Chuin gamsung pumpi-a chun nehding him him aumtapoi; ajehchu kelhah chu akhoh behseh jengtan, Egypt gam le Canaan gam pumpi-a chu keljeh chun alhasam lheh tan ahi.
target: There was no food, however, in the whole region because the famine was severe; both Egypt and Canaan wasted away because of the famine.

source: Chuin Joseph'in achang chohnao man chun Egypt gam le Canaan gama um sum jouse chu akhomsoh heltan ahi. Chuin Joseph'in sum chu Pharaoh in'a achoi luttan ahi.
target: Joseph collected all the money that was to be found in Egypt and Canaan in payment for the grain they were buying, and he brought it to Pharaoh’s palace.

source: Chuin Egypt gam le Canaan gama sum jouse chu akiman chaisoh phatnin, Egypt mite jouse chu Joseph henga ahungun, ajah-a, Nehding neipeuvin, ajehchu namitmu-a hi ipidinga kathi jeng dingu ham? ajehchu ka sum jouseu abeisoh heltai, atiuve.
target: When the money of the people of Egypt and Canaan was gone, all Egypt came to Joseph and said, “Give us food. Why should we die before your eyes? Our money is all gone.”

source: Chuin Joseph'in, nasum'u abeitah-a ahile na gancha hou neipeuvin, chule keiman nangho na gancha hou khelin nehding napenao vinge, ati.
target: “Then bring your livestock,” said Joseph. “I will sell you food in exchange for your livestock, since your money is gone.”

source: Chuin amahon agancha hou Joseph henga ahinpuijun: Joseph'in amaho chu sakol ho, kelngoiho, bongho chule sangan ho khel chun nehding apen ahi. Chuche kum chun agancha hou jouse man chun nehding apen avahtan ahi.
target: So they brought their livestock to Joseph, and he gave them food in exchange for their horses, their sheep and goats, their cattle and donkeys. And he brought them through that year with food in exchange for all their livestock.

source: Chuin chuche kum chu akichai phatnin, ama henga chun akum nina-in ahungun, ajah-a, Ka sum hou iti kaman chaiju ahi ka-pakaiya konin impou vinge; chule kagancha hou jouse jong ka-pakaiya ahitai. Katahsao leh kagam'u tilouvin, ka pakai mitmun imacha khen aumtapoi.
target: When that year was over, they came to him the following year and said, “We cannot hide from our lord the fact that since our money is gone and our livestock belongs to you, there is nothing left for our lord except our bodies and our land.

source: Ipidinga namitmu-a keiho le kagam uhi kamantha jeng dingu ham? Nangman nehman dingin keiho le kagam'u hi neicho taovin, chule keiho le kagam uhi Pharaoh soh-in pang taovinge. Keiho thilouva kahin theina dingu le gamhi agohkeova aumlouna dingin muchi neipeuvin, ahungtiuve.
target: Why should we perish before your eyes—we and our land as well? Buy us and our land in exchange for food, and we with our land will be in bondage to Pharaoh. Give us seed so that we may live and not die, and that the land may not become desolate.”

source: Chuin Joseph'in Egypt gam pumpi chu Pharaoh dingin achotan ahi; ajehchu achunguva kel khohbeh seh tahjeh chun, Egypt mite jousen aloucheh-u ajohdoh taovin ahi. Chutichun gam chu Pharaoh'a ahisoh tan ahi.
target: So Joseph bought all the land in Egypt for Pharaoh. The Egyptians, one and all, sold their fields, because the famine was too severe for them. The land became Pharaoh’s,

source: Chule miho vangchu, aman amaho chu Egypt gam ningkhat lama konin ning langkhat na um khopi ho-a chun akichon lutsah tan ahi.
target: and Joseph reduced the people to servitude, from one end of Egypt to the other.

source: Aman thempuho gam chubou achopon ahi; ajehchu thempuho chun Pharaoh'a konin chantum aneijun, chule Pharaoh'in apeh-u chan chu aneh-u ahi. Hijeh chun amahon agamu chu akijoh pouvin ahi.
target: However, he did not buy the land of the priests, because they received a regular allotment from Pharaoh and had food enough from the allotment Pharaoh gave them. That is why they did not sell their land.

source: Chujouvin Joseph'in miho henga chun, Veuvin, tunia hi keiman nangho le nagamu hi Pharaoh dinga kachohdoh ahitai. Veovin, hikomahin nangho ding muchi aumin, chule nanghon hichu leija natu dingu ahi.
target: Joseph said to the people, “Now that I have bought you and your land today for Pharaoh, here is seed for you so you can plant the ground.

source: Chule chang atphat teng hitiding ahi, hopnga-a hopkhat chu Pharaoh napeh uva, hopnga-a hopli chu nangho nachan diu, hichu louva muchiding, nangho le na-insung miteu nehding le, nachasen hou dinga nehding hiding ahi, ati.
target: But when the crop comes in, give a fifth of it to Pharaoh. The other four-fifths you may keep as seed for the fields and as food for yourselves and your households and your children.”

source: Chuin amahon, Nangman kahinkhou nahuhhing ahitai; ka pakai mitmun lungsetna neimusah-un, chule keiho Pharaoh soh hitaovinge, atiuvin ahi.
target: “You have saved our lives,” they said. “May we find favor in the eyes of our lord; we will be in bondage to Pharaoh.”

source: Chuin Joseph'in, Pharaoh'in hopnga-a hopkhat achandinga dan asem chu Egypt gama dingin tunichan geihin chona danin aumtan ahi. Thempuho gam bouchu Pharaoh'a ahipon ahi.
target: So Joseph established it as a law concerning land in Egypt—still in force today—that a fifth of the produce belongs to Pharaoh. It was only the land of the priests that did not become Pharaoh’s.

source: Chuin Israel chu Egypt gamsung, Goshen gama chun achengtan; chule hia chun amahon gou akholdoh-un, chi tamtah akhaijun, nasatah-in apung taovin ahi.
target: Now the Israelites settled in Egypt in the region of Goshen. They acquired property there and were fruitful and increased greatly in number.

source: Chuin Jacob Egypt gama chun kum som le kum sagi ahingin ahi. Chuti chun Jacob damsung hinkho chu kum jakhat le kum somli le kum sagi ahi.
target: Jacob lived in Egypt seventeen years, and the years of his life were a hundred and forty-seven.

source: Chuin Israel thina ding phat ahung naitan ahi. Chuin aman achapa Joseph chu akouvin, ajah-a, Tuahi namitmu-a lungsetna kachana ahile, nahenga katao ahi, nakhut chu kapheipi noija hinkoijin lang, lungset le thutah-in kachunga natongin; katao ahi, Egypt gama hin neihin vuihih-in.
target: When the time drew near for Israel to die, he called for his son Joseph and said to him, “If I have found favor in your eyes, put your hand under my thigh and promise that you will show me kindness and faithfulness. Do not bury me in Egypt,

source: Ahin kapu kapate toh neilupkhom sah-in; Egypt gama kona hin neipuidoh inlang, akivuinao mun'a chun neivuijin, ati. Chuin aman, Nasei banga kabol ding ahi, ati.
target: but when I rest with my fathers, carry me out of Egypt and bury me where they are buried.” “I will do as you say,” he said.

source: Chuin aman, Kahenga kihahsel in, ati. Chuin ama ahenga akihahseltai. Chuin Israel ajalkhun lulhunna chun akunin ahi.
target: “Swear to me,” he said. Then Joseph swore to him, and Israel worshiped as he leaned on the top of his staff.

source: Chuin hicheng jouse nunghin ahitin ahi, Joseph henga, Vetan, napa anai atipeh-un ahi. Chuin aman achapa teni Manasseh le Ephraim akipuijin achetan ahi.
target: Some time later Joseph was told, “Your father is ill.” So he took his two sons Manasseh and Ephraim along with him.

source: Chuin Jacob henga, Vetan, nachapa Joseph nahenga ahunge, atipeh-un ahi. Chuin Israel ama le ama akiha bolin, jalkhun chunga chun atouvin ahi.
target: When Jacob was told, “Your son Joseph has come to you,” Israel rallied his strength and sat up on the bed.

source: Chuin Jacob'in Joseph henga, Imajouse bolthei Pathen hat chungnung chu Canaan gama Luz mun'a chun kahenga ahung kilah in, phatthei eiboh-in,
target: Jacob said to Joseph, “God Almighty appeared to me at Luz in the land of Canaan, and there he blessed me

source: Chule kahenga, Vetan, keiman nangma chi tamtah khaisah ingting, kapunsah ding, chule keiman nangma vaipi tamtah kahisah ding; chule hiche gamhi nanunga nachilhahte dinga tonsotna agou dinguva kapeh ding ahi, ati.
target: and said to me, ‘I am going to make you fruitful and increase your numbers. I will make you a community of peoples, and I will give this land as an everlasting possession to your descendants after you.’

source: Chule tun Egypt gama nahenga kahung masanga Egypt gama nanei, nachapa teni Ephraim le Manasseh hi keija ahilhone. Reuben le Simeon keija ahibanga, amani hi keija hiding ahi.
target: “Now then, your two sons born to you in Egypt before I came to you here will be reckoned as mine; Ephraim and Manasseh will be mine, just as Reuben and Simeon are mine.

source: Amani nunga cha le nao nanei vang chu nangma mi hitantin, amaho chu asopite gou le minlah-a kisimtha nante.
target: Any children born to you after them will be yours; in the territory they inherit they will be reckoned under the names of their brothers.

source: Chule keima vang, Padan-Aram'a kona kahung chun Rachel chu Canaan gama Ephrath phah nading gamla thim avat nalaijin, lamdunga ka-angsunga athitan ahi. Chuin keiman Ephrath lamdunga chun kavuitan ahi; Hichu Bethlehem chu ahi.
target: As I was returning from Paddan, to my sorrow Rachel died in the land of Canaan while we were still on the way, a little distance from Ephrath. So I buried her there beside the road to Ephrath” (that is, Bethlehem).

source: Chuin Israel chun Joseph chapateni chu aven, Amani hi koi hilhon ham? ati.
target: When Israel saw the sons of Joseph, he asked, “Who are these?”

source: Chuin Joseph'in apa henga, Amani hi hiche mun'a Pathen'in eipeh kachapa teni ahilhone, ati. Chuin aman nahenga katao ahi, kahenga hinpuijin, chule keiman amani vangboh ingkate, ati.
target: “They are the sons God has given me here,” Joseph said to his father. Then Israel said, “Bring them to me so I may bless them.”

source: Tun Israel chu atehjeh-in amit athimtan, kho amuthei tapon ahi. Chuin Joseph'in amani chu ahenga ahinpui naijin; chuin aman amani chu achopmin, apomtan ahi.
target: Now Israel’s eyes were failing because of old age, and he could hardly see. So Joseph brought his sons close to him, and his father kissed them and embraced them.

source: Chuin Israel'in Joseph henga, Namel muding kana gelphah lou ahitan; ahin vetan, Pathen'in nachilhah kisan eimusahtai, ati.
target: Israel said to Joseph, “I never expected to see your face again, and now God has allowed me to see your children too.”

source: Chuin Joseph'in amani chu apa pheichunga konin apuidoh'in, amatah chu tolla aboh khupmin ahi.
target: Then Joseph removed them from Israel’s knees and bowed down with his face to the ground.

source: Chuin Joseph'in anilhon chun akaijin, Ephraim chu akhut jetlamin Israel khut veilam, chule Manasseh chu akhut veilamin Israel khut jetlama ahin kaijin, ahenga ahinpui naijin ahi.
target: And Joseph took both of them, Ephraim on his right toward Israel’s left hand and Manasseh on his left toward Israel’s right hand, and brought them close to him.

source: Chuin Israel'in akhut jetlam ahin lhang doh-in, aneojopa Ephraim lu chunga chun angamin ahi, chule akhut veilama chu Manasseh lu chunga angamin, akhut chu henasan ajam pelin ahi; ajehchu Manasseh chu apeng masa ahi.
target: But Israel reached out his right hand and put it on Ephraim’s head, though he was the younger, and crossing his arms, he put his left hand on Manasseh’s head, even though Manasseh was the firstborn.

source: Chuin aman Joseph chu phatthei aboh-in, kapute kapa, Abraham le Isaac namasanga anavale nalhon Pathen, kahinkho lhumkeija, tuni nikho geija eihin ching jinga Pathen,
target: Then he blessed Joseph and said, “May the God before whom my fathers Abraham and Isaac walked faithfully, the God who has been my shepherd all my life to this day,

source: Thil gilou tinchenga kona eina huhdoh jing vantil chun, chapang teni hi phatthei hinboh hen; chule amani chunga hin keima min, kapu kapa Abraham le kapa Isaac min hinpu lhonhen; chujong le amani hi leiset vaipi jalah-a mipi atama tamin hung punglhon hen ati.
target: the Angel who has delivered me from all harm —may he bless these boys. May they be called by my name and the names of my fathers Abraham and Isaac, and may they increase greatly on the earth.”

source: Chuin Joseph'in apan akhut jetlam Ephraim luchunga angap chu amuphatnin, alung phamotan ahi. Chuin aman apa khut chu Ephraim lu-a kona Manasseh lu-a chon dingin atuh-in ahi.
target: When Joseph saw his father placing his right hand on Ephraim’s head he was displeased; so he took hold of his father’s hand to move it from Ephraim’s head to Manasseh’s head.

source: Chuin Joseph'in apa henga, Chutiponte, kapa; ajehchu hiche pahi apeng masa ahin, nakhut jetlam chu alu chunga koijin, ati.
target: Joseph said to him, “No, my father, this one is the firstborn; put your right hand on his head.”

source: Chuin apa chu anom pon, Keiman kahenai, chapa, keiman kahenai; amajong namkhat hunghi ding, chule amajong lending ahinai. Amavang tahbeh-a anaopa johhi ama sanga hunglen joding, achilhahte chu nam tamtah hung hiding ahiuve, ati.
target: But his father refused and said, “I know, my son, I know. He too will become a people, and he too will become great. Nevertheless, his younger brother will be greater than he, and his descendants will become a group of nations.”

source: Chuin aman chuche nichun amani chu phatthei aboh-in, Nangni min pana Israel'in Phatthei abohding, Pathen'in nangma Ephraim le Manasseh bangin nasem hen, ati dingu ahi, atin; aman Ephraim chu Manasseh masanga akoitan ahi.
target: He blessed them that day and said, “In your name will Israel pronounce this blessing: ‘May God make you like Ephraim and Manasseh.’ ” So he put Ephraim ahead of Manasseh.

source: Chuin Israel'in Joseph henga, vetan, keima kathiding ahitai. Hijongle Pathen'in nangma naumpi jing ding, chule aman nangma napu napate gamsunga nahin lepui kitding ahi.
