target: Then Israel said to Joseph, “I am about to die, but God will be with you and take you back to the land of your fathers.

source: Chuche chung chon chun Amor mite-a kona kachemjam le kathalpi-a kona kaladoh chu, keiman nangma nasopite chan sangin tamin chan khat kapehben ahi ati.
target: And to you I give one more ridge of land than to your brothers, the ridge I took from the Amorites with my sword and my bow.”

source: Chuin Jacob'in achapate chu akouvin, ahenguva, Ninunung nile nachung uva ipi hung chuding ham tichu kaseipeh theina dingun, hung kikhom khomun, ati.
target: Then Jacob called for his sons and said: “Gather around so I can tell you what will happen to you in days to come.

source: Nangho Jacob chapate, hung kikhom khomun lang ngaijun; napau Israel thusei hi ngai phaovin.
target: “Assemble and listen, sons of Jacob; listen to your father Israel.

source: Reuben nangma kachapa lenpen nahin, kathilbol theina, chule kathahat kipatna, kichoisang na chungnung pen le thahatna chungnung pen chu nahi.
target: “Reuben, you are my firstborn, my might, the first sign of my strength, excelling in honor, excelling in power.

source: Twisih banga dingdetlou nahin, nangma achung nungpen nahilou ding ahi, ajehchu nangma napa jalkhuna nakaldoh-in, nasuboh-in ahi: ama kalupna-a akaldoh-in ahi.
target: Turbulent as the waters, you will no longer excel, for you went up onto your father’s bed, onto my couch and defiled it.

source: Simeon le Levi ucha ahilhonin; hunam galvon ho chu amani chena-a aumin ahi.
target: “Simeon and Levi are brothers— their swords are weapons of violence.

source: Vo kalhagao, nangma amani thuguh-a chun hunglut hih-in; vo kaloupina, amani kiloikhomna-a chun lha hih-in. Ijeh inem itile alunghan nalam lhonin mi athat lhonin, chule a-engset nalam lhonin bongchal ho asatbai lhonin ahi.
target: Let me not enter their council, let me not join their assembly, for they have killed men in their anger and hamstrung oxen as they pleased.

source: Alunghana lhon chu kichat umtah ahijeh le, alungsatna lhon chu phaloutah ahijehchun gaosap hihen. Keiman amani Jacob sunga homkhen ningting, Israel lah-a kathecheh ding ahi.
target: Cursed be their anger, so fierce, and their fury, so cruel! I will scatter them in Jacob and disperse them in Israel.

source: Judah nangma nasopiten avahchoi dingu chu nahi; nakhut chu namelmate ngonga umding; napa chate chu na angsunga kundiu ahi.
target: “Judah, your brothers will praise you; your hand will be on the neck of your enemies; your father’s sons will bow down to you.

source: Judah hi keipi bahkai nou ahi; kachapa nasamat na-a konin nakaltou tan ahi. Ama abohmat depmin, keipi bahkai bangle keipi bahkai teh bangin akolin ahi; koiham asuthou dinga?
target: You are a lion’s cub, Judah; you return from the prey, my son. Like a lion he crouches and lies down, like a lioness—who dares to rouse him?

source: Lal tenggol chu Judah'a konin kichon mang pontin, chule danpe- jong akeng kah-a konin kichon mang ponte, Shiloh ahung masangsen; chule ama henga namtin kikhop khomna umding ahi.
target: The scepter will not depart from Judah, nor the ruler’s staff from between his feet, until he to whom it belongs shall come and the obedience of the nations shall be his.

source: Asangan lengpi guija ahenin, asangan nou chu lengpigui phatah-a ahenin, aman avonho chu lengpitwija asopmin, chule apon chu lengpitwi thisanin asopmin ahi.
target: He will tether his donkey to a vine, his colt to the choicest branch; he will wash his garments in wine, his robes in the blood of grapes.

source: Amit chu lengpitwi sangin asan jon, chule aha chu bongnoi sangin abang jon ahi.
target: His eyes will be darker than wine, his teeth whiter than milk.

source: Zebulun chu twikhanglen kama chengding; chule amachu kongho dinga ngahmun hung hiding; chule agamgi chu Sidon toh kijopmat ding ahi.
target: “Zebulun will live by the seashore and become a haven for ships; his border will extend toward Sidon.

source: Issachar hi sangan hattah, pohgih tah ni kah-a boh ahi.
target: “Issachar is a rawboned donkey lying down among the sheep pens.

source: Chule aman acholngah namun chu aphan, chule gamchu anome, ti amun; hijeh chun aman thilgih pudingin alengkou anemsah-in, hunama natohna mun'a soh ahung hitan ahi.
target: When he sees how good is his resting place and how pleasant is his land, he will bend his shoulder to the burden and submit to forced labor.

source: Dan hin Israel phung ho lah-a khat banga amite chu vai ahom ding ahi.
target: “Dan will provide justice for his people as one of the tribes of Israel.

source: Dan hi lampi pama gul, lampi laija gulse, achunga toupa akinung lelhahna khopma sakol nungkeng chua hiding ahi.
target: Dan will be a snake by the roadside, a viper along the path, that bites the horse’s heels so that its rider tumbles backward.

source: Vo Pakai, nami huhhingna chu kangah jinge.
target: “I look for your deliverance, Lord .

source: Gad hi gal mihon ajoding ahin; ahivangin akhon nale aman ale joding ahi.
target: “Gad will be attacked by a band of raiders, but he will attack them at their heels.

source: Asher'a kona aneh phading ahin, chule aman lengho anneh tuitah tahho aso sah ding ahi.
target: “Asher’s food will be rich; he will provide delicacies fit for a king.

source: Naphtali hi sajuhpi kilhaso ahin; aman thupha tah ho aseijin ahi.
target: “Naphtali is a doe set free that bears beautiful fawns.

source: Joseph hi aga phatah thingbah chu ahin, twikhuh panga aga phatah thingbah ngei chu ahi; abahho chun bang ajamkhup mun ahi.
target: “Joseph is a fruitful vine, a fruitful vine near a spring, whose branches climb over a wall.

source: Thalpi kap ho chun ama nasatah-in asugentheijun, akap uvin, chule ahotbolun ahi.
target: With bitterness archers attacked him; they shot at him with hostility.

source: Ahivangin athalpi chu long louvin athahat jingin, chule akhut banthaho chu imajouse bolthei Jacob Pathen'in ahatsah-in, (Chua kon chun Kelngoi ching, Israel songpi chu hung uma ahi:)
target: But his bow remained steady, his strong arms stayed limber, because of the hand of the Mighty One of Jacob, because of the Shepherd, the Rock of Israel,

source: Nakithopi dinga napa Pathen, chule phatthei naboh ding imajouse bolthei hat chungnung chun, chung van'a kona phattheina ho-a, noilanga thutah-a um phattheina ho, chule ang le naobu phattheina ho-a nahatsah ahi.
target: because of your father’s God, who helps you, because of the Almighty, who blesses you with blessings of the skies above, blessings of the deep springs below, blessings of the breast and womb.

source: Napa phattheina ho hin kapu kapate phatthei naho chu tonsot lhangho khodong geijin akhupjon ahi. Hiho chu Joseph luchunga umding, chule asopite-a kona kikhendohpa lujanga chu umding ahi.
target: Your father’s blessings are greater than the blessings of the ancient mountains, than the bounty of the age-old hills. Let all these rest on the head of Joseph, on the brow of the prince among his brothers.

source: Benjamin ngei banga nehpap ahin: jingkah le asamat chu aneh-a, chule nilhah le athilchom chu ahopkhen ding ahi, ati.
target: “Benjamin is a ravenous wolf; in the morning he devours the prey, in the evening he divides the plunder.”

source: Hicheng jouse hi Israel phung som le phung ni chu ahiuve. Chule hiche hi apauvin amaho phatthei aboh-a, ahenguva aseichu ahin; amatoh kitoh phatthei bohna-a khatcheh-a phatthei aboh ahi.
target: All these are the twelve tribes of Israel, and this is what their father said to them when he blessed them, giving each the blessing appropriate to him.

source: Chuin aman amaho chu athulhah-in ahenguva, Kamite toh puikhoma umding kahitai. Hit mi Ephron louva songkoa chun kapu kapate lah-a neivuijun;
target: Then he gave them these instructions: “I am about to be gathered to my people. Bury me with my fathers in the cave in the field of Ephron the Hittite,

source: Hiche songko chu Canaan gama Mamre koma Machpelah louva um ahin, alou muntoh goma Abraham'in Hit mi Ephron'a kona kivuina mun'a neidinga ana choh ahi.
target: the cave in the field of Machpelah, near Mamre in Canaan, which Abraham bought along with the field as a burial place from Ephron the Hittite.

source: Chukoma chun amahon Abraham le a-inneipi Sarah chu anavuijun, Isaac le a-inneipi Rebekah jong avuijun; chule chua chun keiman Leah kana vuijin ahi.
target: There Abraham and his wife Sarah were buried, there Isaac and his wife Rebekah were buried, and there I buried Leah.

source: Aloumun le asunga um songko chu Heth chate ho-a kona ana kichoa ahi, ati.
target: The field and the cave in it were bought from the Hittites.”

source: Chuin Jacob'in achapate chu athupeh jouvin, akeng jalkhuna asep doh in, alhagao alhan, chule amite toh gopkhomin aumtan ahi.
target: When Jacob had finished giving instructions to his sons, he drew his feet up into the bed, breathed his last and was gathered to his people.

source: Chuin Joseph'in apa mai le amai asuton, akapmin, achopmin ahi.
target: Joseph threw himself on his father and wept over him and kissed him.

source: Chuin Joseph'in apa long chu monthei louva asemna diuvin asohte louthem ho chu thu apen ahi. Chuin louthem ho chun Israel chu Amon theilou dingin asemtaovin ahi.
target: Then Joseph directed the physicians in his service to embalm his father Israel. So the physicians embalmed him,

source: Chuin ama chunga chun nisomli alutnun ahi; ajehchu amon louna dinga kisem miho ding chun ni chujatchu lutji-a ahi. Chuin Egypt mite chun amachu ni somsagi a-opmuvin ahi.
target: taking a full forty days, for that was the time required for embalming. And the Egyptians mourned for him seventy days.

source: Chuin ama a-opnau nikho ho chu akichai phatnin, Joseph Pharaoh insung mite henga chun, Tu-a hi namit muva lungsetna kachana ahile, lungset tah-in Pharaoh henga hitin neisei peh-un;
target: When the days of mourning had passed, Joseph said to Pharaoh’s court, “If I have found favor in your eyes, speak to Pharaoh for me. Tell him,

source: Kapan eikihahsel sah-in, kahenga, Vetan, keima athiding kon kahitan; Canaan gama keiman keimatah dinga kasemsa lhana chu neivuiding ahi, ati. Hijeh chun tun nahenga katao ahi, kapa vuidingin neiche tousah-in, chujouleh hungkit tange, ati, tin neisei peh-un, ati.
target: ‘My father made me swear an oath and said, “I am about to die; bury me in the tomb I dug for myself in the land of Canaan.” Now let me go up and bury my father; then I will return.’ ”

source: Chuin Pharaoh'in, Aman nangma nakihahsel sah bang chun chetouvin lang, napa chu gavuitan, ati.
target: Pharaoh said, “Go up and bury your father, as he made you swear to do.”

source: Chuin Joseph apa vuidingin achetoutan; chule Pharaoh sohte jouse, a-insunga upaho, chule Egypt gamsunga upaho jouse ama toh alhonun,
target: So Joseph went up to bury his father. All Pharaoh’s officials accompanied him—the dignitaries of his court and all the dignitaries of Egypt—

source: Chule Joseph insung mite jouse, asopiteho, chule apa insung miho chu amatoh achetou khomun ahi. Achasen hou, akelngoihon hou, chule abonghon ho bou Goshen gama adalhauvin ahi.
target: besides all the members of Joseph’s household and his brothers and those belonging to his father’s household. Only their children and their flocks and herds were left in Goshen.

source: Chuin amachu sakol kangtalai ho leh sakol chunga tou mihon akilhon piuvin, chule amaho chu tamtah ahiuve.
target: Chariots and horsemen also went up with him. It was a very large company.

source: Chuin amaho Jordan luigala Atad chang chilna pholmun alhung taovin, chule amaho chua chun lhasetah-in akapmun ahi. Chuin aman nisagi sungin apa puldouna abolin ahi.
target: When they reached the threshing floor of Atad, near the Jordan, they lamented loudly and bitterly; and there Joseph observed a seven-day period of mourning for his father.

source: Chuin chuche gama cheng Canaan miho chun Atad chang chilna phola thi-opna chu amuphatnun, Hiche hi Egypt mite dinga lunghemna nasatah ahi, atiuvin; hiche jehchun chuche munchu Abel-mizraim asahtaove; hichu Jordan luigala um ahi.
target: When the Canaanites who lived there saw the mourning at the threshing floor of Atad, they said, “The Egyptians are holding a solemn ceremony of mourning.” That is why that place near the Jordan is called Abel Mizraim.

source: Chuin achapate chun ama thulhah bangtah-in abolpeh taovin ahi.
target: So Jacob’s sons did as he had commanded them:

source: Ajehchu achapaten ama chu Canaan gama apolutnun, Abraham'in kivuina dinga Hit mi Ephron koma aloumun toh achohtha, Mamre koma Machpela louva songkoa chun avuitaovin ahi.
target: They carried him to the land of Canaan and buried him in the cave in the field of Machpelah, near Mamre, which Abraham had bought along with the field as a burial place from Ephron the Hittite.

source: Chuin Joseph'in apa avuijou chun asopite toh, apa vuidinga akilhonpi chengse toh, Egypt gama akilekit taovin ahi.
target: After burying his father, Joseph returned to Egypt, together with his brothers and all the others who had gone with him to bury his father.

source: Chuin Joseph asopite chun apau thichu amuphatnun, Joseph hin ijemtin eivetdao vintin, thil gilouho achunga inabolu chu lethuhding hin ngaito theijinte, akitiuvin ahi.
target: When Joseph’s brothers saw that their father was dead, they said, “What if Joseph holds a grudge against us and pays us back for all the wrongs we did to him?”

source: Chuin amahon Joseph henga thupokhat asolun, hitin aseijuve, Napan athi masangin hiche thulhah hi anadalhan ahi;
target: So they sent word to Joseph, saying, “Your father left these instructions before he died:

source: Hitia hi Joseph henga nasei dingu ahi, Nahenga katao ahi, nasopite suhkhelna le achonsetnao ngaidamin; ajehchu amahon nachunga thilgilou anaboltaove, tin aseije. Chule tun nahenga kataovu ahi, Napa Pathen sohteho suhkhelna chu ngaidamtan, atiuvin ahi. Chuin amahon ahenga hichu aseiphatnun Joseph akaptan ahi.
target: ‘This is what you are to say to Joseph: I ask you to forgive your brothers the sins and the wrongs they committed in treating you so badly.’ Now please forgive the sins of the servants of the God of your father.” When their message came to him, Joseph wept.

source: Chuin asopite jong chu ahungun, a-angsunga abohkhup jengun; ajah-a, Vetan, keiho hi nasohte kahiuve, atiuve.
target: His brothers then came and threw themselves down before him. “We are your slaves,” they said.

source: Chuin Joseph'in ahenguva, Kicha hih-un: ajehchu keima Pathen khela kitung kahi mongem?
target: But Joseph said to them, “Don’t be afraid. Am I in the place of God?

source: Ahin nangho vangin kachunga hi thilgilou bol nagotnu anahin; ahinla hichu Pathen'in tunikho-a bang ngeija hi mitamtah hinkho huhdoh-a aumna dinga apha dinga anagot ahijoi.
target: You intended to harm me, but God intended it for good to accomplish what is now being done, the saving of many lives.

source: Hijeh chun tun, kicha hih-un; keiman nangho le nachasenhou vahnang kate, ati. Chuin aman amaho chu alhamonin, damheochan ahouvin ahi.
target: So then, don’t be afraid. I will provide for you and your children.” And he reassured them and spoke kindly to them.

source: Chuin Joseph chu ama le apa inkote toh Egypt gama chun achengun ahi. Chule Joseph chu kum jakhat le kum som ahingin ahi.
target: Joseph stayed in Egypt, along with all his father’s family. He lived a hundred and ten years

source: Chule Joseph chun Ephraim chate akhang thum lhinna tuson thum chan amu manin ahi. Chule Manasseh chapa Machir chateho jong Joseph pheichunga aseilenun ahi.
target: and saw the third generation of Ephraim’s children. Also the children of Makir son of Manasseh were placed at birth on Joseph’s knees.

source: Chule Joseph'in asopite henga, Kathiding ahitai; ahin Pathen'in nahungvil tei dingu ahin, hiche gama kona hi napui doh uva, Abraham, Isaac chule Jacob henga ana kihahselna gama chu napui tei dingu ahi.
target: Then Joseph said to his brothers, “I am about to die. But God will surely come to your aid and take you up out of this land to the land he promised on oath to Abraham, Isaac and Jacob.”

source: Chuin Joseph'in Israel chate chu akihahsel sah-in, Pathen'in thonlouva nahung vil dingu ahin, chutengle kagu hohi hia konahi napoh tou dingu ahi, ati.
target: And Joseph made the Israelites swear an oath and said, “God will surely come to your aid, and then you must carry my bones up from this place.”

source: Hitichun Joseph chu kum jakhat le kum som alhinin athitan ahi. Chuin amahon along chu amonthei louna din asemun, Egypt gamsunga thikong sunga akoitaove.
target: So Joseph died at the age of a hundred and ten. And after they embalmed him, he was placed in a coffin in Egypt.

source: Tun hichehi Egypt gama hunglutna Israel chateho min chu ahi; amitakip le a-insung miteu Jacob toh ahungun ahi.
target: These are the names of the sons of Israel who went to Egypt with Jacob, each with his family:

source: Reuben, Simeon, Levi, chule Judah,
target: Reuben, Simeon, Levi and Judah;

source: Issachar, Zebulun, chule Benjamin,
target: Issachar, Zebulun and Benjamin;

source: Dan le Naphtali, Gad le Asher,
target: Dan and Naphtali; Gad and Asher.

source: Chule Jacob taiguija kona pengdoh mihing chu aboncha mi somsagi ahiuve. Joseph vang chu Egypt gama ana umsa ahitai.
target: The descendants of Jacob numbered seventy in all; Joseph was already in Egypt.

source: Chuin Joseph le asopite chule chuche khanga miho jouse chu athigam taovin ahi.
target: Now Joseph and all his brothers and all that generation died,

source: Chujouvin Israel chate chu achipha lheh jengun, apungtul tullun, atamlheh jeng taovin, chule hattah ahitaovin; gamsung chu alosoh taovin ahi.
target: but the Israelites were exceedingly fruitful; they multiplied greatly, increased in numbers and became so numerous that the land was filled with them.

source: Tun Egypt gama chun Joseph hephalou lengthah khat ahung lengchang tan ahi.
target: Then a new king, to whom Joseph meant nothing, came to power in Egypt.

source: Chuin aman amite jah-a, Veuvin, Israel chate mipi hi eiho sangin atamjouvin, chule ahatjouvin ahi.
target: “Look,” he said to his people, “the Israelites have become far too numerous for us.

source: Hungun, eihon amaho hi chingthei tah-in bolu hite: achuti louleh amaho pungcheh cheh-untin, hung hitiding ahi, gal kisatna khattou ahung umteng, amaho imelmateu lama hung pangun tin, eiho eisat untin, hitichun gamsunga konin potdoh getnunte, ati.
target: Come, we must deal shrewdly with them or they will become even more numerous and, if war breaks out, will join our enemies, fight against us and leave the country.”

source: Hijeh chun amahon apohgih houva amaho gimbol dingin achunguva tohvai homho apansah taove. Chule amahon Pharaoh dingin gou kholna khopiho Pithom le Rameses asauvin ahi.
target: So they put slave masters over them to oppress them with forced labor, and they built Pithom and Rameses as store cities for Pharaoh.

source: Ahivangin amahon amaho chu abolgim chanun apung cheh-un, akhangcheh cheh-un ahi. Chuin amahon Israel chate jehchun alunggim taovin ahi.
target: But the more they were oppressed, the more they multiplied and spread; so the Egyptians came to dread the Israelites

source: Chule Egypt miten Israel chate chu gimtah-in ana-u atohsah-un ahi.
target: and worked them ruthlessly.

source: Amahon natoh hahsatah ho bon nganin, cheh-in, chule loujaova natoh jat tintangin ahinkhou chu asugenthei lheh jengun: ana-u atohsahna jouseuva genthei tah-in atohsah-un ahi.
target: They made their lives bitter with harsh labor in brick and mortar and with all kinds of work in the fields; in all their harsh labor the Egyptians worked them ruthlessly.

source: Chule Egypt lengpan Hebrew mi naososah teni, khatnu min Shiphrah le khatnu min Pu-ah chu akihoupin;
target: The king of Egypt said to the Hebrew midwives, whose names were Shiphrah and Puah,

source: Ajah lhona, Nangnin Hebrew numei ho nao nasosah lhonteng, naososahna touna chunga chun amaho chu velhonin; iti hama hichu pasal ahile natha lhonding ahi: ahin numei ahivangle hinghoi lhonin, ati.
target: “When you are helping the Hebrew women during childbirth on the delivery stool, if you see that the baby is a boy, kill him; but if it is a girl, let her live.”

source: Ahivangin naososah teni chun Pathen aging lhonin, Egypt Lengpa thupeh bangchun abol lhonpon, ahin naosen pasal ho chu ahinghoiji lhonin ahi.
target: The midwives, however, feared God and did not do what the king of Egypt had told them to do; they let the boys live.

source: Chuphatnin Egypt lengpan naososah teni chu akouvin, ajah lhona, Ipi dinga hicheho hi nabol lhona, naosen pasal ho chu nahing hoi lhon ham? ati.
target: Then the king of Egypt summoned the midwives and asked them, “Why have you done this? Why have you let the boys live?”

source: Chuin nao sosah teni chun Pharaoh jah-a, Hebrew numei hohi Egypt numei ho tobang ahilou jeh-u ahi; ajehchu amaho adamtheijun, nao sosah ho ahengu alhun masangle anasoh lhaji taovin ahi, atilhone.
target: The midwives answered Pharaoh, “Hebrew women are not like Egyptian women; they are vigorous and give birth before the midwives arrive.”

source: Chutichun Pathen'in nao sosah teni chung chun aphalam tah-in na atongin ahi: chuin miho chu apung tul tul jengun, nasatah-in ahatdoh taovin ahi.
target: So God was kind to the midwives and the people increased and became even more numerous.

source: Chuin ahitin ahi, nao sosah teni chun Pathen aginjeh lhonin, a-insungmi lhonding apen ahi.
target: And because the midwives feared God, he gave them families of their own.

source: Chuin Pharaoh'in amite chu athupeh-in, Pasal chapang pengtapou chu vadunga seplutnun, numei chapang tapou chu hing hoijun, atitai.
target: Then Pharaoh gave this order to all his people: “Every Hebrew boy that is born you must throw into the Nile, but let every girl live.”

source: Chuin Levi phunga peng pasal khat achen Levi chanu khat ji dingin akipuitan ahi.
target: Now a man of the tribe of Levi married a Levite woman,

source: Chuin amanu chun nao avopmin, chapa khat ahingtai. Amanun ama chu naosen hoitah ahichu amu phatnin, lhathum aselin ahi.
target: and she became pregnant and gave birth to a son. When she saw that he was a fine child, she hid him for three months.

source: Amanun ama chu aselbe joulou phatnin, pumpenga kisa sinkhup khat alan, thingnai man le vahaibonin aloibitnin, asunga chun naosen chu akhumin; vadung kama peng lah-a chun agakoitai.
target: But when she could hide him no longer, she got a papyrus basket for him and coated it with tar and pitch. Then she placed the child in it and put it among the reeds along the bank of the Nile.

source: Chule achunga ipi ahung sohdem ti ve dingin asopinu chu gamlatah-a adingin ahi.
target: His sister stood at a distance to see what would happen to him.

source: Chuin Pharaoh chanu chu kisil dingin vadunga chun ahung suh-in; chule asoh numei ho chu lui panga chun avah leovin ahi: chuin amanun peng lah-a sinkhup chu amuphatnin, hichu galadin asohnu chu asolin ahi.
target: Then Pharaoh’s daughter went down to the Nile to bathe, and her attendants were walking along the riverbank. She saw the basket among the reeds and sent her female slave to get it.

source: Chuin amanun hichu ahon phatnin naosen chu amutai: chule, veuvin, naosen chu ahung kapmin ahi. Chuin amanun amapa chu alung asen, Hichehi Hebrew chate lah-a khat ahi, ati.
target: She opened it and saw the baby. He was crying, and she felt sorry for him. “This is one of the Hebrew babies,” she said.

source: Chujouvin a-unu chun Pharaoh chanu jah-a chun, Keima kache-a hiche naosen hi nadonpeh dinga Hebrew naodon numei kaga koupeh ding ham? ati.
target: Then his sister asked Pharaoh’s daughter, “Shall I go and get one of the Hebrew women to nurse the baby for you?”

source: Chuin Pharaoh chanun amanu jah-a, Chen, ati. Chuin nungahnu chu achen, naosen nuchu agakoupeh tan ahi.
target: “Yes, go,” she answered. So the girl went and got the baby’s mother.

source: Chuin Pharaoh chanu chun amanu henga, Hiche naocha hi kipuijin lang keima dingin neihin vah peh-in, chule keiman natohman kapeh ding nahi ati. Chuin numei chun chapang chu akipuijin, avahtan ahi.
target: Pharaoh’s daughter said to her, “Take this baby and nurse him for me, and I will pay you.” So the woman took the baby and nursed him.

source: Chuin chapang chu ahung khandoh phatnin, naodonnu chun Pharaoh chanu henga ahinpuijin, ama amanu chapa ahitan; chule amanun amin Mosi asah tai: Ajehchu keiman twilah-a kona kalahdoh ahi, ati.
target: When the child grew older, she took him to Pharaoh’s daughter and he became her son. She named him Moses, saying, “I drew him out of the water.”

source: Chuin hiche laichun ahitin ahi, Mosi akikhanlhit phatnin, asopite henga agachen, apohgih-u chu agaven ahile, Egypt mikhatnin asopi Hebrew mi khat aden chu amulhi tan ahi.
target: One day, after Moses had grown up, he went out to where his own people were and watched them at their hard labor. He saw an Egyptian beating a Hebrew, one of his own people.

source: Chuin aman akimvel dung avelen, koimacha amulou phatnin Egypt mipa chu athatnin, neldi lah-a aselin ahi.
target: Looking this way and that and seeing no one, he killed the Egyptian and hid him in the sand.

source: Chule ani ni channia apotdohkit phatnin, veuvin, Hebrew mi ni akidel lhonin: aman athemo jopa henga, Ipidinga nasopi naden ham? ati.
target: The next day he went out and saw two Hebrews fighting. He asked the one in the wrong, “Why are you hitting your fellow Hebrew?”

source: Chuin amapan, Keiho chunga pipui le thutan dinga kon natunham? Egypt mipa natha banga chu keijong thading neigot ham? ati. Chuin Mosi akichatan, Tahbeh-a hiche thilhi kihedoh-a ahitai, ati.
target: The man said, “Who made you ruler and judge over us? Are you thinking of killing me as you killed the Egyptian?” Then Moses was afraid and thought, “What I did must have become known.”

source: Tun Pharaoh'in hichehi ajah phatnin, Mosi chu thadingin aholtan ahi. Ahin Mosi Pharaoh maikoh-a konin ajam mangin, Midian gama achengin: chule ama twikul panga atouvin ahi.
target: When Pharaoh heard of this, he tried to kill Moses, but Moses fled from Pharaoh and went to live in Midian, where he sat down by a well.

source: Tun Midian thempupa chun chanu sagi aneijin ahi. Chuin maho chu twi thalin ahungun, apa kelngoihon chip dingin kongho chu athal dimun ahi.
target: Now a priest of Midian had seven daughters, and they came to draw water and fill the troughs to water their father’s flock.

source: Chuin kelngoi chingho chu ahungun amaho chu anodoh-un ahi: ahivangin Mosi adingdoh-in amaho chu akithopin, akelngoi honu chu twi achipsah-in ahi.
target: Some shepherds came along and drove them away, but Moses got up and came to their rescue and watered their flock.

source: Chuin amaho apau Reuel henga ahung phatnun, aman ahenguva, Iti dana tunia nahiti hungvah uham? ati.
target: When the girls returned to Reuel their father, he asked them, “Why have you returned so early today?”

source: Chuin amahon, Egypt mikhatnin kelngoi chingho khutna konin eihuhdoh-un, chule keiho dingin lhingsetnin twi jong eithal peh-un, kelngoihon jong twi achipsah-in ahi, atiuve.
target: They answered, “An Egyptian rescued us from the shepherds. He even drew water for us and watered the flock.”

source: Chuin aman achanute jah-a, Ama chu hoija umtam? ipidinga mipa chu nahin dalhah-u ham? an nedingin gakouvun, ati.
target: “And where is he?” Reuel asked his daughters. “Why did you leave him? Invite him to have something to eat.”

source: Chuin Mosi chuche pa toh chending chu anomtan: chule aman achanu Zipporah chu Mosi apetan ahi.
target: Moses agreed to stay with the man, who gave his daughter Zipporah to Moses in marriage.

source: Chuin amanun chapa khat ahinpeh-in, amin Gershom asahtai: ajehchu aman, Keima mi gama khopema kahi, ati.
target: Zipporah gave birth to a son, and Moses named him Gershom, saying, “I have become a foreigner in a foreign land.”

source: Chuin phat chomkhat jouvin ahitin ahi, Egypt lengpa chu athitan ahi. Chuin Israel chate chu asohchan jeh-un akhoisauvin, akapmun, chule asohchan jeh uva akanao chu Pathen kom alhungtan ahi.
target: During that long period, the king of Egypt died. The Israelites groaned in their slavery and cried out, and their cry for help because of their slavery went up to God.

source: Chuin Pathen'in akhoisat nao chu ajahpeh tan, Abraham, Isaac, chule Jacob toh akitepna chu ageldoh tan ahi.
target: God heard their groaning and he remembered his covenant with Abraham, with Isaac and with Jacob.

source: Chuin Pathen'in Israel chate chu ahinven, amaho chu akhohsah tan ahi.
target: So God looked on the Israelites and was concerned about them.

source: Tun Mosi'n Midian thempu anupa pa Jethro kelngoihon achingin ahi. Chuin kelngoihon chu neldi gam nunglam panga chun apuijin, Pathen molsang Horeb ahunglhung tan ahi.
target: Now Moses was tending the flock of Jethro his father-in-law, the priest of Midian, and he led the flock to the far side of the wilderness and came to Horeb, the mountain of God.

source: Chuin Pakai Vantil chu hamboh lah-a konin meikongin ahung kilah-in ahi. Chuin aman aven ahile, veuvin, hamboh chu meikongin akouvin, ahinla hamboh chu akavampon ahi.
target: There the angel of the Lord appeared to him in flames of fire from within a bush. Moses saw that though the bush was on fire it did not burn up.

source: Chuin Mosi'n, Tun keima kiheijing ting, i-atile hamboh khu kalouham, hiche melchihna nasatah hi gavenge, atin ahi.
target: So Moses thought, “I will go over and see this strange sight—why the bush does not burn up.”

source: Chuin avedinga akihei chu Pakaiyin amu phatnin, hamboh lah-a konchun Pathen'in ahin kouvin, Mosi, Mosi, ati. Chuin aman, Hikoma kaume, ati.
target: When the Lord saw that he had gone over to look, God called to him from within the bush, “Moses! Moses!” And Moses said, “Here I am.”

source: Chuin aman, Hilam hin nai hih-in: nakenga konin nakeng chot sutlhan, ajehchu nadinna chu muntheng ahi, ati.
target: “Do not come any closer,” God said. “Take off your sandals, for the place where you are standing is holy ground.”

source: Chukalvallin aman, Keima napu napate Pathen, Abraham Pathen, Isaac Pathen, Jacob Pathen kahi, ati. Chuin Mosi'n amai aseltai: ajehchu aman Pathen avet ngamlou ahi.
target: Then he said, “I am the God of your father, the God of Abraham, the God of Isaac and the God of Jacob.” At this, Moses hid his face, because he was afraid to look at God.

source: Chuin Pakaiyin, Keiman Egypt gama kamite kisuh genthei kichen tah-in kamutan, chule tohvai homho jala akanao kajatai; ajehchu keiman agenthei nao kahetai.
target: The Lord said, “I have indeed seen the misery of my people in Egypt. I have heard them crying out because of their slave drivers, and I am concerned about their suffering.

source: Chule Egypt miho khutna kona huhdoh dingle amaho chuche gama kona chu puidoh-a, gamphatah le gamlentah khoiju le bongnoi lonna gam, Canaan mite, Hit mite, Amor mite, Perizz mite, Hiv mite, chule Jebus mite gama puitou dinga hung kumlha kahi.
target: So I have come down to rescue them from the hand of the Egyptians and to bring them up out of that land into a good and spacious land, a land flowing with milk and honey—the home of the Canaanites, Hittites, Amorites, Perizzites, Hivites and Jebusites.

source: Hijeh chun tun, ven, Israel chate kana chu kakom ahung lhung tai: chule Egypt miten amaho abolgenthei nao jong kamudoh tai.
target: And now the cry of the Israelites has reached me, and I have seen the way the Egyptians are oppressing them.

source: Hijeh chun tun hungin, kami Israel chate Egypt gama kona napuidoh theina dingin Pharaoh henga nasol ing kate, ati.
target: So now, go. I am sending you to Pharaoh to bring my people the Israelites out of Egypt.”

source: Chuin Mosi'n Pathen henga, Keima koi kahia, Pharaoh henga kache-a, Egypt gama kona Israel chate chu kagapui doh ding ham? ati.
target: But Moses said to God, “Who am I that I should go to Pharaoh and bring the Israelites out of Egypt?”

source: Chuin aman, Tahbeh-a keiman nangma kaumpi ding nahi; chule hichehi keiman kasol nahi amelchihna hiding ahi: nangman miho chu Egypt ma kona nahin puidoh teng, hiche molsanga hi Pathen najen dingu ahi, ati.
target: And God said, “I will be with you. And this will be the sign to you that it is I who have sent you: When you have brought the people out of Egypt, you will worship God on this mountain.”

source: Chuin Mosi'n Pathen henga, Vetan, keima Israel chate heng kagalhuna, amaho jah-a, Napu napateu Pathen'in naheng uva eihinsol ahi, kati tengle; amahon, Amin ipiham? tia ahinsei tei dingu ahin, ahenguva ipi kasei ding ham? ati.
target: Moses said to God, “Suppose I go to the Israelites and say to them, ‘The God of your fathers has sent me to you,’ and they ask me, ‘What is his name?’ Then what shall I tell them?”

source: Chuin Pathen'in Mosi henga, KEIMA CHU KEIMA KAHI: chule Israel chate jah-a chu KEIMA kitipan nangho henga eihinsol ahi tia nasei ding ahi, ati.
target: God said to Moses, “ I am who I am . This is what you are to say to the Israelites: ‘ I am has sent me to you.’ ”

source: Chukal valin Pathen'in Mosi jah-a, Israel chate henga chun, Napu napateu Pakai Pathen, Abraham Pathen, Isaac Pathen, chule Jacob Pathen'in naheng uva eihinsol ahi: hichehi tonsotna kamin, chule nakhang khanguva neihet jingna dingu ahi tin seipeh-in.
target: God also said to Moses, “Say to the Israelites, ‘The Lord , the God of your fathers—the God of Abraham, the God of Isaac and the God of Jacob—has sent me to you.’ “This is my name forever, the name you shall call me from generation to generation.

source: Chen, Israel upaho chu gakhom khomin lang, ahenguva, Napu napateu Pakai Pathen, Abraham Pathen, Isaac Pathen, chule Jacob Pathen chu kahenga ahung kilah-in, kajah-a, Keiman nangho tahbeh-in kahung vilun, chule Egypt gama nachung uva kibol chu kamutan:
target: “Go, assemble the elders of Israel and say to them, ‘The Lord , the God of your fathers—the God of Abraham, Isaac and Jacob—appeared to me and said: I have watched over you and have seen what has been done to you in Egypt.

source: Chuin keiman, Nangho Egypt suhgentheina-a kona kapuidoh uva, Canaan mite, Hit mite, Amor mite, Perizz mite, Hiv mite, chule Jebus mite gam, bongnoi le khoiju lonna gama chu kapuilut dingu nahiuve, tin kaseije, gatin.
target: And I have promised to bring you up out of your misery in Egypt into the land of the Canaanites, Hittites, Amorites, Perizzites, Hivites and Jebusites—a land flowing with milk and honey.’

source: Chutengle amahon nathusei angai dingu ahi. Chutengle nangma le Israel upa ho Egypt lengpa koma nahung diu, ajah-a, Hebrew mite Pakai Pathen'in keiho eikimu piuvin ahi: tun Pakai ka Pathen'u henga ganlhaina kaganei nadingun, gamthipma nithum lampi neiche sah-un tia nahenga kataovu ahi, tia nasei dingu ahi.
target: “The elders of Israel will listen to you. Then you and the elders are to go to the king of Egypt and say to him, ‘The Lord , the God of the Hebrews, has met with us. Let us take a three-day journey into the wilderness to offer sacrifices to the Lord our God.’

source: Ahin Egypt lengpa chun khut thahat tah tilouva nasoldoh louheldiu ahi ti kichen tah-in kahei.
target: But I know that the king of Egypt will not let you go unless a mighty hand compels him.

source: Chule keiman kakhut kahin lhandoh ding, alah uva kabolding thil kidanga chu Egypt kajepding: chujouteng aman nangho nasoldoh dingu ahi.
target: So I will stretch out my hand and strike the Egyptians with all the wonders that I will perform among them. After that, he will let you go.

source: Chule keiman Egypt mite mitmu-a hiche mitehi khotona kapeh ding, chule hung hiti ding ahi, nangho nache tengule agoh-a nache lou dingu ahi.
target: “And I will make the Egyptians favorably disposed toward this people, so that when you leave you will not go empty-handed.

source: Ahin numei takipmin a-inheng le a-in'a pemho henga dangka le sana-a kijepna ho, ponsil nihchen ho apa-a alah dingu: hicheho chu nachapa teo le nachanu teo najepnadiu; hitia chu nanghon Egypt mite chu nachom dingu ahi, ati.
target: Every woman is to ask her neighbor and any woman living in her house for articles of silver and gold and for clothing, which you will put on your sons and daughters. And so you will plunder the Egyptians.”

source: Chuin Mosi'n adonbutnin ajah-a, Hijongle ven, amahon eitahsan lou dingu, kathujong angailou dingu ahi: ajehchu amahon, Nahenga Pakai akilahpoi ati dingu ahi, ati.
target: Moses answered, “What if they do not believe me or listen to me and say, ‘The Lord did not appear to you’?”

source: Chuin Pakaiyin ahenga, Nakhutna umchu ipiham? ati. Chuin aman, Tenggol ahi, ati.
target: Then the Lord said to him, “What is that in your hand?” “A staff,” he replied.

source: Chuin aman, Tolla seplhan ati. Chuin aman hichu tolla aseplhan ahile gul asohtan; chuin Mosi chuche masanga konchun ajamtan ahi.
target: The Lord said, “Throw it on the ground.” Moses threw it on the ground and it became a snake, and he ran from it.

source: Chuin Pakaiyin Mosi jah-a, Nakhut lhangin lang hichu ameijin manin; (Chuin aman akhut alhangin, amanin ahile, akhutna tenggol asoh kit tai:)
target: Then the Lord said to him, “Reach out your hand and take it by the tail.” So Moses reached out and took hold of the snake and it turned back into a staff in his hand.

source: Amahon apu apateu Pakai Pathen, Abraham Pathen, Isaac Pathen, chule Jacob Pathen chu nahenga ahung kilahnai ti atahsan theina dingun, ati.
target: “This,” said the Lord , “is so that they may believe that the Lord , the God of their fathers—the God of Abraham, the God of Isaac and the God of Jacob—has appeared to you.”

source: Chuin Pakaiyin ahenga asei kitnin, Tun nakhut chu na-opma koijin, atin ahi. Chuin aman akhut a-opma akoitan ahi: chuin hichu alahdoh phatnin, veuvin, akhutchu aphah-in buhbang bangin abangtan ahi.
target: Then the Lord said, “Put your hand inside your cloak.” So Moses put his hand into his cloak, and when he took it out, the skin was leprous—it had become as white as snow.

source: Hichun aman, Nakhut chu na-opma koikitnin, ati. Aman akhut chu a-opma akoikitnin ahile, a-opma akhut chu atidang bang bang ahi kit tai.
target: “Now put it back into your cloak,” he said. So Moses put his hand back into his cloak, and when he took it out, it was restored, like the rest of his flesh.

source: Chule hung hiti ding ahi, amahon nangma natahsan lou uva, chule melchihna masajong chu angai louvule, amahon melchihna nunung joh chu atahsan dingu ahi.
target: Then the Lord said, “If they do not believe you or pay attention to the first sign, they may believe the second.

source: Chule hung hiti ding ahi, Amahon hiche melchihna ni teni jonghi atahsan lou uva, chule na thusei jong angai lou uva ahileh, nangman vadung twi nalah-a, tolgo chunga nasunlhah ding ahi. Chule nangman vadunga kona nalahdoh twi chu tolgo chunga chu thisan hungsoh ding ahi, ati.
target: But if they do not believe these two signs or listen to you, take some water from the Nile and pour it on the dry ground. The water you take from the river will become blood on the ground.”

source: Chuin Mosi'n Pakai henga, Vo ka Pakai, keima tumasangin jong, chule nangman nasoh henga thu nahinseija patnin jong mi kamnal kahipoi: ahin keima thusei ngongkai le lei kipehlou kahi, ati.
target: Moses said to the Lord , “Pardon your servant, Lord. I have never been eloquent, neither in the past nor since you have spoken to your servant. I am slow of speech and tongue.”

source: Chuin Pakaiyin ama henga, Mihem kam sema koiham? Ahiloule paomo le na-ngong, chule kho muthei le mitcho sema chu koiham? Pakai keima kahi hilouham?
target: The Lord said to him, “Who gave human beings their mouths? Who makes them deaf or mute? Who gives them sight or makes them blind? Is it not I, the Lord ?

source: Hijeh chun tun chen, keiman nakam kaumpi jinga, nasei ding kahil ding ahi ati.
target: Now go; I will help you speak and will teach you what to say.”

source: Chuin aman, Vo ka Pakai, nahenga katao ahi, nangman nasolnom dang khat solmaijin ati.
target: But Moses said, “Pardon your servant, Lord. Please send someone else.”

source: Chuin Pakai lunghanna chu Mosi chunga akoujahtan, ahenga, Levi mi nasopipa Aaron uma hilouham? aman thu phatah-in aseitheije ti kahei. Chujongle ven, ama nangma kimupi din ahungdoh-e: aman nangma namuteng alungsung kipahding ahi.
target: Then the Lord ’s anger burned against Moses and he said, “What about your brother, Aaron the Levite? I know he can speak well. He is already on his way to meet you, and he will be glad to see you.

source: Chule nangman ama henga thu nasei ding, akamsunga thuho nakoipeh ding ahi: chule keiman nangma kam le ama kam kaumpi ding, chule nabol lhonding kahil ding ahi.
target: You shall speak to him and put words in his mouth; I will help both of you speak and will teach you what to do.

source: Chule amachu nangma dinga mipi ho henga thuseija pangding: ama chu nangma dinga nakam khela panga, chule nangma ama dinga Pathen khela napan ding ahi.
target: He will speak to the people for you, and it will be as if he were your mouth and as if you were God to him.

source: Chule nangman hiche tenggol hi nakhutna nakichoi ding, hichea hi melchihna ho nabolding ahi, ati.
target: But take this staff in your hand so you can perform the signs with it.”

source: Chuin Mosi anupa pa Jethro henga ahung kilen, ajah-a, Nahenga katao ahi, Egypt gama kasopite henga kinungle kit dingin neisolin, hingnalai naovem gavenge, ati. Chuin Jethro'n Mosi jah-a, Lung mongin chetan, ati.
target: Then Moses went back to Jethro his father-in-law and said to him, “Let me return to my own people in Egypt to see if any of them are still alive.” Jethro said, “Go, and I wish you well.”

source: Chuin Pakaiyin Midian gama Mosi henga, Chen, Egypt gama kilekit tan, ajehchu nangma thadinga nahol ho jouse chu athigam taove, ati.
target: Now the Lord had said to Moses in Midian, “Go back to Egypt, for all those who wanted to kill you are dead.”

source: Chuin Mosi'n a-inneipi le achapate chu apuijin, sangan chunga atousah-in, Egypt gama akiletan ahi. Chule Mosi'n Pathen tenggol chu akhutna akichoijin ahi.
target: So Moses took his wife and sons, put them on a donkey and started back to Egypt. And he took the staff of God in his hand.

source: Chuin Pakaiyin Mosi jah-a, Ven, Egypt gama nakile teng nakhutna kakoi thil kidang ho jouse chu Pharaoh angsunga nabol ding ahi: hijongle aman miho chu asoldoh louna dinga Pharaoh lung chu katahsah ding ahi.
target: The Lord said to Moses, “When you return to Egypt, see that you perform before Pharaoh all the wonders I have given you the power to do. But I will harden his heart so that he will not let the people go.

source: Chule nangman Pharaoh jah-a, Pakaiyin hitihin aseije, Israel chu kachapa, apeng masapen ahi.
target: Then say to Pharaoh, ‘This is what the Lord says: Israel is my firstborn son,

source: Chule keiman najah-a kasei ahi, Aman keima eijen theina dingin kachapa chu soldoh tan: chule nangman ama soldoh ding nanop louva ahile, ven, keiman nachapa katha ding, apeng masapentah chu kathading ahi, tia nasei ding ahi, ati.
target: and I told you, “Let my son go, so he may worship me.” But you refused to let him go; so I will kill your firstborn son.’ ”

source: Chule lampia jinlhun in'a chun ahitin ahi, Pakaiyin ama chu akimupin, thadin aholtan ahi.
target: At a lodging place on the way, the Lord met Moses and was about to kill him.

source: Hichun Zipporah'in meituh songhem khat alan, achapa chep atanpeh-in, hichu akengbula aseplhan, Tahbeh-in nangma hi keima dinga thisanso inneipu nahi, ati.
target: But Zipporah took a flint knife, cut off her son’s foreskin and touched Moses’ feet with it. “Surely you are a bridegroom of blood to me,” she said.

source: Hitichun amachu alhadoh tan ahi. Chuin amanun, Cheptan jeh-a chu nangma keima dinga thisanso inneipu nahi ahi, ati.
target: So the Lord let him alone. (At that time she said “bridegroom of blood,” referring to circumcision.)

source: Chuin Pakaiyin Aaron henga, Gamthipma Mosi kimupi din chen, ati. Chuin ama achen, Pathen molsanga chun ama akimupin, achopmin ahi.
target: The Lord said to Aaron, “Go into the wilderness to meet Moses.” So he met Moses at the mountain of God and kissed him.

source: Chuin Mosi'n Aaron henga chun asolpa Pakai thusei jouse le athupeh melchihna jouse chu aseipehtan ahi.
target: Then Moses told Aaron everything the Lord had sent him to say, and also about all the signs he had commanded him to perform.

source: Chuin Mosi le Aaron achelhonin, Israel upaho jouse akhom khom lhontai.
target: Moses and Aaron brought together all the elders of the Israelites,

source: Chuin Aaron'in Pakaiyin Mosi henga asei thu jouse chu aseijin, miho mitmun melchihna ho chu aboltan ahi:
target: and Aaron told them everything the Lord had said to Moses. He also performed the signs before the people,

source: Chuin mipi chun atahsan taove. Chuin Pakaiyin Israel chate avila, athohgimnao ahinvet pehchu ajah phatnun, amaho akunun Pathen ahou taovin ahi.
target: and they believed. And when they heard that the Lord was concerned about them and had seen their misery, they bowed down and worshiped.

source: Chuche jouchun Mosi le Aaron alut lhonin, Pharaoh henga, Israel Pakai Pathen'in hitin aseije, gamthipma keima dinga Kut aboltheina diuvin kamite solin ati, tin asei lhonin ahi.
target: Afterward Moses and Aaron went to Pharaoh and said, “This is what the Lord , the God of Israel, says: ‘Let my people go, so that they may hold a festival to me in the wilderness.’ ”

source: Ahinla Pharaoh'in, Pakai chu koi hija, keiman athu kangaija Israelte kasoldoh ding ham? Keiman Pakai chu kahepon, Israelte jong kasoldoh louding ahi, ati.
target: Pharaoh said, “Who is the Lord , that I should obey him and let Israel go? I do not know the Lord and I will not let Israel go.”

source: Hichun amanin, Hebrew mite Pathen'in eikimupi lhon ahi. Nahenga kataolhon ahi, Pakai ka Pathen'u henga ganlhaina gabol dingin nithum lampia neisolun: achutiloule aman ichunguva gamna hise ahiloule chemjam achuhsah ding ahi, atilhone.
target: Then they said, “The God of the Hebrews has met with us. Now let us take a three-day journey into the wilderness to offer sacrifices to the Lord our God, or he may strike us with plagues or with the sword.”

source: Chuin Egypt lengpan amani henga, Nangni Mosi le Aaron'in ipidinga mipi hohi anatoh-u nangahsah lhonham? napohgih hou gakipoh thim thimun, ati.
target: But the king of Egypt said, “Moses and Aaron, why are you taking the people away from their labor? Get back to your work!”

source: Chuin Pharaoh'in, Veuvin, hiche gam mihohi tun tamtah ahiuvin, nangnin amaho chu apohgih houva konin nakicholdo sah lhontan ahi, ati.
target: Then Pharaoh said, “Look, the people of the land are now numerous, and you are stopping them from working.”

source: Chuin chuche nile le chun Pharaoh'in tohvai poho le alamkai ho athupeh-in, ajah uva,
target: That same day Pharaoh gave this order to the slave drivers and overseers in charge of the people:

source: Nanghon masanga banga chu miho chu cheh aden nadingu changpol napehkit lou dingu ahitai: amaho cheohen lang amaho ding cheh pol gakihol khomu hen.
target: “You are no longer to supply the people with straw for making bricks; let them go and gather their own straw.

source: Chule tumasanga acheh denjiu jatjat chu nadensah jing dingu: hichea kona chu nalhomsah loudiu ahi: ajehchu amaho thaseuva ahi; hijeh-a, Ka-Pathen'u henga ganlhaina gabol dingin neisolun tia pengu ahi.
target: But require them to make the same number of bricks as before; don’t reduce the quota. They are lazy; that is why they are crying out, ‘Let us go and sacrifice to our God.’

source: Hahsa tah-a atoh diuvin chuche miho chunga chun natoh hahsacheh koibe peh-un; amahon thumanlou ngaisah daohen, ati.
target: Make the work harder for the people so that they keep working and pay no attention to lies.”

source: Chuin mipi tohvai poho le toh lamkai chu achedoh-un, mipi ho henga chun, Pharaoh'in hitihin aseije, Keiman nangho changpol kapehlou dingu ahitai.
target: Then the slave drivers and the overseers went out and said to the people, “This is what Pharaoh says: ‘I will not give you any more straw.

source: Nangho cheovin lang namu nathei theijuva pol gakiholun; hijongle nanatoh-u chu kilhomsah deh louding ahi, agatiuve.
target: Go and get your own straw wherever you can find it, but your work will not be reduced at all.’ ”

source: Chutichun mipi chu changpol khela manding changkung gakhom khom dingin Egypt gam pumpi-a akithecheh taovin ahi.
target: So the people scattered all over Egypt to gather stubble to use for straw.

source: Chuin tohlamkai ho chun amaho chu anouvin, nanitin natoh houchu changpol aumlai bang chun tong bukimun, atiuve.
target: The slave drivers kept pressing them, saying, “Complete the work required of you for each day, just as when you had straw.”

source: Chuin Pharaoh toh lamkaiho chun mipi ho chunga apansah Israel chate lamkaiho chu avouvin, Ipi dinga nacheh dennu natoh chu masanga banga janhi le tunia nabol bulhit lou uham? tin aphohsal taovin ahi.
target: And Pharaoh’s slave drivers beat the Israelite overseers they had appointed, demanding, “Why haven’t you met your quota of bricks yesterday or today, as before?”

source: Hichun Israel chate lamkaiho chu ahungun Pharaoh henga agakapmun, Ibola nangman nasohte hi neihiti bolu hitam?
target: Then the Israelite overseers went and appealed to Pharaoh: “Why have you treated your servants this way?

source: Nasohte hi changpol la eikipe pouvin, chule amahon kahenguva, Cheh denguvin eitiuvin ahi. Chule ven, nasohte hi eivouvin, ahivangin athemmo chu namite ahiuve, atiuvin ahi.
target: Your servants are given no straw, yet we are told, ‘Make bricks!’ Your servants are being beaten, but the fault is with your own people.”

source: Ahivangin aman, Nangho thase nahiuve, nangho thase nahiuve: hijeh-a chu nanghon, Cheohitin Pakai henga ganlhaina gabolu hite natiu ahi.
target: Pharaoh said, “Lazy, that’s what you are—lazy! That is why you keep saying, ‘Let us go and sacrifice to the Lord .’

source: Hijeh chun tun cheovin lang na gatongun: ajehchu nangho changpol kipelou ding nahiuve, hijongle nacheh dendiu jat chu nabulhit dingu ahi, ati.
target: Now get to work. You will not be given any straw, yet you must produce your full quota of bricks.”

source: Nanghon niseh-a nanatoh naova na cheh dendiujat chu nalhomsah loudiu ahi tia akiseipeh phatnu chun, Israel chate lamkaihon achunguva thilphalou chua ahitai ti amudoh taovin ahi.
target: The Israelite overseers realized they were in trouble when they were told, “You are not to reduce the number of bricks required of you for each day.”

source: Chuin amaho Pharaoh koma kona ahungpot doh-u toh kilhonin, lampia anading Mosi le Aaron chu akimutopi taovin ahi.
target: When they left Pharaoh, they found Moses and Aaron waiting to meet them,

source: Chuin amahon amani henga, Pakaiyin nave lhonhen lang nachung thu lhon tanhen; ajehchu nangnin keiho thana dinga akhutnuva chemjam koina dingin Pharaoh mitmu le asohte mitmun thet umtah in neisem taovin ahi, atiuve.
target: and they said, “May the Lord look on you and judge you! You have made us obnoxious to Pharaoh and his officials and have put a sword in their hand to kill us.”

source: Chuin Mosi Pakai henga akinungle kitnin, Pakai, ipi dinga hiche mite chungahi phalou tah-a na natoh ham? Ipi dinga neisol ham?
target: Moses returned to the Lord and said, “Why, Lord, why have you brought trouble on this people? Is this why you sent me?

source: Ajehchu Pharaoh henga namina thusei dinga kahunga pat hin, aman hiche mite chunga thilse abol jingin; chule nangman jong namite nahuhdoh hihhelin ahi, ati.
target: Ever since I went to Pharaoh to speak in your name, he has brought trouble on this people, and you have not rescued your people at all.”

source: Chujouvin Pakaiyin Mosi henga, Keiman Pharaoh chunga ipi kabol ding tu-a hi nangman namu ding ahi. Ajehchu khut thahat hin amaho chu asol ding, chule khut thahat hin amaho chu agamsunga kona adeldoh tho sah ding ahi, ati.
target: Then the Lord said to Moses, “Now you will see what I will do to Pharaoh: Because of my mighty hand he will let them go; because of my mighty hand he will drive them out of his country.”

source: Chuin Pathen'in Mosi henga thu aseijin, ajah-a hitin aseije, keima Pakai chu kahi.
target: God also said to Moses, “I am the Lord .

source: Chule keima Abraham, Isaac, chule Jacob hengah Pathen hat chungnung minin kana kilah-in; ahinla amahon kamin JEHOVAH hin eina hepouvin ahi.
target: I appeared to Abraham, to Isaac and to Jacob as God Almighty, but by my name the Lord I did not make myself fully known to them.

source: Chule gamdangmi ahinao akholjina gamu Canaan gam chu amaho pehdingin keiman amahotoh kakitepna kaphut doh-in ahi.
target: I also established my covenant with them to give them the land of Canaan, where they resided as foreigners.

source: Chule Egypt miten sohchanga ahennaova Israel chate akhoisatnao jong chu kajan; chule kakitepna chu kageldoh tan ahi.
target: Moreover, I have heard the groaning of the Israelites, whom the Egyptians are enslaving, and I have remembered my covenant.

source: Hijeh chun Israel chate henga hitin seijin, Keima Pakai kahin, chule Egypt mite pohgih ho noija kona kapui diu, apohgih houva kona kalhadoh uva, chule keiman ban jahdoh le thutanna nasatah puma kahuhdoh ding nahiuve.
target: “Therefore, say to the Israelites: ‘I am the Lord , and I will bring you out from under the yoke of the Egyptians. I will free you from being slaves to them, and I will redeem you with an outstretched arm and with mighty acts of judgment.

source: Chule nangho kamite hidinga kalah uva, chule keima na-Pathen'u kahi ding: chule Egypt mite pohgih ho-a kona napuidoh uva Pakai na-Pathen'u kahichu nahetdingu ahi.
target: I will take you as my own people, and I will be your God. Then you will know that I am the Lord your God, who brought you out from under the yoke of the Egyptians.

source: Abraham, Isaac, chule Jacob henga pehdinga kana kihahselna gamachu kapuilut ding nahiuvin; chule hichu nagoulo diuva kapeh ding nahiuve: keima Pakai chu kahi, tin, ati.
target: And I will bring you to the land I swore with uplifted hand to give to Abraham, to Isaac and to Jacob. I will give it to you as a possession. I am the Lord .’ ”

source: Chuin Mosi'n Israel chate hengah thu aseijin; ahivangin alhagaovu ahesoh jehle asoh channu akhoh behseh jehchun Mosi thusei chu angaipeh pouvin ahi.
target: Moses reported this to the Israelites, but they did not listen to him because of their discouragement and harsh labor.

source: Chuin Pakaiyin Mosi henga aseijin, hitin ati.
target: Then the Lord said to Moses,

source: Chenlang Egypt lengpa Pharaoh chun agama kona Israel chate asoldoh nadingin gaseijin, ati.
target: “Go, tell Pharaoh king of Egypt to let the Israelites go out of his country.”

source: Chuin Mosi'n Pakai henga, Vetan, Israel chaten bon kathu angailou uva ahile; Pharaoh'in keima kam chepkitanlou thuhi iti angaiding ham? ati.
target: But Moses said to the Lord , “If the Israelites will not listen to me, why would Pharaoh listen to me, since I speak with faltering lips?”

source: Chuin Pakaiyin Mosi le Aaron henga thu aseijin, Egypt gama kona Israel chate puidoh nadingin, Israel chate le Egypt lengpa Pharaoh'a henga seiding thu apen ahi.
target: Now the Lord spoke to Moses and Aaron about the Israelites and Pharaoh king of Egypt, and he commanded them to bring the Israelites out of Egypt.

source: Hichenghi apu apateo insung aluchangho chu ahiuve; Israel'a kona apeng masapen Reuben chapate chu Hanoch, Pallu, Hezron le Carmi ahiuve. Hichenghi Reuben insung mite ahiuve.
target: These were the heads of their families: The sons of Reuben the firstborn son of Israel were Hanok and Pallu, Hezron and Karmi. These were the clans of Reuben.

source: Chule Simeon chapate chu Jemuel, Jamin, Ohad, Jachin le Zoher, chule Canaan numeinu chapa Shaul ahiuve. Hichenghi Simeon insung mite ahiuve.
target: The sons of Simeon were Jemuel, Jamin, Ohad, Jakin, Zohar and Shaul the son of a Canaanite woman. These were the clans of Simeon.

source: Chule hicheng hi amaho khanggui dungjuija Levi chapate min chu ahi; Gershon, Kohath, chule Merari ahiuve. Chule Levi damsung kumkho chu kum jakhat le somthum le sagi ahi.
target: These were the names of the sons of Levi according to their records: Gershon, Kohath and Merari. Levi lived 137 years.

source: Gershon chapate chu, a-insungu dungjuijin Libni le Shimei ahilhone.
target: The sons of Gershon, by clans, were Libni and Shimei.

source: Chule Kohath chapate chu, Amran, Izhar, Hebron, chule Uzziel ahiuve. Chule Kohath damsung kumkho chu kum jakhat le somthum le thum ahi.
target: The sons of Kohath were Amram, Izhar, Hebron and Uzziel. Kohath lived 133 years.

source: Chule Merari chapate chu, Mahli le Mushi ahilhone. Hichenghi akhangguiju dungjuija Levi insung mite ahiuve.
target: The sons of Merari were Mahli and Mushi. These were the clans of Levi according to their records.

source: Chuin Amram'in apa sopinu chanu Jochebed chu aji dingin akipuijin; amanun Aaron le Mosi ahinpeh-in ahi. Chule Amram damsung kumho chu kum jakhat le somthum le sagi ahi.
target: Amram married his father’s sister Jochebed, who bore him Aaron and Moses. Amram lived 137 years.

source: Chule Izhar chapate chu, Korah, Napheg, chule Zichri ahiuve.
target: The sons of Izhar were Korah, Nepheg and Zikri.

source: Chule Uzziel chapate chu Mishael, Elzaphan, chule Zithri ahiuve.
target: The sons of Uzziel were Mishael, Elzaphan and Sithri.

source: Chuin Aaron'in Amminadab chanu Nahshon sopinu Elisheba chu aji dingin akipuijin; chule amanun Nadab, Abihu, Eleazar, chule Ithamar ahinpeh-in ahi.
target: Aaron married Elisheba, daughter of Amminadab and sister of Nahshon, and she bore him Nadab and Abihu, Eleazar and Ithamar.

source: Chule Korah chapate chu, Assir, Elkanah, chule Abiasaph ahiuve. Hichenghi Korah insung mite ahiuve.
target: The sons of Korah were: Assir, Elkanah and Abiasaph. These were the Korahite clans.

source: Chuin Aaron chapa Eleazar chun Putiel chanute lah-a khat aji dingin akipuijin; chule amanun Phinehas ahinpeh-in ahi. Hichenghi a-insungu dungjui cheh-a Levi ho pate bulpiho ahiuve.
target: Eleazar son of Aaron married one of the daughters of Putiel, and she bore him Phinehas. These were the heads of the Levite families, clan by clan.

source: Hiche teni hi Pakaiyin, Egypt gama konin Israel chate chu galsat miho dungjuijin puidoh lhonin tia asei na Aaron le Mosi chu ahillhone.
target: It was this Aaron and Moses to whom the Lord said, “Bring the Israelites out of Egypt by their divisions.”

source: Hiche teni hi ahi Egypt gama kona Israel chate puidohna dinga Egypt lengpa Pharaoh henga thusei teni chu: Hiche teni hi chuche Mosi le Aaron chu ahilhone.
target: They were the ones who spoke to Pharaoh king of Egypt about bringing the Israelites out of Egypt—this same Moses and Aaron.

source: Chuin Egypt gama Pakaiyin Mosi henga thu aseini chun ahitin ahi,
target: Now when the Lord spoke to Moses in Egypt,

source: Pakaiyin Mosi henga thu aseijin, Keima Pakai chu kahi: keiman nahenga kasei jouse chu Egypt lengpa Pharaoh henga seijin, ati.
target: he said to him, “I am the Lord . Tell Pharaoh king of Egypt everything I tell you.”

source: Chuin Mosi'n Pakai angsunga chun, Vetan, keima kam cheptanlou kahin, chule Pharaoh'in iti kasei angaiding ham, ati.
target: But Moses said to the Lord , “Since I speak with faltering lips, why would Pharaoh listen to me?”

source: Chuin Pakaiyin Mosi henga, Ven, keiman nangma Pharaoh henga dingin pathen'in kasemtai; chule nasopipa chu nangma themgao hiding ahi.
target: Then the Lord said to Moses, “See, I have made you like God to Pharaoh, and your brother Aaron will be your prophet.

source: Nangman kathupeh jouse chu aboncha naseidoh ding; chule nasopipa Aaron'in agamma kona Israel chate chu asoldohna dinga Pharaoh henga aseiding ahi
target: You are to say everything I command you, and your brother Aaron is to tell Pharaoh to let the Israelites go out of his country.

source: Chule keiman Pharaoh lungchang kasuhtah ding, Egypt gamsunga chu kamelchih naho le kathil kidangho kapunsah ding ahi.
target: But I will harden Pharaoh’s heart, and though I multiply my signs and wonders in Egypt,

source: Hijongleh Egypt gamsunga kakhut kalhah nading le, kagalsat miho le kami Israel chate chu thutanna nasatah-a Egypt gamsunga kona kapuidoh nadinga Pharaoh'in nasei angaideh louding ahi.
target: he will not listen to you. Then I will lay my hand on Egypt and with mighty acts of judgment I will bring out my divisions, my people the Israelites.

source: Chule keiman Egypt chunga kakhut kajah-a, amaho lah-a kona Israel chate kapuidoh teng, keima Pakai kahi chu Egypt miten ahet dingu ahi, ati.
target: And the Egyptians will know that I am the Lord when I stretch out my hand against Egypt and bring the Israelites out of it.”

source: Chutichun Mosi le Aaron'in Pakaiyin athupeh bang bangin abol lhonin, chuti chun abol lhon tai.
target: Moses and Aaron did just as the Lord commanded them.

source: Chule amanin Pharaoh henga thu aseilhon chun Mosi kum somget alhingtan, chule Aaron chu kum somget le kum thum alhingtan ahi.
target: Moses was eighty years old and Aaron eighty-three when they spoke to Pharaoh.

source: Chuin Pakaiyin Mosi le Aaron henga thu aseijin, hitin ati,
target: The Lord said to Moses and Aaron,

source: Pharaoh'in najah lhona, Nangnin thilkidang vetsah lhonin atiteng; nangman Aaron hengah, Natenggol chu lanlang Pharaoh angsunga seplhan, natiding ahi. Chuteng hichu gul hungsoh ding ahi, ati.
target: “When Pharaoh says to you, ‘Perform a miracle,’ then say to Aaron, ‘Take your staff and throw it down before Pharaoh,’ and it will become a snake.”

source: Chuin Mosi le Aaron Pharaoh henga alutlhonin, Pakai thupeh bangchun abol lhontan ahi. Chuin Aaron'in atenggol chu Pharaoh masang le asohte masanga aseplhan ahile, hichu gul asohtan ahi.
target: So Moses and Aaron went to Pharaoh and did just as the Lord commanded. Aaron threw his staff down in front of Pharaoh and his officials, and it became a snake.

source: Chuphatnin Pharaoh'in jong miching ho le doi themho akoukhom tai. Tun Egypt mitpheldoi themho, amaho jong chun adoijuva konin chutobang bang chun aboltheijun ahi.
target: Pharaoh then summoned wise men and sorcerers, and the Egyptian magicians also did the same things by their secret arts:

source: Ajehchu amaho amitakipmin atenggol cheh-u chu aseplhaovin ahile hicheho chu gul asohtan ahi: ahivangin Aaron tenggol chun atenggol hou chu avallhum gamtan ahi.
target: Each one threw down his staff and it became a snake. But Aaron’s staff swallowed up their staffs.

source: Chuin Pharaoh lungsung chu Pakaiyin aseibang chun amani thusei angailouna dingin, Aman atahsah tan ahi.
target: Yet Pharaoh’s heart became hard and he would not listen to them, just as the Lord had said.

source: Chuin Pakaiyin Mosi henga, Pharaoh lungsung akisuh tah jeh-a aman miho chu achesah nomlou ahi.
target: Then the Lord said to Moses, “Pharaoh’s heart is unyielding; he refuses to let the people go.

source: Nangma jingkah le Pharaoh henga gachen: ven, ama twikhuh lama chun achei; chule nangma amato kimuto dinga vadung panga chu nanading ding; chule gul naso sahna tenggol chu nakhutna nakichoi ding ahi.
target: Go to Pharaoh in the morning as he goes out to the river. Confront him on the bank of the Nile, and take in your hand the staff that was changed into a snake.

source: Chutengle nangman ama henga, Hebrew mite Pakai Pathen'in nangma henga, Amahon keima gamthipma eijen theina diuvin kamite chesah-in, tia seidinga eihinsol ahi: ahinla ven, tugeihin hichu nangman nangaipoi.
target: Then say to him, ‘The Lord , the God of the Hebrews, has sent me to say to you: Let my people go, so that they may worship me in the wilderness. But until now you have not listened.

source: Pakaiyin hitin aseije, Hichea konahi Pakai kahi chu neihet ding ahi. Ven, kakhut na tenggola hi vadunga twi chu kajepding ahin, chule hichu thisan sohding ahi.
target: This is what the Lord says: By this you will know that I am the Lord : With the staff that is in my hand I will strike the water of the Nile, and it will be changed into blood.

source: Chule vadunga um nga hochu thiding, vadung chu uiding ahin; chule Egypt miten vadunga twi chu donding akidah diu ahi, ati.
target: The fish in the Nile will die, and the river will stink; the Egyptians will not be able to drink its water.’ ”

source: Chuin Pakaiyin Mosi henga, Aaron jah-a, Natenggol chu lanlang Egypt twiho chunga, aluidung hou chunga, vadung ho chunga, atuikul hou chunga, chule atuikul hou jouse chunga aboncha thisan asotheina ding le Egypt gam pumpi-a thing kongho le song kongho-a jong thisan aumna dingin nakhut jahdoh-in tin seijin, ati.
target: The Lord said to Moses, “Tell Aaron, ‘Take your staff and stretch out your hand over the waters of Egypt—over the streams and canals, over the ponds and all the reservoirs—and they will turn to blood.’ Blood will be everywhere in Egypt, even in vessels of wood and stone.”

source: Chuin Pakai thupeh bang chun Mosi le Aaron'in abol lhontan ahi; chuin aman atenggol chu alamin, Pharaoh mitmu le asohte mitmun vadunga um twi chu ajeptan ahi; chuin vadunga um twi jouse chu thisan asohtai.
target: Moses and Aaron did just as the Lord had commanded. He raised his staff in the presence of Pharaoh and his officials and struck the water of the Nile, and all the water was changed into blood.

source: Chuin vadunga um nga ho chu athin; vadung chu a-uitan, Egypt miten vadung twi chu adonthei tapouvin; chule Egypt gamsung pumpi-a chun thisan aumtan ahi.
target: The fish in the Nile died, and the river smelled so bad that the Egyptians could not drink its water. Blood was everywhere in Egypt.

source: Chuin Egypt mitpheldoi themho chun adoi uva konin chutobangma chun abolun ahi. Chule Pharaoh lung chu tahsah-in aumin, Pakaiyin aseibang chun aman amani thusei angai dehpon ahi.
target: But the Egyptian magicians did the same things by their secret arts, and Pharaoh’s heart became hard; he would not listen to Moses and Aaron, just as the Lord had said.

source: Chuin Pharaoh chu akiheijin a-insunga aluttan, hiche thuhi alungsunga angaito pon ahi.
target: Instead, he turned and went into his palace, and did not take even this to heart.

source: Chuin Egypt miten donding twi holna-in vadung vel chu alaitauvin ahi; ajehchu amahon vadung twi chu adonthei louvu ahitai.
target: And all the Egyptians dug along the Nile to get drinking water, because they could not drink the water of the river.

source: Chule Pakaiyin vadung chu avoh-a pat nisagi alhingtan ahi.
target: Seven days passed after the Lord struck the Nile.

source: Chuin Pakaiyin Mosi jah-a, Pharaoh henga gachen lang, ajah-a hitin gaseijin, Pakaiyin hitin aseije, Eijen theina diuvin kamite soldoh tan.
target: Then the Lord said to Moses, “Go to Pharaoh and say to him, ‘This is what the Lord says: Let my people go, so that they may worship me.

source: Chule nangman amaho chu nasol nomlouva ahile, ven, keiman nagamsung pumpi uphoh-a kajep ding ahi.
target: If you refuse to let them go, I will send a plague of frogs on your whole country.

source: Chule vadung chun uphoh atama tam ahinsepdoh ding, hicheho chu na-in sung, na-indan sung, najalkhun chung, nasohte insung, namite chung, nathuh khuh sung, chule nachang bong mehnao kong houva hunglut ding ahiuve.
target: The Nile will teem with frogs. They will come up into your palace and your bedroom and onto your bed, into the houses of your officials and on your people, and into your ovens and kneading troughs.

source: Chule uphoh ho chu nangma chungle namite chung, chule nasohte jouse chunga hung kaltou diu ahi, tin seijin ati.
target: The frogs will come up on you and your people and all your officials.’ ”

source: Chuin Pakaiyin Mosi henga, Aaron henga seijin, Vachadung ho chule vadung hole twikul ho chunga natenggol pumin nakhut chu jahdoh inlang uphoh hochu Egypt gam chunga hungdoh sah-in, tin, ati.
target: Then the Lord said to Moses, “Tell Aaron, ‘Stretch out your hand with your staff over the streams and canals and ponds, and make frogs come up on the land of Egypt.’ ”

source: Hiti chun Aaron'in Egypt twi chunga chun akhut ajahdoh-in ahile uphoh ho chu ahungdoh-un, Egypt gam chu alodim taovin ahi.
target: So Aaron stretched out his hand over the waters of Egypt, and the frogs came up and covered the land.

source: Chuin mitphel doithem ho jong chun adoiju chu mangchan chutobangma chun abolun, Egypt gam chunga chun uphoh hochu ahungdoh sah-un ahi.
target: But the magicians did the same things by their secret arts; they also made frogs come up on the land of Egypt.

source: Hichun Pharaoh'in Mosi le Aaron akouvin, ajah lhona, Keima le kamite-a kona uphoh hohi alahmang nadingin Pakai henga ngeh lhonin; chutengle Pakai henga ganlhaina boldinga mipi chu kasol ding ahi, ati.
target: Pharaoh summoned Moses and Aaron and said, “Pray to the Lord to take the frogs away from me and my people, and I will let your people go to offer sacrifices to the Lord .”

source: Chuin Mosi'n Pharaoh jah-a, Lunglhai selin neithu peh-in, itih phatle nangma le na-insunga kona uphoh ho suhmanga auma vadunga bou aumna dinga nangma-a ding, nasohte-a ding, chule namite dinga katao dingham? ati.
target: Moses said to Pharaoh, “I leave to you the honor of setting the time for me to pray for you and your officials and your people that you and your houses may be rid of the frogs, except for those that remain in the Nile.”

source: Chuin aman, Jingle ati. Chuin aman, Pakai ka Pathen'u bang hi koimacha dang aumpoi ti nahet nadingin: nathusei dungjuijin hitahen.
target: “Tomorrow,” Pharaoh said. Moses replied, “It will be as you say, so that you may know there is no one like the Lord our God.

source: Chule uphoh hochu nangma-a kon, na-insung ho-a kon, nasohte-a kon, chule namite-a kona chemanguva, vadunga bou umdingu ahitai, ati.
target: The frogs will leave you and your houses, your officials and your people; they will remain only in the Nile.”

source: Chuin Mosi le Aaron chu Pharaoh koma konin apotdoh lhontai. Chuin Mosi'n Pharaoh douna-a uphoh ho asosah jehchun Pakai henga ataotan ahi.
target: After Moses and Aaron left Pharaoh, Moses cried out to the Lord about the frogs he had brought on Pharaoh.

source: Chuin Pakaiyin Mosi thu dungjuijin ahinboltan: chuin uphoh ho chu inho, kho ho, chule louho-a konchun athigam taovin ahi.
target: And the Lord did what Moses asked. The frogs died in the houses, in the courtyards and in the fields.

source: Chuin amahon hiho chu alhuh lhuh-in asekhom mun: gamsung chu apumpin a-uitan ahi.
target: They were piled into heaps, and the land reeked of them.

source: Ahivangin Pharaoh'in chomkhat akicholdona amuphatnin, Pakaiyin anasei bangin alung atahsah-in; amani thusei chu angaipeh tapon ahi.
target: But when Pharaoh saw that there was relief, he hardened his heart and would not listen to Moses and Aaron, just as the Lord had said.

source: Chuin Pakaiyin Mosi henga, Aaron jah-a, Egypt gam pumpi-a leivuichu kha ahung so nadin natenggol lamin lang gamsunga leivui chu jepmin, tin seijin, ati.
target: Then the Lord said to Moses, “Tell Aaron, ‘Stretch out your staff and strike the dust of the ground,’ and throughout the land of Egypt the dust will become gnats.”

source: Chuin amanin chutichun abol lhontan ahi: ajehchu Aaron'in atenggol chu akhut toh alamin, leisetna leivui chu ajepmin ahile sa le mihem chunga chun kha ahung langtan; chuin Egypt gam pumpi-a chun tolla leivui jouse chu kha ahungsoh tan ahi.
target: They did this, and when Aaron stretched out his hand with the staff and struck the dust of the ground, gnats came on people and animals. All the dust throughout the land of Egypt became gnats.

source: Chule mitphel doithem hochun adoiju chu amang chaovin kha asosah gouvin, ahivangin amahon abolthei tapouvin ahi. Chutichun sa le mihem chunga chun kha alangtan ahi.
target: But when the magicians tried to produce gnats by their secret arts, they could not. Since the gnats were on people and animals everywhere,

source: Chujouvin mitpheldoi themho chun Pharaoh henga, Hichehi Pathen khutjung ahi atiuvin ahi. Chuin Pakaiyin anaseisa bang chun Pharaoh lungsung chu tahsah-in aumin; aseilhon angaipeh tapon ahi.
target: the magicians said to Pharaoh, “This is the finger of God.” But Pharaoh’s heart was hard and he would not listen, just as the Lord had said.

source: Chuin Pakaiyin Mosi henga, Jingpi matah-in thouvin lang Pharaoh anga gadingin: ven, ama twikhuh lama ahunge; chule nangman ajah-a, Pakaiyin hitin aseije, Amahon eijen theina dingun kamite soldoh-in ati.
target: Then the Lord said to Moses, “Get up early in the morning and confront Pharaoh as he goes to the river and say to him, ‘This is what the Lord says: Let my people go, so that they may worship me.

source: Chutilouva, nangman kamite nasoldoh louva ahile, ven, nangma chung, nasohte chung, namite chung, chule na-insung chunga thousivaibong kahin lansah ding; Egypt mite insungho le adinnau leiset chunga chu thousivaibong dimset ding ahi.
target: If you do not let my people go, I will send swarms of flies on you and your officials, on your people and into your houses. The houses of the Egyptians will be full of flies; even the ground will be covered with them.

source: Chuche nikho chule kamite chenna Goshen gamchu kakhendoh ding, chukoma chu thousivaibong himhim umlou ding; chuteng keima leiset lailung Pakai kahi nahetdoh ding ahi.
target: “ ‘But on that day I will deal differently with the land of Goshen, where my people live; no swarms of flies will be there, so that you will know that I, the Lord , am in this land.

source: Chule keiman kamite le namite kah-a kikhenna kakoi ding: jingle hiche melchihna chu hung umding ahi, gatin, ati.
target: I will make a distinction between my people and your people. This sign will occur tomorrow.’ ”

source: Chuin Pakaiyin chutichun aboltan; Pharaoh insung le asohte insunga, chule Egypt gam pumpi-a chun genthei umtah thousivaibong ahung lhungtan: thousivaibong jehchun gam chu suhboh-in aumtan ahi.
target: And the Lord did this. Dense swarms of flies poured into Pharaoh’s palace and into the houses of his officials; throughout Egypt the land was ruined by the flies.

source: Chuin Pharaoh'in Mosi le Aaron chu akouvin, ahenglhona, Nangho cheovin lang hiche gamahin na-Pathen'u henga ganlhaina ganei taovin, ati.
target: Then Pharaoh summoned Moses and Aaron and said, “Go, sacrifice to your God here in the land.”

source: Chuin Mosi'n, Chutobanga bolding chu thildih ahipoi; ajehchu keihon Egypt mite-a dinga thet umtah hochu Pakai ka-Pathen'u henga ganlhaina-a kaneidiu ahi: ven, Egypt mite dinga thet umtah hochu amitmu tah uva ganlhaina-a kaneijuva ahile, amahon songa eiselou dingu ham?
target: But Moses said, “That would not be right. The sacrifices we offer the Lord our God would be detestable to the Egyptians. And if we offer sacrifices that are detestable in their eyes, will they not stone us?

source: Aman eithupeh banguva gamthip nithum lama kacheuva, Pakai ka-Pathen'u henga ganlhaina kanei dingu ahi, ati.
target: We must take a three-day journey into the wilderness to offer sacrifices to the Lord our God, as he commands us.”

source: Chuin Pharaoh'in, Pakai na Pathen'u henga gamthipma ganlhaina nanei theina dingun nasolu vinge; ahin gamlatah-a vang nachelou dingu ahi: keima dingin neitao peh-un, ati.
target: Pharaoh said, “I will let you go to offer sacrifices to the Lord your God in the wilderness, but you must not go very far. Now pray for me.”

source: Chuin Mosi'n, Ven, keima nakoma kona kachedoh-a, Pharaoh le asohte, chule amite-a kona thousivaibong hohi jinga patna achemang nadiuvin Pakai koma kagatao ding ahi: ahin mipi ho chu Pakai henga ganlhaina neidinga chesah louna dingin, Pharaoh'in dohan neibolkit tahih-un, ati.
target: Moses answered, “As soon as I leave you, I will pray to the Lord , and tomorrow the flies will leave Pharaoh and his officials and his people. Only let Pharaoh be sure that he does not act deceitfully again by not letting the people go to offer sacrifices to the Lord .”

source: Chuin Mosi Pharaoh anga konin apotdoh-in, Pakai henga ataotan ahi.
target: Then Moses left Pharaoh and prayed to the Lord ,

source: Chuin Pakaiyin Mosi thusei bangchun abolin; chule thousivaibong hochu Pharaoh'a kon le asohtea kon, chule amite-a konin aladoh-in; khatcha jong aumdena aumpon ahi.
target: and the Lord did what Moses asked. The flies left Pharaoh and his officials and his people; not a fly remained.

source: Chuin Pharaoh'in hiche chunga jong hi alung atahsah-in, miho chu asoldoh dehpon ahi.
target: But this time also Pharaoh hardened his heart and would not let the people go.

source: Chujouvin Pakaiyin Mosi henga, Pharaoh koma lutnin lang ajah-a, Hebrew mite Pakai Pathen'in hitin aseije, Keima eihou theina diuvin kamite chu soldoh tan.
target: Then the Lord said to Moses, “Go to Pharaoh and say to him, ‘This is what the Lord , the God of the Hebrews, says: “Let my people go, so that they may worship me.”

source: Nangman amaho soldoh ding nada-a, nahen jing nahlaija ahile,
target: If you refuse to let them go and continue to hold them back,

source: Ven, loujaova um naganchaho chung, sakol ho, sanganho, sangongsang ho, bongchalho, kelngoiho chungah Pakai khut chuding: gancha pul khohtah langding ahi.
target: the hand of the Lord will bring a terrible plague on your livestock in the field—on your horses, donkeys and camels and on your cattle, sheep and goats.

source: Chule Pakaiyin Israel mite gancha honle Egypt mite gancha hon chu achomkhen ding: chule Israel chate-a poupou chu khatcha jong thilou ding ahi, tin gaseijin, ati.
target: But the Lord will make a distinction between the livestock of Israel and that of Egypt, so that no animal belonging to the Israelites will die.’ ”

source: Chuin Pakaiyin phatbih khat atepmin, Pakaiyin jing nikhole hiche thilhi gamsunga abolding ahi, ati.
target: The Lord set a time and said, “Tomorrow the Lord will do this in the land.”

source: Chutichun ajing nikhon Pakaiyin chuche thil chu aboltan, Egypt gamsunga gancha jouse chu athitai: ahinla Israel chate gancha ho chu khatcha jong athipon ahi.
target: And the next day the Lord did it: All the livestock of the Egyptians died, but not one animal belonging to the Israelites died.

source: Chuin Pharaoh'in mi asolin, chule veuvin, Israel mite gancha khatcha jong athi aumpon ahi. Chuin Pharaoh lungthim chu akisutah-in; chule miho chu alhadoh dehpon ahi.
target: Pharaoh investigated and found that not even one of the animals of the Israelites had died. Yet his heart was unyielding and he would not let the people go.

source: Chuin Pakaiyin Mosi le Aaron henga, Nangnin thuh sunga konin vut khutdim la lhonin lang, hichu Mosi'n Pharaoh mitmu tah-in van lama thehen.
target: Then the Lord said to Moses and Aaron, “Take handfuls of soot from a furnace and have Moses toss it into the air in the presence of Pharaoh.

source: Hichu Egypt gamsung jouse-a leivuinel soh ding, Egypt gamsung pumpi-a mihem chungle gancha chunga uilut le mase nasatah chaljal ding ahi, ati.
target: It will become fine dust over the whole land of Egypt, and festering boils will break out on people and animals throughout the land.”
