source: Chuin amanin thuh sunga vut chu ahamlhonin, Pharaoh angsunga ading lhonin; chuin Mosi'n hichu van lama athen ahile, mihemle gancha chunga chun uilut ahungsoh tan, mase khohtah achaljal tan ahi.
target: So they took soot from a furnace and stood before Pharaoh. Moses tossed it into the air, and festering boils broke out on people and animals.

source: Chuin chuche uilut jehchun mitpheldoi themho chu Mosi masanga adingthei tapouvin ahi; ajehchu uilut chu mitphel doithemho le Egypt mite jouse chunga chu-ah ahi.
target: The magicians could not stand before Moses because of the boils that were on them and on all the Egyptians.

source: Chuin Pakaiyin Pharaoh lungthim chu atahsah-in, Pakaiyin Mosi henga aseibang chun athu seilhon chu angai pehpon ahi.
target: But the Lord hardened Pharaoh’s heart and he would not listen to Moses and Aaron, just as the Lord had said to Moses.

source: Chuin Pakaiyin Mosi henga, Jingpitah-in thouvin lang, Pharaoh henga gadingin, chule ahenga, Hebrew mite Pakai Pathen'in hitin aseije, Keima eihou theina diuvin kamite soldoh tan.
target: Then the Lord said to Moses, “Get up early in the morning, confront Pharaoh and say to him, ‘This is what the Lord , the God of the Hebrews, says: Let my people go, so that they may worship me,

source: Ajehchu leiset chung jouse-a hin keima tobang koimacha aumpoi ti nahet nadinga, tuchunga hi nangma lungsung chung le nasohte chung, chule namite chunga ka hise jouse kahin chuhsah ding ahi.
target: or this time I will send the full force of my plagues against you and against your officials and your people, so you may know that there is no one like me in all the earth.

source: Ajehchu nangma le namite chu hise-a kajep theina dinguva, tu-a hi keiman kakhut kalhandoh ding: chule nangma leisetna kona paidoh-a naum ding ahi.
target: For by now I could have stretched out my hand and struck you and your people with a plague that would have wiped you off the earth.

source: Chule kathahat nahi nangma vetsah nading le kamin hi vannoi leiset pumpi-a phondoh-a aumna dinga, hiche jeh tah-a hi nangma katundoh nahi.
target: But I have raised you up for this very purpose, that I might show you my power and that my name might be proclaimed in all the earth.

source: Tugeihin nangman amaho nasoldoh louva konhin, kamite douna-in nangle nang naki choisangin ahi.
target: You still set yourself against my people and will not let them go.

source: Ven, jing nikho tuphat tah hile Egypt gam kiphudoh-a pat tuchan geija anaumkha louhel, gel nasatah chu kahin juhsah ding ahi.
target: Therefore, at this time tomorrow I will send the worst hailstorm that has ever fallen on Egypt, from the day it was founded till now.

source: Hijeh chun tun mi solinlang, loujaova um nagancha jouse gakhop khom sah-in; ajehchu in'a kipuilut louva loujaova um mihemle gancha chung jouse-a chu gel hunglha ding, amaho chu thiding ahiuve, gatin, ati.
target: Give an order now to bring your livestock and everything you have in the field to a place of shelter, because the hail will fall on every person and animal that has not been brought in and is still out in the field, and they will die.’ ”

source: Chuin Pharaoh sohte lah-a Pakai thu gingho chun asohteu le aganchahou chu insunga ajamlut sah loijun ahi.
target: Those officials of Pharaoh who feared the word of the Lord hurried to bring their slaves and their livestock inside.

source: Chule Pakai thu ngaisah louho chun asohteu le aganchahou chu louva adalha denun ahi.
target: But those who ignored the word of the Lord left their slaves and livestock in the field.

source: Chuin Pakaiyin Mosi henga, Egypt gam jouse mihem chung le gancha chung, chule Egypt gamsung jouse-a louva hampaho jouse chunga gel ahunglhah nadingin, van lama nakhut jahdoh-in, ati.
target: Then the Lord said to Moses, “Stretch out your hand toward the sky so that hail will fall all over Egypt—on people and animals and on everything growing in the fields of Egypt.”

source: Chuin Mosi'n atenggol chu van lama ajahdoh tan ahi. Chuin Pakaiyin van ginle gel ahinsoltan; mei chu leichunga avahmat jengin; hitichun Pakaiyin Egypt gam chunga chun gel alhah sahtan ahi.
target: When Moses stretched out his staff toward the sky, the Lord sent thunder and hail, and lightning flashed down to the ground. So the Lord rained hail on the land of Egypt;

source: Chutichun gel, meito kihal gel alhan, akhohset danchu namkhat ahung hiuvapat Egypt gamsunga hitobang hi aumkha khapon ahi.
target: hail fell and lightning flashed back and forth. It was the worst storm in all the land of Egypt since it had become a nation.

source: Chuin Egypt gam jouse-a loujaova thil um jouse, mihem le gancha jong gel chun aseplih gamin; chule gel chun loujaova hampa louhing jouse aseplih-in, gama thing jouse jong asepbong gamtan ahi.
target: Throughout Egypt hail struck everything in the fields—both people and animals; it beat down everything growing in the fields and stripped every tree.

source: Israel chate umna Goshen gama chun bou gel alhapon ahi.
target: The only place it did not hail was the land of Goshen, where the Israelites were.

source: Chuin Pharaoh'in mi asolin, Mosi le Aaron chu agakou sah-in, aheng lhona chun, Tuchung hin keima kachonse tai; Pakai chu achonpha ahin, keima le kamite vang gilou kahiuve.
target: Then Pharaoh summoned Moses and Aaron. “This time I have sinned,” he said to them. “The Lord is in the right, and I and my people are in the wrong.

source: Van gin nasatah le gel hi abeina dingin, Pakai henga ngeh lhonin, (ajehchu phasetna ahitai;) keiman nangho kasoldoh uva, nangho na-umsot tahlou dingu ahi, ati.
target: Pray to the Lord , for we have had enough thunder and hail. I will let you go; you don’t have to stay any longer.”

source: Chuin Mosi'n ahenga, Keima khopi sunga kona kapotdoh dohle Pakai henga kakhut kajahdoh ding: leiset hi Pakaiya ahi nahetdoh nadinga van gin chu thipding, geljong lhahbe louding ahitai, ati.
target: Moses replied, “When I have gone out of the city, I will spread out my hands in prayer to the Lord . The thunder will stop and there will be no more hail, so you may know that the earth is the Lord ’s.

source: Ahivangin nangma le nasohte thudol vang, nanghon Pakai Pathen chu nagindeh lou dingu ahi kahei, ati.
target: But I know that you and your officials still do not fear the Lord God.”

source: Chule tupat phungle sakol chang chu suhmangin aumtan ahi. Ajehchu sakol chang chu avui ahungdoh tan, tupat phung vang chu apahlaitah ahi.
target: (The flax and barley were destroyed, since the barley had headed and the flax was in bloom.

source: Ahin suhlou chang le butun vang akedoh loulai jeh-in suhmangin aumpon ahi.
target: The wheat and spelt, however, were not destroyed, because they ripen later.)

source: Chuin Mosi Pharaoh koma konin khopi chu adalhan, Pakai henga akhut ajahdoh-in ahi; chuin van ginle gel chu atangtan, lei chunga go ajutapon ahi.
target: Then Moses left Pharaoh and went out of the city. He spread out his hands toward the Lord ; the thunder and hail stopped, and the rain no longer poured down on the land.

source: Chuin Pharaoh'in go le gel chule van gin ho atan amuphatnin, chonset abolbe nalaijin, amale asohte chun alungthimu atahsah kit taovin ahi.
target: When Pharaoh saw that the rain and hail and thunder had stopped, he sinned again: He and his officials hardened their hearts.

source: Chuin Pharaoh lungthim chu suhtah-in aumin, Pakaiyin Mosi henga anasei bang chun, Israel chate chu alhadoh dehpon ahi.
target: So Pharaoh’s heart was hard and he would not let the Israelites go, just as the Lord had said through Moses.

source: Chuin Pakaiyin Mosi henga, Pharaoh koma galutnin: ajehchu hiche kamelchihna hohi amasanga kamusah theina dinga, amale asohte lungsung chu katahsah ahi:
target: Then the Lord said to Moses, “Go to Pharaoh, for I have hardened his heart and the hearts of his officials so that I may perform these signs of mine among them

source: Chutia chu nangman nachapate le natupate nabenga Egypt gamsunga kathilbol ho leh alah uva kamelchihna bolho naseipeh uva; chule keima Pakai kahi nahetna dingu ahi, ati.
target: that you may tell your children and grandchildren how I dealt harshly with the Egyptians and how I performed my signs among them, and that you may know that I am the Lord .”

source: Chuin Mosi le Aaron Pharaoh hengah ahunglut lhonin, ajah-a, Hebrew mite Pakai Pathen'in hiti hin ati, Nangma itihchan ka-angsunga kineosah ding nada nahlai ding ham? Keima eihou theina dingun kamite soldoh tan.
target: So Moses and Aaron went to Pharaoh and said to him, “This is what the Lord , the God of the Hebrews, says: ‘How long will you refuse to humble yourself before me? Let my people go, so that they may worship me.

source: Chutilouva, kamite nasoldoh nomlouva ahile, ven, jingle nagam pumpi-a khaokho kahin lhalut ding ahi.
target: If you refuse to let them go, I will bring locusts into your country tomorrow.

source: Chule koiman tol amu theilou leuva amahon leiset chung alosoh dingu ahi: chule gel suhset moh, nahenga umnalai jouse chu anehjou hel diu, chule nangma-a dinga keh loujaova thingphung jouse jong chu aneh jouhel dingu ahi.
target: They will cover the face of the ground so that it cannot be seen. They will devour what little you have left after the hail, including every tree that is growing in your fields.

source: Chule amahon na-insung le nasohte jouse insung, chule Egypt mite jouse insung chu alodim sohdiu; hichu napateu le naputeuvin jong leiset chunga achenuva pat tuni geija amukhah lou dingu ahi, ati. Chuin ama akiheijin, Pharaoh henga konin apotdoh tai.
target: They will fill your houses and those of all your officials and all the Egyptians—something neither your parents nor your ancestors have ever seen from the day they settled in this land till now.’ ” Then Moses turned and left Pharaoh.

source: Chuin Pharaoh sohte chun ahenga, Hiche mipahi itih chan eiho dinga thanga pang dingham? Pakai a-Pathen'u chu ajen theina diuvin miho chu soldoh tan: Egypt gamhi suhmangin aumtai ti nahet loulai ham? atiuve.
target: Pharaoh’s officials said to him, “How long will this man be a snare to us? Let the people go, so that they may worship the Lord their God. Do you not yet realize that Egypt is ruined?”

source: Chuin Mosi le Aaron chu Pharaoh henga ahinpui kitnun ahi. Chuin aman aheng lhonna, Cheovin, Pakai na-Pathen'u chu gajen taovin: ahin koi koi cheding nahiuvem? ati.
target: Then Moses and Aaron were brought back to Pharaoh. “Go, worship the Lord your God,” he said. “But tell me who will be going.”

source: Chuin Mosi'n, Keiho kakhangdong hou le katehse hou toh, kachapateu le kachanuteu toh, kabong honhou le kakelngoi honhou toh kache dingu ahi; ajehchu keihon Pakai henga Kut kabol dingu ahi, ati.
target: Moses answered, “We will go with our young and our old, with our sons and our daughters, and with our flocks and herds, because we are to celebrate a festival to the Lord .”

source: Chuin aman ajah lhona, Keiman nachasen houtoh kasoldoh uva ahile, Pakaiyin na-umpiu hen: chingtheijun, ajehchu namasanguva thilphalou aume.
target: Pharaoh said, “The Lord be with you—if I let you go, along with your women and children! Clearly you are bent on evil.

source: Chutiponte: tun nangho pasal chengchu cheovin lang Pakai chu gajen taovin: ajehchu hichu nangaichatnu ahi, ati. Chuin Pharaoh angsunga konin amani chu anodoh taovin ahi.
target: No! Have only the men go and worship the Lord , since that’s what you have been asking for.” Then Moses and Aaron were driven out of Pharaoh’s presence.

source: Chuin Pakaiyin Mosi henga, Khaokhote Egypt gamsung chunga ahungchuh uva, hiche gama gel seset moh hampa louhing jouse anehthei nadiuvin, khaokhote-a dingin Egypt gamsung chunga hin nakhut jahdoh-in ati.
target: And the Lord said to Moses, “Stretch out your hand over Egypt so that locusts swarm over the land and devour everything growing in the fields, everything left by the hail.”

source: Chuin Mosi'n Egypt gam chunga atenggol chu ajahdoh-in ahile, Pakaiyin sun nilhum jankhovah-in gamchunga chun solam hui anunsah tan, chuin jingkah ahung hi phatnin solam hui chun khaokho hochu ahin polut tan ahi.
target: So Moses stretched out his staff over Egypt, and the Lord made an east wind blow across the land all that day and all that night. By morning the wind had brought the locusts;

source: Chuin khaokho ho chu Egypt gam jouse chunga ahung taovin, Egypt gam pumpi jouse-a chun acholnga taovin ahi. Hiho chu akhohse lheh jengun; amaho masanga hin amaho tobang khaokho ana umkhapon, amaho nunga jong chutobang umkit louding ahi.
target: they invaded all Egypt and settled down in every area of the country in great numbers. Never before had there been such a plague of locusts, nor will there ever be again.

source: Ajehchu hicheho chun leiset pumpi chu atomchah jeng taovin, chutichun gamsung chu athim jengtan; chule gelin asuhset moh gama hamhing tincheng le thingna jouse chu anegam hel taovin ahi. Chutichun Egypt gamsung jouse-a chun thingphung ho-a thing hing le loujaoa hampa louhing a-eng him him khatcha jong aumtapon ahi.
target: They covered all the ground until it was black. They devoured all that was left after the hail—everything growing in the fields and the fruit on the trees. Nothing green remained on tree or plant in all the land of Egypt.

source: Chuin Pharaoh'in Mosi le Aaron chu gangtah-in akouvin, ajahlhona, Keima Pakai na Pathen lhonle nangni douna-in kachonse tai.
target: Pharaoh quickly summoned Moses and Aaron and said, “I have sinned against the Lord your God and against you.

source: Hijeh chun tun, katao ahi, Kachonset hi khatveiseh neingaidam kit lhonin, hiche thina hi keija kona alahmang theina din Pakai na Pathen henga neitaopeh lhonin, ati.
target: Now forgive my sin once more and pray to the Lord your God to take this deadly plague away from me.”

source: Chuin ama Pharaoh koma konin apotdoh in, Pakai henga atao tai.
target: Moses then left Pharaoh and prayed to the Lord .

source: Chuin Pakaiyin lhumlam hui hattah anunsah-in ahile, hichun khaokho ho chu alhoh mangin, twipi sana alhoh lutsoh keijin; Egypt gam pumpi-a chun khaokho khatcha jong aumtapon ahi.
target: And the Lord changed the wind to a very strong west wind, which caught up the locusts and carried them into the Red Sea. Not a locust was left anywhere in Egypt.

source: Ahivangin Pakaiyin Pharaoh lung chu atahsah-in, chuti chun aman Israel chate chu asoldoh dehpon ahi.
target: But the Lord hardened Pharaoh’s heart, and he would not let the Israelites go.

source: Chuin Pakaiyin Mosi henga, Egypt gam chunga tohkhah thei hel khopma muthim ahung umtheina dingin van lama nakhut jahdoh-in, ati.
target: Then the Lord said to Moses, “Stretch out your hand toward the sky so that darkness spreads over Egypt—darkness that can be felt.”

source: Chuin Mosi'n van lama akhut ajahdoh tan ahile, nithum Egypt gam pumpi chunga chun nasatah-in mu athimtan ahi.
target: So Moses stretched out his hand toward the sky, and total darkness covered all Egypt for three days.

source: Amaho khatle khat akimuto thei tapouvin, nithum sung chun koimacha aumna munna kona kipatdoh aumpon ahi. Ahivangin Israel chate jouse chennaho-a chun vah aneicheh-un ahi.
target: No one could see anyone else or move about for three days. Yet all the Israelites had light in the places where they lived.

source: Chuin Pharaoh'in Mosi chu akouvin, ajah-a, Nangho cheovin lang, Pakai chu gajen taovin; nabonghon houle na kelngoihon hou bouchu umhen: nachasen hou jong chu nangho toh lhonuhen, ati.
target: Then Pharaoh summoned Moses and said, “Go, worship the Lord . Even your women and children may go with you; only leave your flocks and herds behind.”

source: Chuin Mosi'n, Nangman Pakai ka-Pathen'u henga ganlhaina-a kato dinguva ganlhaina thilto dingle govam thilto ding jong neipeh dingu ahi.
target: But Moses said, “You must allow us to have sacrifices and burnt offerings to present to the Lord our God.

source: Kagancha hou jong keiho toh lhonding ahi: gancha kengtin khatjong dalhah-a umlou ding ahi: ajehchu Pakai ka-Pathen'u kajen nadinguva phabep kalhendoh dingu ahin; amun kalhun masang seova hoichepena hi Pakai kajen dingu kihet louvu ahi, ati.
target: Our livestock too must go with us; not a hoof is to be left behind. We have to use some of them in worshiping the Lord our God, and until we get there we will not know what we are to use to worship the Lord .”

source: Ahivangin Pakaiyin Pharaoh lung chu atahsah tan, amaho chu asoldoh nompon ahi.
target: But the Lord hardened Pharaoh’s heart, and he was not willing to let them go.

source: Chuin Pharaoh'in ahenga, Kakoma konin chemangtan, kichih theijin, kamai mukit tahih-in; ajehchu kamai namukit ninileh nathi ding ahi, ati.
target: Pharaoh said to Moses, “Get out of my sight! Make sure you do not appear before me again! The day you see my face you will die.”

source: Chuin Mosi'n, Nangman nasei dih-e, keiman namai kamukit louding ahitai ati.
target: “Just as you say,” Moses replied. “I will never appear before you again.”

source: Chuin Pakaiyin Mosi henga, Pharaoh chung le Egypt gam chunga hise khat kalhunsah be nahlai ding ahin; chujouteng leh hikoma kona hi nasoldoh diu ahitai: aman nasoldoh tengule, thonlouva nanodoh tho sohkei jeng dingu ahi.
target: Now the Lord had said to Moses, “I will bring one more plague on Pharaoh and on Egypt. After that, he will let you go from here, and when he does, he will drive you out completely.

source: Tun mipi ho henga seipeh-in, chule pasal jouse le numei jousen aheng akoma konin dangka le sana-a kisem kijepnaho kithum cheh uhen, ati.
target: Tell the people that men and women alike are to ask their neighbors for articles of silver and gold.”

source: Chuin Pakaiyin Egypt mitmu-a chun Israel miho chu khohsahna apetan ahi. Chukal valin mipa Mosi chu mipi mitmu le Pharaoh sohte mitmun Egypt gam sunga mi minthang tah ahitan ahi.
target: (The Lord made the Egyptians favorably disposed toward the people, and Moses himself was highly regarded in Egypt by Pharaoh’s officials and by the people.)

source: Chuin Mosi'n, Pakaiyin hitin aseije, Jan khangkim donle Egypt gamsung lailung tah-a kalut ding:
target: So Moses said, “This is what the Lord says: ‘About midnight I will go throughout Egypt.

source: Chule Egypt gamsunga chapa peng masapen jouse, laltouna-a tou Pharaoh chapa lenpena pat, sumheija sohnu chapa lenpen changeija thisoh hel dingu; chule gancha asoh masapen ho jong thisoh hel dingu ahi.
target: Every firstborn son in Egypt will die, from the firstborn son of Pharaoh, who sits on the throne, to the firstborn son of the female slave, who is at her hand mill, and all the firstborn of the cattle as well.

source: Chule Egypt gamsung jouse-a chu kana nasatah umding, hitobang hi anaum khalou ahin, umjong umkit louhel ding ahi.
target: There will be loud wailing throughout Egypt—worse than there has ever been or ever will be again.

source: Ahin Israel chate douna-a vang, mihem douna hihen le gancha douna hijongle, uichan jong alei achalohsah louding ahi; chutia chu nanghon Egypt mite le Israel kah-a Pakaiyin ichana kikhena akoiham ti nahet ding ahi.
target: But among the Israelites not a dog will bark at any person or animal.’ Then you will know that the Lord makes a distinction between Egypt and Israel.

source: Chuteng hiche nasohte jouse hi kahenga hung suh uva, ka-angsunga bohkhup diu, Chedohtan, nanungjui mipi jouse toh: ahung tidingu; chujou teng keima kachedoh ding ahi, ati. Chuin ama Pharaoh koma konchun lunghang tah-in apotdohtan ahi.
target: All these officials of yours will come to me, bowing down before me and saying, ‘Go, you and all the people who follow you!’ After that I will leave.” Then Moses, hot with anger, left Pharaoh.

source: Chuin Pakaiyin Mosi henga, Egypt gamsunga hi kathilbol kidang apun chehcheh theina dinga Pharaoh'in nathu angailou ding ahi, ati.
target: The Lord had said to Moses, “Pharaoh will refuse to listen to you—so that my wonders may be multiplied in Egypt.”

source: Chuin Mosi le Aaron'in Pharaoh angsunga hiche thilkidang hojouse hi abol lhonin: chule Israel chate chu agama kona asoldohlou nadingin, Pakaiyin Pharaoh lung chu atahsah-in ahi.
target: Moses and Aaron performed all these wonders before Pharaoh, but the Lord hardened Pharaoh’s heart, and he would not let the Israelites go out of his country.

source: Chuin Pakaiyin Egypt gama Mosi le Aaron henga chun aseijin, hitin ati,
target: The Lord said to Moses and Aaron in Egypt,

source: Hiche lhahi nangho dinga lha kipatna hiding: nangho dinga kumsunga lha masapen chu hiding ahi.
target: “This month is to be for you the first month, the first month of your year.

source: Israel mipi kikhom ho jouse henga chun thu seilhonin lang, hitin seilhonin, Hiche lha nisom chan ni hile mitinin ama-a dingin kelngoinou khatcheh kilah-u hen, apu apateu insung dungjuija in khatna dinga kelngoinou khatcheh hiding ahi:
target: Tell the whole community of Israel that on the tenth day of this month each man is to take a lamb for his family, one for each household.

source: Chule ijemtia insung khat chu kelngoinou khat dinga alhom behseh-a ahile, amale a-inhengpa chun kelngoinou khat chu amijatnu dungjuijin kilah-u hen; mitinin ava khamcheh-a aneh dingjat dungjuija kelngoinouva dinga chu mi nasimtoh dingu ahi.
target: If any household is too small for a whole lamb, they must share one with their nearest neighbor, having taken into account the number of people there are. You are to determine the amount of lamb needed in accordance with what each person will eat.

source: Na kelngoinouvu chu nolna beihel, achal kum khat lhingbep hiding: nanghon hichu kelngoi ham, ahiloule kelcha hama kona nalah dingu ahi.
target: The animals you choose must be year-old males without defect, and you may take them from the sheep or the goats.

source: Chule nanghon chuche lha ni somle nili chan ni geija nakoi dingu: chule Israel mipi kikhom khomho jouse chun nilhah teng atha dingu ahi.
target: Take care of them until the fourteenth day of the month, when all the members of the community of Israel must slaughter them at twilight.

source: Chule amahon athisan chu alah uva, aneh nadiu inho kotchung teni le achung jolla chu anu dingu ahi.
target: Then they are to take some of the blood and put it on the sides and tops of the doorframes of the houses where they eat the lambs.

source: Chule amaho chuche jan chule aphe chu meija agouva, cholsolou changlhah toh an-che kha toh ame dingu ahi.
target: That same night they are to eat the meat roasted over the fire, along with bitter herbs, and bread made without yeast.

source: Asela naneh loudiu, chule twija kihon jong naneh lou dingu, amavang alu jong akeng jong chule asung jouse puma meija nasahmin tho dingu ahi.
target: Do not eat the meat raw or boiled in water, but roast it over a fire—with the head, legs and internal organs.

source: Chule nanghon jingkah geija khatcha nakoilou dingu ahi; jingkah geija anaumden tapouchu meija nagovam dingu ahi.
target: Do not leave any of it till morning; if some is left till morning, you must burn it.

source: Chule hitia hi naneh dingu ahi; tai kigah pum le kengchot kise pum, chule nakhut uva natenggolu kichoi puma kinotah-a naneh dingu ahi: hichehi Pakai kalchuh ahi.
target: This is how you are to eat it: with your cloak tucked into your belt, your sandals on your feet and your staff in your hand. Eat it in haste; it is the Lord ’s Passover.

source: Ajehchu tujan tengle keiman Egypt gamsung kahin jotpa ding, Egypt gamsunga mihem le gancha apeng masa jouse kathagam ding; chule Egypt pathen jouse chunga jong thutanna kalhunsah ding ahi: keima Pakai chu kahi.
target: “On that same night I will pass through Egypt and strike down every firstborn of both people and animals, and I will bring judgment on all the gods of Egypt. I am the Lord .

source: Chule thisan chu nangho dinga na-umnao inho chunga melchih na-a pangding; chule thisan chu kamu teng, nangho chu kakalchuh ding; Egypt gam kahin got teng, hise chu nangho sumang dinga nachung uva chulou ding ahi.
target: The blood will be a sign for you on the houses where you are, and when I see the blood, I will pass over you. No destructive plague will touch you when I strike Egypt.

source: Chule hiche nikho hi nangho dinga hetjingna hiding; chule nanghon hichehi nakhang lhumkei uva Pakaiya dinga kutna nanit dingu; nanghon hiche kut hi a-itih-a chonna dan kisuna nanit dingu ahi.
target: “This is a day you are to commemorate; for the generations to come you shall celebrate it as a festival to the Lord —a lasting ordinance.

source: Nanghon ni sagi cholsolou changlhah naneh diu; ni masa ni-a patna na-in houva kona chol nakoidoh diu ahi. Ajehchu koihile nimasa ni-a patna ni sagi changeija chola kisem changlhah netapou chu, hiche mipa chu Israel lah-a kona paidoh-a umding ahi.
target: For seven days you are to eat bread made without yeast. On the first day remove the yeast from your houses, for whoever eats anything with yeast in it from the first day through the seventh must be cut off from Israel.

source: Chule nimasani chule nangho dinga kikhoppi theng umding; chule ani sagi ni jongleh kikhoppi theng umkit ding ahi; chule hiche nikho ho-a chu natoh imacha natohlou dingu; amitinin anehsohkei dingu ahin, nehding bou chu nakibol thei dingu ahi.
target: On the first day hold a sacred assembly, and another one on the seventh day. Do no work at all on these days, except to prepare food for everyone to eat; that is all you may do.

source: Chule nanghon cholsolou changlhah kut chu nanit dingu ahi; ajehchu chuche nilele-a chu nagalsat hou Egypt gama kona kapuidoh ahiuve. Hijeh-a chu hiche nikho hi a-itih-a akhang akhanga chonna dan kisuna nanit dingu ahi.
target: “Celebrate the Festival of Unleavened Bread, because it was on this very day that I brought your divisions out of Egypt. Celebrate this day as a lasting ordinance for the generations to come.

source: Nanghon lha masapen chuche lha nisomle nili nilhah-a pat, chuche lha mama nisomni le nikhat nilhah changeija cholsolou changlhah naneh dingu ahi.
target: In the first month you are to eat bread made without yeast, from the evening of the fourteenth day until the evening of the twenty-first day.

source: Ni sagi sunga chu chol him him na-inhouva kimulouhel ding ahi: ajehchu koi hijongle chol kiso netapou chu, maljin hihen, gamsunga peng hijongle, chutobang michu Israel mipi kikhomho lah-a kona paidoh-a umding ahi.
target: For seven days no yeast is to be found in your houses. And anyone, whether foreigner or native-born, who eats anything with yeast in it must be cut off from the community of Israel.

source: Chol kiso tapou imacha nanehlou dingu ahi; nachenna mun jouseuva cholsolou changlhah bou naneh dingu ahi, ati.
target: Eat nothing made with yeast. Wherever you live, you must eat unleavened bread.”

source: Chujouvin Mosi'n Israel upaho jouse akouvin, ajah uva, Kelngoinou chu kikaijun lang, na insungmi cheh-u dungjuijin kalchuh sa chu that taovin.
target: Then Moses summoned all the elders of Israel and said to them, “Go at once and select the animals for your families and slaughter the Passover lamb.

source: Chule nanghon hyssop bohkhat nalah uva, lheng sunga um thisan lah-a chu nadelut dingu, chuche lheng sunga um thisana chu kotbeng teni le kotchungjol chu nanu dingu: chule jingkah ahunghi kahse-a koimacha a-inkot khah-a kona potdoh louding ahi.
target: Take a bunch of hyssop, dip it into the blood in the basin and put some of the blood on the top and on both sides of the doorframe. None of you shall go out of the door of your house until morning.

source: Ajehchu Egypt mite sugam dinga Pakaiyin ahin jotpa ding ahin; chule aman kotchin teni le kotchungvuma thisan chu amutengle, Pakaiyin hiche kot chu akalchuh ding, nangho sugam dinga suhmangna chu na-insungu ahin lutsah louding ahi.
target: When the Lord goes through the land to strike down the Egyptians, he will see the blood on the top and sides of the doorframe and will pass over that doorway, and he will not permit the destroyer to enter your houses and strike you down.

source: Chule hiche thil hi nangho le nachapa teovin a-itih-a chonna danna nanit jing dingu ahi.
target: “Obey these instructions as a lasting ordinance for you and your descendants.

source: Chule hung hitiding ahi, athutep banga Pakaiyin napeh dingu gamsung chu nalhun phat tengu jongle, hiche natoh hi nanit jomjing dingu ahi.
target: When you enter the land that the Lord will give you as he promised, observe this ceremony.

source: Chule hung hitiding ahi, nachateovin naheng uva, Hiche natoh hi ipi vetsahna ham? ati phat tengule;
target: And when your children ask you, ‘What does this ceremony mean to you?’

source: Nanghon, Aman Egypt mite asuhgama eiho eihuhdoh laijuva, Egypt gama Israel chate inho kalchuhpa Pakai kalchuh ganlhaina chu ahi nati dingu ahi, ati. Chuin mipi chu akunun Pathen ahou taovin ahi.
target: then tell them, ‘It is the Passover sacrifice to the Lord , who passed over the houses of the Israelites in Egypt and spared our homes when he struck down the Egyptians.’ ” Then the people bowed down and worshiped.

source: Chuin Israel chate chu achemangun, Pakaiyin Mosi le Aaron athupeh bangchun aboltaove.
target: The Israelites did just what the Lord commanded Moses and Aaron.

source: Chuin ahitin ahi, Pakaiyin khangkimin alaltouna-a tou Pharaoh cha masapena pat gal hing kikaija songkul'a kihen cha masapen geijin, Egypt gamsunga apeng masapen jouse athat gamin; chule gancha masapen ho jouse jong athat gam tan ahi.
target: At midnight the Lord struck down all the firstborn in Egypt, from the firstborn of Pharaoh, who sat on the throne, to the firstborn of the prisoner, who was in the dungeon, and the firstborn of all the livestock as well.

source: Chuin Pharaoh chu jan-in athouvin, asohho jouse le Egypt mite jouse chu athoudoh uvin; chule Egypt gama chun kana nasatah aumtan ahi; ajehchu mithi louna in khatcha jong umlou ahi.
target: Pharaoh and all his officials and all the Egyptians got up during the night, and there was loud wailing in Egypt, for there was not a house without someone dead.

source: Chuin aman jan-in Mosi le Aaron chu akouvin, aheng lhona, Kipatdoh-un, nangni le Israel chate chu kamite-a konin chedoh taovin; chule cheovin lang nasei bangin Pakai chu gajen taovin.
target: During the night Pharaoh summoned Moses and Aaron and said, “Up! Leave my people, you and the Israelites! Go, worship the Lord as you have requested.

source: Chule naseilhon bangin nabonghou le nagancha hou jouse jong kipuijun lang chetaovin; chule keijong phatthei neiboh-un, ati.
target: Take your flocks and herds, as you have said, and go. And also bless me.”

source: Chuin Egypt mite chun chuche miho chu gamsunga kona gangtah-a soldoh loina ding chun akinotaove; ajehchu amahon, Eiho mithi ihisoh diu ahitai, atiuve.
target: The Egyptians urged the people to hurry and leave the country. “For otherwise,” they said, “we will all die!”

source: Chuin miho chun achangbong amehsao chu chol kiso masangin akichoijun, achanglhah mehnao kongho pona kijel chu alengkou uva akiput taovin ahi.
target: So the people took their dough before the yeast was added, and carried it on their shoulders in kneading troughs wrapped in clothing.

source: Chule Israel chate chun Mosi seibang chun abolun; amahon Egypt mite-a konin sana le dangka-a kisem kijepnaho le vonho chu akithumun ahi.
target: The Israelites did as Moses instructed and asked the Egyptians for articles of silver and gold and for clothing.

source: Chuin Pakaiyin Israel mite chu Egypt mite mitmun khotona amusah-in, hiti chun amahon athum chanu chu apeuvin ahi. Chutichun amahon Egypt mite chu achom gamun ahi.
target: The Lord had made the Egyptians favorably disposed toward the people, and they gave them what they asked for; so they plundered the Egyptians.

source: Chuin Israel chate chu Rameses'a konin Succoth lama ajin taovin, amaho chu nunao chapang simlouvin, kenga lamjot cheh pasal sangjagup ahiuve.
target: The Israelites journeyed from Rameses to Sukkoth. There were about six hundred thousand men on foot, besides women and children.

source: Chule choplop mihonpi chu amaho toh achetou khomun; chule kelngoihon, bonghon, chule gancha tamtah toh alhon khomun ahi.
target: Many other people went up with them, and also large droves of livestock, both flocks and herds.

source: Chule amahon Egypt gama kona ahinkipoh-u changbong mehsa-a chun cholsolou changlhah akangun ahi, ajehchu chol kiso louva ahi; ijeh inem itile Egypt gama kona asotdoh tho jengu ahijeh-a, amaho akhongai sot thei louvu, nehding imacha akigotman louvu ahi.
target: With the dough the Israelites had brought from Egypt, they baked loaves of unleavened bread. The dough was without yeast because they had been driven out of Egypt and did not have time to prepare food for themselves.

source: Tun Egypt gama cheng Israel chate akhopemnao phatsung chu kum jali le kum somthum ahi.
target: Now the length of time the Israelite people lived in Egypt was 430 years.

source: Chuin kum jali le kum somthum kichaijin ahitin ahi, chuche nile le chun ahitin ahi, Pakai janel jouse chu Egypt gama konin apotdoh taovin ahi.
target: At the end of the 430 years, to the very day, all the Lord ’s divisions left Egypt.

source: Hiche hi Egypt gama kona ahinpuidoh jeh uva Pakai geldohna dinga anitdiu jan chu ahi. Hiche hi Israel chate jousen akhanguva anitdiu Pakai jan chu ahi.
target: Because the Lord kept vigil that night to bring them out of Egypt, on this night all the Israelites are to keep vigil to honor the Lord for the generations to come.

source: Chuin Pakaiyin Mosi le Aaron henga, Kalchuh kut kiman dingdan chu hichehi ahi; maljin koimachan hichu aneh louding ahi:
target: The Lord said to Moses and Aaron, “These are the regulations for the Passover meal: “No foreigner may eat it.

source: Ahin suma kicho soh vangchu, nangman achep natanjou tengle, hichu aneh theiding ahi.
target: Any slave you have bought may eat it after you have circumcised him,

source: Gamchom mi le soh sum thalo vang chun hichu aneh theilou ding ahi.
target: but a temporary resident or a hired worker may not eat it.

source: Hichu inkhat sunga nehding ahin; nanghon aphe khatjeng jong inpolama nachoidoh lou dingu; chule agujong nasuhboh lou dingu ahi.
target: “It must be eaten inside the house; take none of the meat outside the house. Do not break any of the bones.

source: Israel mipi ho chun hiche hi anit dingu ahi.
target: The whole community of Israel must celebrate it.

source: Maljin khat nakoma pema auma, Pakai dinga kalchuh kut anit dinga ahile, apasal jousen chep tanu henlang, chujou tengle hinnai hen, chule hichu nit hen; chutengle ama chuche gama penga mikhat tobang hiding ahi. Ajehchu chep tanlou tapou chun hichu anehlou dingu ahi.
target: “A foreigner residing among you who wants to celebrate the Lord ’s Passover must have all the males in his household circumcised; then he may take part like one born in the land. No uncircumcised male may eat it.

source: Agam sunga peng hihen, nalah uva hung khopem gamdangmi hijongle, dan khat bou hiding ahi, ati.
target: The same law applies both to the native-born and to the foreigner residing among you.”

source: Chutichun Israel chate jousen abol taovin; Pakaiyin Mosi le Aaron athupeh bangchun abol taovin ahi.
target: All the Israelites did just what the Lord had commanded Moses and Aaron.

source: Chuin chuche nilele chun ahitin ahi, Pakaiyin Israel chate chu aloi loijin Egypt gama konin apuidohtan ahi.
target: And on that very day the Lord brought the Israelites out of Egypt by their divisions.

source: Chuin Pakaiyin Mosi henga thu aseijin, hitin ati,
target: The Lord said to Moses,

source: Israel chate lah-a naobu hinphukeh-a apeng masa jouse chu mihem hihen gancha hijongle kahenga thenso soh keijun: hichu keija ahi, ati.
target: “Consecrate to me every firstborn male. The first offspring of every womb among the Israelites belongs to me, whether human or animal.”

source: Chuin Mosi'n mipi ho henga aseijin, Nanghon Egypt gamsung sohchana in'a kona nahungdoh nao hiche nikhohi hejingun; ajeh chu Pakaiyin khut thahatna hiche mun'a kona chu nahin puidoh-u ahi. Chol kiso changlhah naneh loudingu ahi.
target: Then Moses said to the people, “Commemorate this day, the day you came out of Egypt, out of the land of slavery, because the Lord brought you out of it with a mighty hand. Eat nothing containing yeast.

source: Abib lha hiche nikho-a hi nahung potdoh-u ahi.
target: Today, in the month of Aviv, you are leaving.

source: Chule Pakaiyin Canaan miho, Hit miho, Amon miho, Hiv miho, chule Jebus miho gam, napu napateu pehdinga akihahselna khoiju le bangnoi lona gama chu napuilut phat tengule, hiche lha ngeija hi hiche kin kibol hi nanit jing dingu ahi.
target: When the Lord brings you into the land of the Canaanites, Hittites, Amorites, Hivites and Jebusites—the land he swore to your ancestors to give you, a land flowing with milk and honey—you are to observe this ceremony in this month:

source: Nisagi cholsolou changlhah naneh dingu, chule ani sagi ni chu Pakaiya dinga kut hiding ahi.
target: For seven days eat bread made without yeast and on the seventh day hold a festival to the Lord .

source: Nisagi chol solou changlhah nehding ahin; nakom him himuva chol kiso changlhah kimulou ding, nachennao mun jouse vellah-a jong chol him him kimulou ding ahi.
target: Eat unleavened bread during those seven days; nothing with yeast in it is to be seen among you, nor shall any yeast be seen anywhere within your borders.

source: Chule chuche nikho chule nachapa nahetsah-a, ajah-a, Egypt gama kona kahung potdoh-a Pakaiyin kachunga anatohho jeh-a hichehi kibola ahi, tia naseipeh ding ahi.
target: On that day tell your son, ‘I do this because of what the Lord did for me when I came out of Egypt.’

source: Chule Pakai danthu chu nakama aumtheina dinga, hiche hi nakhut chunga melchihna hiding, chule namit teni kikah-a hetjingna hiding ahi. Ajehchu Pakaiyin khut thahat tah-a Egypt gama kona napuidoh ahi.
target: This observance will be for you like a sign on your hand and a reminder on your forehead that this law of the Lord is to be on your lips. For the Lord brought you out of Egypt with his mighty hand.

source: Hijeh chun kumseh le hiche dan kisem hi aphatseh-a nanit jingding ahi.
target: You must keep this ordinance at the appointed time year after year.

source: Chule napu napate le nangma henga ana kihahselna banga, Pakaiyin Canaan miho gama napuilutna, hiche gam chu napeh tengle hitiding ahi,
target: “After the Lord brings you into the land of the Canaanites and gives it to you, as he promised on oath to you and your ancestors,

source: Nangman naobu hinphukeh masa jouse le nagancha apeng masa chengse chu Pakai dinga nachom khen ding ahi; pasal ho chu Pakaiya ding ahi.
target: you are to give over to the Lord the first offspring of every womb. All the firstborn males of your livestock belong to the Lord .

source: Chule sangan asoh masa chengse chu kelngoinouva nalhatdoh ding; nalhatdoh louding ahile angong chu naheboh ding ahi. Nachate lah-a apeng masapen pasal jouse chu nalhatdoh ding ahi.
target: Redeem with a lamb every firstborn donkey, but if you do not redeem it, break its neck. Redeem every firstborn among your sons.

source: Chule hitiding ahi, phat ahung lhung ding ho-a chu nachapan, Hichehi ipi tina ham? tia nahindoh tengle, nangman ahenga, Pakaiyin akhut thahat chun Egypt gam sohchana in'a kona eina lhatdoh ahi:
target: “In days to come, when your son asks you, ‘What does this mean?’ say to him, ‘With a mighty hand the Lord brought us out of Egypt, out of the land of slavery.

source: Chule ahitin ahi, Pharaoh chun eisoldoh nomlou phatnun, Pakaiyin Egypt gama mihem le gancha apeng masa jouse chu atha gam jeh-a keiman naobu hinphukeh-a apeng masa pasal jouse chu Pakai koma kalhandoh ahi; ahivangin kachate lah-a apeng masa jouse chu kalhatdoh-in ahi.
target: When Pharaoh stubbornly refused to let us go, the Lord killed the firstborn of both people and animals in Egypt. This is why I sacrifice to the Lord the first male offspring of every womb and redeem each of my firstborn sons.’

source: Chule hiche hi nakhut chunga melchihna le namit teni kikah-a hetjingna hiding ahi: ajehchu khut thahatna Pakaiyin Egypt gama kona eipuidoh-u ahi, nati ding ahi, ati.
target: And it will be like a sign on your hand and a symbol on your forehead that the Lord brought us out of Egypt with his mighty hand.”

source: Chuin ahitin ahi, Pharaoh'in mipi ho chu asoldoh phatnin, alampi chu anai vangin Pathen'in Philistine mite gam jotna lampia chun amaho apuipon ahi: ajehchu Pathen'in, Achuti loule mipi ho chun galkisat amutengule kisih untin, Egypt lama kilekit getnunte, ati ahi.
target: When Pharaoh let the people go, God did not lead them on the road through the Philistine country, though that was shorter. For God said, “If they face war, they might change their minds and return to Egypt.”

source: Ahin Pathen'in mipi chu twipi san jotna gamthip lampia chun apuijin;chule Israel chate chu Egypt gama kon chun galsat dinga kigosan akitol tou taovin ahi.
target: So God led the people around by the desert road toward the Red Sea. The Israelites went up out of Egypt ready for battle.

source: Chuin Mosi'n Joseph guho chu apon ahi: ajehchu aman Israel chate chu ana kihahsel sah-a, ajah uva, Pathen'in nangho thonlouva nahungvil dingu ahin; chule nanghon kagu hi hikoma kona napohtou dingu ahi, anati ahi.
target: Moses took the bones of Joseph with him because Joseph had made the Israelites swear an oath. He had said, “God will surely come to your aid, and then you must carry my bones up with you from this place.”

source: Chuin amaho Succoth'a konin akipat doh-un, gamthip chin Etham'a agebuh-u asongun ahi.
target: After leaving Sukkoth they camped at Etham on the edge of the desert.

source: Chuin sun le jana achetheina diuvin Pakai chu sun le meibang khompin amasanguva achen, chule jan le meikong khompin amaho chu vah pedingin amasanguva achepeh-in ahi.
target: By day the Lord went ahead of them in a pillar of cloud to guide them on their way and by night in a pillar of fire to give them light, so that they could travel by day or night.

source: Hitichun sun na meibang khompi le jana meikong khompi chu mipi ho masanga konchun alamangpon ahi.
target: Neither the pillar of cloud by day nor the pillar of fire by night left its place in front of the people.

source: Chuin Pakaiyin Mosi henga thu aseijin, hitin ati,
target: Then the Lord said to Moses,

source: Israel chate henga, amaho kiheijuva Baal-zephon maijona um Migdol le twikhanglen kah-a Pi-hahiroth mun'a gebuh akison nadiuvin seipeh-in: hiche masanga chu twikhanglen panga gebuh nason dingu ahi.
target: “Tell the Israelites to turn back and encamp near Pi Hahiroth, between Migdol and the sea. They are to encamp by the sea, directly opposite Baal Zephon.

source: Ajehchu Pharaoh'in Israel chate thudola, Amaho gamsunga chun a-ohden taovin, gamthip chun amaho akhakhum den ahitaove, atiding ahi.
target: Pharaoh will think, ‘The Israelites are wandering around the land in confusion, hemmed in by the desert.’

source: Chule keiman Pharaoh lungsung chu kasuh tah ding, aman amaho ahin nungdel ding ahin; chule Egypt miten keima Pakai kahi ahetna dinguva, keima Pharaoh le asepaiho jouse chunga jabola kaum ding ahi. Chuin amahon hiti chun abol taovin ahi.
target: And I will harden Pharaoh’s heart, and he will pursue them. But I will gain glory for myself through Pharaoh and all his army, and the Egyptians will know that I am the Lord .” So the Israelites did this.

source: Chuin Egypt lengpa henga mipi chu ajam taove ti aseipeh taovin ahi. Chuin Pharaoh le asohte lungsung chu mipi ho douna chun akiheitan, chule amahon, Ipi dinga hiche hi inaboluva, eiho eijen naova kona Israel chu isoldoh-u hitam? atiuve.
target: When the king of Egypt was told that the people had fled, Pharaoh and his officials changed their minds about them and said, “What have we done? We have let the Israelites go and have lost their services!”

source: Chuin aman asakol kangtalai chu akigotnin, amite chu akipuijin ahi.
target: So he had his chariot made ready and took his army with him.

source: Chuin aman lhentum sakol kangtalai jagup le Egypt sakol kangtalai jouse, chule khatcheh chunga sepai lamkaiho chu akipuijin ahi.
target: He took six hundred of the best chariots, along with all the other chariots of Egypt, with officers over all of them.

source: Chuin Pakaiyin Egypt lengpa Pharaoh lungsung chu atahsahtan, aman Israel chate chu anungdel tai; chule Israel chate chu hangtah-a chedoh-a ahitaove.
target: The Lord hardened the heart of Pharaoh king of Egypt, so that he pursued the Israelites, who were marching out boldly.

source: Ahivangin Egypt mite chun Pharaoh sakol kangtalai ho le sakol jouse, asakol chung tou miho, chule asepaihon chutoh amaho chu anungdel taovin, chuin amaho chu Baal-zephon phah masang Pi-hahiroth kom, twikhanglen panga agebuh ason naova chun apha taovin ahi.
target: The Egyptians—all Pharaoh’s horses and chariots, horsemen and troops—pursued the Israelites and overtook them as they camped by the sea near Pi Hahiroth, opposite Baal Zephon.

source: Chuin Pharaoh ahung nai phatnin, Israel chate akhodah uvin ahile, veuvin, Egypt mite chu anunguva ahung kijot jot jenguvin; chuin amaho akicha talheh jengun ahi. Chuin Israel chate chu Pakai henga atao taovin ahi.
target: As Pharaoh approached, the Israelites looked up, and there were the Egyptians, marching after them. They were terrified and cried out to the Lord .

source: Chuin amahon Mosi henga, Egypt gama lhankhuh umlou hija gamthipma thidinga neipuidoh-u ham? Nangman ibola Egypt gama kona neipuidoh uva, hitia hi neibolu ham?
target: They said to Moses, “Was it because there were no graves in Egypt that you brought us to the desert to die? What have you done to us by bringing us out of Egypt?

source: Egypt mite kajen theina diuvin neilimsah hih-un tia Egypt gama kanaseiju chu hiche thuhi hilou ham? ajehchu gamthipma kathigam sang uva Egypt mite kajenu chu keiho dinga phajo ahi, atiuve.
target: Didn’t we say to you in Egypt, ‘Leave us alone; let us serve the Egyptians’? It would have been better for us to serve the Egyptians than to die in the desert!”

source: Chuin Mosi'n mipi henga, Nangho kicha hih-un, ding thimbeh-un lang, Aman nangho tunia namusah dingu Pakai mi huhhingna chu veuvin: ajehchu tunia namu-u Egypt mite hi a-imatih chana avela namu kitlou dingu ahitai.
target: Moses answered the people, “Do not be afraid. Stand firm and you will see the deliverance the Lord will bring you today. The Egyptians you see today you will never see again.

source: Pakaiyin nangho dinga gal asatding, chule nangho na-umthim beh dingu ahi, ati.
target: The Lord will fight for you; you need only to be still.”

source: Chuin Pakaiyin Mosi henga, Ipi dinga kahenga naka uham? Israel chate chu amalamuva ache nadiuvin ahenguva seipeh-in.
target: Then the Lord said to Moses, “Why are you crying out to me? Tell the Israelites to move on.

source: Ahin nangman natenggol chu domsangin lang, twikhanglen chunga chun nakhut jahdoh-in, hichu hom khenin: chule Israel chaten tolgoa twikhanglen lailung chu ajotdingu ahi.
target: Raise your staff and stretch out your hand over the sea to divide the water so that the Israelites can go through the sea on dry ground.

source: Chule keima, ven, keimatah-in Egypt mite lungsung kasuhtah ding, chule amahon amaho nung chu ajui dingu ahi. Chule Pharaoh le ajanelho jouse, asakol kangtalai ho, chule asakol chunga tou miho chunga keiman jabolna kamuding ahi.
target: I will harden the hearts of the Egyptians so that they will go in after them. And I will gain glory through Pharaoh and all his army, through his chariots and his horsemen.

source: Chule Pharaoh chung le asakol kangtalai chung, chule asakol chungtou miho chunga jabola kaum tengle, Egypt miten keima Pakai kahi chu ahet dingu ahi, ati.
target: The Egyptians will know that I am the Lord when I gain glory through Pharaoh, his chariots and his horsemen.”

source: Chuin Israel gebuh masanga che Pathen vantil chu akichonin, anunguva achen; chule meilhang khompi chu amasanguva kon chun akichonin, anunguva adingtan ahi.
target: Then the angel of God, who had been traveling in front of Israel’s army, withdrew and went behind them. The pillar of cloud also moved from in front and stood behind them,

source: Chuin hichu Israel miho gebuh le Egypt miho gebuh kikah-a chun ahungin; hichu amaho ding chun meilhang le muthim ahin, khat ho ding vang chun janle vah apen ahi. Chutichun jankhovah keijin khatnin khat chu anailutpon ahi.
target: coming between the armies of Egypt and Israel. Throughout the night the cloud brought darkness to the one side and light to the other side; so neither went near the other all night long.

source: Chuin Mosi'n twipi chunga chun akhut ajahdoh tan ahi; chuin Pakaiyin hiche jan chun solam hui hattah mangchan twipi chu alelon sah-in, twipi chu tolgo asosahtan, twiho chu akikhentan ahi.
target: Then Moses stretched out his hand over the sea, and all that night the Lord drove the sea back with a strong east wind and turned it into dry land. The waters were divided,

source: Chuin Israel chate chu twipi lailung tolgoa chun alut taovin; chule twiho chu jetle veija bang bangin akisungin ahi.
target: and the Israelites went through the sea on dry ground, with a wall of water on their right and on their left.

source: Chuin Egypt miho chun anung delun, Pharaoh sakol ho, akangtalai ho, asakol chunga tou miho jouse chu amaho nunga chun twipi lailunga chun alut taovin ahi.
target: The Egyptians pursued them, and all Pharaoh’s horses and chariots and horsemen followed them into the sea.

source: Chuin ahitin ahi, jingkah ahiphatnin Pakaiyin Egypt mite chu meilhang le meikong khompia konin ahinven, Egypt mite janel chu asunohphah tan,
target: During the last watch of the night the Lord looked down from the pillar of fire and cloud at the Egyptian army and threw it into confusion.

source: Asakol kangtalaiju kangho chu alahdoh peh-in ahile amahon gihsatah in atolun ahi. Hijeh chun Egypt miten, Eiho Israel maikoh-a konhin jamtao hite; ajehchu Pakaiyin amaho dinga Egypt mitehi asat ahitai, atiuvin ahi.
target: He jammed the wheels of their chariots so that they had difficulty driving. And the Egyptians said, “Let’s get away from the Israelites! The Lord is fighting for them against Egypt.”

source: Chuin Pakaiyin Mosi henga, Egypt mite sakol ho, akangtalaihou, chule asakol chunga touhou chunga twiho chu ahung lonkhom kitna dingin, twipi chunga chun nakhut jahdoh-in, ati.
target: Then the Lord said to Moses, “Stretch out your hand over the sea so that the waters may flow back over the Egyptians and their chariots and horsemen.”

source: Chuin Mosi'n twipi chunga chun akhut ajahdoh-in ahile, jingkah ahunghi phatnin twipi chu angaija alonhat bangin ahunglong kit tai; chuin Egypt hiche lama chun ajamun; Pakaiyin Egypt mite chu twipi lailunga chun alehlut gamtan ahi.
target: Moses stretched out his hand over the sea, and at daybreak the sea went back to its place. The Egyptians were fleeing toward it, and the Lord swept them into the sea.

source: Chuin twiho chu ahung long gom kitnin, sakol ho, kangtalai ho, sakol chunga touho, chule amaho hin nungdel twipi sunga lut ho Pharaoh janelho jouse chu achuptan; khatcha jong asohcha aum pouvin ahi.
target: The water flowed back and covered the chariots and horsemen—the entire army of Pharaoh that had followed the Israelites into the sea. Not one of them survived.

source: Ahivangin Israel chaten twipi lailunga chun tolgo laija lam ajotnun; chule twiho chu amaho dingin ajetlam le aveilam uva bang bangin akisungin ahi.
target: But the Israelites went through the sea on dry ground, with a wall of water on their right and on their left.

source: Chutichun Pakaiyin chuche nikho chun Israel chate chu Egypt mite khutna konin ahuhhingtan; chule twipanga konin Israelte chun Egypt mite athiu chu amuvin ahi.
target: That day the Lord saved Israel from the hands of the Egyptians, and Israel saw the Egyptians lying dead on the shore.

source: Chuin Israel ten Egypt mite chunga Pakai natoh loupi chu amutaovin ahi: chule mipichun Pakai chu aging taovin, Pakai le asoh Mosi chu atahsan taove.
target: And when the Israelites saw the mighty hand of the Lord displayed against the Egyptians, the people feared the Lord and put their trust in him and in Moses his servant.

source: Chujouvin Mosi le Israel chate chun Pakai henga hiche la hi asaovin, hitihin aseijuve: Loupitah-a gal ajotah jeh-in, keiman Pakai henga la sange; aman sakol le achunga toupa chu twipi sunga alehlut tai.
target: Then Moses and the Israelites sang this song to the Lord : “I will sing to the Lord , for he is highly exalted. Both horse and driver he has hurled into the sea.

source: Pakai chu kahatna le ka la ahin, chule eihuhinga jong ahung hitai. Ama ka Pathen ahin, keiman ama kavahchoi ding; Ama kapa Pathen ahin, keiman kachoi sang ding ahi.
target: “The Lord is my strength and my defense; he has become my salvation. He is my God, and I will praise him, my father’s God, and I will exalt him.

source: Pakai chu gal hatmi ahi. Pakai chu amin ahi.
target: The Lord is a warrior; the Lord is his name.

source: Pharaoh sakol kangtalai ho le asepai janel chu aman twipi sunga alehlutnin; asepai lamkai lhenchom ho jongchu twipi sana alhalut gam tan ahi.
target: Pharaoh’s chariots and his army he has hurled into the sea. The best of Pharaoh’s officers are drowned in the Red Sea.

source: Twi thuh-in achupsoh taovin; twi thuhtah noija chun song bangin alhalut taove.
target: The deep waters have covered them; they sank to the depths like a stone.

source: Vo Pakai nakhut jetlam chu thanei na-in aloupin: vo Pakai nakhut jetlam chun melma chu asuchip tan ahi.
target: Your right hand, Lord , was majestic in power. Your right hand, Lord , shattered the enemy.

source: Naletna chungnunga chun nangma douna-a kipanho chu najoutan; nalunghanna chu nahin soldoh-in, amaho chu changpol bangin akavam taovin ahi.
target: “In the greatness of your majesty you threw down those who opposed you. You unleashed your burning anger; it consumed them like stubble.

source: Nanah hai chun twiho chu akhom khomin, twisoh chu alhuh-in adingden tan, chule twithuh chu twipi lailunga adingchah dentan ahi.
target: By the blast of your nostrils the waters piled up. The surging waters stood up like a wall; the deep waters congealed in the heart of the sea.

source: Melma chun, Keiman kanungdel ding, kaphah pa-a thil kichomdohho chu kahop khending; kangaichat chu achunguva kasuh bulhit ding; kachemjam kasa doh-a, kakhutnin amaho asuhmang ding ahi, ati.
target: The enemy boasted, ‘I will pursue, I will overtake them. I will divide the spoils; I will gorge myself on them. I will draw my sword and my hand will destroy them.’

source: Nangman nahui chun namutnin ahile, twipi chun amaho chu akhukhum tan: twi thuh sunga chun amaho chu ngen bangin alhalut taovin ahi.
target: But you blew with your breath, and the sea covered them. They sank like lead in the mighty waters.

source: Vo Pakai, pathen ho lah-a hi nangma tobang koi umam? nangma tobanga thenna-a loupi, pachat naho-a gin um, chule thil kidang ho bolla koi umam?
target: Who among the gods is like you, Lord ? Who is like you— majestic in holiness, awesome in glory, working wonders?

source: Nangman nakhut jetlam najah doh-in, leisetnin amaho chu aval lhumtai.
target: “You stretch out your right hand, and the earth swallows your enemies.

source: Nangman nami hepina-in nalhatdohsa namite chu napui doh-in, nangman nathahatna-in amaho chu nachenna munthenga chun napui lhungtan ahi.
target: In your unfailing love you will lead the people you have redeemed. In your strength you will guide them to your holy dwelling.

source: Mipi chun jaovintin, chule kichadiu: Philistine mite chenna munchu lungkham na-a dimding ahi.
target: The nations will hear and tremble; anguish will grip the people of Philistia.

source: Chuteng Edom lenghon hichu kidang asahdiu; Moab mihat ho chu kihot hotdiu; Canaan gama cheng ho jouse chu junmang diu ahi.
target: The chiefs of Edom will be terrified, the leaders of Moab will be seized with trembling, the people of Canaan will melt away;

source: Nangman nachohdohsa namite chu agalkai kahseovin, Vo Pakai, namite chu agalkai kahseuva kichat le tijat na chu amaho chunga chuding; naban thahat nasatah-a chu amaho song banga umthimbeh dingu ahi.
target: terror and dread will fall on them. By the power of your arm they will be as still as a stone— until your people pass by, Lord , until the people you bought pass by.

source: Vo Pakai nangman nachenna dinga nasemna mun, Vo Pakai nakhut tah-a naphudet muntheng, nagoulo molsanga chu amaho chu napuilutna nachensah ding ahi.
target: You will bring them in and plant them on the mountain of your inheritance— the place, Lord , you made for your dwelling, the sanctuary, Lord, your hands established.

source: Pakaiyin atonsot atonsotna lengvai apohding ahi.
target: “The Lord reigns for ever and ever.”

source: Ajehchu Pharaoh sakol ho, akangtalai ho leh, asakol chunga touho toh twipi sunga alutnuvin, chuin Pakaiyin twipi chu achunguva alonsah kittan ahi; ahivangin Israel chate chu twipi lailung tolgo chunga chun acheuvin ahi.
target: When Pharaoh’s horses, chariots and horsemen went into the sea, the Lord brought the waters of the sea back over them, but the Israelites walked through the sea on dry ground.

source: Chuin Aaron sopinu Miriam themgaonu chun akhutna thih khutbeh khat akilah-in; chule numei jouse chun thih khutbeh choipum le lampumin anung ajuijun ahi.
target: Then Miriam the prophet, Aaron’s sister, took a timbrel in her hand, and all the women followed her, with timbrels and dancing.

source: Chuin Miriam'in amaho chu adonbutnin, Nanghon Pakai henga la saovin, ajehchu aman loupitah-a gal ajou tan ahi; aman sakol le achunga toupa chu twipi sunga aleh lutan ahi, ati.
target: Miriam sang to them: “Sing to the Lord , for he is highly exalted. Both horse and driver he has hurled into the sea.”

source: Chuti chun Mosi'n Israel chu twipi sana konchun ahin puijin, Shur gamthipma alut taovin ahi; chuin amaho gamthipma chun nithum acheuvin ahile twi amu tapouvin ahi.
target: Then Moses led Israel from the Red Sea and they went into the Desert of Shur. For three days they traveled in the desert without finding water.

source: Chuin Marah ahung lhun phatnun, Marah mun'a twiho chu akhat jeh-in adonthei tapouvin ahi. Hiche jeh-a chu hiche mun chu Marah kisah-a ahi.
target: When they came to Marah, they could not drink its water because it was bitter. (That is why the place is called Marah.)

source: Chuin mipi ho chu Mosi chunga aphun taovin, Ipi kadondiu ham? atiuvin ahi.
target: So the people grumbled against Moses, saying, “What are we to drink?”

source: Chuin ama Pakai henga akaptan ahileh, Pakaiyin thingphung khat amusah-in, hichu twiho lah-a chun akholutnin ahile, twiho chu atwi tan ahi. Chua chun aman amaho dingin chonadan le thupeh asemin, chule chuachun amaho chu apatepmin,
target: Then Moses cried out to the Lord , and the Lord showed him a piece of wood. He threw it into the water, and the water became fit to drink. There the Lord issued a ruling and instruction for them and put them to the test.

source: Ajah uva, Nanghon Pakai na Pathen'u aw hi chingthei tah-a nangai uva, amitmu-a adih chu nabol uva, chule achondan thu jouse nanit uva ahile, keiman Egypt mite chunga kachuhsah hiche natho hi khatcha jong nachung uva kachuhsah louding ahi; ajehchu keima nangma damsah-a Pakai chu kahi ati.
target: He said, “If you listen carefully to the Lord your God and do what is right in his eyes, if you pay attention to his commands and keep all his decrees, I will not bring on you any of the diseases I brought on the Egyptians, for I am the Lord , who heals you.”

source: Chuin amaho Elim ahung lhungun, chukoma chun twikhuh somleni le lusuphung somsagi aumin ahi. Chuin amahon twipanga chun gebuh asongun ahi.
target: Then they came to Elim, where there were twelve springs and seventy palm trees, and they camped there near the water.

source: Chuin amaho Elim'a konin akholjin kitnun, Egypt gam adalhahnao lhanina ni somle ninga ni tah chun Israel chate mipi kikhomho jouse chu Sinai le Elim kikah-a um Sin gamthip ahunglhung taovin ahi.
target: The whole Israelite community set out from Elim and came to the Desert of Sin, which is between Elim and Sinai, on the fifteenth day of the second month after they had come out of Egypt.

source: Chuin gamthipma chun Israel chate mipi kikhomho jouse chu Mosi le Aaron dounan aphun taovin;
target: In the desert the whole community grumbled against Moses and Aaron.

source: Israel chate chun aheng lhona, Pathen'in Egypt gama sabel ho koma katou uva, nengtah-a changlhah kaneh laijuva Pakai khutna eina thisah joh-u hitavele; ajehchu nangnin hichea mipi ho hi kella thisah dinga hiche gamthipma hi neihin puilutnu ahi, atiuvin ahi.
target: The Israelites said to them, “If only we had died by the Lord ’s hand in Egypt! There we sat around pots of meat and ate all the food we wanted, but you have brought us out into this desert to starve this entire assembly to death.”

source: Hichun Pakaiyin Mosi henga, Ven, keiman nangho dinga van'a kona changlhah kahinjuhsah ding ahin; amaho kadan thua achonuleh achonlouvu kapatep theina dinga, mipi ho chu potdoh uva niseh-a anehkham cheh diu aga kilokhom dingu ahi.
target: Then the Lord said to Moses, “I will rain down bread from heaven for you. The people are to go out each day and gather enough for that day. In this way I will test them and see whether they will follow my instructions.

source: Chule hung hiti ding ahi, anigup nile ahin lokhom hou chu akigontup dingu; hichu niseh-a alokhomu jatni hiding ahi, ati.
target: On the sixth day they are to prepare what they bring in, and that is to be twice as much as they gather on the other days.”

source: Chuin Mosi le Aaron'in Israel chate jouse henga, Nilhah tengleh Egypt gama kona nahinpui doh uva chu Pakai ahi nahet dingu:
target: So Moses and Aaron said to all the Israelites, “In the evening you will know that it was the Lord who brought you out of Egypt,

source: Chule jingkah tengleh Pakai loupi namu dingu ahi; ajehchu Pakai douna-a naphunchel nao chu aman ajatai: keini ipi kahi lhona keini chunga naphunu ham? atilhone.
target: and in the morning you will see the glory of the Lord , because he has heard your grumbling against him. Who are we, that you should grumble against us?”

source: Chuin Mosi'n, Hiche hi nilhah teng Pakaiyin nanehdiu sa napeh uva, jingkah teng changlhah nengtah-a napeh tengule namu dingu ahi; ajehchu Pakaiyin naphun nao, ama douna-a naphun chelnao chu ajatan ahi. Keini koi kahilhon ham? keini douna-a phun nahipouvin, Pakai douna-a phun nahijo bouvui, ati.
target: Moses also said, “You will know that it was the Lord when he gives you meat to eat in the evening and all the bread you want in the morning, because he has heard your grumbling against him. Who are we? You are not grumbling against us, but against the Lord .”

source: Chuin Mosi'n Aaron henga, Israel chate mipi kikhomho henga, Pakai angsunghi hinaijun; ajehchu aman naphun nahou chu ajatai, tin seipeh-in ati.
target: Then Moses told Aaron, “Say to the entire Israelite community, ‘Come before the Lord , for he has heard your grumbling.’ ”

source: Chuin ahitin ahi, Aaron'in Israel chate mipi kikhomho henga thu aseipat patnin, amahon gamthiplam chu aveovin ahile, veuvin, Pakai loupi nachu meilhang lah-a ahung kilah-in ahi.
target: While Aaron was speaking to the whole Israelite community, they looked toward the desert, and there was the glory of the Lord appearing in the cloud.

source: Chuin Pakaiyin Mosi henga thu aseijin, hitin ati,
target: The Lord said to Moses,

source: Israel chate phunchel nachu keiman kajatan ahi. Amaho henga chun, Nilhah teng sa naneh dingu, chule jingkah tengle changlhah-a navaset dingu; chutengle keima Pakai na-Pathen'u kahi nahet dingu ahi, tin seijin, ati.
target: “I have heard the grumbling of the Israelites. Tell them, ‘At twilight you will eat meat, and in the morning you will be filled with bread. Then you will know that I am the Lord your God.’ ”

source: Chuin ahitin ahi, nilhah-in vengkeho chu ahungdoh-un, agebuh uchu atomchah tan ahi. Chule jingkah-in janelho kimvela chun daitwi analhan ahi.
target: That evening quail came and covered the camp, and in the morning there was a layer of dew around the camp.

source: Chuin daitwi lha chu ahul phatnin, veuvin, gamthip tol chunga chun thil lumpilpel neocha cha, buhbang neocha cha tobangin amuvin ahi.
target: When the dew was gone, thin flakes like frost on the ground appeared on the desert floor.

source: Chuin Israel chate chun hichu amuphatnun khatle khat akihouvun, Hiche hi manna ahi atiuve: ajehchu ipi ahi ahetlouvu ahi. Chuin Mosi'n ahenguva, Hichehi Pakaiyin naneh dinguva napeh-u changlhah chu ahi.
target: When the Israelites saw it, they said to each other, “What is it?” For they did not know what it was. Moses said to them, “It is the bread the Lord has given you to eat.

source: Hiche thil hi Pakaiyin ana thupeh chu ahi: Mitinin ama nehkhop cheh, na-insung mijat dungjuijun mikhat cheh-a dingin omer khatcheh; amitakipmin aponbuh sunga umho jouse-a dingin kilokhom cheh hen, ati.
target: This is what the Lord has commanded: ‘Everyone is to gather as much as they need. Take an omer for each person you have in your tent.’ ”

source: Chuin Israel chaten hitichun abolun, abangin atamjep chule abangin alhomjep akilo khomun ahi.
target: The Israelites did as they were told; some gathered much, some little.

source: Chuin amahon omer-a ate phatnun, atam lodoh panjong imacha amoh aneipon, chule alhom lodoh pajong chu alhinglel dehpon; amitinin anehkhop cheh ding akilo khomun ahi.
target: And when they measured it by the omer, the one who gathered much did not have too much, and the one who gathered little did not have too little. Everyone had gathered just as much as they needed.

source: Chuin Mosi'n, Koimachan jingkah changeijin khenhih hen, ati.
target: Then Moses said to them, “No one is to keep any of it until morning.”

source: Ahivangin amahon Mosi thusei chu angaipouvin; alah uva mi phabepmin jingkah geija dingin akhenun, ahin hichu ana thanin, a-uitan ahi. Chuin Mosi achunguva alunghang tan ahi.
target: However, some of them paid no attention to Moses; they kept part of it until morning, but it was full of maggots and began to smell. So Moses was angry with them.

source: Chuti chun jingkah seh le amitakipmin anehkhop cheh ding akilokhom jiuvin; nisa ahung sat tengleh hichu ajunmang jitan ahi.
target: Each morning everyone gathered as much as they needed, and when the sun grew hot, it melted away.

source: Chuin ahitin ahi, anigup ni chule changlhah chu ajatni, mikhat dingin omer nicheh alohkhom jiuvin ahi. Chuin mipi kikhom vaipoho jouse chu ahungun, Mosi ahung hetsah taovin ahi.
target: On the sixth day, they gathered twice as much—two omers for each person—and the leaders of the community came and reported this to Moses.

source: Chuin aman amaho henga chun, Hiche hi Pakaiyin asei chu ahi, Jingkhu Pakaiya dinga kicholdo ni cholngah nitheng ahi. Nahon dingu chu tunin honunlang, nakan dingu chu kanguvin, chua amoh umchu jingkah lama dingin kikoijun, ati.
target: He said to them, “This is what the Lord commanded: ‘Tomorrow is to be a day of sabbath rest, a holy sabbath to the Lord . So bake what you want to bake and boil what you want to boil. Save whatever is left and keep it until morning.’ ”

source: Chuin Mosi'n aseibang chun jingkah changei chun akoijuvin ahile, hichu anengpon, thanjong athan pon ahi.
target: So they saved it until morning, as Moses commanded, and it did not stink or get maggots in it.

source: Chuin Mosi'n, Hichu tunin neovin; ajehchu tuni hi Pakaiya dinga cholngah ni ahi: tunia hichu loujaova namu lou dingu ahi.
target: “Eat it today,” Moses said, “because today is a sabbath to the Lord . You will not find any of it on the ground today.

source: Hichu nigup sunga nalokhom dingu; ajing nisagi ni chu cholngah ni ahin, chuche nikho chule khatcha jong umlou ding ahi, ati.
target: Six days you are to gather it, but on the seventh day, the Sabbath, there will not be any.”

source: Chuin ahitin ahi, mi phabep nisagi ni chun aloh khomdin apotdoh un, ahin khatcha amupouve.
target: Nevertheless, some of the people went out on the seventh day to gather it, but they found none.

source: Chuin Pakaiyin Mosi henga, Kathupeh ho le kadan thuho hi itihchan nitnom louva naum dingu ham?
target: Then the Lord said to Moses, “How long will you refuse to keep my commands and my instructions?

source: Veovin, Pakaiyin cholngah ni napeh jeh uvin, nigup chan nileh nini-a ding changlhah napeh-u ahi; amitakip namun cheh-a umun lang, nisagi nileh aumna mun'a konin koimacha potdoh hihhen, ati.
target: Bear in mind that the Lord has given you the Sabbath; that is why on the sixth day he gives you bread for two days. Everyone is to stay where they are on the seventh day; no one is to go out.”

source: Chutichun mipi chu nisagi nin acholdo taovin ahi.
target: So the people rested on the seventh day.

source: Chuin Israel insung chun hichu amin manna asah-un ahi. Hichu pathikhom mu tobanga bangleh ahin, atuidan chu khoijutoh kihala kisem changlhah tobang ahi.
target: The people of Israel called the bread manna. It was white like coriander seed and tasted like wafers made with honey.

source: Chuin Mosi'n, Hiche thilhi Pakai thupeh chu ahi, Egypt gama kona kapuidoh laijuva gamthipma kavahnao changlhah chu amutheina diuvin; nakhang khanguva umjing dingin omer dimkhat koijun, ati.
target: Moses said, “This is what the Lord has commanded: ‘Take an omer of manna and keep it for the generations to come, so they can see the bread I gave you to eat in the wilderness when I brought you out of Egypt.’ ”

source: Chuin Mosi'n Aaron henga, Bel khat lan lang asunga chun manna omer dimkhat koijin; hichu nakhang khanguva umjing dingin Pakai angsunga koijin, ati.
target: So Moses said to Aaron, “Take a jar and put an omer of manna in it. Then place it before the Lord to be kept for the generations to come.”

source: Chuin Pakaiyin Mosi thu apehbang chun chin jing dingin hettohsahna angsunga chun akoitan ahi.
target: As the Lord commanded Moses, Aaron put the manna with the tablets of the covenant law, so that it might be preserved.

source: Hitichun Israel chaten alo dingu gamsung ahung lhun kahseovin, kum somli sung chun manna chu aneovin; Canaan gam gamgiho ahunglhun kahseovin manna chu aneuvin ahi.
target: The Israelites ate manna forty years, until they came to a land that was settled; they ate manna until they reached the border of Canaan.

source: Tun omer khat chu ephah hop soma hopkhat ahi.
target: (An omer is one-tenth of an ephah.)

source: Chuin Israel chate kikhom khom pumpi chu Sin gamthipma konchun akipatdoh kitnun, Pakai thupeh dungjuijin Rephidim'a chun gebuh asongun ahi. Chuin chukoma chun mipi ho donding twi aumtapon ahi.
target: The whole Israelite community set out from the Desert of Sin, traveling from place to place as the Lord commanded. They camped at Rephidim, but there was no water for the people to drink.

source: Hijeh chun mipi chun Mosi akinah piuvin ajah-a, Kadon dinguvin twi neipeovin atiuvin ahi. Chuin Mosi'n ahenguva, Ipi dinga kei neiki nahpiu ham? Ipi dinga Pakai chu napatep uham? ati.
target: So they quarreled with Moses and said, “Give us water to drink.” Moses replied, “Why do you quarrel with me? Why do you put the Lord to the test?”

source: Chumuna chun mipi chu twi ngaichan adangchah taovin; chule mipichu Mosi chunga chun aphun uvin, ajah-a, Ipi dinga keiho le kachateu chule kagancha hou hi dangchah-a thigamsah dinga Egypt gama kona neipuidoh-u ham? atiuvin ahi.
target: But the people were thirsty for water there, and they grumbled against Moses. They said, “Why did you bring us up out of Egypt to make us and our children and livestock die of thirst?”

source: Chuin Mosi Pakai henga akapmin, Hiche mipi hohi i-kaloding hitam? amahon keima songa selih ding eigo taove, ati.
target: Then Moses cried out to the Lord , “What am I to do with these people? They are almost ready to stone me.”

source: Chuin Pakaiyin Mosi henga, Mipi masanga chun chen, chule Israel upaho chu kipuijin; chule vadung navohna tenggol chu nakhutna kichoijin lang, chen.
target: The Lord answered Moses, “Go out in front of the people. Take with you some of the elders of Israel and take in your hand the staff with which you struck the Nile, and go.

source: Ven, keima namasanga um Horeb songpi chunga khu kadin ding; chule nangman songpi chu navoh ding, hichea kona chu twi hungput doh-a, hichu mipin adonthei dingu ahi, ati. Hitichun Mosi'n Israel upaho mitmu tahchun hitichun aboltan ahi.
target: I will stand there before you by the rock at Horeb. Strike the rock, and water will come out of it for the people to drink.” So Moses did this in the sight of the elders of Israel.

source: Israel chaten Mosi akinahpi jeh-u le Pakai chu ilah uva umam umhih-em, tia Pakai chu apatep jeh uvin, aman chuche mun chu Massah le Meribah asah tan ahi.
target: And he called the place Massah and Meribah because the Israelites quarreled and because they tested the Lord saying, “Is the Lord among us or not?”

source: Chujouvin Amalek mite chu ahungun, Rephidim mun'a chun Israelte chu ahungsat taovin ahi.
target: The Amalekites came and attacked the Israelites at Rephidim.

source: Chuin Mosi'n Joshua jah-a, Ilah uva mi lhengdoh-in, chule cheovinlang Amalek mite khu gakisat piuvin: jingtengle kakhutna Pathen tenggol choipuma lhang chungvuma kadin ding ahi, ati.
target: Moses said to Joshua, “Choose some of our men and go out to fight the Amalekites. Tomorrow I will stand on top of the hill with the staff of God in my hands.”

source: Chutichun Mosi'n ahenga aseibang chun Joshua'n abolin, Amalek mite akisatpi taovin: chuin Mosi, Aaron le Hur chu lhangvuma chun akaltou taovin ahi.
target: So Joshua fought the Amalekites as Moses had ordered, and Moses, Aaron and Hur went to the top of the hill.

source: Chuin ahitin ahi, Mosi'n akhut adopsang phatle Israelte chun ajou jiuvin; aman akhut adoplhah phat phatle Amalek mite chun ajou jiuvin ahi.
target: As long as Moses held up his hands, the Israelites were winning, but whenever he lowered his hands, the Amalekites were winning.

source: Ahin Mosi khut chu ahung khamtan; chuin amanin song alalhonin, anoija akoilhonin, ama achunga atouvin; chule Aaron le Hur chu asih langkhat gela apang lhonin, akhut teni chu adomsang jing lhonin; chutichun akhut chu nisalhum kahsen det tah-in apang tan ahi.
target: When Moses’ hands grew tired, they took a stone and put it under him and he sat on it. Aaron and Hur held his hands up—one on one side, one on the other—so that his hands remained steady till sunset.

source: Chutah chun Joshua'n Amalek le amite chu chemjamin ajoutan ahi.
target: So Joshua overcame the Amalekite army with the sword.

source: Chuin Pakaiyin Mosi henga, Hichehi hetjinga aumna dingin lekhabua suninlang, Joshua nabenga jong jahsah kitnin; ajehchu keiman vannoi'a hi Amalek het jingna chu kasuh manghel ding ahi, ati.
target: Then the Lord said to Moses, “Write this on a scroll as something to be remembered and make sure that Joshua hears it, because I will completely blot out the name of Amalek from under heaven.”

source: Chuin Mosi'n maicham khat asemin, hichu Jehovah-nissi asah-in ahi.
target: Moses built an altar and called it The Lord is my Banner.

source: Ijeh inem itile aman, Ajehchu Pakaiyin akhang khanga Amalek douna-a gal asatding ahi tin Pakai akihahselin ahi, ati.
target: He said, “Because hands were lifted up against the throne of the Lord , the Lord will be at war against the Amalekites from generation to generation.”

source: Chuin Mosi nupapa Midian gam thempu Jethro'n Pathen'in Mosi le ami Israelte athil bolpeh jouse le Egypt gama kona Pakaiyin Israel ahin puidoh chu ajah phatnin;
target: Now Jethro, the priest of Midian and father-in-law of Moses, heard of everything God had done for Moses and for his people Israel, and how the Lord had brought Israel out of Egypt.

source: Mosi nupapa Jethro chun Mosi'n anungsol kit inneipi Zipporah chu apuijin;
target: After Moses had sent away his wife Zipporah, his father-in-law Jethro received her

source: Chule achapa teni, khatpa min chu Gershom ahi; ajehchu aman, Hetlouna gama maljin kahi, ati:
target: and her two sons. One son was named Gershom, for Moses said, “I have become a foreigner in a foreign land”;

source: Chule khatjopa min chu Eliazar ahi; ajehchu aman, Kapa Pathen chu eikithopia ahin, Pharaoh chemjam'a konin eihuhdoh-e, ati:
target: and the other was named Eliezer, for he said, “My father’s God was my helper; he saved me from the sword of Pharaoh.”

source: Chuin Mosi nupapa Jethro'n Mosi achapa teni le a-inneipi ahinpuijin, gamthip Pathen molsang mun'a agebuh sahna mun'a chun ahenga ahungun ahi.
target: Jethro, Moses’ father-in-law, together with Moses’ sons and wife, came to him in the wilderness, where he was camped near the mountain of God.

source: Chuin aman Mosi jah-a, Keima nanupapa Jethro, na-inneipi toh achapa teni toh kahunguve, ati.
target: Jethro had sent word to him, “I, your father-in-law Jethro, am coming to you with your wife and her two sons.”

source: Chuin Mosi anupapa lamto dingin apotdoh-in, jana apen, achopmin; chule amani khatle khat aumchan akidongto lhonin; pon insunga ahunglut lhontan ahi.
target: So Moses went out to meet his father-in-law and bowed down and kissed him. They greeted each other and then went into the tent.

source: Chuin Mosi'n anupapa Jethro henga Pakaiyin Israelte akhohsahna jala Pharaoh le Egypt miho chunga athilbol jouse, lamdunga achunguva gentheina hungchu ho jouse, chuleh Pakaiyin amaho alhatdoh jeo chu aseipehtan ahi.
target: Moses told his father-in-law about everything the Lord had done to Pharaoh and the Egyptians for Israel’s sake and about all the hardships they had met along the way and how the Lord had saved them.

source: Chuin Pakaiyin Israel chu Egypt mite khutna kona ahin huhdoh-a, achunga athilpha abol hojouse jehchun Jethro akipah lheh jengin ahi.
target: Jethro was delighted to hear about all the good things the Lord had done for Israel in rescuing them from the hand of the Egyptians.

source: Chuin Jethro'n, Egypt mite khutna kon le Pharaoh khutna kona nahuhdohpa, Egypt mite khutnoija kona mipi ho chu huhdohpa Pakai chu nunnom hen.
target: He said, “Praise be to the Lord , who rescued you from the hand of the Egyptians and of Pharaoh, and who rescued the people from the hand of the Egyptians.

source: Tun Pakai chu pathen jouse sangin aloupi joi ti kahetai; ajehchu amahon kiletsah tah-a thil abolnao jenga jong chun, amachu amaho sangin achung nungjon ahi, ati.
target: Now I know that the Lord is greater than all other gods, for he did this to those who had treated Israel arrogantly.”

source: Chuin Mosi nupapa Jethro'n govam thilto alan Pathen'a dingin ganlhaina abolin ahi. Chuin Aaron le Israel upa ho jouse chu Pathen angsunga Mosi nupapa Jethro toh an nedingin ahunguvin ahi.
target: Then Jethro, Moses’ father-in-law, brought a burnt offering and other sacrifices to God, and Aaron came with all the elders of Israel to eat a meal with Moses’ father-in-law in the presence of God.

source: Chuin ajingin ahitin ahi, Mosi chu mipi ho thutan dingin atoutan: chule mipi ho chu jingkah-a patnin nilhah geijin Mosi koma chun adingun ahi.
