source: Chuin amapan amanu jah-a, Nahenga katao ahi, dondingin twi themkhat neipen, ajehchu kadang achah lheh-e ati. Chuin amanun bongnoi hai ahongin, amapa adonsah-in, chule akhu khumtai.
target: “I’m thirsty,” he said. “Please give me some water.” She opened a skin of milk, gave him a drink, and covered him up.

source: Chule amanu koma aseikitnin, Pon in kotna dingin lang, chule hiti ding ahi, mikhattou nahenga ahunga, Hikoma hi mi umam? tia nadoh ule, aumpoi tin seijin, ati.
target: “Stand in the doorway of the tent,” he told her. “If someone comes by and asks you, ‘Is anyone in there?’ say ‘No.’ ”

source: Hiche jouchun Heber jinu Jael'in pon in kilna thingkil chu alan, akhutna sehtumkhat alan, ahenga kangchan achen, angeichanga chun akhenlutnin, toltoh akilmat jengin ahi; ajehchu ama acholjeh-a aihmumil hela ahi. Hitichun amapa athitai.
target: But Jael, Heber’s wife, picked up a tent peg and a hammer and went quietly to him while he lay fast asleep, exhausted. She drove the peg through his temple into the ground, and he died.

source: Chuin veuvin, Barak'in Sisera ahinjui laijin, Jael chu amapa kimutopi dingin apotdoh-in, chule ahenga, Hungin, keiman naholpa chu vetsah inge, ati. Chuin amapa amanu ponbuh-a ahung phatnin, veuvin Sisera chu athisan analumin, thingkil chu angeichanga ana kiphut in ahi.
target: Just then Barak came by in pursuit of Sisera, and Jael went out to meet him. “Come,” she said, “I will show you the man you’re looking for.” So he went in with her, and there lay Sisera with the tent peg through his temple—dead.

source: Hitichun hiche nikho chun Pathen'in Canaan lengpa Jabin chu Israelte masanga asunemtai.
target: On that day God subdued Jabin king of Canaan before the Israelites.

source: Chuin Israel chate khut akhangtou chehcheh-in, Canaan lengpa Jabin asuhmang kahseovin, Canaan lengpa Jabin chu ajoupeh-un ahi.
target: And the hand of the Israelites pressed harder and harder against Jabin king of Canaan until they destroyed him.

source: Chujouvin Deborah le Abhinoam chapa Barak in hiche nikho chun la asalhonin, hitin atilhone,
target: On that day Deborah and Barak son of Abinoam sang this song:

source: Mipite amaho le amaho akipehdoh uva, Israel phu alahpeh jeh-in, Pakai chu avahchoijun.
target: “When the princes in Israel take the lead, when the people willingly offer themselves— praise the Lord !

source: Vo lengho, ngaijun; Vo pipuiho, nana hinsungun; kei, keimatah in Pakaiya la sangting, Israel Pakai Pathen vahchoi La kasah ding ahi.
target: “Hear this, you kings! Listen, you rulers! I, even I, will sing to the Lord ; I will praise the Lord , the God of Israel, in song.

source: Pakai, Seir'a kona nangma nahung doh-a, Edom loujaova kona nahung kondoh chun, leiset akihot nemin, vanho apullhan, meilhang ho atuisoh gamtai.
target: “When you, Lord , went out from Seir, when you marched from the land of Edom, the earth shook, the heavens poured, the clouds poured down water.

source: Molsang ho chu Pakai masanga ajunlhan, Sinai jengjong chu Israel Pathen masanga ajunlha tai.
target: The mountains quaked before the Lord , the One of Sinai, before the Lord , the God of Israel.

source: Anath chapa Shamgar nikho laijin, Jael nikho laijin, Lamlhongpiho athipbeh-in, kholjinle hon lampel ajotnuve.
target: “In the days of Shamgar son of Anath, in the days of Jael, the highways were abandoned; travelers took to winding paths.

source: Khosunga chengho aum tapouvin, Israel sunga aum tapouve; Keima Deborah kakipat doh-a, Israel sunga minu khatna kakipatdoh masangsen.
target: Villagers in Israel would not fight; they held back until I, Deborah, arose, until I arose, a mother in Israel.

source: Amahon pathen thah ho akilhennun, chuin kotpi sunga gal anaume. Israel sangsomli lah-a lumle teng ana umam?
target: God chose new leaders when war came to the city gates, but not a shield or spear was seen among forty thousand in Israel.

source: Kalungthim hi mipi lah-a kona achamtah-a kipedoh Israel gamvaipoho lah-a aume, Pakai chu nunnom hen.
target: My heart is with Israel’s princes, with the willing volunteers among the people. Praise the Lord !

source: Seijuvin, nangho sangan kang chunga touho, thupi tanna-a touho, chule lamdunga cheleho.
target: “You who ride on white donkeys, sitting on your saddle blankets, and you who walk along the road, consider

source: Atuikhainau munho-a thalkap ho thal len gina kona kihuh dohhon, chumuna chu amahon Pakai chonphatna natoh aseiphong diu, chonphatna natoh ngei chu Israel sunga akho sunguva chengho lah-a ajahsah diu; chuteng Pakai mite kotpi phunga kumsuh diu ahitai.
target: the voice of the singers at the watering places. They recite the victories of the Lord , the victories of his villagers in Israel. “Then the people of the Lord went down to the city gates.

source: Thouvin, thouvin, Deborah; thouvin, thouvin, la khat san: kipat doh-in, nangma Abinoam chapa Barak, chule gal hinga ki kaiho gal hingin kaijin.
target: ‘Wake up, wake up, Deborah! Wake up, wake up, break out in song! Arise, Barak! Take captive your captives, son of Abinoam.’

source: Chujouvin aman ahingdohpa chu miho lah-a miloupiho chunga vaihomin apansah-in; Pakaiyin keima mihat ho chunga vai eipohsah-in ahi.
target: “The remnant of the nobles came down; the people of the Lord came down to me against the mighty.

source: Ephraim'a konin Amalek douding amaho lah-a jung khat aumin, nangma nungin namite lah-a Benjamin; Machir'a konin gamvaipoho ahungsuh-un, chule Zebulun'a konin thil sunhon lekhamol tuhho ahungsuh-un ahi.
target: Some came from Ephraim, whose roots were in Amalek; Benjamin was with the people who followed you. From Makir captains came down, from Zebulun those who bear a commander’s staff.

source: Chule Issachar leng chapa ho chu Daborah toh aumkhomun; Issachar jengjong, chule Barak jong aumin: ama chu kengin phaichama lama akisolin ahi. Reuben kikhentel jeh-in lungsunga lunggel lentah asohdoh-in ahi.
target: The princes of Issachar were with Deborah; yes, Issachar was with Barak, sent under his command into the valley. In the districts of Reuben there was much searching of heart.

source: Kelngoiho pen gin ngaidinga, kelngoi honlah-a ibola nangma uma nahim? Reuben kikhentel jeh-in lungsung kikholna nasatah aumin ahi.
target: Why did you stay among the sheep pens to hear the whistling for the flocks? In the districts of Reuben there was much searching of heart.

source: Gilead chu Jordan gal langa achenge: chule Dan chu ibola kong innei sunga umden ham? Asher twipi panga aumjingin, chule abahho kah-a achengin ahi.
target: Gilead stayed beyond the Jordan. And Dan, why did he linger by the ships? Asher remained on the coast and stayed in his coves.

source: Zebulun le Naphtali hi gam sanglam loulaija thina ginglouva ahinkholhon phaldoh-a mi ahilhone.
target: The people of Zebulun risked their very lives; so did Naphtali on the terraced fields.

source: Lengho ahungun gal ahungsatnun, Megiddo twipi pang Taanach mun'a Canaan lengho asatnun; Amahon gamthil le sum alapouvin ahi.
target: “Kings came, they fought, the kings of Canaan fought. At Taanach, by the waters of Megiddo, they took no plunder of silver.

source: Amahon van'a konin gal asatnun, ahsihon alamlhah uva konin Sisera asatnun ahi.
target: From the heavens the stars fought, from their courses they fought against Sisera.

source: Kishon vapidungin amaho alhoh mangun, hichu malai vapi, Kishon vapi chu ahi. O kahinna, nangman thahatna nachotpha ahitai.
target: The river Kishon swept them away, the age-old river, the river Kishon. March on, my soul; be strong!

source: Chujouvin sakol ho chu akihatil jeh-un, amihatpaovin ahatil jeh-un, atinhou alhong gamtan ahi.
target: Then thundered the horses’ hooves— galloping, galloping go his mighty steeds.

source: Meroz chu samseuvin, tin Pakai vantil'in aseije, asunga chengho jouse chu nasatah-in samseuvin; ajehchu Pakai kithopi din ahung pouvin, ahat ho doudinga Pakai kithopi dingin amaho ahung pouvin ahi.
target: ‘Curse Meroz,’ said the angel of the Lord . ‘Curse its people bitterly, because they did not come to help the Lord , to help the Lord against the mighty.’

source: Numei ho jouse chungvuma Ken mi Heber jinu Jael chu phatthei changding ahin; ponbuh-a cheng numei ho jouse chungvuma phatthei changding ahi.
target: “Most blessed of women be Jael, the wife of Heber the Kenite, most blessed of tent-dwelling women.

source: Amapan twi athumle amanun bongnoi apen; amanun milen kongsunga bongnoi ha ahin domin ahi.
target: He asked for water, and she gave him milk; in a bowl fit for nobles she brought him curdled milk.

source: Amanun akhutnin thingkil alan, akhut jetlama natongho seh alan; seh-a chun Sisera akhenin, amanun angeichang akhet pai phatnin alu chu avochiptan ahi.
target: Her hand reached for the tent peg, her right hand for the workman’s hammer. She struck Sisera, she crushed his head, she shattered and pierced his temple.

source: Amapa amanu kengbula aboh khupmin, alhun, akijamtai: amanu kengbula aboh khupmin, alhun; abohkhupna-a chun athisan akijamtai.
target: At her feet he sank, he fell; there he lay. At her feet he sank, he fell; where he sank, there he fell—dead.

source: Sisera nuchun bangkotna konin aven, avangkah-a konin apengjah-in, Ipidinga akangtalai hung geisangham? Ipidinga akangtalai kangho khongai ahidem?
target: “Through the window peered Sisera’s mother; behind the lattice she cried out, ‘Why is his chariot so long in coming? Why is the clatter of his chariots delayed?’

source: Aloi numei chinghon adonbutnun, Henge, amanu amale ama akidonbutnin,
target: The wisest of her ladies answer her; indeed, she keeps saying to herself,

source: Amaho gangjou louvu hitam? Gal thilkichom kihom louvu ham? Pasal takip dinga nungah khat ahiloule ni; Sisera dinga gal thillah jemchom chom, gal thillah kikhui pahjem chomchom, alangtoa kikhuipah jem chomchom, galthil kilahho ngonga dinga kilomho amujou louvu ahidem? ati.
target: ‘Are they not finding and dividing the spoils: a woman or two for each man, colorful garments as plunder for Sisera, colorful garments embroidered, highly embroidered garments for my neck— all this as plunder?’

source: O Pakai, Hitichun nagalmiteu mangthah hen: ahivanginla ama ngailuho chu thahat tah-a chelai nisa banguhen. Chuin gamsung chu kum somli acholdon ahi.
target: “So may all your enemies perish, Lord ! But may all who love you be like the sun when it rises in its strength.” Then the land had peace forty years.

source: Chule Israel chaten Pakai mitmun thilse jeng abolun ahile; Pakaiyin amaho chu Midia te khutna kum sagi apedoh tan ahi.
target: The Israelites did evil in the eyes of the Lord , and for seven years he gave them into the hands of the Midianites.

source: Chuin Midia te khut chun Israelte chu ajoutan: chule Midia mite jehchun Israel chaten molsang ho-a kokhuh, leikoho, chule kuldet akisem taovin ahi.
target: Because the power of Midian was so oppressive, the Israelites prepared shelters for themselves in mountain clefts, caves and strongholds.

source: Chuin ahitin ahi, Israel ten muchi atu tengule Midia miho ahung tou jiuvin, chule Amalek miho le solam chateho jongchu amaho doudin ahung tou jiuvin;
target: Whenever the Israelites planted their crops, the Midianites, Amalekites and other eastern peoples invaded the country.

source: Chule amaho dounan gebuh asong jiuvin, Gaza geijin leisetna kon muchi jouse chu asuse jiuvin, chule Israelte dingin nehding himhim akhenji pouvin, kelngoiho, bongho, sanganho jong akhenji pouvin ahi.
target: They camped on the land and ruined the crops all the way to Gaza and did not spare a living thing for Israel, neither sheep nor cattle nor donkeys.

source: Ajehchu amaho aganchahou le aponbuh-u toh hungtou jiuva, mihonpi chu khaokho banga hung kitol jiuva ahi; ajehchu amahole asangongsang hou chu simjou lou ahiuvin, gamsung sumang dinga hunglut jiu ahi.
target: They came up with their livestock and their tents like swarms of locusts. It was impossible to count them or their camels; they invaded the land to ravage it.

source: Chule Midia mite jeh chun Israelte chu nasatah-in avaicha taovin; chuin Israel chate Pakai henga apeng taovin ahi.
target: Midian so impoverished the Israelites that they cried out to the Lord for help.

source: Chuin ahung hitin ahi, Midia mite jeh-a Israel chaten Pakai asap phatnun,
target: When the Israelites cried out to the Lord because of Midian,

source: Pakaiyin Israel chate dingin themgao khat ahinsol peh-in, ama chun ahenguva hitihin thu aseijin, Israel Pakai Pathen'in hitihin aseije, Keiman Egypt'a kona kahinpuidoh uva, nabul putnaova kona kahinpuidoh nahiuvin;
target: he sent them a prophet, who said, “This is what the Lord , the God of Israel, says: I brought you up out of Egypt, out of the land of slavery.

source: Chule Egypt mite khutna konle, nabol gentheihou khutna kona kahuhdoh uva, namasanguva kona kadeldoh-a, agamu nangho kapeh nahiuve;
target: I rescued you from the hand of the Egyptians. And I delivered you from the hand of all your oppressors; I drove them out before you and gave you their land.

source: Chule keiman naheng uva, Keimahi Pakai na-Pathen'u kahi; nanghon agamuva nachennao Amor mite pathenho chu ging hih-un, kanatin: ahinla nanghon kathu nanit pouvin ahi, ati.
target: I said to you, ‘I am the Lord your God; do not worship the gods of the Amorites, in whose land you live.’ But you have not listened to me.”

source: Chuin Pakai vantil khat ahungin, Ophrah kho-a um Abiezer mi Joash gangpi phung noija atouvin; chule achapa Gideon chun Midia mite-a kona sel dingin lengpiga chilna-a suhlou chang achilin ahi.
target: The angel of the Lord came and sat down under the oak in Ophrah that belonged to Joash the Abiezrite, where his son Gideon was threshing wheat in a winepress to keep it from the Midianites.

source: Chuin Pakai vantil chu ahenga akilah-in, ajah-a, Nangma mihang gal hatpa, Pakaiyin naumpi, ati.
target: When the angel of the Lord appeared to Gideon, he said, “The Lord is with you, mighty warrior.”

source: Chuin Gideon'in ama henga, Vo ka Pakai, Pakaiyin eiumpiuva ahileh, hichengpihi ibola kachunguva chu-a ham? Chule kapu kapateuvin keiho henga Pakaiyin keiho Egypt'a kona eihin puidoh-u hilouham, tia anaseiju athilbol kidangho chu hoilamba hija hitam? Ahinla tun Pakaiyin eida lhaovin, Midia mite khutna eipedoh taove, ati.
target: “Pardon me, my lord,” Gideon replied, “but if the Lord is with us, why has all this happened to us? Where are all his wonders that our ancestors told us about when they said, ‘Did not the Lord bring us up out of Egypt?’ But now the Lord has abandoned us and given us into the hand of Midian.”

source: Chuin Pakaiyin amapa aven, hitin aseije, Hiche nathahatna-a hin konin, chule nangman Midia te khutna konin Israel nahuhdoh ding ahi, keiman kasol nahi hilouham? ati.
target: The Lord turned to him and said, “Go in the strength you have and save Israel out of Midian’s hand. Am I not sending you?”

source: Chuin aman ahenga, Vo ka Pakai, iti dana keiman Israel kahuhdoh dingham? Ven, ka-insung hi Manasseh sunga dinga alhasampen ahin, chule keimahi kapa insunga dinga alhumpen kahi, ati.
target: “Pardon me, my lord,” Gideon replied, “but how can I save Israel? My clan is the weakest in Manasseh, and I am the least in my family.”

source: Chuin Pakaiyin ahenga, Thonlouva keiman nangma kaumpi ding nahin, chule nangman Midia mite chu mikhat tha-a natha ding ahi, ati.
target: The Lord answered, “I will be with you, and you will strike down all the Midianites, leaving none alive.”

source: Chuin aman ahenga, Tu-a namitmu-a lungsetna kachana ahile, nangman nei kihoupina melchihna neimusah-in.
target: Gideon replied, “If now I have found favor in your eyes, give me a sign that it is really you talking to me.

source: Nahenga katao ahi, nahenga kahunga thilpeh kahin choidoh-a na anga kakoi kahsen, hiche mun'a konin chedoh hih-in, ati. Chuin aman, Nahung kahse-a kana ngading nahi, ati.
target: Please do not go away until I come back and bring my offering and set it before you.” And the Lord said, “I will wait until you return.”

source: Chuin Gideon alutnin, kelnou khat athatnin, chule changbong chol solou ephah khat aga kangin; saphe chu pocha sunga ahengin, atwi chu bel sunga asunglutnin, gangpi phung noija aumna-a chun ahinchoijin, amapa chu apen ahi.
target: Gideon went inside, prepared a young goat, and from an ephah of flour he made bread without yeast. Putting the meat in a basket and its broth in a pot, he brought them out and offered them to him under the oak.

source: Chuin Pathen vantil chun ahenga, Saphe le chol solou changlhah chu lanlang songpi chungahin koijin lang, atuichu sunglhan ati. Chuin hitichun aboltai.
target: The angel of God said to him, “Take the meat and the unleavened bread, place them on this rock, and pour out the broth.” And Gideon did so.

source: Chuin Pakai vantil'in akhutna um tenggol muh-a chun saphe le cholsolou changlhah chu agah tongkhan ahileh, songpi-a konchun mei ahung kongdoh-in, saphe le cholsolou changlhah chu akamangtan ahi. Chujouvin Pakai vantil chu amitmua konin achemang tai.
target: Then the angel of the Lord touched the meat and the unleavened bread with the tip of the staff that was in his hand. Fire flared from the rock, consuming the meat and the bread. And the angel of the Lord disappeared.

source: Chuin Gideon'in ama chu Pakai vantil ahi ahet phatnin, Gideon'in, Ohe Pakai Pathen! ajehchu keiman Pakai vantil chu kimaito tah-in kakimupi tai, ati.
target: When Gideon realized that it was the angel of the Lord , he exclaimed, “Alas, Sovereign Lord ! I have seen the angel of the Lord face to face!”

source: Chuin Pakaiyin ahenga, Lung mongin umin, kicha hih-in; nathi louding ahi, ati.
target: But the Lord said to him, “Peace! Do not be afraid. You are not going to die.”

source: Chuin Gideon'in Pakai dingin chua chun maicham khat atungdoh-in, hichu Jehovah-shalom asahtai. Tuni geijin Abiezer mite umna Ophrah'a aum jingin ahi.
target: So Gideon built an altar to the Lord there and called it The Lord Is Peace. To this day it stands in Ophrah of the Abiezrites.

source: Chuin hiche jan mama chun ahitin ahi, Pakaiyin ahenga aseijin, Napa bongchal gol, kum sagi lhing bongchal gol nina ngei chu lanlang, napa Baal maicham chu suchimin, chule akoma um thingbom chu phuhlhun;
target: That same night the Lord said to him, “Take the second bull from your father’s herd, the one seven years old. Tear down your father’s altar to Baal and cut down the Asherah pole beside it.

source: Chule hiche songpi chunga hin Pakai na Pathen dingin maicham khat sanlang, hoitah-in goltupmin, chule bongchal nina chu lanlang, naphuh ding thingbom thinga chun halvam thilpeh chu toh-in, ati.
target: Then build a proper kind of altar to the Lord your God on the top of this height. Using the wood of the Asherah pole that you cut down, offer the second bull as a burnt offering.”

source: Chujouvin Gideon'in asohte mi som apuijin, Pakaiyin ahenga aseibang chun aboltan ahi. Chule ahitin ahi, apa insung mihole khopi-a miho aginjeh chun sunnin abolngam pon, jannin abolin ahi.
target: So Gideon took ten of his servants and did as the Lord told him. But because he was afraid of his family and the townspeople, he did it at night rather than in the daytime.

source: Chuin khopi miho chu jingpi tah-a ahungthodoh phatnun, veuvin Baal maicham chu ana kisulhun, chule akoma um thingbom jong chu ana kiphuh lhutan, chule Maicham kisa chunga chun bongchal nina chu ganlhaijin ana kitoh-in ahi.
target: In the morning when the people of the town got up, there was Baal’s altar, demolished, with the Asherah pole beside it cut down and the second bull sacrificed on the newly built altar!

source: Chuin amaho khatle khat, Hichehi koibolham? tin akidong touvin ahi. Chule amahon akholuva adoh phatnun, Hichehi Joash chapa Gideon bol ahi, tin adonbutnun ahi.
target: They asked each other, “Who did this?” When they carefully investigated, they were told, “Gideon son of Joash did it.”

source: Chujouvin khopi sunga mihon Joash henga, Nachapa hinpuidoh in, thitei tei ding ahi. Ajehchu aman Baal maicham asuchimin, chule akoma um thingbom chu aphuh lhun ahi, atiuve.
target: The people of the town demanded of Joash, “Bring out your son. He must die, because he has broken down Baal’s altar and cut down the Asherah pole beside it.”

source: Chuin Joash'in akidin tepiho jouse henga, Nanghon Baal dinga thu naseipeh dingu ham? Nanghon ama nahuhhing dingu ham? Koihile ama-a dinga thusei chanchu tu jingkah ahipet hin kithat jenghen; ama pathen ahile achungthu kisei hen, ajehchu mikhatnin amaicham asuhchim pehtai, ati.
target: But Joash replied to the hostile crowd around him, “Are you going to plead Baal’s cause? Are you trying to save him? Whoever fights for him shall be put to death by morning! If Baal really is a god, he can defend himself when someone breaks down his altar.”

source: Hijeh chun aman, Baal'in amapa dounan achungthu kiseihen, ajehchu aman a-maicham asuhchim pehtai, atin, amapa chu Jerubbaal asahtai.
target: So because Gideon broke down Baal’s altar, they gave him the name Jerub-Baal that day, saying, “Let Baal contend with him.”

source: Chujouvin Midia te jousele Amalek mite chule solama chateho akikhomun, agalkaijun, Jezreel phaichama pon in asong taovin ahi.
target: Now all the Midianites, Amalekites and other eastern peoples joined forces and crossed over the Jordan and camped in the Valley of Jezreel.

source: Ahivangin Pakai lhagao chu Gideon chunga ahung chun, chule aman sumkon amutnin; Abiezer miho anunga ahung kikhomun ahi.
target: Then the Spirit of the Lord came on Gideon, and he blew a trumpet, summoning the Abiezrites to follow him.

source: Chuin aman Manasseh mite umna jouse-a thusep asolin, amaho anunga ahung kikhomun ahi. Chule Asher henga jong, Zebulun henga jong, Naphtali henga jong thusep asolin; chuin amaho ama kimutopi din ahung touvun ahi.
target: He sent messengers throughout Manasseh, calling them to arms, and also into Asher, Zebulun and Naphtali, so that they too went up to meet them.

source: Chuin Gideon'in Pathen henga, Nangman nasei banga kakhutna Israel nahuhdoh dinga ahile,
target: Gideon said to God, “If you will save Israel by my hand as you have promised—

source: Ven, keiman tollhanga kelngoi mul kakoi ding; daitwi chu kelngoimul chungabou alhah-a, akivela leiset chungchu agotseh-a ahile, nasei banga chu kakhutna Israel nahuhdoh ding ahi tichu kahet ding ahi, ati.
target: look, I will place a wool fleece on the threshing floor. If there is dew only on the fleece and all the ground is dry, then I will know that you will save Israel by my hand, as you said.”

source: Chuin chutichu ahitai. Ajehchu ajing jingkah matah-in athouvin, kelngoimul ho chu achom khomin, atuichu kelngoi mula kona chu ahehlhan ahile, kongkhat adimsetnin ahi.
target: And that is what happened. Gideon rose early the next day; he squeezed the fleece and wrung out the dew—a bowlful of water.

source: Chuin Gideon'in Pathen henga, Kachunga lunghang hih beh-in, khatvei sehseh bou seikit inge: katao ahi, hiche kelngoi mula hin khatvei patep kit inge; tun kelngoimul chung bouchu gotsah inlang, leiset chung vang daitwi kotsah-in, ati.
target: Then Gideon said to God, “Do not be angry with me. Let me make just one more request. Allow me one more test with the fleece, but this time make the fleece dry and let the ground be covered with dew.”

source: Chuin Pathen'in hiche janchun hitichun aboltai. Ajehchu kelngoi mul chung bouchu ago-in, leiset chung jouse chu dai akotnin ahi.
target: That night God did so. Only the fleece was dry; all the ground was covered with dew.

source: Chujouvin Jerubbaal, (hichu Gideon ahi,) le aumpi miho jouse chu jingpi tah-in athoudoh-un, Harod twikul panga chun ponbuh asongun; hitichun Midia sepai janel chu asahlam uva Moreh lhang chin phaichama aumun ahi.
target: Early in the morning, Jerub-Baal (that is, Gideon) and all his men camped at the spring of Harod. The camp of Midian was north of them in the valley near the hill of Moreh.

source: Chuin Pakaiyin Gideon henga, Akhutnuva Midia mite kapehdohna din nalhonpi miho chu atam behseh uve, achuti loule Israelte kei dounan hoithou vintin, kakhut tah-in eihuhdoh ahi tigetnunte, ati.
target: The Lord said to Gideon, “You have too many men. I cannot deliver Midian into their hands, or Israel would boast against me, ‘My own strength has saved me.’

source: Hijeh chun tun chenlang mipi ho jahdin gaseiphongin, Koitobang akicha le atijachan chu, Gilead molsanga konhin kinungle loihen, tin ati. Chuin mipi-a konchun mi sangsomni le ni akinunglen, sangsom aum denun ahi.
target: Now announce to the army, ‘Anyone who trembles with fear may turn back and leave Mount Gilead.’ ” So twenty-two thousand men left, while ten thousand remained.

source: Chuin Pakaiyin Gideon henga, Mipi hohi atam behseh nalaijui; Amaho hi twiphunga puilhan, chukoma chu keiman nangma-a dingin kapatep ding ahi. Chule hitiding ahi, keiman, Amahi nangma toh lhonkhom ding ahi katichan chu nangma toh lhonkhom ding; chule koi hijongle nahenga, Amahi nangma toh lhonkhom louding ahi kati chanchun, nangma toh lhonkhom louding ahi, ati.
target: But the Lord said to Gideon, “There are still too many men. Take them down to the water, and I will thin them out for you there. If I say, ‘This one shall go with you,’ he shall go; but if I say, ‘This one shall not go with you,’ he shall not go.”

source: Hitichun aman mipi ho chu twiphunga apuilhan ahi. Chuin Pakaiyin Gideon henga, Koihile uicha banga twi chu aleija letho chanchu achoma nakhendoh ding, chutobang ma-a chu akhupma bohkhupma donho jong nakhendoh ding ahi, ati.
target: So Gideon took the men down to the water. There the Lord told him, “Separate those who lap the water with their tongues as a dog laps from those who kneel down to drink.”

source: Chuin akama akhut koija letho ho jouse chu jathum ahiuvin; mipi adangse vangchu akhupma dilsua dontho ho ahiuve.
target: Three hundred of them drank from cupped hands, lapping like dogs. All the rest got down on their knees to drink.

source: Chuin Pakaiyin Gideon henga, Ale-tho mi jathum hochu mangcha-a nangma kahuh hinga, Midia te chu nakhutna kapehdoh ding ahi. Adangse vangchu ama ama muncheh-a chetaohen,
target: The Lord said to Gideon, “With the three hundred men that lapped I will save you and give the Midianites into your hands. Let all the others go home.”

source: Hitichun mihon aneh dingu le asumkon cheh-u akhutnuva akichoijun ahi. Chuin aman Israel dangse chu amitakip aponbuh cheh-a asolin, hiche mi jathum ho chu aumdensah-in ahi: chule Midia mipi janel chu ama noija phaichama chun aumun ahi.
target: So Gideon sent the rest of the Israelites home but kept the three hundred, who took over the provisions and trumpets of the others. Now the camp of Midian lay below him in the valley.

source: Chuin hiche jan mama chun ahung hitin ahi, Pakaiyin ahengah, Thoudoh-in, mipi janel lah-a khun chesuh-in; ajehchu nakhutna kapehdoh
target: During that night the Lord said to Gideon, “Get up, go down against the camp, because I am going to give it into your hands.

source: Amavang chesuh ding nakichatle, nasohpa Purah kilhonpin lang janel lah-a chun chesuh-in;
target: If you are afraid to attack, go down to the camp with your servant Purah

source: Chule amahon ipi aseijiu nagajah ding ahin, chutengle mipi janel henga chesuhna dinga nakhut chu suhhatna umding ahitai, ati. Chujouvin ama asohpa Purah toh mipi janelho lah-a sepai manchah choiho umna china chun aga chesuh lhonin ahi.
target: and listen to what they are saying. Afterward, you will be encouraged to attack the camp.” So he and Purah his servant went down to the outposts of the camp.

source: Chule Midia miho, Amalek miho, chule solam chate mipi ho chu khaokhote banga tamin phaicham lhonlhunga aumun; chule asangongsao houchu simsenglou, twikhanglen panga neldi banga tam ahi.
target: The Midianites, the Amalekites and all the other eastern peoples had settled in the valley, thick as locusts. Their camels could no more be counted than the sand on the seashore.

source: Chuin Gideon ahung phatnin, veuvin, chukoma chun mikhatnin agolpa koma amang aseijin, hitin ati, Ngaijin, keiman mang khat kamatnin, ven, Midia mipi janel lah-a butunna kisem changlhah pheng ahung kilih lutnin, ponbuh geijin ahung lutnin, hichun ahinse-a ahileh asuchimtan, akilehkhup min, athalin akijamtai, ati.
target: Gideon arrived just as a man was telling a friend his dream. “I had a dream,” he was saying. “A round loaf of barley bread came tumbling into the Midianite camp. It struck the tent with such force that the tent overturned and collapsed.”

source: Chuin aloipan adonbutnin, Hichu Israel mikhat Joash chapa Gideon chemjam tilou imadang hiponte. Ajehchu Pathen'in akhutna Midia te le mipi janel hi apehdoh ahitai ati.
target: His friend responded, “This can be nothing other than the sword of Gideon son of Joash, the Israelite. God has given the Midianites and the whole camp into his hands.”

source: Chuin ahitin ahi, Gideon'in mang kisei le aledohna kisei chu ajah phatnin, Pathen ahouvin, Israel mipi ho lah-a akinunglen, hitin aseije, Thouvun, ajehchu Pakaiyin nakhut uva Midia mipi janel chu apedohtai, ati.
target: When Gideon heard the dream and its interpretation, he bowed down and worshiped. He returned to the camp of Israel and called out, “Get up! The Lord has given the Midianite camp into your hands.”

source: Chuin aman mi jathum chu loithumin akhenin, akhutcheh uva sumkon khatcheh apen, chule leibel keu khatcheh, asunga thaomei kikoi leibel keu khatcheh toh apen ahi.
target: Dividing the three hundred men into three companies, he placed trumpets and empty jars in the hands of all of them, with torches inside.

source: Chuin aman ahenguva, keima neiveuvin lang, kabol bang bangin bollun. Chule veuvin, keima ngahmun pam kahung lhun tengle hung hitiding ahi, keima bol bangbang chu nabol cheh dingu ahi.
target: “Watch me,” he told them. “Follow my lead. When I get to the edge of the camp, do exactly as I do.

source: Keima le kaumpi jousen sumkon kamut tengule, nanghon jong ngahmun jouse pang tinna sumkon namut uva, Pakai le Gideon chemjam, nati diu ahi, ati.
target: When I and all who are with me blow our trumpets, then from all around the camp blow yours and shout, ‘For the Lord and for Gideon.’ ”

source: Hitichun jan khangkim kipat tah-in Gideon le aumpi mi jakhat chu gebuh pam chu ahung lhungun, amaho chu ngahtup ana kikhel jou pettah-u ahin; chuin amahon sumkon amutnun, akhutnuva leibel keuho chu avokeh uvin ahi.
target: Gideon and the hundred men with him reached the edge of the camp at the beginning of the middle watch, just after they had changed the guard. They blew their trumpets and broke the jars that were in their hands.

source: Chule loithumho chun asumkonnu chu amutnun, bel homho jong chu asukeh un, akhut veijun meivah ho chu adomun, akhut jetna sumkon tuh in amutnun, chuin Pakai le Gideon chemjam tin a-ao taovin, ahi.
target: The three companies blew the trumpets and smashed the jars. Grasping the torches in their left hands and holding in their right hands the trumpets they were to blow, they shouted, “A sword for the Lord and for Gideon!”

source: Chuin ngahphol kimvella chun amitakip adinna cheh uva adingun ahi. Chuin janel chu alhaijun, hatah in apengun ajammang taovin ahi.
target: While each man held his position around the camp, all the Midianites ran, crying out as they fled.

source: Chuin loithumho chun asumkonu amutnun ahile, Pakaiyin mitin chemjam chu aloipa chunga achuhsah-in, mipi janel pumpi lah ngeija chun; chuin mipi janel chu Zererath'a mun'a um Beth-shittah lama le, Tabbath lama Abel-meholah gamgi geijin ajamtaovin ahi.
target: When the three hundred trumpets sounded, the Lord caused the men throughout the camp to turn on each other with their swords. The army fled to Beth Shittah toward Zererah as far as the border of Abel Meholah near Tabbath.

source: Chuin Israel mijouse chu Naphtali'a kon, Asher akon, Manasseh'a konin akikhomun, Midia miho chu anung delun ahi.
target: Israelites from Naphtali, Asher and all Manasseh were called out, and they pursued the Midianites.

source: Chuin Gideon'in Ephraim molsang jouse-a thusep asolin, ahenguva, Midia mite doudin hungsuh un, chule amaho masanga konin Bethbarah le Jordan geijin atwi neh-u chu lahpeh-un, atin ahi. Chujouvin Ephraim mijouse chu akikhom khomun, Bethbarah le Jordan geijin amaho-a konin atwi neh-u chu alah peh-un ahi.
target: Gideon sent messengers throughout the hill country of Ephraim, saying, “Come down against the Midianites and seize the waters of the Jordan ahead of them as far as Beth Barah.” So all the men of Ephraim were called out and they seized the waters of the Jordan as far as Beth Barah.

source: Chule amahon Midia mite leng chapa ni Oreb le Zeeb chu amanun; chuin amahon Oreb chu Oreb song chunga athatnun, chule Zeeb chu Zeeb lengpiga chilna-a athatnun, Midia te chu anungdelun, Oreb le Zeeb luchang chu Jordan gallanga Gideon henga ahinpouvin ahi.
target: They also captured two of the Midianite leaders, Oreb and Zeeb. They killed Oreb at the rock of Oreb, and Zeeb at the winepress of Zeeb. They pursued the Midianites and brought the heads of Oreb and Zeeb to Gideon, who was by the Jordan.

source: Chule Ephraim mihon ahenga, ibola nangin keiho neihiti bol uva, Midia mite toh kisatna nacheuva chu neikou louvu ham? atiuvin amachu nasatah-in ahouseuvin ahi.
target: Now the Ephraimites asked Gideon, “Why have you treated us like this? Why didn’t you call us when you went to fight Midian?” And they challenged him vigorously.

source: Chuin aman amaho henga, Nang hotoh tekah dinga tu-a keiman ipi kabol em? Abiezer theichang ga lokhom sanga Ephraim lengpiga lokhom chu phajo louham?
target: But he answered them, “What have I accomplished compared to you? Aren’t the gleanings of Ephraim’s grapes better than the full grape harvest of Abiezer?

source: Pathen'in nakhut uva Midia leng chapa teni Oreb le Zeeb chu apedoh tan: keiman nang hotoh tekah dinga ipi katoh jouding ham? atin ahi. Chuin chuche aseiphatnin ama chunga lunghan nau chu adailhatan ahi.
target: God gave Oreb and Zeeb, the Midianite leaders, into your hands. What was I able to do compared to you?” At this, their resentment against him subsided.

source: Chuin Gideon Jordan'a ahungin, apalgalkai paijin, amale alhonpi mi jathum chu amaho nungdel nan alhadah taovin ahi.
target: Gideon and his three hundred men, exhausted yet keeping up the pursuit, came to the Jordan and crossed it.

source: Chuin aman Succoth miho henga, Naheng uva katao ahi, kanung juija miho hi changlhah peovin, ajehchu amaho alhadah taove, chule keiman Midia leng teni Zebah le Zalmunna nung kadel ahi, ati.
target: He said to the men of Sukkoth, “Give my troops some bread; they are worn out, and I am still pursuing Zebah and Zalmunna, the kings of Midian.”

source: Chuin Succoth leng chapate chun, Zebah le Zalmunna khutchu nakhutna umbeh hita-a, keihon nasepai ho chu changlhah kapeh dingu ham? atiuvin ahi.
target: But the officials of Sukkoth said, “Do you already have the hands of Zebah and Zalmunna in your possession? Why should we give bread to your troops?”

source: Chuin Gideon'in, Hiche jeh-a chu Pakaiyin Zebah le Zalmunna kakhutna eipehdoh phatle, keiman gamthipma lingho le khaogui lingneiho-a naphe-u kabotel ding ahi, ati.
target: Then Gideon replied, “Just for that, when the Lord has given Zebah and Zalmunna into my hand, I will tear your flesh with desert thorns and briers.”

source: Chuin ama Penuel geijin achepeh-in, hitobangma chun ahenguva aseijin; chule Penuel'a um miho jongchun, Succoth mihon adonbutna bangu chun anadonbutnun ahi.
target: From there he went up to Peniel and made the same request of them, but they answered as the men of Sukkoth had.

source: Chuin aman Penuel miho henga aseijin, Lungmonga kahungkit tengle, hiche insanghi kasuhchim ding ahi, atin ahi.
target: So he said to the men of Peniel, “When I return in triumph, I will tear down this tower.”

source: Tun Zebah le Zalmunna chu Karkor munna aumlhonin, chule aumpi miho chu sangsom le sangnga ahiuvin, abonuva chu solam chate janel hon lah-a amoh ngen ahiuve. Ajehchu chemjam lamthei cheh mi sangjakhat le sangsomni athiuvin ahi.
target: Now Zebah and Zalmunna were in Karkor with a force of about fifteen thousand men, all that were left of the armies of the eastern peoples; a hundred and twenty thousand swordsmen had fallen.

source: Chuin Gideon Nabah le Jogbehah solam sanga chengho ponbuh lampia chun achetouvin, chule janel chu aban tha gamin ahi: ajehchu amaho mongtah-a umuva ahi.
target: Gideon went up by the route of the nomads east of Nobah and Jogbehah and attacked the unsuspecting army.

source: Chuin Zebah le Zalmunna ajam phatnin, aman anung delin, chule Midia lengteni Zebah le Zalmunna chu amanin, janel pumpi chu amaimoh sahtan ahi.
target: Zebah and Zalmunna, the two kings of Midian, fled, but he pursued them and captured them, routing their entire army.

source: Chuin Joash chapa Gideon chu nisa sodoh masangin galmuna konin ahung kinungle tan ahi.
target: Gideon son of Joash then returned from the battle by the Pass of Heres.

source: Chuin Succoth mi golhang khat amanin, adongin ahile, amapan Succoth leng chapateho le, a-upahou mi somsagi le sagi geijin phatechan ahiltai.
target: He caught a young man of Sukkoth and questioned him, and the young man wrote down for him the names of the seventy-seven officials of Sukkoth, the elders of the town.

source: Chuin Succoth miho henga chun ahungin, chule ajah uva, Veuvin Zebah le Zalmunna, Tu-a hi nakhutna Zebah le Zalmunna khut chu umbeh hija, namite lhasamho chu changlhah kapeh diuham? tia neitaitom nao chu, atin ahi.
target: Then Gideon came and said to the men of Sukkoth, “Here are Zebah and Zalmunna, about whom you taunted me by saying, ‘Do you already have the hands of Zebah and Zalmunna in your possession? Why should we give bread to your exhausted men?’ ”

source: Chuin aman khopi-a upaho chu amanin, gamthipma lingle khaogui lingnei chu alan, hicheho-a chun Succoth miho chu ahiltan ahi.
target: He took the elders of the town and taught the men of Sukkoth a lesson by punishing them with desert thorns and briers.

source: Chule Penuel insang chu asuhchimin, khopi-a miho chu athatnin ahi.
target: He also pulled down the tower of Peniel and killed the men of the town.

source: Chujouvin Zebah le Zalmunna henga, Tabor munna nathaho chu itobang mi hiuvem, atin ahi. Chuin amanin, Amaho chu nangma tobang ahiuvin, amitakip leng chapate tobang cheh ahiuve, tin adonbut lhone.
target: Then he asked Zebah and Zalmunna, “What kind of men did you kill at Tabor?” “Men like you,” they answered, “each one with the bearing of a prince.”

source: Chuin aman, Amaho chu kasopite ahiuvin, kanu chapa ngen ahiuve: Pakai ahin jing bangin, nangman amaho chu nana hinghoi hile, keiman nangni hi kathalhon louding nahi, ati.
target: Gideon replied, “Those were my brothers, the sons of my own mother. As surely as the Lord lives, if you had spared their lives, I would not kill you.”

source: Chuin aman achapa masapen Jether henga, Kipatdoh inlang amani hi thatnin, ati. Ahinla gollhang chun achem adohdohpoi: ajehchu ama chapang nalai ahijeh-in akichan ahi.
target: Turning to Jether, his oldest son, he said, “Kill them!” But Jether did not draw his sword, because he was only a boy and was afraid.

source: Chujouvin Zebah le Zalmunna'in, Nangma kipat inlang kachung lhonna hung chun; ajehchu mi ahi dungjuija, athahat jong umding ahi, atilhone. Chuin Gideon akipat doh-in, Zebah le Zalmunna chu athatnin, chule a-sangongsao ngonga um kijepnaho chu alan, ahi.
target: Zebah and Zalmunna said, “Come, do it yourself. ‘As is the man, so is his strength.’ ” So Gideon stepped forward and killed them, and took the ornaments off their camels’ necks.

source: Chujouchun Israel mihon Gideon henga, Nangmale nachate, chule natute geijin kachunguva vaihomin. Ajehchu nangman Media miho-a konin neihuhdoh uvin ahi, atiuve.
target: The Israelites said to Gideon, “Rule over us—you, your son and your grandson—because you have saved us from the hand of Midian.”

source: Chuin Gideon'in amaho henga, Keima kahin, kachate ahiuvin jong nangho chunga vai kahomlou dingu ahi; Pakaiyin nangho chunga vai ahom ding ahi, ati.
target: But Gideon told them, “I will not rule over you, nor will my son rule over you. The Lord will rule over you.”

source: Chuin Gideon amaho henga, Keiman nangho henga ngehnom khat kaneije, mijousen agalthil chomuva kona bilba ho jouse chu keima neipeuvin, ati (Ajehchu amahon sana bilba aneiju ahi; ajehchu amaho Ishmael mi hiuva ahi).
target: And he said, “I do have one request, that each of you give me an earring from your share of the plunder.” (It was the custom of the Ishmaelites to wear gold earrings.)

source: Chuin amahon adonbutnun, Keihon hicheho chu kipahtah-in peuvinge, atiuve. Chuin amahon pon aphaovin, ami takipmin gal thila kichomdoh bilba hochu asepkhom taovin ahi.
target: They answered, “We’ll be glad to give them.” So they spread out a garment, and each of them threw a ring from his plunder onto it.

source: Chuin aman athum sana bilbaho chu sana shekel sangkhat toh jasagi in agih-in; hicheho lah-a chu Midia lengho kivon na ngong'o, ponsandup ho, chule sangongsao hon angonguva aki-o'u khivuiho kisimtha lou ahi.
target: The weight of the gold rings he asked for came to seventeen hundred shekels, not counting the ornaments, the pendants and the purple garments worn by the kings of Midian or the chains that were on their camels’ necks.

source: Chuin Gideon'in thempu boitong sangkhol khat asemin, hichu ama khopi Ophrah ngeija akoijin ahi. Chuin Israelte jousen chukom mun'a chun acheuvin, noti'n apangun; hiche chu Gideon le a-insungmite dingin thang ahung sohtan ahi.
target: Gideon made the gold into an ephod, which he placed in Ophrah, his town. All Israel prostituted themselves by worshiping it there, and it became a snare to Gideon and his family.

source: Hitichun Midia te chun kiletsahna-a aluchangu aputkit louna dingun Israel chate masanga suhnemin aumtan ahi. Chule Gideon nikho sungin gamsung chu kum somli mongtah-in aumtan ahi.
target: Thus Midian was subdued before the Israelites and did not raise its head again. During Gideon’s lifetime, the land had peace forty years.

source: Chuin Joash chapa Jerubbaal achen, a-in'a agachengtan ahi.
target: Jerub-Baal son of Joash went back home to live.

source: Chule Gideon ama laigila kon chapa somsagi ahingin ahi. Ajehchu aman ji tamtah anei ahi.
target: He had seventy sons of his own, for he had many wives.

source: Chule Shechem'a cheng athaikemnu jongchun chapa khat ahinpeh-in, amin Abimelech asah-in ahi.
target: His concubine, who lived in Shechem, also bore him a son, whom he named Abimelek.

source: Chuin Joash chapa Gideon chu tehkem setnin athitan, Abiezer mite umna Ophrah mun'a um apa Joash vuikhuh-a chun avuitaovin ahi.
target: Gideon son of Joash died at a good old age and was buried in the tomb of his father Joash in Ophrah of the Abiezrites.

source: Chuin ahitin ahi, Gideon athi joujou chun, Israel chate chu akilehei kitnun, chule Baal henga noti chonin achon kitnun, Baal-berith chu a-pathen diuvin akisemuvin ahi.
target: No sooner had Gideon died than the Israelites again prostituted themselves to the Baals. They set up Baal-Berith as their god

source: Chule Israel chate amun jouse-a agaltehou khutna kona amaho huhdoh-a Pakai a-Pathen'u chu ageldoh tapouve.
target: and did not remember the Lord their God, who had rescued them from the hands of all their enemies on every side.

source: Chule Israelte anamusah phatna jouse dungjuijin jong, Gideon kiti Jerubbaal insung miho henga jong khotona amusah pouvin ahi.
target: They also failed to show any loyalty to the family of Jerub-Baal (that is, Gideon) in spite of all the good things he had done for them.

source: Chuin Jerubbaal chapa Abimelech chu Shechem'a anu sopite henga achen, amaho akihoupin, anu pa le a-insungmi jouse henga hitin aseije,
target: Abimelek son of Jerub-Baal went to his mother’s brothers in Shechem and said to them and to all his mother’s clan,

source: Katao ahi, Shechem'a cheng mijouse jah dingin seijun, Jerubbaal chapate somsagi chun nangho chunga vai ahom chu phajo-am, ahiloule mikhatnin nachung uva vai ahom chu phajo em? Keimahi nagu-u leh naphe-u kahi tijong geldoh-un, ati.
target: “Ask all the citizens of Shechem, ‘Which is better for you: to have all seventy of Jerub-Baal’s sons rule over you, or just one man?’ Remember, I am your flesh and blood.”

source: Chuin anu sopiho jousen Shechem'a cheng mijouse jah-a ama chungchanga hiche thu jouse chu aseijun ahile; alungun Abimelech nung juidingin aumtaove; ajehchu amahon, Amahi isopiu ahi, atiuve.
target: When the brothers repeated all this to the citizens of Shechem, they were inclined to follow Abimelek, for they said, “He is related to us.”

source: Chuin amahon Baal-berith in'a konin dangka somsagi apeuvin, hiche-a chun Abimelech'in pannabei le thulahlou miho agoijin, amahon anung ajuijun ahi.
target: They gave him seventy shekels of silver from the temple of Baal-Berith, and Abimelek used it to hire reckless scoundrels, who became his followers.

source: Chuin ama apa in Ophrah'ah achen, asopiho Jerubbaal chapate somsagi chu song khat chunga athatnin ahi. Jerubbaal chapa aneopen Jotham vangchu ahing hoijin ahi; ajehchu ama kisela ahi.
target: He went to his father’s home in Ophrah and on one stone murdered his seventy brothers, the sons of Jerub-Baal. But Jotham, the youngest son of Jerub-Baal, escaped by hiding.

source: Chuin Shechem miho jousele Millo insungmi jouse akikhomun, acheuvin, Abimelech chu Shechem'a um khompi phaichama chun lengin atungtaovin ahi.
target: Then all the citizens of Shechem and Beth Millo gathered beside the great tree at the pillar in Shechem to crown Abimelek king.

source: Chuin hichu Jotham aseipeh phatnun, ama achen Gerizim molvum'a adingin, aw sangtah-in asamin, amaho henga, Shechem'a um mihon, Pathen'in nathuseiju angainadin, keima thusei hi ngaijun.
target: When Jotham was told about this, he climbed up on the top of Mount Gerizim and shouted to them, “Listen to me, citizens of Shechem, so that God may listen to you.

source: Khatvei chu thingphung ho achunguva leng changding thao nu dingin achedoh-un; Olive thingjeh-a, Kachung uvah vaipon pangin atiuvin ahi.
target: One day the trees went out to anoint a king for themselves. They said to the olive tree, ‘Be our king.’

source: Ahinla Olive thing chun ahenguva, Mihem le Pathen jabolna kineiji kathao hi kadalhah-a, thingphung ho chunga dopsanga umdinga kache dingham? ati.
target: “But the olive tree answered, ‘Should I give up my oil, by which both gods and humans are honored, to hold sway over the trees?’

source: Chuin thingho chun theichang thing henga, Nangma hungin lang kachunguva vai hungpon atiuve.
target: “Next, the trees said to the fig tree, ‘Come and be our king.’

source: Ahinla theichang thing chun ahenguvah, Keiman kalhum na leh kaga phatah hi kadalhah-a, thingphung ho chunga dopsanga umdinga kache dingham? ati.
target: “But the fig tree replied, ‘Should I give up my fruit, so good and sweet, to hold sway over the trees?’

source: Chujou phatnin thingho chun lengpigui henga, Nangma hungin lang kachunguva vai hungpon atiuve.
target: “Then the trees said to the vine, ‘Come and be our king.’

source: Chuin lengpigui chun ahenguva, Mihem le Pathen kipasah ka ju hi kadalhah-a, thingphung ho chunga dopsanga umdinga kache dingham? ati.
target: “But the vine answered, ‘Should I give up my wine, which cheers both gods and humans, to hold sway over the trees?’

source: Chujou phatnin thing jouse chun theimi koma, Nangma hungin lang kachunguva vai hungpon, atiuve.
target: “Finally all the trees said to the thornbush, ‘Come and be our king.’

source: Chuin theimi chun thingho henga, Nanghon tahbeh-a nachung uva leng hidinga thao neinu uva ahileh, hungun lang natahsan naochu kalim'a hung ngam uvin: achuti louva ahile, theimi-a konhin mei hungpot doh henlang, Lebenon'a cedar thingho hi hung kavam hen, ati.
target: “The thornbush said to the trees, ‘If you really want to anoint me king over you, come and take refuge in my shade; but if not, then let fire come out of the thornbush and consume the cedars of Lebanon!’

source: Hiche jehchun tun, dihtahle lung thengsela Abimelech chu lenga nalhenu ahi-a, Jerubbaal le a-insung mite chunga phatecha nabolu ahi-a, chule akhutna achandinga kilom dungjuija achunga natong nahiuva ahile,
target: “Have you acted honorably and in good faith by making Abimelek king? Have you been fair to Jerub-Baal and his family? Have you treated him as he deserves?

source: (Ajehchu kapan nangho dinga gal asatna, ahinkho set toh dinga aphala, Midia miho khutna kona nahuh doh-u ahin;
target: Remember that my father fought for you and risked his life to rescue you from the hand of Midian.

source: Ahinla nanghon tunin kapa le a-insung mite dounan nakipat doh-un, achapate mi somsagi chu song khat chunga nathatnun, chule asohnu chapa Abimelech chu nasopiu ahijeh-in Shechem miho chunga lengin nasemun ahi.)
target: But today you have revolted against my father’s family. You have murdered his seventy sons on a single stone and have made Abimelek, the son of his female slave, king over the citizens of Shechem because he is related to you.

source: Tunia hi nanghon Jerubbaal le a-insung mite chunga kitah tahle lunggiltah-a natong nahi vangule, nangho Abimelech chunga kipah unlang, amajong nangho chunga kipahhen.
target: So have you acted honorably and in good faith toward Jerub-Baal and his family today? If you have, may Abimelek be your joy, and may you be his, too!

source: Amavang chuti ahi louva ahileh, Abimelech'a konin mei hungdoh henlang, Shechem miho le Millo insung chu kavamhen; chule Shechem mihole Millo insunga konin mei hungdoh henlang, Abimelech chu kavamhen, ati.
target: But if you have not, let fire come out from Abimelek and consume you, the citizens of Shechem and Beth Millo, and let fire come out from you, the citizens of Shechem and Beth Millo, and consume Abimelek!”

source: Chuin Jotham alhaijin, ajam mangin, Beer kho-a achen, asopipa Abimelech agin jeh-in chuachun achengtai.
target: Then Jotham fled, escaping to Beer, and he lived there because he was afraid of his brother Abimelek.

source: Israelte chunga Abimelech'in kumthum vai apoh jouvin,
target: After Abimelek had governed Israel three years,

source: Pathen'in Abimelech le Shechem miho kikah-a lhagao phalou ahinsolin; chule Shechem miho chun Abimelech chu lungthim kitahloutah-in abolun:
target: God stirred up animosity between Abimelek and the citizens of Shechem so that they acted treacherously against Abimelek.

source: Hichu gilou tah-a anabolu Jerubbaal chate mi somsagi ho phu chu achunguva achuh theina dingle, athisannu phu chu athatnuva pang asopipau Abimelech chunga achuh-a; chule asopihou thana dinga kithopi-a Shechem miho chunga achuh theina dinga chuti ahi.
target: God did this in order that the crime against Jerub-Baal’s seventy sons, the shedding of their blood, might be avenged on their brother Abimelek and on the citizens of Shechem, who had helped him murder his brothers.

source: Chuin Shechem miho chun molchunga ama changlhi ding akoijun, chule amahon chuche lampia amaho hinhopa jouse chu achomun: chule hiche thu chu Abimelech henga akiseipeh tan ahi.
target: In opposition to him these citizens of Shechem set men on the hilltops to ambush and rob everyone who passed by, and this was reported to Abimelek.

source: Chuin Ebed chapa Gaal chu asopihotoh ahungin, Shechem agalkaijun; chule Shechem miho chun ama chu atahsanun ahi.
target: Now Gaal son of Ebed moved with his clan into Shechem, and its citizens put their confidence in him.

source: Chuin amaho loujaova apotdoh-un, alengpi theihou chu alohkhomun, achilun, kipa golnop abolun, chule a-pathen'u in'a alutnun, aneuvin, adonnun, chule Abimelech chu agaosap uvin ahi.
target: After they had gone out into the fields and gathered the grapes and trodden them, they held a festival in the temple of their god. While they were eating and drinking, they cursed Abimelek.

source: Chuin Ebed chapa Gaal'in, Abimelech chu koi hija, chule Shechem chu koi hija, eihon ama ijendiu ham? Amachu Jerubbaal chapa hilouham? Chule avaipo chu Zebul hilou ham? Shechem pa Hamor miho chu jenuvin: ajehchu ipidinga ama ijendingu ham?
target: Then Gaal son of Ebed said, “Who is Abimelek, and why should we Shechemites be subject to him? Isn’t he Jerub-Baal’s son, and isn’t Zebul his deputy? Serve the family of Hamor, Shechem’s father! Why should we serve Abimelek?

source: Chule amahohi Pathen'in kakhutnoija aumsah hile, keiman Abimelech kalahdoh ding ahi, ati. Chuin aman Abimelech henga, Nagalsat mi supungin lang, hung doh-in, ati.
target: If only this people were under my command! Then I would get rid of him. I would say to Abimelek, ‘Call out your whole army!’ ”

source: Chuin khopi vaipo Zebul chun Ebed chapa Gaal thusei ajah phatnin, alunghan akongjah tan ahi.
target: When Zebul the governor of the city heard what Gaal son of Ebed said, he was very angry.

source: Chuin aman Abimelech henga guhthimin thupo asolin, ajah-a, Ven, Ebed chapa Gaal le asopiho Shechem'a ahungun; chule vetemin, amahon nangma dounan khopi kul akai taove.
target: Under cover he sent messengers to Abimelek, saying, “Gaal son of Ebed and his clan have come to Shechem and are stirring up the city against you.

source: Hijeh chun tun nangma naumpi nasopi ho toh jan-in kipat unlang, loujaova chang lhiuvin;
target: Now then, during the night you and your men should come and lie in wait in the fields.

source: Chule hitiding ahi, jingkah-a nisa ahungso sole, nangma jingpitah-in thoudoh inlang, khopi chu nokhumin: chule ven, amale aumpiho nang douna ahung tengule, nangman aphat namu dungjuija achunguva na natohding ahi, ati.
target: In the morning at sunrise, advance against the city. When Gaal and his men come out against you, seize the opportunity to attack them.”

source: Chuin Abimelech aumpiho toh jannin athouvun, chule loi li akiso-un Shechem douna-in achang pangun ahi.
target: So Abimelek and all his troops set out by night and took up concealed positions near Shechem in four companies.

source: Chuin Ebed chapa Gaal apotdoh-in, khopi lutna kotpi-a chun adingin; chule Abimelech le aumpiho chu akisel naova konin ahungpot doh-un ahi.
target: Now Gaal son of Ebed had gone out and was standing at the entrance of the city gate just as Abimelek and his troops came out from their hiding place.

source: Chuin Gaal'in miho chu amuphatnin, Zebul henga, Ven mipikhu molsang chunga konin miho ahungsuh uve, ati. Chuin Zebul'in ahenga, Molsang le-lim ho chu nangin mi-a namu hinte, atin ahi.
target: When Gaal saw them, he said to Zebul, “Look, people are coming down from the tops of the mountains!” Zebul replied, “You mistake the shadows of the mountains for men.”

source: Chuin Gaal'in aseikitnin, Ven, lampia gamsung kimlai tah-a konin miho ahung suh-in, chule loi dangjong Meonemin phaicham ahunge ati.
target: But Gaal spoke up again: “Look, people are coming down from the central hill, and a company is coming from the direction of the diviners’ tree.”

source: Hichun Zebul'in ahenga, Abimelech chu koi hija, amachu ijen diuham? tia nathuseina nakam chu tu-a hoilama um hitam? Hiche mihohi hilou ham nangin nataitom chu? Katao ahi, potdoh inlang, gakisatpin ati.
target: Then Zebul said to him, “Where is your big talk now, you who said, ‘Who is Abimelek that we should be subject to him?’ Aren’t these the men you ridiculed? Go out and fight them!”

source: Chuin Gaal chu Shechem miho masanga achedoh-in, Abimelech akisatpi tai.
target: So Gaal led out the citizens of Shechem and fought Abimelek.

source: Chuin Abimelech'in ama chu adelin ahile, ama masanga ajamtan; kotpi lutna geijin mi tamtah alhun, akitongkhan ahi.
target: Abimelek chased him all the way to the entrance of the gate, and many were killed as they fled.

source: Chuin Abimelech Arumah'a achengtai. Chule Zebul'in Gaal leh asopiho chu Shechem'a achen nalou diuvin anomangin ahi.
target: Then Abimelek stayed in Arumah, and Zebul drove Gaal and his clan out of Shechem.

source: Chuin ajingin ahitin ahi, mipi chu lou jaova apotdoh-un; hichu Abimelech aseipeh taovin ahi.
target: The next day the people of Shechem went out to the fields, and this was reported to Abimelek.

source: Chuin aman mipi chu akipuijin, hopthum in ahomin, loujaova chun achang pangun, chule aveovin ahile, veuvin, mipi ho chu khopi-a kona ahungdoh-un; chuin amaho dounan akipatdoh-in, amaho chu athat tai.
target: So he took his men, divided them into three companies and set an ambush in the fields. When he saw the people coming out of the city, he rose to attack them.

source: Chuin Abimelech le aumpiho chu amasang lamuva alhaijun, khopi lutna kotpi-a chun adingun; adang loini chun loujaova umho chu anokhumun, athatgam taovin ahi.
target: Abimelek and the companies with him rushed forward to a position at the entrance of the city gate. Then two companies attacked those in the fields and struck them down.

source: Chuin Abimelech'in nilhum keijin khopi chu akisatpin; chule khopi chu alan, asunga cheng jouse chu athatnin, khopi chu asuchimin, asugoi selin ahi.
target: All that day Abimelek pressed his attack against the city until he had captured it and killed its people. Then he destroyed the city and scattered salt over it.

source: Chuin Shechem daivei insanga umhon hichu ajah phatnun, Berith pathen in'a kohomsung khatna alut taove.
target: On hearing this, the citizens in the tower of Shechem went into the stronghold of the temple of El-Berith.

source: Chuin Shechem daivei insanga um mijouse akikhom khomtai tichu Abimelech ahil taovin ahi.
target: When Abimelek heard that they had assembled there,

source: Chuin Abimelech ama le aumpi mijousetoh Zalmon molsanga akaldoh-un; chule Abimelech'in akhutna heicha akichoijin, thinga konin abah alhamlhan, hichu alan, alenga apun, chule aumpiho henga chun, Ipi kabol namu bangun, kino uvin, kabol bang banghin bolun, ati.
target: he and all his men went up Mount Zalmon. He took an ax and cut off some branches, which he lifted to his shoulders. He ordered the men with him, “Quick! Do what you have seen me do!”

source: Chuin mipi jouse chun Abimelech bol bang chun athingbah ding cheh-u alham lhaovin, Abimelech nung ajuijun, kohoma chun akoijun, achunguva kohom chu ahal khumun; hitichun Shechem daivei insanga umho jong chu athi taovin, amaho chu numei le pasal sangkhat tobang ahiuve.
target: So all the men cut branches and followed Abimelek. They piled them against the stronghold and set it on fire with the people still inside. So all the people in the tower of Shechem, about a thousand men and women, also died.

source: Chujouvin Abimelech chu Thebez'ah achen, chule Thebez kho dounan gebuh agasongin, ahin latan ahi.
target: Next Abimelek went to Thebez and besieged it and captured it.

source: Ahinla khopi sunga chun daivei insang dettah khat aumin, hiche sunga chun numei le pasal, chule khopi sunga um mijouse chu akikha khumun; kul chunga chun ahung kaldoh-un ahi.
target: Inside the city, however, was a strong tower, to which all the men and women—all the people of the city—had fled. They had locked themselves in and climbed up on the tower roof.

source: Chuin Abimelech insanga chun ahungin, ahung satnin, meija hal dingin insang kotphung lama ahungin ahi.
target: Abimelek went to the tower and attacked it. But as he approached the entrance to the tower to set it on fire,

source: Chuin numei khatnin sumheisong halkhatnin Abimelech luchang ahinsepmin, alugu asepkeh tan ahi.
target: a woman dropped an upper millstone on his head and cracked his skull.

source: Hichun aman agalvonpo gollhangpa chu gangtah-in akouvin, ahenga, Mihon numei tha ahi eiti lounadin nachemjam satdoh inlang neithatnin ati. Chuin gollhangpa chun asunpaijin ama athitai.
target: Hurriedly he called to his armor-bearer, “Draw your sword and kill me, so that they can’t say, ‘A woman killed him.’ ” So his servant ran him through, and he died.

source: Chuin Israel miho chun Abimelech athi amuphatnuvin, amitakip ama mun cheh-a achetauve.
target: When the Israelites saw that Abimelek was dead, they went home.

source: Hitichun Pathen'in Abimelech'in asopi somsagi atha-a, apa chunga akhansetna jouse chu alethuh tan ahi.
target: Thus God repaid the wickedness that Abimelek had done to his father by murdering his seventy brothers.

source: Chule Shechem miho thilse bol jouse chu Pathen'in aluchung uva akhuhpeh-in; chule achunguva Jerubbaal chapa Jotham sapsetna chu ahung lhungtan ahi.
target: God also made the people of Shechem pay for all their wickedness. The curse of Jotham son of Jerub-Baal came on them.

source: Chuin Abimelech nungin Issachar mi Dodo chapa, Pu-ah chaoa, Tolla chu Israel huhdohdin ahung kipatdoh-in; chule amachu Ephraim molsanga um Shamir kho-a cheng ahi.
target: After the time of Abimelek, a man of Issachar named Tola son of Puah, the son of Dodo, rose to save Israel. He lived in Shamir, in the hill country of Ephraim.

source: Chuin aman kum somni le kumthum Israelte thu atanin, chuin athin, Shamir'a akivuijin ahi.
target: He led Israel twenty-three years; then he died, and was buried in Shamir.

source: Chuin ama nungin Gilead mi Jair ahung kipatdoh-in, kum somni le kumni Israelte thu atanin ahi.
target: He was followed by Jair of Gilead, who led Israel twenty-two years.

source: Chule aman sanganchal chunga toucheh chapa somthum aneijin, chule amahon khopi somthum aneijun, tunichan geihin Havoth-jair akitin, hicheho chu Gilead gamsunga um ahi.
target: He had thirty sons, who rode thirty donkeys. They controlled thirty towns in Gilead, which to this day are called Havvoth Jair.

source: Chuin Jair athin, chule Camon'a akivuitan ahi.
target: When Jair died, he was buried in Kamon.

source: Chuin Israel chate chun Pakai masanga thil gilou abolkit taovin, Baal le Ashtaroth, chule Syria pathenho, Zion pathenho, Moab pathenho, Ammon chate pathenho, chule Philistine te pathenho ajenun, Pakai chu adalhaovin, amachu jenjong ajen pouvin ahi.
target: Again the Israelites did evil in the eyes of the Lord . They served the Baals and the Ashtoreths, and the gods of Aram, the gods of Sidon, the gods of Moab, the gods of the Ammonites and the gods of the Philistines. And because the Israelites forsook the Lord and no longer served him,

source: Chuin Pakai lunghana chu Israelte chunga asoudoh tan, chule aman Philistine te khut le Ammon chate khutna ajoh dohtan ahi.
target: he became angry with them. He sold them into the hands of the Philistines and the Ammonites,

source: Chuin hiche kum-a patchun amahon Israel chate, Jordan gala um Amor mite gam Gilead'a um Israel chate jouse chu kum somle kumget sung asugentheijun, anoijuva akun sah-un ahi.
target: who that year shattered and crushed them. For eighteen years they oppressed all the Israelites on the east side of the Jordan in Gilead, the land of the Amorites.

source: Chukalvalin Ammon chate chu Judah douna le, Benjamin douna, chule Ephraim insungmi douna kisatpi dingin Jordan agalkaijun; hitichun Israel ahesoh lheh jengtan ahi.
target: The Ammonites also crossed the Jordan to fight against Judah, Benjamin and Ephraim; Israel was in great distress.

source: Chuin Israel chate chu Pakai henga apengun, Nangma dounan kachonse taove, ajehchu ka Pathen'u kadalhaovin, Baal jeng kahoutaovin ahi, atiuve.
target: Then the Israelites cried out to the Lord , “We have sinned against you, forsaking our God and serving the Baals.”

source: Chuin Pakaiyin Israel chate henga, Keiman nangho Egypt mite-a kona, Amor mite-a kona, Ammon chate-a kon, chule Philistine te-a kona kahuhdoh nahilouvu ham?
target: The Lord replied, “When the Egyptians, the Amorites, the Ammonites, the Philistines,

source: Zidon miten jong, Amalek mite, chule Maon miten nasuh gentheijuvin; chuin kahenga natao ule, amaho khutna konin kahuhdoh-un ahi.
target: the Sidonians, the Amalekites and the Maonites oppressed you and you cried to me for help, did I not save you from their hands?

source: Ahijeng vangin nanghon keima neidalhaovin, pathen dangho najenun ahi; hijeh chun keiman nangho nahuhdoh kit tapouvinge.
target: But you have forsaken me and served other gods, so I will no longer save you.

source: Cheovinlang nanghon nakilhenu pathenho henga chun gakap taovin; amaho chun nangho nahesoh genthei naova konin nahuhdoh-u hen, ati.
target: Go and cry out to the gods you have chosen. Let them save you when you are in trouble!”

source: Chuin Israel chate chun Pakai henga, Keiho kachonse taove. Nangman pha nasah dungjuijin kachunguva boljengin; kataovu ahi, tuni hin nei huhdoh pou pouvun, atiuve.
target: But the Israelites said to the Lord , “We have sinned. Do with us whatever you think best, but please rescue us now.”

source: Chuin amahon alah uva konin gamdang pathenho chu apaimangun, Pakai chu ajen taove. Chuin Israelte gim gentheina chu athohjou tapon ahi.
target: Then they got rid of the foreign gods among them and served the Lord . And he could bear Israel’s misery no longer.

source: Chujouchun Ammon chate akikhom khomun, Gilead'a gebuh asongtaove. Chule Israel chate jong akikhom khomun, Mizpeh'a gebuh asongtaovin ahi.
target: When the Ammonites were called to arms and camped in Gilead, the Israelites assembled and camped at Mizpah.

source: Chuin Gilead leng chapatele miho chu khatle khat akihouvun, Ammon chate douna kisatpi dinga hung kipandoh ding chu itobang mi ham? Ama chu Gilead gama chengho jouse lamkaija pang ding ahi, atiuve.
target: The leaders of the people of Gilead said to each other, “Whoever will take the lead in attacking the Ammonites will be head over all who live in Gilead.”

source: Tun Gilead mi Jephthah chu mihat hangsantah ahin, amahi noti chapa ahin; chule Gilead'in Jephthah ahingin ahi.
target: Jephthah the Gileadite was a mighty warrior. His father was Gilead; his mother was a prostitute.

source: Chule Gilead jinu chun chapate ahingin; chule ajinu chapate chu ahungkhang lennun, amahon Jephthah chu anomangun, ahenga, Nangman kapao in nalo louding ahi; ajehchu nangma hetlou numei cha nahi, atiuve.
target: Gilead’s wife also bore him sons, and when they were grown up, they drove Jephthah away. “You are not going to get any inheritance in our family,” they said, “because you are the son of another woman.”

source: Chujouvin asopiho-a konin Jephthah ajamangin, Tob gama agachengtai. Chuin pannabei miho Jephthah toh akiloijun, amatoh michomin ache jiuvin ahi.
target: So Jephthah fled from his brothers and settled in the land of Tob, where a gang of scoundrels gathered around him and followed him.

source: Chujou chomkhat jouvin ahung hitin ahi, Ammon chate chun Israel chunga gal ahin bolun ahi.
target: Some time later, when the Ammonites were fighting against Israel,

source: Chuin ahitin ahi, Ammon chaten Israel chunga gal abol phatnun, Gilead upaho chu Tob gama kona Jephthah puidoh dingin achedoh taove.
target: the elders of Gilead went to get Jephthah from the land of Tob.

source: Chuin amahon Jephthah henga, Hungin, Ammon chate toh ikisat theina dingun, keiho gal lamkaijin hung pangin, atiuve.
target: “Come,” they said, “be our commander, so we can fight the Ammonites.”

source: Chuin Jephthah'in Gilead upaho henga, Nanghon neihot uva, Kapa in'a kona neikai doh-u hilou ham? Chule ibola tu-a hi nagenthei phatnuva kahenga hunga nahiuvem? ati.
target: Jephthah said to them, “Didn’t you hate me and drive me from my father’s house? Why do you come to me now, when you’re in trouble?”

source: Chuin Gilead upaho chun Jephthah henga, Hiche jeh-a chu Ammon chateho toh kisat dinga nangma keiho to nalhona, chule Gilead'a chengho jouse chunga kalamkai uva napana dinga, nahenga hung kihei kit kahiuve, atiuvin ahi.
target: The elders of Gilead said to him, “Nevertheless, we are turning to you now; come with us to fight the Ammonites, and you will be head over all of us who live in Gilead.”

source: Chuin Jephthah'in Gilead upaho henga, Ammon chate satdinga in'a neipui kitnuva, chule Pakaiyin amaho chu ka angsunga eipehdoh-a ahile, keima nalamkai uva kapan mongding ham? ati.
target: Jephthah answered, “Suppose you take me back to fight the Ammonites and the Lord gives them to me—will I really be your head?”

source: Chuin Gilead upahon Jephthah henga, Nathu sei banga kabol lou uleh, Pakai chu ikah uva ahetoh hihen, atiuve.
target: The elders of Gilead replied, “The Lord is our witness; we will certainly do as you say.”

source: Chuin Jephthah Gilead upaho toh alhonin, chule miho chun amachu achunguva vaipo dingle alamkai diuvin asemun; chule Jephthah'in hicheng thu jousehi Mizpah mun'a Pakai angsunga asei ahi.
target: So Jephthah went with the elders of Gilead, and the people made him head and commander over them. And he repeated all his words before the Lord in Mizpah.

source: Chuin Jephthah'in Ammon chate lengpa henga thupo ho asolin, ajah-a, Nangman keima ilo ding neiti-a, kagam sunga keima douva kisatpi dinga hunga nahim? atin ahi.
target: Then Jephthah sent messengers to the Ammonite king with the question: “What do you have against me that you have attacked my country?”

source: Chuin Ammon chate lengpan Jephthah thupo ho chu adonbutnin, Israel ten Egypt gama ahungdoh laijuva kagam'u Arnon'a kona Jabbok, chule Jordan geija alo jeh-u ahi: hijeh chun tun hiche gamho chu kicham delin neilepeh kit taovin, atin ahi.
target: The king of the Ammonites answered Jephthah’s messengers, “When Israel came up out of Egypt, they took away my land from the Arnon to the Jabbok, all the way to the Jordan. Now give it back peaceably.”

source: Chuin Jephthah in Ammon chate lengpa henga thusep mi asol kitnin:
target: Jephthah sent back messengers to the Ammonite king,

source: Ahenga, Jephthah'in hitihin aseije, Israel'in Moab gam alahpeh pouvin, chule Ammon chate gam jong alahmang peh pouvin ahi.
target: saying: “This is what Jephthah says: Israel did not take the land of Moab or the land of the Ammonites.

source: Ahin Israel Egypt'a kona ahungdoh-u chun, twipisan geijin gamthip gam ahin jotnun, chule Kadesh ahung lhungun ahi.
target: But when they came up out of Egypt, Israel went through the wilderness to the Red Sea and on to Kadesh.

source: Chuin Israel'in Edom lengpa henga thusep asolin, Nahenga katao ahi, nagamsung neijot galkai sah-in, atin; ahinla Edom lengpan angaipeh pon ahi. Chuin hiche bangma chun Moab lengpa henga thusep asolkitnin; ahin aman jong anoppeh dehpoi. Hijeh chun Israel Kadesh'a aumdentai.
target: Then Israel sent messengers to the king of Edom, saying, ‘Give us permission to go through your country,’ but the king of Edom would not listen. They sent also to the king of Moab, and he refused. So Israel stayed at Kadesh.

source: Chujouvin amahon gamthip lah ahin jotnun, Edom gam le Moab gam chu avelkolun, Moab gam solam sanga ahungun, Arnon gal lampanga gebuh asaovin, ahivangin Moab gam gamgi sunga ahunglut pouvin ahi. Ajehchu Arnon hi Moab gamgi ahi.
target: “Next they traveled through the wilderness, skirted the lands of Edom and Moab, passed along the eastern side of the country of Moab, and camped on the other side of the Arnon. They did not enter the territory of Moab, for the Arnon was its border.

source: Chuin Israel'in Amor mite lengpa, Heshbon lengpa Sihon henga thusep asolin, chule Israel'in ahenga, Nahenga katao ahi, kagam kalut theina dingin, nagam chu neipal galkaisah-in, ati.
target: “Then Israel sent messengers to Sihon king of the Amorites, who ruled in Heshbon, and said to him, ‘Let us pass through your country to our own place.’

source: Ahin Sihon'in agamsung pal galkai ding chun Israel chu atahsan pon: ahivangin Silhon'in amiteho jouse akhom khomin, Jahaz'a gebuh asongun, chule Israel akisatpi tan ahi.
target: Sihon, however, did not trust Israel to pass through his territory. He mustered all his troops and encamped at Jahaz and fought with Israel.

source: Ahivangin Pakai Israel Pathen'in Shihon le amite jouse chu Israel khutna apedoh tan, chuin amahon amaho chu athatnuvin ahi. Hitichun Israel'in chuche gama cheng Amor mite gam jouse chu alo taovin ahi.
target: “Then the Lord , the God of Israel, gave Sihon and his whole army into Israel’s hands, and they defeated them. Israel took over all the land of the Amorites who lived in that country,

source: Chuin amahon Arnon'a kon Jabbok geijin jong, chule gamthip gama kon Jordan geijin Amor mite gamsung chu alo taovin ahi.
target: capturing all of it from the Arnon to the Jabbok and from the desert to the Jordan.

source: Hitichun tun Israel Pakai Pathen'in Amor mite chu amite Israel masanga konchun anodoh ahitan; nangman hichu nalo dingham?
target: “Now since the Lord , the God of Israel, has driven the Amorites out before his people Israel, what right have you to take it over?

source: Nangman na-pathen Chemosh'in nalo dinga napeh chu nalo louding ham? Hijeh chun Pakai ka Pathen'un kamasanguva kona adeldoh hou gamsung chu kalo dingu ahi.
target: Will you not take what your god Chemosh gives you? Likewise, whatever the Lord our God has given us, we will possess.

source: Chule tu-a hi nangho Moab leng Zippor chapa Balak sanga phajo nahiuvem? Aman Israel douna kiphin kha-em? Ahiloule amaho akidoupi khah-em?
target: Are you any better than Balak son of Zippor, king of Moab? Did he ever quarrel with Israel or fight with them?

source: Israel chu Heshbon le akholenho, Arnon le akholenho, Aroer le akholenho, chule Arnon panga khopiho jouse-a kum jathum achen laija chu? Chuche phat sunga chu ibola ana kinunglah kitlou nahim?
target: For three hundred years Israel occupied Heshbon, Aroer, the surrounding settlements and all the towns along the Arnon. Why didn’t you retake them during that time?

source: Hijeh chun keima nangma dounan kachonsepoi, nangman keima neidouhi kachunga dihlou joh nahi. Thutan Pakai chun tunikho hin Israel chate le Ammon chate kikah-a thu tanhen, ati.
target: I have not wronged you, but you are doing me wrong by waging war against me. Let the Lord , the Judge, decide the dispute this day between the Israelites and the Ammonites.”

source: Ahivangin Ammon chate lengpan Jephthah'in ahin misol ahinsola thu asei chu ngaipeh-in aneipon ahi.
target: The king of Ammon, however, paid no attention to the message Jephthah sent him.

source: Chujouvin Pakai Lhagao chu Jephthah chunga achun, chule ama Gilead le Manasseh agalkaijin, Gilead gama Mizpeh agalkaijin, chule Mizpeh'a um Gilead gama Mizpeh'a konin Ammon chate umnalam ajonin ahi.
target: Then the Spirit of the Lord came on Jephthah. He crossed Gilead and Manasseh, passed through Mizpah of Gilead, and from there he advanced against the Ammonites.

source: Chuin Jephthah'in Pakai henga kihahsel na-in akihahselin, chule hitin aseije, Nangman Ammon chate chu kakhutna thonlouva neipehdoh-a ahile,
target: And Jephthah made a vow to the Lord : “If you give the Ammonites into my hands,

source: Hitiding ahi, Ammon chate-a kona lungmonga kahung kilekit tengle, eikimutopi dinga kakotna kona hungpotdoh masapen chu thonlouva Pakaiya hiding, chule keiman govam thilto-a katoding ahi, ati.
target: whatever comes out of the door of my house to meet me when I return in triumph from the Ammonites will be the Lord ’s, and I will sacrifice it as a burnt offering.”

source: Hitichun Jephthah chu Ammon mite satdingin ahenglam uva achen; chule Pakaiyin amaho chu akhutna apedoh tan ahi.
target: Then Jephthah went over to fight the Ammonites, and the Lord gave them into his hands.

source: Chuin aman amaho chu Aroer'a kipat in Minnith changeijin athatpeh-in, khopi somnijen, chule lengpilei phaicham geijin hathan athattan ahi. Hitichun Ammon chate chu Israel chate masanga suhnemin aumun ahi.
target: He devastated twenty towns from Aroer to the vicinity of Minnith, as far as Abel Keramim. Thus Israel subdued Ammon.

source: Chuin Jephthah Mizpeh kho-a a-in'a ahungin ahile, veuvin, achanu ama kimupi din khongcha beng pumle lam pumin ahungdoh-in ahi. Amahi chanu changkhat seh ahin; amanu tailou hi chapa le chanu dang aneilou ahi.
target: When Jephthah returned to his home in Mizpah, who should come out to meet him but his daughter, dancing to the sound of timbrels! She was an only child. Except for her he had neither son nor daughter.

source: Chuin ahitin ahi, aman amanu amuphatnin, apon abotkeh-in, Kaden Kachanu! nangman keima neisunem lheh-in, chule nangma hi eisugimho lah-a khat nahitai. Ajehchu keima Pakai henga kana kamkatan, chule kih theilou ding kahitai, ati.
target: When he saw her, he tore his clothes and cried, “Oh no, my daughter! You have brought me down and I am devastated. I have made a vow to the Lord that I cannot break.”

source: Chuin amanun ahenga, Hepa, nangman Pakai henga nakam nanakat ahitah-a ahile, nangman nakama nana phondoh bangbang chun kachunga boltan; ajehchu Pakaiyin nagalmite Ammon chate chunga phu nalahpeh ahitai, ati.
target: “My father,” she replied, “you have given your word to the Lord . Do to me just as you promised, now that the Lord has avenged you of your enemies, the Ammonites.

source: Chuin amanun apa henga, Hichehi keima dingin neibol peh-in, Molsang chung dunga kachesuh kachetouva, kagol hotoh nungah theng kahina pul kagadou nadiuvin, lhani neichang lhan, ati.
target: But grant me this one request,” she said. “Give me two months to roam the hills and weep with my friends, because I will never marry.”

source: Chuin aman, Chen, ati. Hitichun aman amanu chu lhani sunga dinga asolmang tan ahi. Chuin amanu aloiho toh achen, molsang chungho-a chun nungah theng ahina pul chu agadou tan ahi.
target: “You may go,” he said. And he let her go for two months. She and her friends went into the hills and wept because she would never marry.

source: Chuin lhani nungin ahitin ahi, amanu apa henga ahung kinunglen, aman akitepna bangin amanu chunga atongtan: chule amanu pasal to akitimat pon ahi. Chule hichehi Israelte chonna dan ahung hitan,
target: After the two months, she returned to her father, and he did to her as he had vowed. And she was a virgin. From this comes the Israelite tradition

source: Hitichun Israel chanute chu Gilead mi Jephthah chanu lunghempi nan kumseh leh nili achedoh jiuvin ahi.
target: that each year the young women of Israel go out for four days to commemorate the daughter of Jephthah the Gileadite.

source: Chuin Ephraim miho chu akikhom khomun, sahlama acheuvin, Jephthah henga, Ipijeh-a Ammon chate kisatpi dinga nahung galkaija, chule ibola naki lhonpi dinga neikou lou uham? Na inpuma kahal khum dingu nahi, atiuve.
target: The Ephraimite forces were called out, and they crossed over to Zaphon. They said to Jephthah, “Why did you go to fight the Ammonites without calling us to go with you? We’re going to burn down your house over your head.”

source: Chuin Jephthah ahenguva, Keima le kamite Ammon chateto hatah in kakisat nun, kahinkou laijun akhut uva konin neihuh doh pouve.
target: Jephthah answered, “I and my people were engaged in a great struggle with the Ammonites, and although I called, you didn’t save me out of their hands.

source: Chuin neihuhdoh louvu kahet phatnin, kahinkho kaki choithon, Ammon chate kisatpi din kagalkaijin, Pakaiyin amaho chu kakhutna eipehdohtan ahi. Achutile ibola tunia hi keima to kisat dinga nahung kon uham? ati.
target: When I saw that you wouldn’t help, I took my life in my hands and crossed over to fight the Ammonites, and the Lord gave me the victory over them. Now why have you come up today to fight me?”
