source: Chuin Jephthah'in Gilead mihojouse akhomin, Ephraim toh akisat tai. Chule Gilead mihon Ephraim miho chu athat taove; ajehchu amahon, Nangho Gilead mite hi Ephraim'a kona jammang, Ephraim mite le Manasseh mite lah-a kona jam mangho nahiuve, atijiu ahi.
target: Jephthah then called together the men of Gilead and fought against Ephraim. The Gileadites struck them down because the Ephraimites had said, “You Gileadites are renegades from Ephraim and Manasseh.”

source: Chuin Gilead miho chun Ephraim miho lhun masanga Jordan galkainaho chu ana laovin: chule ahung hitin ahi Ephraim mite ahung jamdoh hochun, nei galkai sah-un ati tengule; Gilead miho chun ahenguva, Nangma Ephraim mi nahim? tin adong jiuvin; amahon, Kahipoi, ati-a ahile,
target: The Gileadites captured the fords of the Jordan leading to Ephraim, and whenever a survivor of Ephraim said, “Let me cross over,” the men of Gilead asked him, “Are you an Ephraimite?” If he replied, “No,”

source: Amahon ahenga, Chuti ahile Shibboleth gah ti-in ati jiuvin: chuteng aman Sibboleth ati jin ahi; ajehchu dihtah-a aseidoh thei jilou ahi. Chuteng amahon amapa chu aman jiuvin, Jordan vadung lampia chun athat jiuvin ahi. Hitichun hiche chunga chun Ephraim chu mi sangsomli le sangni athatnun ahi.
target: they said, “All right, say ‘Shibboleth.’ ” If he said, “Sibboleth,” because he could not pronounce the word correctly, they seized him and killed him at the fords of the Jordan. Forty-two thousand Ephraimites were killed at that time.

source: Chule Jephthah'in Israelte chunga kumgup thu atanin ahi. Chujouvin Gilead mi Jephthah chu athitan, chule Gilead khopi ho sung khatna akivuitan ahi.
target: Jephthah led Israel six years. Then Jephthah the Gileadite died and was buried in a town in Gilead.

source: Chuin ama nungin Bethlehem'a um Ibzan'in Israelte thu atanin ahi.
target: After him, Ibzan of Bethlehem led Israel.

source: Chule aman chapa somthum le chanu somthum aneijin, aman hiche achanute chu gamdanga asolin, chule achapate dingchu gamdangmi chanu somthum apuipeh-in ahi. Chule ama Israelte chunga kum sagi thutanin apangin ahi.
target: He had thirty sons and thirty daughters. He gave his daughters away in marriage to those outside his clan, and for his sons he brought in thirty young women as wives from outside his clan. Ibzan led Israel seven years.

source: Chujouvin Ibzan athitan, Bethlehem'a avuitaovin ahi.
target: Then Ibzan died and was buried in Bethlehem.

source: Chuin amanungin Zebulun mi Elon'in Israel chate thu atanin; chule aman Israelte chunga kumsom thutanin apangin ahi.
target: After him, Elon the Zebulunite led Israel ten years.

source: Chuin Zebulun mi Elon athitan, chule Zebulun gamsunga um Aijalon mun'a akivuitan ahi.
target: Then Elon died and was buried in Aijalon in the land of Zebulun.

source: Chule amanungin Pirathon mi Hillel chapa Abdon chu Israelte thutanin apangin ahi.
target: After him, Abdon son of Hillel, from Pirathon, led Israel.

source: Chule aman chapa somli leh tu somthum aneijin, sangan gol somsagi chunga atouvin ahi. Aman Israelte chunga kumget thu anatanin ahi.
target: He had forty sons and thirty grandsons, who rode on seventy donkeys. He led Israel eight years.

source: Chuin Pirathon mi Hillel chapa Abdon athitan, Ephraim gama Amalek mite molsanga um Pirathon munna akivuijin ahi.
target: Then Abdon son of Hillel died and was buried at Pirathon in Ephraim, in the hill country of the Amalekites.

source: Chuin Israel chaten Pakai mitmun thilse abolkit taovin ahile, Pakaiyin amaho chu Philistine te khutna kum somli apedohtan ahi.
target: Again the Israelites did evil in the eyes of the Lord , so the Lord delivered them into the hands of the Philistines for forty years.

source: Hichelai chun Zorah kho-a Dan phunga kon Manoah kiti khat anaumin; chule ajinu chu aching ahin, chaneilou ahi.
target: A certain man of Zorah, named Manoah, from the clan of the Danites, had a wife who was childless, unable to give birth.

source: Chuin Pakai vantil chu numeinu henga chun ahung kilah-in, amanu henga, Tun vetemin, nangma achinga nahin, cha nahingpoi; ahinla nangman nao nahinvop ding, chule chapa khat naneiding ahi.
target: The angel of the Lord appeared to her and said, “You are barren and childless, but you are going to become pregnant and give birth to a son.

source: Katao ahi, hichejeh chun chingtheijin, ju le khamnathei donhih-in, chule thilthenglou kiti poupou jong nehih-in.
target: Now see to it that you drink no wine or other fermented drink and that you do not eat anything unclean.

source: Ajehchu vetan, nangma gaijin natin, chapa khat nanei ding; aluchanga samchem kilam louding ahi. Ajehchu naosen chu naobu-a kon Pathen'a dinga Nazir hiding ahi. Chule ama chun Israelte chu Philistinte khutna kona ahuhdoh patding ahi, ati.
target: You will become pregnant and have a son whose head is never to be touched by a razor because the boy is to be a Nazirite, dedicated to God from the womb. He will take the lead in delivering Israel from the hands of the Philistines.”

source: Chujouvin numeinu chu ahungin ajipa henga, Pathen mi khat kahenga ahungin, amaiso chu Pathen vantil maisotoh abangin, Kichat aumlheh-e; ahinla keiman hoija hungkon nahim tinjong kadongpon, chule aman jong kahenga amin eiseipehpoi:
target: Then the woman went to her husband and told him, “A man of God came to me. He looked like an angel of God, very awesome. I didn’t ask him where he came from, and he didn’t tell me his name.

source: Ahin aman kahenga, Ven, nangman nao navopding, chapa khat nanei ding ahi; chule nangman tun ju le khamna thei donhih-in, thilthenglou kiti poupou jong nehih-in: ajehchu chapang chu naobu-a kona athini geija Pathen'a dinga Nazir hiding ahi, tin aseije, ati.
target: But he said to me, ‘You will become pregnant and have a son. Now then, drink no wine or other fermented drink and do not eat anything unclean, because the boy will be a Nazirite of God from the womb until the day of his death.’ ”

source: Chuin Manoah Pakai henga ataovin, hitin aseije, Vo ka pakai, nahinsol Pathen mipa chu kakom lhona hungkit henlang, ahung pengding chapang chunghi ipi katohlhon dingham eihung hil lhonhen, ati.
target: Then Manoah prayed to the Lord : “Pardon your servant, Lord. I beg you to let the man of God you sent to us come again to teach us how to bring up the boy who is to be born.”

source: Chuin Pathen'in Manoah aw chu angaipeh-in; amanu loujaova atouna-a Pathen vantil chu amanu henga ahung kitnin; ahinla ajipa Manoah chu amatoh anaumpon ahi.
target: God heard Manoah, and the angel of God came again to the woman while she was out in the field; but her husband Manoah was not with her.

source: Chuin numeinu chu mangang tah in alhai jel-in, ajipa chu agahilin, ahenga, Ven, nikhat ni-a kahenga hung kilah mipa chu kahenga ahung kilah kitne, agati.
target: The woman hurried to tell her husband, “He’s here! The man who appeared to me the other day!”

source: Chuin Manoah akipat doh-in, ajinu nung ajuijin, mipa koma chun ahungin, ahenga, Nangma hiche numei to kihouva chu nahim? ati. Chuin aman ahenga, Kahi, ati.
target: Manoah got up and followed his wife. When he came to the man, he said, “Are you the man who talked to my wife?” “I am,” he said.

source: Chuin Manoah'in, Tun nathuseiho chu hung guilhung hen. Chapang chu iti kakhou khah lhona, chule achunga ipi kabol lhon dingham? ati.
target: So Manoah asked him, “When your words are fulfilled, what is to be the rule that governs the boy’s life and work?”

source: Chuin Pakai vantil chun Manoah henga, Numeinu henga kasei jouse bangchun amanu kichih thei hen.
target: The angel of the Lord answered, “Your wife must do all that I have told her.

source: Amanun lengpi guija kona kisem ipi thil hijongle nehda hen, chule ju le khamnathei jong dondahen, chule thilthenglou kiti poupou jong nehdahen: kathupeh jouse chu amanun juihen, ati.
target: She must not eat anything that comes from the grapevine, nor drink any wine or other fermented drink nor eat anything unclean. She must do everything I have commanded her.”

source: Chuin Manoah'in Pakai vantil henga, Nahenga katao ahi, keinin nang dinga kelnou khat kagagot lhon kahsen neiumpeh lhonin, ati.
target: Manoah said to the angel of the Lord , “We would like you to stay until we prepare a young goat for you.”

source: Chuin Pakai vantil chun Manoah henga, Nangman nei khongaisah jongle chun keiman nachanglhah neponge: chule nangman govam thilto nato dinga ahile, Pakai henga nato ding ahi, ati. Ajehchu Manoah'in amachu Pakai vantil ahilam ahetlou ahi.
target: The angel of the Lord replied, “Even though you detain me, I will not eat any of your food. But if you prepare a burnt offering, offer it to the Lord .” (Manoah did not realize that it was the angel of the Lord .)

source: Chuin Manoah'in Pakai vantil henga, Nathusei aguilhun tengle nangma kajolbol theilhon na dingin, namin ipiham neisei peh-in, ati.
target: Then Manoah inquired of the angel of the Lord , “What is your name, so that we may honor you when your word comes true?”

source: Chuin Pakai vantil'in ahenga, Akiselguh ahi munasa-a, ibola hitachu kamin neidoh ham? ati.
target: He replied, “Why do you ask my name? It is beyond understanding.”

source: Hitichun Manoah'in kelnou khat chu anneh thilto toh alan, songchung khatna Pakai henga atoh doh-in ahi. Chuin vantil chun kidang tah-in abolin, Manoah le ajinun hichu avelhonin ahi.
target: Then Manoah took a young goat, together with the grain offering, and sacrificed it on a rock to the Lord . And the Lord did an amazing thing while Manoah and his wife watched:

source: Ajehchu ahung hitin ahi, meikou chu maichama kona van lama alentou chun, Pakai vantil chu maicham meikou lah-a chun alengtou tan ahi. Chuin Manoah le ajinun hichu avelhonin, amailhon tolla asulut lhontan ahi.
target: As the flame blazed up from the altar toward heaven, the angel of the Lord ascended in the flame. Seeing this, Manoah and his wife fell with their faces to the ground.

source: Ahivangin Pakai vantil chu Manoah le ajinu henga akilahkit tapoi. Hichun Manoah'in Pakai vantil ahichu ahedohtai.
target: When the angel of the Lord did not show himself again to Manoah and his wife, Manoah realized that it was the angel of the Lord .

source: Chuin Manoah'in ajinu henga, Eini thonlouva ithitei lhonding ahitai, ajehchu einin Pathen imulhontai, ati.
target: “We are doomed to die!” he said to his wife. “We have seen God!”

source: Ahinla ajinun amahenga, Pakaiyin eini eithanom lhona ahile, govam thilto le neh thilto chu eini khutna kona akisan louding, chule hicheho jouse jonghi eivetsah lhon louding, chujongle tuphat tah-a hi hitobang thilho jong hi eiseipeh lhon lou ding ahi, ati.
target: But his wife answered, “If the Lord had meant to kill us, he would not have accepted a burnt offering and grain offering from our hands, nor shown us all these things or now told us this.”

source: Chuin numeinu chun chapa khat ahingin, Samson asahtai. Chuin chapang chu ahung khangin, Pakaiyin phatthei aboh-in ahi.
target: The woman gave birth to a boy and named him Samson. He grew and the Lord blessed him,

source: Chuin Zorah le Eshtaol kikah-a Dan gebuh-a chun Pakai lhagaovin achunga na atong pantan ahi.
target: and the Spirit of the Lord began to stir him while he was in Mahaneh Dan, between Zorah and Eshtaol.

source: Chuin Samson chu Timnah'a achesuh-in, chule Timnah'a chun Philistine te chanuho numei khat amun ahi.
target: Samson went down to Timnah and saw there a young Philistine woman.

source: Chuin ama ahung touvin anule apa henga aseijin, hitin ati, Keiman Timnah'a Philistine te chanuho numei khat kamui: hijeh chun amanu chu kaji dingin gapui lhonin, ati.
target: When he returned, he said to his father and mother, “I have seen a Philistine woman in Timnah; now get her for me as my wife.”

source: Hiche phatchun anule apan ahengah, Nasopi ho chanute ahiloule kamite jouse lah-a numei umlouhel hija, cheptanlou Philistine te kichenpi ding nagot ham? atilhonin ahi. Chuin Samson'in apa henga, Amanu neipui peh-in; ajehchu amanun kalung atoh lheh-e, ati.
target: His father and mother replied, “Isn’t there an acceptable woman among your relatives or among all our people? Must you go to the uncircumcised Philistines to get a wife?” But Samson said to his father, “Get her for me. She’s the right one for me.”

source: Achuti vangin anule apan hichu Pakaiya kon ahi le, aman Philistine te douna-a phat gomkom ahol ahi chu ahelhon pon ahi. Ajehchu hiche petna chu Philistine ten Israelte chunga vai ahomu ahi.
target: (His parents did not know that this was from the Lord , who was seeking an occasion to confront the Philistines; for at that time they were ruling over Israel.)

source: Chujouvin Samson anule apa toh Timnah'a achesuh-un, chule Timnah kho lengpi leilai ahung lhung taovin: chuin veuvin, keipi bahkai golbep khatnin ahin ngih tai.
target: Samson went down to Timnah together with his father and mother. As they approached the vineyards of Timnah, suddenly a young lion came roaring toward him.

source: Chuin Pakai Lhagao chu thanei tah-in achunga ahung chun ahile, aman kelnou alhetel bangin, akhutna imacha choilouvin abottel tan ahi. Ahinla aman athilbol chu anule apa henga aseidoh pon ahi.
target: The Spirit of the Lord came powerfully upon him so that he tore the lion apart with his bare hands as he might have torn a young goat. But he told neither his father nor his mother what he had done.

source: Chuin ama achesuh-in, numei chutoh akihoulimin; chule amanun Samson alunglhaisah lheh-in ahi.
target: Then he went down and talked with the woman, and he liked her.

source: Chuin phat chomkhat jouvin amanu puidingin ahung kilekitnin, akeipi bahkai thasa longchu ve dingin akiheijin ahile; veuvin, keipi bahkai long sunga chun khoilhah anakaijin ahi.
target: Some time later, when he went back to marry her, he turned aside to look at the lion’s carcass, and in it he saw a swarm of bees and some honey.

source: Chuin aman akhutnin alan, alamjot pumin anen, anule apa koma ahungin, amani jong apen, chule amanin jong anelhonin ahi. Ahinla hiche khoiju chu keipi bahkai thilong sunga kona alah ahi chu anule apa aseipeh pon ahi.
target: He scooped out the honey with his hands and ate as he went along. When he rejoined his parents, he gave them some, and they too ate it. But he did not tell them that he had taken the honey from the lion’s carcass.

source: Hitichun apachu numeinu koma chun achesuh tan ahi. Chuin Samson'in chukhoma chun golvah abolin ahi; ajehchu gollhang hon hitia chu abolngai mong ahi.
target: Now his father went down to see the woman. And there Samson held a feast, as was customary for young men.

source: Chuin ahitin ahi, amahon ama amuphatnun, ama koma umdingin loi somthum ahinpuijun ahi.
target: When the people saw him, they chose thirty men to be his companions.

source: Chuin Samson'in ahenguva, Keiman naheng uva thuchih khat kasei ding: hiche chu nanghon golvah nisagi sunga neihilchen theijuva, nahetdoh uva ahile, keiman nangho ponsil somthum, chule kikhelna von somthum kapeh dingu ahi.
target: “Let me tell you a riddle,” Samson said to them. “If you can give me the answer within the seven days of the feast, I will give you thirty linen garments and thirty sets of clothes.

source: Amavang neihilchen theilouvu leh, nanghon ponsil somthum le kikhelna von somthum neipeh dingu ahi, ati. Chuin amahon ahenga, Nathuchih chu seijin, keihon ngaijuvinge, atiuve.
target: If you can’t tell me the answer, you must give me thirty linen garments and thirty sets of clothes.” “Tell us your riddle,” they said. “Let’s hear it.”

source: Chuin aman amaho henga, Mi ne-a konin nehding ahung potnin, thahat tah-a kona thil lhumtah ahung potne, ati. Chuin amahon nithum geijin thuchih chu ahedoh thei pouvin ahi.
target: He replied, “Out of the eater, something to eat; out of the strong, something sweet.” For three days they could not give the answer.

source: Chuin nisagi nin ahitin ahi, amahon Samson jinu henga, Hiche thuchih hi eihil chetna dingun najipa jolin, achutiloule nangma le napa inhi meija kahal dingu ahi: nangman kanei hou lahpeh dinga neikouvu ham? Hiti chu hilouham? atiuvin ahi.
target: On the fourth day, they said to Samson’s wife, “Coax your husband into explaining the riddle for us, or we will burn you and your father’s household to death. Did you invite us here to steal our property?”

source: Chuin Samson jinu chu ahenga akapmin, hitin aseije, Nangman nei ngailut ahipon, neihot joh ahi: Nangman kamite henga thuchih nadongin, keima neiseipeh poi, ati. Chuin aman amanu henga, Ven, keiman kanu kapa koma jong kaseilou ahin, hiche chu nangma koma kasei ding ham? ati.
target: Then Samson’s wife threw herself on him, sobbing, “You hate me! You don’t really love me. You’ve given my people a riddle, but you haven’t told me the answer.” “I haven’t even explained it to my father or mother,” he replied, “so why should I explain it to you?”

source: Chuin agolvah-u kibol sungse, nisagi ni chun amanu a-angsunga akapkap jengtan ahi. Chuin ni sagi nin ahitin ahi, amanun aha ngeh behseh jehchun aseidoh pehtan ahi. Chuin amanun thuchih chu amite chateho henga aseipeh tan ahi.
target: She cried the whole seven days of the feast. So on the seventh day he finally told her, because she continued to press him. She in turn explained the riddle to her people.

source: Chuin ni sagi ni nisalhum masangin khopi-a cheng pasal ho chun ahenga, Khoiju sanga lhumjo ipiham? chule keipi bahkai sanga hatjo ipi ham? atiuvin ahi. Chuin aman amaho henga chun, Kabongla-a hi lou nakai louvu hile, kathuchih hi hedoh pouvin nate, ati.
target: Before sunset on the seventh day the men of the town said to him, “What is sweeter than honey? What is stronger than a lion?” Samson said to them, “If you had not plowed with my heifer, you would not have solved my riddle.”

source: Chuin Pakai Lhagao achunga ahungchun, ama Ashkelon'a achesuh-in, mi somthum athatnin, avonhou chu ahinlan, athuchih aseidohho henga chun kikhelna von somthum chu apetan ahi. Chuin alunghan akoujah-in, apa in lama achetou tan ahi.
target: Then the Spirit of the Lord came powerfully upon him. He went down to Ashkelon, struck down thirty of their men, stripped them of everything and gave their clothes to those who had explained the riddle. Burning with anger, he returned to his father’s home.

source: Chule Samson jinu chu agolpa, agolpha pena aneipa henga chun ape taovin ahi.
target: And Samson’s wife was given to one of his companions who had attended him at the feast.

source: Ahinla chomkhat jouvin ahung hitin ahi, suhlou chang atlaijin, Samson'in kelnou khat apon ajinu agavilin; chule, Indan sunga kajinu henga kagalut ding ahi, ati. Ahin ajinu pa-in alutding aphalpon ahi.
target: Later on, at the time of wheat harvest, Samson took a young goat and went to visit his wife. He said, “I’m going to my wife’s room.” But her father would not let him go in.

source: Chuin ajinu pan, Keiman najinu nahot mongmonga kangaito ahitan; hijeh-a chu naloipa kapeh ahitai. Anaonu hi ama sanga hoijoa hilouham? Nahenga katao ahi, amanu khelin kipuitan, ati.
target: “I was so sure you hated her,” he said, “that I gave her to your companion. Isn’t her younger sister more attractive? Take her instead.”

source: Chuin Samson'in amaho chungchanga hitin aseitai, Tun keiman amaho chunga mona boljong leng Philistine mihon a-engkhan eihisah thei pouvinte, ati.
target: Samson said to them, “This time I have a right to get even with the Philistines; I will really harm them.”

source: Chuin Samson achen sial jathum amanin, ameiju akan matnin, meisel phabep alan, amei le amei kikah-a chun akanmat pehtan ahi.
target: So he went out and caught three hundred foxes and tied them tail to tail in pairs. He then fastened a torch to every pair of tails,

source: Chuin meisel ho-a chun mei atih-in, Philistine te changphung dinglah-a alhalut nin ahile, changphal le changphung dinglai ho, lengpilei le Olive thing jouse geijin akamangtan ahi.
target: lit the torches and let the foxes loose in the standing grain of the Philistines. He burned up the shocks and standing grain, together with the vineyards and olive groves.

source: Chujouvin Philistine ten, Hichehi kon abol ham? atiuve. Chuin amahon, Timnah tupa Samson bol ahi, ajehchu aman ajinu alahpeh-a aloipa apeh jeh ahi, tin adonbut uve. Chuin Philistine te ahungun, amanu chule apa chu meijin ahal lih taovin ahi.
target: When the Philistines asked, “Who did this?” they were told, “Samson, the Timnite’s son-in-law, because his wife was given to his companion.” So the Philistines went up and burned her and her father to death.

source: Chuin Samson'in amaho henga, Nanghon hiche nabol jeh uva hi, keiman nachung uva phu kalah ding ahi, hichu kabol chaiteng umthim bepding kahi, ati.
target: Samson said to them, “Since you’ve acted like this, I swear that I won’t stop until I get my revenge on you.”

source: Chuin aman amaho chu khotona beijin mitamtah athatnin; chule achesuh-in Etam songpi vuma agacheng tan ahi.
target: He attacked them viciously and slaughtered many of them. Then he went down and stayed in a cave in the rock of Etam.

source: Chujouvin Philistine te achetouvun, Judah gamsunga gebuh asonguvin, chule Lehi mun'a chun akithe jalun ahi.
target: The Philistines went up and camped in Judah, spreading out near Lehi.

source: Chuin Judah miten, Ipi bola keiho douna-a hunga nahiuvem, atiuve. Chuin amahon adonbutnun, Samson kantum dingle, kachung uva abol bang banga achunga bol dinga hungtouva kahiuve, atiuve.
target: The people of Judah asked, “Why have you come to fight us?” “We have come to take Samson prisoner,” they answered, “to do to him as he did to us.”

source: Chuphatnin Judah mi sangthum Etam molsang songpi chunga chun achetouvun, chule Samson henga, Philistine hi eiho chunga vaipo ahiuve ti nahetlou ham? Chule nangman kachunguva nabol pihi ipi ham? atiuve. Chuin aman amaho henga, Ka chunga atoh bang banguva chu keiman jong amaho chunga katoh ahi, ati.
target: Then three thousand men from Judah went down to the cave in the rock of Etam and said to Samson, “Don’t you realize that the Philistines are rulers over us? What have you done to us?” He answered, “I merely did to them what they did to me.”

source: Chule amahon ama henga, Keihon nangma Philistine te khutna kapehdoh theina dinguva, nangma kantum dinga hunga kahiuve, atiuve. Chuin Samson'in ahenguvah, Nangho tah-in neitha louna dingun kahenga kihahselun,atin ahi.
target: They said to him, “We’ve come to tie you up and hand you over to the Philistines.” Samson said, “Swear to me that you won’t kill me yourselves.”

source: Chuin amahon ahenga, Ahipoi, keihon nangma kakanchah uva, amaho khutna kapehdoh dingu ahibouve; keihon nangma nathat pouvinge, atiuve. Chuin amahon amachu khao thahbet nin akanun, song chunga konchun ahin puidoh-un ahi.
target: “Agreed,” they answered. “We will only tie you up and hand you over to them. We will not kill you.” So they bound him with two new ropes and led him up from the rock.

source: Chule ama Lehi mun ahunglhun phatnin, Philistine te chu ama dounan hatah in a-aovun ahi. Hichun Pakai Lhagao thanei tah-in achunga ahung chun ahile, akhut kikanna khaoho chu meija kihaltan abang jengin, akhutna konin akikan naho chu alhamang tan ahi.
target: As he approached Lehi, the Philistines came toward him shouting. The Spirit of the Lord came powerfully upon him. The ropes on his arms became like charred flax, and the bindings dropped from his hands.

source: Chule aman Sangan khagu thahbet khat amun, hichu alan, hiche-a chun mi asang asang avolihtan ahi.
target: Finding a fresh jawbone of a donkey, he grabbed it and struck down a thousand men.

source: Chuin Samson'in, Sangan khagu mangchan, athop athopmin kavolhun, Sangan khagu mangchan, mi sangkhat kathatnin ahi, ati.
target: Then Samson said, “With a donkey’s jawbone I have made donkeys of them. With a donkey’s jawbone I have killed a thousand men.”

source: Chuin ahung hitin ahi, aman thu aseijouvin, sangan khagu chu akhutna konin apaimangin, hichemun chu Ramath-lehi asahtai.
target: When he finished speaking, he threw away the jawbone; and the place was called Ramath Lehi.

source: Chuin ama hatah-in adang chahtan, Pakai hengah ataovin, hitin ati, Nangman nasoh khutna hi hitobang lhatdohna nasatah hi napeh ahitan; tu-a hi dangchah-a kathi-a, cheptan louho khutna hi kalhuh ding ham? ati.
target: Because he was very thirsty, he cried out to the Lord , “You have given your servant this great victory. Must I now die of thirst and fall into the hands of the uncircumcised?”

source: Hijeh chun Pathen'in Lehi mun'a chun komtong apokehsah-in ahile, chu-a kon chun twi ahung longdoh-in; chule aman adonphatnin, alungthim ahatdoh kitnin, ahaldoh kit tai. Hijeh chun hiche mun chu En-hakkore asah tan, hichu tuni geijin Lehi mun'a aum jingin ahi.
target: Then God opened up the hollow place in Lehi, and water came out of it. When Samson drank, his strength returned and he revived. So the spring was called En Hakkore, and it is still there in Lehi.

source: Chuin aman Philistine te nikho laijin Israelte chunga kum somni thu anatanin ahi.
target: Samson led Israel for twenty years in the days of the Philistines.

source: Chujouvin Samson Gaza'ah achen ahile numei kijoh khat amun, amanu henga chun alut tan ahi.
target: One day Samson went to Gaza, where he saw a prostitute. He went in to spend the night with her.

source: Chuin Gaza mite henga, Samson hilama ahunge, ti aseipeh taovin ahi. Chuin amahon a-um na munm chu a-umkimvelun, chule jan khovah keijin khopi kotpi-a chun achanguvin, jan khovah in thipchetnin aumun, Jingkah kho ahungvah vahleh itha dingu ahi, akitiuvin ahi.
target: The people of Gaza were told, “Samson is here!” So they surrounded the place and lay in wait for him all night at the city gate. They made no move during the night, saying, “At dawn we’ll kill him.”

source: Chuin Samson khangkimgei alumin, khangkimin athoudoh-in, khopi kotpi kotkhahle akhom tenitoh abotdoh-in, abonchan alengkouva apun, Hebron maijona um lhangvum khatna apudoh pehtan ahi.
target: But Samson lay there only until the middle of the night. Then he got up and took hold of the doors of the city gate, together with the two posts, and tore them loose, bar and all. He lifted them to his shoulders and carried them to the top of the hill that faces Hebron.

source: Chule hiche nung chun ahitin ahi, aman Sorak phaichama numei khat amin Delilah kitinu chu adeicha tan ahi.
target: Some time later, he fell in love with a woman in the Valley of Sorek whose name was Delilah.

source: Chuin Philistine vaipoho chu amanu henga ahungun, ahenga, Amapa hi kakan tum uva achunga kachuh theina dingun, iti achunga tha kanei thei dingu ham ti hetdohna dingin, amapa khu anajolin lang, athahatna nasatah khu hoija umham ana hedoh-in: chule keiho mikhat cheh-in nangma dangka sangkhat le jakhat kapeh dingu ahi, atiuve.
target: The rulers of the Philistines went to her and said, “See if you can lure him into showing you the secret of his great strength and how we can overpower him so we may tie him up and subdue him. Each one of us will give you eleven hundred shekels of silver.”

source: Chuin Delilah'in Samson henga, Nahenga katao ahi, nathahatna nasatah hi hoija uma hija, chule nangma suhgentheina dinga hi ipi-a naki kan dingham? neiseipeh temin, ati.
target: So Delilah said to Samson, “Tell me the secret of your great strength and how you can be tied up and subdued.”

source: Chuin Samson'in amanu henga, Ago khalou khaogui hing sagi in eikanleo, keima lhasam tangting, midangho bang bang kahi ding ahitai, ati.
target: Samson answered her, “If anyone ties me with seven fresh bowstrings that have not been dried, I’ll become as weak as any other man.”

source: Hiche phatchun Philistine vaipohon chun amanu henga, ago khalou khaogui hing sagi ahinchoijun, chule amanun hicheho-a chun akanin ahi.
target: Then the rulers of the Philistines brought her seven fresh bowstrings that had not been dried, and she tied him with them.

source: Tun mi phabepmin ama chu achang lhiuvin, indan sunga chu amanu toh uma ahiuve. Chuin amanun ahenga, Samson, Philistine te nachunga chuding ahi taove, ati. Chuin aman khaoguiho chu patdum kipheh meija kihaltan bangin abottan jengtan ahi. Hitichun athahatna chu hetdoh ahipon ahi.
target: With men hidden in the room, she called to him, “Samson, the Philistines are upon you!” But he snapped the bowstrings as easily as a piece of string snaps when it comes close to a flame. So the secret of his strength was not discovered.

source: Chuin Delilah'in Samson henga, Ven, nangman neidai chavaijin, jouvin neilheme. Tu-a hi katao ahi, ipi-a nakikan tum thei dingham? ati.
target: Then Delilah said to Samson, “You have made a fool of me; you lied to me. Come now, tell me how you can be tied.”

source: Chuin aman amanu jah-a, amahon mi kikanna khahlou khao thahbet-a eikan leu, kalhahsam ding ahitan, chuteng midangho bang bang kahi ding ahitai, ati.
target: He said, “If anyone ties me securely with new ropes that have never been used, I’ll become as weak as any other man.”

source: Hitichun Delilah'in khao thahbet alan, Samson chu akanin, ajah-a, Samson, Philistine te nachunga chuding ahitaove, atin ahi. Chule mi phabepmin indan sunga achanlhih jingu ahi. Chuin aman hicheho chu patjang kibot tan bangin akhutna konin atumtan tan ahi.
target: So Delilah took new ropes and tied him with them. Then, with men hidden in the room, she called to him, “Samson, the Philistines are upon you!” But he snapped the ropes off his arms as if they were threads.

source: Chuin Delilah'in Samson henga, Tuni geihin nangman neidai chavaijin, jouvin nei lheme: ipi-a kikan ding nahim, neihilin, ati. Chuin aman, Nangman kalua kasam pheh sagi hi hehkople chun, ati.
target: Delilah then said to Samson, “All this time you have been making a fool of me and lying to me. Tell me how you can be tied.” He replied, “If you weave the seven braids of my head into the fabric on the loom and tighten it with the pin, I’ll become as weak as any other man.” So while he was sleeping, Delilah took the seven braids of his head, wove them into the fabric

source: Chuin aman ahehkopmin akildet chetnin, ahenga, Samson, Philistine te nachunga chuding ahitaove, ati. Chuin ama a-imutna konin athoudoh-in, asam lom kihehkop leh akilna chu abotdoh tan ahi.
target: and tightened it with the pin. Again she called to him, “Samson, the Philistines are upon you!” He awoke from his sleep and pulled up the pin and the loom, with the fabric.

source: Chuin amanun ahenga, Nalungsung keima koma umlouva, nangman kalungsetne iti neitithei ham? Nangman hiche thumvei neidai chavaijin, nahatna nasatah hi hoilaija umham neiseipeh poi, ati.
target: Then she said to him, “How can you say, ‘I love you,’ when you won’t confide in me? This is the third time you have made a fool of me and haven’t told me the secret of your great strength.”

source: Chuin ahitin ahi, amanun aniseh-a angah jinga, adoh jing phatnin, amapa thiding khopmin alung gimtan ahileh;
target: With such nagging she prodded him day after day until he was sick to death of it.

source: Hichun alungthim jouse amanu henga aseijin, hitin ati, Kalu chunga samchem kipan khalou ahi; ajehchu keima kanu oisunga patna Pathen'a dinga Nazir mi kahi. Kasam akivo chaija ahile kahatna keija kona chemanga, kalhahsam ding, midangho bang bang kahiding ahitai, ati.
target: So he told her everything. “No razor has ever been used on my head,” he said, “because I have been a Nazirite dedicated to God from my mother’s womb. If my head were shaved, my strength would leave me, and I would become as weak as any other man.”

source: Chuin Delilah'in amapan ahenga alungsunga um jouse aseidoh chu amuphatnin, Philistine vaipoho koudingin mi asolin, ajah uva, Khatvei hungtou kitnun, ajehchu aman alungsunga um jouse eiseipehtai, ati. Chujouvin Philistine vaipoho chu ahungun, akhutnuva sum jong ahin choijun ahi.
target: When Delilah saw that he had told her everything, she sent word to the rulers of the Philistines, “Come back once more; he has told me everything.” So the rulers of the Philistines returned with the silver in their hands.

source: Chuin amanun amapa chu apheipi chunga alupsah-in a-imutsah-in; asam voudingin mi akouvin, alua lom sagi-a asam kikan chu avolhah pehtan ahi. Chuin amanun asugim panin, chule athahatna chu ama-a konin achemang tan ahi.
target: After putting him to sleep on her lap, she called for someone to shave off the seven braids of his hair, and so began to subdue him. And his strength left him.

source: Chuin amanun, Samson, Philistine te nachunga chuding ahi taove, ati. Chuin ama a-imutna-a konin ahung thouvin, chule, Nidang bangin chedoh ingting, kithing lhange ati. Ahinla Pakaiyin ama adalhah chu ahepon ahi.
target: Then she called, “Samson, the Philistines are upon you!” He awoke from his sleep and thought, “I’ll go out as before and shake myself free.” But he did not know that the Lord had left him.

source: Ahinla Philistine ten amanun, amit teni akaldoh-un, Gaza'a apui lhaovin, sum-eng henkol abupeh-un; songkul inna sumhei goijin apangtai.
target: Then the Philistines seized him, gouged out his eyes and took him down to Gaza. Binding him with bronze shackles, they set him to grinding grain in the prison.

source: Ahinla alu-a asam chu akivotol nungin ahung khangpan kit tan ahi.
target: But the hair on his head began to grow again after it had been shaved.

source: Chujou phatnin Philistine vaipoho chu a-pathenu Dagon henga kilhaina loupitah bola, kipa thanop boldingin akikhom khom taovin ahi. Ajehchu amahon, I-pathen'u hin imelmapao Samson hi ikhutnuva eipehdoh-u ahi, atiu ahi.
target: Now the rulers of the Philistines assembled to offer a great sacrifice to Dagon their god and to celebrate, saying, “Our god has delivered Samson, our enemy, into our hands.”

source: Chuin mipin ama amuphatnun a-pathen'u chu avahchoijun ahi. Ajehchu amahon, I-pathen'un imelmapao, chule eiho tamtah eithatnuva, igamsungu sumangpa hi ikhutnuva apehdoh ahitai, atiuve.
target: When the people saw him, they praised their god, saying, “Our god has delivered our enemy into our hands, the one who laid waste our land and multiplied our slain.”

source: Chuin ahitin ahi, amaho alungthimu akipa phat chun, Vetnom um eibolpeh diuvin Samson gakouvun atiuvin ahi. Chuin amahon songkul in'a konchun Samson agakouvun, chule aman amaho dingchun vetnom um abolpehtai. Chuin amahon amachu khom lentah ni kah-a adinsah-un ahi.
target: While they were in high spirits, they shouted, “Bring out Samson to entertain us.” So they called Samson out of the prison, and he performed for them. When they stood him among the pillars,

source: Chuin Samson'in akhut kaile-a pang chapangpa henga chun, Inpi kingapna khom teni chu kaki ngainadin neituh sah-in, ati.
target: Samson said to the servant who held his hand, “Put me where I can feel the pillars that support the temple, so that I may lean against them.”

source: Tun in chu numei le pasal dimsetna ahin, chule Philistine vaipoho jouse chu umsoh keijuva; Chule in chunga chu Samson vetnom um bol vedinga numei pasal mi sangthum jen uma ahiuve.
target: Now the temple was crowded with men and women; all the rulers of the Philistines were there, and on the roof were about three thousand men and women watching Samson perform.

source: Chuin Samson Pakai henga ataovin, Vo Pathen, Philistinte chunga khatvei sehseh kamit teni asuhchotnao phu kalah theinadin; Vo Pakai Pathen, katao ahi, neigel doh-in, chule katao ahi, tu khatvei sehseh hi katha hatsah-in, ati.
target: Then Samson prayed to the Lord , “Sovereign Lord , remember me. Please, God, strengthen me just once more, and let me with one blow get revenge on the Philistines for my two eyes.”

source: Chuin Samson'in inpi douva pang, alaija inpi kidouna khomteni chu atuh-in; chule khatna chun akhut jetlam angamin, khat joh-a chun akhut veilam angamin ahi.
target: Then Samson reached toward the two central pillars on which the temple stood. Bracing himself against them, his right hand on the one and his left hand on the other,

source: Chuin Samson'in, Philistine mite hito thitha tange, atin ahi. Chuin aman athahat jouse-a asonin ahile, inpi chu vaipoho jouse le asunga umho jouse chunga chun achimtan ahi. Hitichun hiche athinia amitha chu ahinlaija atha sangin atamjon ahi.
target: Samson said, “Let me die with the Philistines!” Then he pushed with all his might, and down came the temple on the rulers and all the people in it. Thus he killed many more when he died than while he lived.

source: Chujouvin asopitele apa insung mite ahungsuh-un, along chu alauvin, ahin potouvun, Zorah le Eshtaol kikah-a apa Manoah lhankhuh-a chun avui taovin ahi. Aman Israelte chunga kum somni thu anatanin ahi.
target: Then his brothers and his father’s whole family went down to get him. They brought him back and buried him between Zorah and Eshtaol in the tomb of Manoah his father. He had led Israel twenty years.

source: Chule Ephraim molsanga chun Micah kiti mikhat aumin ahi.
target: Now a man named Micah from the hill country of Ephraim

source: Chuin aman anu henga, Nangma-a kona dangka shekel sangkhat le jakhat kiladoh, nana gaosap khum, chule keima jah-a jong nanasei chu, ven, hiche dangka chu kakoma aume; keima lah ahi, ati. Chuin anun, Kachapa, Pakaiya phattheiboh changin, ati.
target: said to his mother, “The eleven hundred shekels of silver that were taken from you and about which I heard you utter a curse—I have that silver with me; I took it.” Then his mother said, “The Lord bless you, my son!”

source: Chuin aman anu koma dangka shekel sangkhat le jakhat chu anungpeh phatnin, anun ahenga, Milim kilha le kikheng semna dinga keiman kakhutna kon kachapa dinga dangka chu Pakaiya kapehdoh ahitai: hijeh-a chu tu-a hi nangma koma kapehdoh ding ahi, ati.
target: When he returned the eleven hundred shekels of silver to his mother, she said, “I solemnly consecrate my silver to the Lord for my son to make an image overlaid with silver. I will give it back to you.”

source: Ahivangin sum chu anu henga alepeh-in ahi. Chuin anun dangka shekel jani chu alan, dangka khengpa apen ahile, aman hiche-a kon chun milim kilha le milim kikheng asemin; chule hicheho chu Micah in'a umin ahi.
target: So after he returned the silver to his mother, she took two hundred shekels of silver and gave them to a silversmith, who used them to make the idol. And it was put in Micah’s house.

source: Chule Micah kitipa chun pathen ho inkhat aneijin, thempu boitong sangkhol le milim houna asemin, chule achapate lah-a khat chu athenso-in, amachu thempun apangin ahi.
target: Now this man Micah had a shrine, and he made an ephod and some household gods and installed one of his sons as his priest.

source: Hiche laichun Israel ten leng aneipouvin, ahinla mijousen ama mitna dih asah chanchu aboljengu ahi.
target: In those days Israel had no king; everyone did as they saw fit.

source: Chule Judah gam Bethlehem'a kon Judah insungmi gollhang khat aumin; ama chu Levi mi ahin, chule chukoma chu khopema ahi.
target: A young Levite from Bethlehem in Judah, who had been living within the clan of Judah,

source: Chule hichepa chun chen nading mun amu muna-a cheng dingin Judah gam Bethlehem khopi chu ahin dalhan ahi. Chuin ama akholjin lena lamin, Ephraim molsanga um Micah in chu ahung lhungin ahi.
target: left that town in search of some other place to stay. On his way he came to Micah’s house in the hill country of Ephraim.

source: Chuin Micah'in amapa henga, Hoija kona hung nahim? ati. Chuin aman ahenga, Keima Judah gam Bethlehem'a kon Levi mi kahin, chule chen nading mun hola kholjin le-a kahi, ati.
target: Micah asked him, “Where are you from?” “I’m a Levite from Bethlehem in Judah,” he said, “and I’m looking for a place to stay.”

source: Chuin Micah in ahenga, Keima toh chengkhomin, chule keima dingin pa le thempu-in pangin, chule keiman kumkhatna dangka shekel som, von tokhat, chule nehle chah kapeh ding ahi, ati. Hitichun Levi mipa chu achengtai.
target: Then Micah said to him, “Live with me and be my father and priest, and I’ll give you ten shekels of silver a year, your clothes and your food.”

source: Chule Levi mipa chu mipatoh umkhom dingchu anomtan, chule gollhangpa amapa dingchun achapa khat tobang ahitan ahi.
target: So the Levite agreed to live with him, and the young man became like one of his sons to him.

source: Chuin Micah chun Levi gollhangpa chu athenson, chule gollhangpa chu athempun apangin, Micah in'a chun aumin ahi.
target: Then Micah installed the Levite, and the young man became his priest and lived in his house.

source: Chujouvin Micah'in, Tun Levi mikhat thempu-in kaneitan, Pakaiyin kachunga thilpha abolding ahi ti kahetai, ati.
target: And Micah said, “Now I know that the Lord will be good to me, since this Levite has become my priest.”

source: Hiche nikho laichun Israelte lah-a leng aumpoi. Chule hiche nikholai machun Dan mite chenna ding gam aholun ahi; ajehchu hiche nikho geija chu Israelte phung lah-a amaho gamlo ding aumloulai ahi.
target: In those days Israel had no king. And in those days the tribe of the Danites was seeking a place of their own where they might settle, because they had not yet come into an inheritance among the tribes of Israel.

source: Chuin Dan chate chun aumnao mun Zorah le Eshtaol kho-a konin a-insungmiu pasal hangsan cheh mi nga gam velhi dingle gamhol dingin asolun; ajah uvah, Cheovinlang gamchu gakholun, atiuve. Hichun Ephraim molsanga um Micah in'a chun aga lhungun, hia chun ageh taovin ahi.
target: So the Danites sent five of their leading men from Zorah and Eshtaol to spy out the land and explore it. These men represented all the Danites. They told them, “Go, explore the land.” So they entered the hill country of Ephraim and came to the house of Micah, where they spent the night.

source: Amaho Micah in'a aumlaijun, amahon Levi gollhangpa chu a-awso-a konin aheuvin; aheng lama akiheijun, ajah-a, Kon hikoma hi nahin puilut ham? Chule hikoma hi ipi nabol ham? chule hikoma hi ipi naneijem? atiuve.
target: When they were near Micah’s house, they recognized the voice of the young Levite; so they turned in there and asked him, “Who brought you here? What are you doing in this place? Why are you here?”

source: Chuin aman ahenguvah, Micah'in hiti khati hin eibolin, eigoijin, chule athempua kapan ahi, ati.
target: He told them what Micah had done for him, and said, “He has hired me and I am his priest.”

source: Chuin amahon ahenga, Nahenga kataovu ahi, kachenao lampia hi kakhantou kakhantou lou dingu kahet theina diuvin, Pathen neidoh peh-un, atiuvin ahi.
target: Then they said to him, “Please inquire of God to learn whether our journey will be successful.”

source: Chuin thempupa chun ahenguvah, Lungmong tah-in cheovin, Pakaiyin nachenao lampia naumpi naove, ati.
target: The priest answered them, “Go in peace. Your journey has the Lord ’s approval.”

source: Chujouvin mi ngaho chun akipat doh-un, Laish kho-a ahung lhungun, hichea chengho Sidon miho bang banga-a chamdela, mongtah le bit keija achenu chu amuvin; chule hiche gama chun ipi lama hijongle ajachatnau boldoh pehding lamkai aneipouvin ahi. Chule amaho Sidon mite-a konin agamlauvin, chule koimato jong kigui jopna anei pouvin ahi.
target: So the five men left and came to Laish, where they saw that the people were living in safety, like the Sidonians, at peace and secure. And since their land lacked nothing, they were prosperous. Also, they lived a long way from the Sidonians and had no relationship with anyone else.

source: Chuin amaho Zorah le Eshtaol'a sopite henga ahungun: chule asopiho chun ahenguva, Ipi seithei nanei uvem? atiuve.
target: When they returned to Zorah and Eshtaol, their fellow Danites asked them, “How did you find things?”

source: Chuin amahon, Amaho doudinga ikontou theina dinguvin, kipat un: ajehchu keihon gamchu kagam'u uvin, chule veovin, gamphatah ahi. Ima nabol got louvu ham? Chu gama cheding le galut ding chule galo ding thase hih-un.
target: They answered, “Come on, let’s attack them! We have seen the land, and it is very good. Aren’t you going to do something? Don’t hesitate to go there and take it over.

source: Nangho nache tengule, mongtah-a cheng miho kom le gam lentah nalhun dingu ahi. Ajehchu Pathen'in leisetna thil um jouse lhahsam louna mun chu nakhut uva napeh-u ahitai, atiuve.
target: When you get there, you will find an unsuspecting people and a spacious land that God has put into your hands, a land that lacks nothing whatever.”

source: Chuin Zorah le Eshtaol kho-a konchun Dan insung mite mi jagup chu manchah pumin ahung kondoh-un ahi.
target: Then six hundred men of the Danites, armed for battle, set out from Zorah and Eshtaol.

source: Chuin amaho achetouvun, Judah gam Kirjath-jearim'a gebuh asongtaove. Hijeh chun hiche munchu tuni geijin Mahaneh-dan asah-un ahi. Veovin hichu Kirjath-jearim nunglama uma ahi.
target: On their way they set up camp near Kiriath Jearim in Judah. This is why the place west of Kiriath Jearim is called Mahaneh Dan to this day.

source: Chuin amaho chua konchun Ephraim molsang lam ajonun, Micah in ahung lhung taovin ahi.
target: From there they went on to the hill country of Ephraim and came to Micah’s house.

source: Chujouvin Laish gam velhia che mi ngaho chun adonbutnun, asopiho henga, Nangho hiche inho-a hi thempu boitong sangkhol, milim ho, milim kilhah le, milim kisoltho aume ti nahet uvem? Hijeh chun tun ipi nabol dingu ham ngaitouvin, atiuve.
target: Then the five men who had spied out the land of Laish said to their fellow Danites, “Do you know that one of these houses has an ephod, some household gods and an image overlaid with silver? Now you know what to do.”

source: Chuin amaho chulama chun akiheijun, Levi gollhangpa umna in, Micah in geija chun ahungun, ama chu chibai aboh-un ahi.
target: So they turned in there and went to the house of the young Levite at Micah’s place and greeted him.

source: Chule Dan insungmi galvon kivona mi jagupho chu kotpi-a chun adinguvin ahi.
target: The six hundred Danites, armed for battle, stood at the entrance of the gate.

source: Chuin gam velhia mi nga chu ache touvun, hilama chun ahung lutnun, milim kisemthu, boitong sangkhol, milimho, milim kilhajolho chu alauvin, chule thempupa chu galvonna kivon mi jagup ho toh kotpi phunga chun adingun ahi.
target: The five men who had spied out the land went inside and took the idol, the ephod and the household gods while the priest and the six hundred armed men stood at the entrance of the gate.

source: Chuin amaho Micah in'a acheuva, milim kisemthu ho, thempu boitong sangkhol, milimho, akisoltho milim ahin lah-u chun, thempupan amaho henga , Ipi bola nahiuvem? ati.
target: When the five men went into Micah’s house and took the idol, the ephod and the household gods, the priest said to them, “What are you doing?”

source: Chuin amahon ahenga, Thipbeh-in, nakhutnin nakam kihupmin lang, kanungu hinjuijin, chule keiho dingin pa le thempu-in pangin. Nangma dinga mi khatseh insunga thempu-a panding phajo-am, ahiloule phung khat le Israel insung khat chunga thempu-a pan phajo-am? atiuve.
target: They answered him, “Be quiet! Don’t say a word. Come with us, and be our father and priest. Isn’t it better that you serve a tribe and clan in Israel as priest rather than just one man’s household?”

source: Chuin thempupa lungsung chu akipah lheh-in, thempu boitong sangkhol, milimho, chule akilhahtho milim chu alan, mipi lailunga chun achetan ahi.
target: The priest was very pleased. He took the ephod, the household gods and the idol and went along with the people.

source: Hitichun amaho akiheijun, akipat doh-un, chule amasanguva chapangho le ganchaho achesah-un ahi.
target: Putting their little children, their livestock and their possessions in front of them, they turned away and left.

source: Chule Micah in'a kona gamla thimtah agei phatnun, Micah invela miho chu akikhom khomun, Dan miho chu adelpha taovin ahi.
target: When they had gone some distance from Micah’s house, the men who lived near Micah were called together and overtook the Danites.

source: Chuin amahon Dan chate chu agah samun ahi. Chuin amaho Micah heng lama chun akiheijun, ahenga, Ipin nabola hitobang mihonpi toh nahung ham, atiuve.
target: As they shouted after them, the Danites turned and said to Micah, “What’s the matter with you that you called out your men to fight?”

source: Chuin aman, Nanghon keiman kakisem ka-pathen le kathempu nakilah uvin nachemang taove. Chule ken idang kanei nahlai ham? chule nanghon kahenga, ipin nabol ham, natiu chu ipi nasei nao ham? ati.
target: He replied, “You took the gods I made, and my priest, and went away. What else do I have? How can you ask, ‘What’s the matter with you?’ ”

source: Chuin Dan chate chun ahenga, Kalah uva na awgin kijah sah hih-in, achuti loule alunghangho nachunga hung chuntin, nahinkho le na-insung pumpi manlo ding ahi, atiuve.
target: The Danites answered, “Don’t argue with us, or some of the men may get angry and attack you, and you and your family will lose your lives.”

source: Chuin Dan chate chu alampiuva achemang taove, chule Micah'in amaho chu ama dinga ahatvalu chu amu phatnin, akinunglen a-in lama achetai.
target: So the Danites went their way, and Micah, seeing that they were too strong for him, turned around and went back home.

source: Chuin amahon Micah thilsemho le athempupa chu ahin laovin, mongtah le bitkeija cheng mite umna Laish kho chu ahunglhung taove. Chuin amahon amaho chu chemhemin athatnun, khopi chu ahallha taove.
target: Then they took what Micah had made, and his priest, and went on to Laish, against a people at peace and secure. They attacked them with the sword and burned down their city.

source: Amaho Zidon'a kona gamlatah ahijeh ule, koimatoh kiguijop lou ahi jeh-u chun ahuhdoh dingu koima aumpon ahi. Hichu Beth-rehob koma phaichama uma ahi. Chuin amahon khopi khat asaovin, chua chun acheng taove.
target: There was no one to rescue them because they lived a long way from Sidon and had no relationship with anyone else. The city was in a valley near Beth Rehob. The Danites rebuilt the city and settled there.

source: Chuin akhopi semu chu Israel'a dinga hungpenga apau Dan min aput sah-un, Dan asah taove. Ahivangin khopi minchu amasa Laish anahin ahi.
target: They named it Dan after their ancestor Dan, who was born to Israel—though the city used to be called Laish.

source: Chuin Dan chate chun semthu milim atungdoh-un; agamu chu sohchanga ache kahseuvin Manasseh chapa, Gershom chapa, Jonathan le achateho chu Dan phunga thempun apanguvin ahi.
target: There the Danites set up for themselves the idol, and Jonathan son of Gershom, the son of Moses, and his sons were priests for the tribe of Dan until the time of the captivity of the land.

source: Chuin amahon Micah'in asemthu milim chu atungdoh-un, hiche phatsungse chu Pathen in chu Shiloh-a aumin ahi.
target: They continued to use the idol Micah had made, all the time the house of God was in Shiloh.

source: Chuin hiche nikho laichun ahung hitin ahi, Israelte lah-a leng aumlou laichun, Ephraim molsang panga chun Levi mikhat ana khopemin, ama chun Juda gam Bethlehem'a konin thaikem khat akipuijin ahi.
target: In those days Israel had no king. Now a Levite who lived in a remote area in the hill country of Ephraim took a concubine from Bethlehem in Judah.

source: Chuin ama thaikemnu chu ama dounan noti'n apangin, chule ama-a konin achedoh-in Juda gam Bethlehem'a apa in'a chun achen, chua chun lhali aga umin ahi.
target: But she was unfaithful to him. She left him and went back to her parents’ home in Bethlehem, Judah. After she had been there four months,

source: Chuin a-inneipu chu amanu kamdama kihoupi ding le hin nungpui kit dingin akipat doh-in, asoh khat le sangan kopto akipuijin, anung ajuijin ahi. Chuin amanun amapa chu apa in'a ahin puijin; chule nungahnu pa chun amapa amuphatnin kipah tah-in alamton ahi.
target: her husband went to her to persuade her to return. He had with him his servant and two donkeys. She took him into her parents’ home, and when her father saw him, he gladly welcomed him.

source: Chuin anupa-pa, nungahnu pachun, amapa chu a-umsah-in; chule amapa jong ama chutoh nithum aumkhomin ahi. Hitichun mahon aneuvin, adonun, chule chu-a chun ageh-un ahi.
target: His father-in-law, the woman’s father, prevailed on him to stay; so he remained with him three days, eating and drinking, and sleeping there.

source: Chuin nili chanin ahung hitin ahi, jingkah matah-a ahung thodoh doh-un, amapa che dingin akipatdoh tan ahi. Hichun nungahnu pa chun achanu jipa henga, Changlhah themkhat beh nenlang nalung suhal photnin, chujou tengle chenan nate, ati.
target: On the fourth day they got up early and he prepared to leave, but the woman’s father said to his son-in-law, “Refresh yourself with something to eat; then you can go.”

source: Chuin amani atou lhonin, anekhom, adonkhom lhonin ahi. Ajehchu nungahnu pa chun mipa henga chu, Katao ahi, lunglhai selin umin, tujan khongaijin lang, nalungthim kipasah-in, atin ahi.
target: So the two of them sat down to eat and drink together. Afterward the woman’s father said, “Please stay tonight and enjoy yourself.”

source: Chuin mipa chu chedinga akipatdoh phatnin, anupa-pa chun alho lhon ahile, amapa aumkit tai.
target: And when the man got up to go, his father-in-law persuaded him, so he stayed there that night.

source: Chuin ani nga ni jingpi tah-in amapa chedingin ahung thoudoh-in ahile, nungahnu pa'n ahenga, Katao ahi, nalung suhal tadin, ati. Chuin amani nisa akihei geijin akhongai lhonin, chule amanin anekhom kit lhonin ahi.
target: On the morning of the fifth day, when he rose to go, the woman’s father said, “Refresh yourself. Wait till afternoon!” So the two of them ate together.

source: Chule mipa chu ama, athaikem, chule asohpa toh chedinga ahung kipatdoh phatnin, anungahnu pa chun ahenga, Ven, tuhi nilhah hiding ahitan, kangeh nahi, tujan khongai nalaijun: ven, nikho kichai ding ahitai, nalungthim kipana dingin hilaija hin geh maijun; chule jingle in nalhun theina dingin, jingpitah le najotna ding jonnan nate, ati.
target: Then when the man, with his concubine and his servant, got up to leave, his father-in-law, the woman’s father, said, “Now look, it’s almost evening. Spend the night here; the day is nearly over. Stay and enjoy yourself. Early tomorrow morning you can get up and be on your way home.”

source: Ahinla mipa chu khongai ding anompon, hijeh chun akipat doh-in achen, Jebus maijon ahung lhungtan, hichu Jerusalem ahi. Chule akoma sangan ni apho lhingset toh, athaikemnu aumin ahi.
target: But, unwilling to stay another night, the man left and went toward Jebus (that is, Jerusalem), with his two saddled donkeys and his concubine.

source: Chuin amaho Jebus kom ahung lhunun, nikho chu beiding ahitan; asohpa chun apu henga, Katao ahi, hungin, Jebus miho khopi-a hin lutnu hitin, gehtao hite, ati.
target: When they were near Jebus and the day was almost gone, the servant said to his master, “Come, let’s stop at this city of the Jebusites and spend the night.”

source: Chuin apupan ahenga, Eiho Israel chate-a hilou, hetkhahlou miho khopi-a ilut loudingu ahi; Gibeah kho geija cheu hite, ati.
target: His master replied, “No. We won’t go into any city whose people are not Israelites. We will go on to Gibeah.”

source: Chuin asohpa henga, Hungin, Gibeah ahiloule Ramah khatjoh joh naiju hitin, jan geh-u hite ati.
target: He added, “Come, let’s try to reach Gibeah or Ramah and spend the night in one of those places.”

source: Chuin amaho acheuvin, alamjot ajomun; chule Benjamin mite kho Gibeah kom alhunun, nisa alhumtan ahi.
target: So they went on, and the sun set as they neared Gibeah in Benjamin.

source: Chuin amaho hilama chu lutding le Gibeah'a chu geh dingin akihei lutnun ahi. Chuin ama alutphatnin, khopisung lamlen khatna atoutan ahi. Ajehchu amaho puiding le a-in'a lhunsah ding koimacha umlouva ahi.
target: There they stopped to spend the night. They went and sat in the city square, but no one took them in for the night.

source: Chuin veuvin nilhah ahiphatnin, tehsepu khat alou kona-a konin ahungin, ama jong chu Ephraim molsanga kon ahin; Gibeah'a khopem ahi: ahivangin chuche mun'a cheng miho chu Benjamin mi ahiuve.
target: That evening an old man from the hill country of Ephraim, who was living in Gibeah (the inhabitants of the place were Benjamites), came in from his work in the fields.

source: Chuin ama agah khodah-in ahile, khopi lampi-a tou kholjin mipa chu amun; chuin tehsepun ajah-a, Hoija cheding nahiuva? chule hoilama hungkon nahiuvem? ati.
target: When he looked and saw the traveler in the city square, the old man asked, “Where are you going? Where did you come from?”

source: Chuin aman amapa henga, Keiho Juda gam Bethlehem'a kon Ephraim molsang jonding kahiuvin, keima chu mun'a kon kahi. Keima Juda gam Bethlehem'a gache-a kahin, ahin tu-a hi Pakai in'a cheding kahi; chule koiman a-in'a eilhunsah ding aumpoi.
target: He answered, “We are on our way from Bethlehem in Judah to a remote area in the hill country of Ephraim where I live. I have been to Bethlehem in Judah and now I am going to the house of the Lord . No one has taken me in for the night.

source: Ahin hikoma hin changpol le ka sangan hou dinga ngaikhoh ho aumin, chule keima ding le kasohnu ding, chule nasohpan alhonpi gollhangpa dingin lengpitwi le changlhah jong aumin ahi, imacha alhasam beihela uma ahi, ati.
target: We have both straw and fodder for our donkeys and bread and wine for ourselves your servants—me, the woman and the young man with us. We don’t need anything.”

source: Chuin tehsepun, Lungmong tah-in umun; hijongle nadei jouseu keima chunga ngamun lang, lamlhonga vang geh hih beh-un, ati.
target: “You are welcome at my house,” the old man said. “Let me supply whatever you need. Only don’t spend the night in the square.”

source: Hitichun tehsepu chun amapa chu a-in'a apuilutnin, a-sangan teni chu nehding apen; chule amahon akengu akisilun, aneovin adonun ahi.
target: So he took him into his house and fed his donkeys. After they had washed their feet, they had something to eat and drink.

source: Chuin amaho alungsungu akipa laitah-un, veuvin, khopi miho phabep, Belial chapa phabep chun aumnao in chu aum kimvelun, akot chu achumun, chule a-inneipa tehsepu henga chun, Na in'a lhungpa chu kaki timatpi dingun hinpui doh-in, atiuvin ahi.
target: While they were enjoying themselves, some of the wicked men of the city surrounded the house. Pounding on the door, they shouted to the old man who owned the house, “Bring out the man who came to your house so we can have sex with him.”

source: Chuin mipa, a-inneipa chu ahenguva achedoh-in, ajah uva, Ahipoi, kasopiho, ahipoi, naheng uva katao ahi, hitilom hin khangse hih-un; hiche mipa hi ka in'a hung ahi namu jeh uvin, hiche ngol hoitah hi bolhih-un.
target: The owner of the house went outside and said to them, “No, my friends, don’t be so vile. Since this man is my guest, don’t do this outrageous thing.

source: Veovin, hikomahin kachanu nungah khat le thaikemnu aume; keiman amani hinpui doh ingting, nanghon amanichu noinep munlang, achung lhona pha nasah sah-u chu boljeng uvin: hichepa chunga vang chutobang thilse chu bol hih-un, ati.
target: Look, here is my virgin daughter, and his concubine. I will bring them out to you now, and you can use them and do to them whatever you wish. But as for this man, don’t do such an outrageous thing.”

source: Ahinla miho chun ama thusei chu ngaisah-in aneipeh pouve. Hitichun mipa chun athaikemnu chu apuijin, amaho henga chun ahin puilut tan ahi; chuin amahon amanu aluppiuvin, jan khovah jingkah geijin akichep naovin ahi. Chuin jingkho ahung vah phatnin, amanu asolmang taove.
target: But the men would not listen to him. So the man took his concubine and sent her outside to them, and they raped her and abused her throughout the night, and at dawn they let her go.

source: Chuin thingjang ahungvah phatnin numeinu chu ahungin, apupa umna mipa kotphunga chun alhun, khovah lhah kahsen hia chun aumtan ahi.
target: At daybreak the woman went back to the house where her master was staying, fell down at the door and lay there until daylight.

source: Chuin jingkah-in a-pakaipa athouvin, inkot chu ahongin, achena ding lampia chu che dingin apotdoh-in ahile; veuvin, athaikem numeinu chu kotbula chun analhun, chule akhut teni chu kotbula ana kingamin ahi.
target: When her master got up in the morning and opened the door of the house and stepped out to continue on his way, there lay his concubine, fallen in the doorway of the house, with her hands on the threshold.

source: Chuin amapan ahenga, Thouvin, chetaohite ati. Ahin adonbut tapoi. Hichun mipan amanu chu a-sangan chunga adomdoh-in, amajong atoudoh-in, achena dinga achetai.
target: He said to her, “Get up; let’s go.” But there was no answer. Then the man put her on his donkey and set out for home.

source: Chuin amapa a-in alhun phatnin, chemcha khat alan, athaikemnu chu atuh-in, agutoh pumin a-at khen khenin, tum somleni ason, chuin Israel gam pumpi-a athot tai.
target: When he reached home, he took a knife and cut up his concubine, limb by limb, into twelve parts and sent them into all the areas of Israel.

source: Chuin ahitin ahi, hiche mujouse chun, Israel chate Egypt gama kona ahung potdoh uva pat tuni chan geihin hitobanghi akibol khapon, mujong akimu khapoi. Hichehi ngaitouvin, thuhilna lauvin lang, nalungthimun thu seijun, atiuve.
target: Everyone who saw it was saying to one another, “Such a thing has never been seen or done, not since the day the Israelites came up out of Egypt. Just imagine! We must do something! So speak up!”

source: Chujouvin Israel chate jouse chu Dan'a pat Beersheba changei, chule Gilead gamsunga konin jong achedoh-un, mihonpi chu mikhat bangin Pakai ansung Mizpeh mun'a akikhom khomun ahi.
target: Then all Israel from Dan to Beersheba and from the land of Gilead came together as one and assembled before the Lord in Mizpah.

source: Chuin mipi jouse lamkaiho, Israel phungho chu Pathen mite kikhopna-a chun apangun, chemjam lamthei cheh kenga kalsong sepai sangjali ahiuvin ahi.
target: The leaders of all the people of the tribes of Israel took their places in the assembly of God’s people, four hundred thousand men armed with swords.

source: (Hichun Benjamin chaten Israel chate chu Mizpeh'a achetou uve ti ajataovin ahi.) Chuin Israel chaten, Iti dana hitobang gitlouna natoh hi sohdoh-a ham? neisei peh-un, atiuve.
target: (The Benjamites heard that the Israelites had gone up to Mizpah.) Then the Israelites said, “Tell us how this awful thing happened.”

source: Chuin Levi mipa, akithat numeinu jipa chun amaho adonbutnin, ahenguva, Benjamin miho khopi Gibeah'a chun keima le kathaikemnu jan gehdingin kahung lhonin ahi.
target: So the Levite, the husband of the murdered woman, said, “I and my concubine came to Gibeah in Benjamin to spend the night.

source: Hichun Gibeah miho keima dounan ahung kipat doh-un, jan-in kaumna in aum kimvelun, thadingin eigouvin: kathaikemnu hunamin abolun ahile, athilotan ahi.
target: During the night the men of Gibeah came after me and surrounded the house, intending to kill me. They raped my concubine, and she died.

source: Chuin keiman kathaikemnu chu kahin pon, kasat tel telin, chule Israelte chenna gamtina kathot kimvel tai. Ajehchu amahon Israel sunga thet umtah jonthanhoi le ngol hoitah na atong doh-un ahi.
target: I took my concubine, cut her into pieces and sent one piece to each region of Israel’s inheritance, because they committed this lewd and outrageous act in Israel.

source: Veovin, nangho nabonun Israel chate ngen nahiuve: hikoma hin nathuhilu le nathumop mu neipeuvin, ati.
target: Now, all you Israelites, speak up and tell me what you have decided to do.”

source: Chuin mipi jouse chu mikhat bangin akipat doh-un, Eiho khatcha iponbuh uva ichelouhel diu, khatcha i-in'uva iche louhel dingu ahi.
target: All the men rose up together as one, saying, “None of us will go home. No, not one of us will return to his house.

source: Ahin eihon tu-a hi Gibeah chunga ibol dingu chu hiche hi ahi: vang kivet dungjuija amaho doudinga ikon tou dingu;
target: But now this is what we’ll do to Gibeah: We’ll go up against it in the order decided by casting lots.

source: Chule amaho Benjamin te khopi Gibeah'a alhun tengule, amahon Israel sunga ngol hoitah aboldoh banguva chu achunguva na atoh theina dinguvin, eihon Israel phung jouse-a kona mipite an thah dinga, mi jakhat lah-a kon som, sangkhat lah-a kona jakhat, chule sangsom lah-a kon sangkhat ilhendoh dingu ahi, atiuvin ahi.
target: We’ll take ten men out of every hundred from all the tribes of Israel, and a hundred from a thousand, and a thousand from ten thousand, to get provisions for the army. Then, when the army arrives at Gibeah in Benjamin, it can give them what they deserve for this outrageous act done in Israel.”

source: Hitichun Israel mite jouse khopi douna chun mikhatseh bangin akipunkhom taovin ahi.
target: So all the Israelites got together and united as one against the city.

source: Chuin Israel phungho chun Benjamin phungho jouse henga mi asolun, Nalah uva kibol hitobang khangitlouna hi ipi hitam?
target: The tribes of Israel sent messengers throughout the tribe of Benjamin, saying, “What about this awful crime that was committed among you?

source: Hichejeh chun tun keihon amaho chu katha uva, Israel lah-a kona gitlounahi kasuhmang nadingun hiche miho, Gibeah'a um Belial chate chu neipedoh-un, atiuve. Ahinla Benjamin chaten asopiho Israel chate thusei chu ngaisah-in aneipeh pouvin:
target: Now turn those wicked men of Gibeah over to us so that we may put them to death and purge the evil from Israel.” But the Benjamites would not listen to their fellow Israelites.

source: Amavang Benjamin chate chu Israel chate satdingin, akhopi houva konin Gibeah khopi-a chun akikhom khomun ahi.
target: From their towns they came together at Gibeah to fight against the Israelites.

source: Chule hiche pettah-a chun Gibeah a chengho lhentum cheh jasagi tilouvin, Benjamin chate chu akhopihou jouse-a konin chemjam lamthei mi sangsomni le sanggup aumin ahi.
target: At once the Benjamites mobilized twenty-six thousand swordsmen from their towns, in addition to seven hundred able young men from those living in Gibeah.

source: Hicheho lah-a chun lhentum cheh veikolong mi jasagi aumun; chule amaho chun samjangte geija khel louhela sepkha thei cheh ahiuve.
target: Among all these soldiers there were seven hundred select troops who were left-handed, each of whom could sling a stone at a hair and not miss.

source: Chule Israel mite chu Benjamin simlouvin chemjam lamthei cheh mi sangjali ahiuvin; amaho hi abonuva galhang cheh ahiuve.
target: Israel, apart from Benjamin, mustered four hundred thousand swordsmen, all of them fit for battle.

source: Chuin Israel chate chu akipat doh-un, Pathen in lama chun ache touvun, Pathen'a konin thumop angeh-un, Keiho lah-a Benjamin chateho toh kisat dinga koipen kachetou masah ding ham? atiuve. Chuin Pakaiyin, Judah chetou masa ding ahi, ati.
target: The Israelites went up to Bethel and inquired of God. They said, “Who of us is to go up first to fight against the Benjamites?” The Lord replied, “Judah shall go first.”

source: Hitichun Israel chate chu jingkah-in athou doh-un, Gibeah dounan gebuh asong taovin ahi.
target: The next morning the Israelites got up and pitched camp near Gibeah.

source: Chuin Israel miho chu Benjamin to kisatdin akondoh uvin; chule Israel chate chu amaho toh kisat dingin Gibeah'a chun akigoltoh taovin ahi.
target: The Israelites went out to fight the Benjamites and took up battle positions against them at Gibeah.

source: Chuin Benjamin chate chu Gibeah'a konin ahung potdoh-un, hiche nikho chun Israel mite sangsomni le sangni jen tolla asat chapmun ahi.
target: The Benjamites came out of Gibeah and cut down twenty-two thousand Israelites on the battlefield that day.

source: Chuin Israel mite chu akitil khouvun, amasani-a akigolna mun mama uva chun galsat dingin akigolkit taovin ahi.
target: But the Israelites encouraged one another and again took up their positions where they had stationed themselves the first day.

source: (Chuin Israel chate achetouvun, nilhah geijin Pakai angsunga akapmun, Pakaiya kon thumop angeh-un, Kasopipa Benjamin chate douva kisatpi dinga kachetoukit ding ham? atiuve. Chuin Pakaiyin, Agakisatpi din kontouvin, ati.)
target: The Israelites went up and wept before the Lord until evening, and they inquired of the Lord . They said, “Shall we go up again to fight against the Benjamites, our fellow Israelites?” The Lord answered, “Go up against them.”

source: Chuin anikho ni channin Israel chate chu Benjamin chate dounan ahung nailut kit taovin ahi.
target: Then the Israelites drew near to Benjamin the second day.

source: Chuin anikho ni chanin Gibeah'a konin Benjamin amaho doudingin ahungdoh-in, Israel chate sangsom le sang get chu tolla asat chapmun ahi; amaho chu abonchauva chemjam lamthei cheh ahiuve.
target: This time, when the Benjamites came out from Gibeah to oppose them, they cut down another eighteen thousand Israelites, all of them armed with swords.

source: Hiche phatchun Israel chate, chule mi jouse chu ache touvun, Pathen in'a ahungun, akapmun, chule Pakai angsunga atouvun, hiche nikho chun nilhah geijin an angolun, chule Pakai angsunga chun govam thilto le chamna thilto atoh-un ahi.
target: Then all the Israelites, the whole army, went up to Bethel, and there they sat weeping before the Lord . They fasted that day until evening and presented burnt offerings and fellowship offerings to the Lord .

source: Chuin Israel chaten Pakai adongun, (ajehchu hiche nikho laija chu Pathen thulhun thingkhong chu hikoma chu uma ahin,
target: And the Israelites inquired of the Lord . (In those days the ark of the covenant of God was there,

source: Chule hiche nikho laichun Aaron chapa Eleazar chapa Phinehas chu a-angsunga chun adingjin ahi), Kasopipa Benjamin chate douva kisatpi dinga kachekit ding ham? atiuve. Chuin Pakaiyin, Kontouvin, ajehchu jingle amaho khu nakhutna kapehdoh ding ahi, ati.
target: with Phinehas son of Eleazar, the son of Aaron, ministering before it.) They asked, “Shall we go up again to fight against the Benjamites, our fellow Israelites, or not?” The Lord responded, “Go, for tomorrow I will give them into your hands.”

source: Chuin Israel ten Gibeah kimvela changpang ding akoigu taovin ahi.
target: Then Israel set an ambush around Gibeah.

source: Chule anithum channin Benjamin chate sat dingin Israel chate akontouvun, nidanga bangin Gibeah'a kidou dingin akigolkit taovin ahi.
target: They went up against the Benjamites on the third day and took up positions against Gibeah as they had done before.

source: Chuin Benjamin chate chu mipi ho dou dingchun ahungdoh-un ahile, khopi-a konchun agamlha taovin ahi. Chule nidang bangin miho chu asatnun, Pathen in chetouna lamlhong le Gibeah jotna loujao lah-a chun Israelte mi somthum tobang athatpan kit taovin ahi.
target: The Benjamites came out to meet them and were drawn away from the city. They began to inflict casualties on the Israelites as before, so that about thirty men fell in the open field and on the roads—the one leading to Bethel and the other to Gibeah.

source: Chuin Benjamin chaten, Amasa bangin imasanguva tha-in aumkit taove, atiuve. Ahinla Israel chate chun, Eiho jamuhitin, khopi-a konin lamlhonga puidoh uhite, atiu ahi.
target: While the Benjamites were saying, “We are defeating them as before,” the Israelites were saying, “Let’s retreat and draw them away from the city to the roads.”

source: Chuin Israel miho jouse chu apanmun cheh uva konin ahung kipatdoh uvin, amaho le amaho Baal-tamar'a akigolun; chule Israel chate changpanga pangho chu aumnao Gibeah phaichama konin ahungdoh-un ahi.
target: All the men of Israel moved from their places and took up positions at Baal Tamar, and the Israelite ambush charged out of its place on the west of Gibeah.

source: Chuin Israel mipi lah-a konin kilhengdoh mi sangsom ho chu Gibeah dou dingin ahungdoh-un, chule gal kisat chu anasa lheh-in ahi. Ahivangin Benjamin miho chun achunguva manthah na akomchaova aume ti ahepouve.
target: Then ten thousand of Israel’s able young men made a frontal attack on Gibeah. The fighting was so heavy that the Benjamites did not realize how near disaster was.

source: Chuin Pakaiyin Benjamin chu Israel masanga agal lel sahtan; chule hiche nikho chun Israel chaten Benjamin mite chu sangsomni le sangnga le jakhat athatnun; amaho chu chemjam lamthei cheh ahiuve.
target: The Lord defeated Benjamin before Israel, and on that day the Israelites struck down 25,100 Benjamites, all armed with swords.

source: Hitichun Benjamin chaten agal lel'u chu amutaovin ahi. Ajehchu Israel miho chun Gibeah pama changpang akoihou chu atahsan jeh uva, Benjamin miho dinga chu mun a-otnu ahi.
target: Then the Benjamites saw that they were beaten. Now the men of Israel had given way before Benjamin, because they relied on the ambush they had set near Gibeah.

source: Chuin changpangho chun kinotah-in Gibeah chu adel khumun; chule changpangho chu akihom khenun, khopi sunga chengho jouse chu chemjamin athat gamtaovin ahi.
target: Those who had been in ambush made a sudden dash into Gibeah, spread out and put the whole city to the sword.

source: Tun Israel miho leh changpangho chun akah uva melchihna khat aneiju ahin, hichu khopi-a kona meikong nasatah le meikhu ajamdohsah dingu ahi.
target: The Israelites had arranged with the ambush that they should send up a great cloud of smoke from the city,

source: Chutichun Israel mite chu agalsat naova kona akicholnga kahlah-un, Benjamin miho chun ahin nokhumun, Israel mi somthum tobang athatnun ahi. Ajehchu amahon, Amahohi kisatna masa-a banga imasanguva gallel kit ahi taove atiu ahi.
target: and then the Israelites would counterattack. The Benjamites had begun to inflict casualties on the Israelites (about thirty), and they said, “We are defeating them as in the first battle.”

source: Ahinla khopi-a kona meikong leh meikhu khompi banga ahung kitundoh phatnin, Benjamin miho chu akinung heijun aveovin ahile, veuvin, khopi-a kon meikong chu van geijin akikho touvin ahi.
target: But when the column of smoke began to rise from the city, the Benjamites turned and saw the whole city going up in smoke.

source: Chuin Israel miho ahung kinunghei kitnun ahile, Benjamin mihon kidang asaovin ahi; ajehchu amahon achunguva manthah na ahung lhungtai ti amuvin ahi.
target: Then the Israelites counterattacked, and the Benjamites were terrified, because they realized that disaster had come on them.

source: Hijeh chun amaho Israelte masang chun akinung heijun, gamthip lama ajam taove; ahinla gal kisatchun apha paovin, khopi-a kona hungdoh hochun alah tah uva konin asumangun ahi.
target: So they fled before the Israelites in the direction of the wilderness, but they could not escape the battle. And the Israelites who came out of the towns cut them down there.

source: Hitichun Benjamin miho chu aumkolun, adelun, Gibeah maijon nisona lam geijin bailam tah-in kengin achilun ahi.
target: They surrounded the Benjamites, chased them and easily overran them in the vicinity of Gibeah on the east.

source: Chuin Benjamin miho chu sangsom le sangget athiuvin; abonchauvin mihangsan jeng ahiuve.
target: Eighteen thousand Benjamites fell, all of them valiant fighters.

source: Chuin amaho akiheijun gamthip Rimmon songpi lama ajam taovin ahi. Chuin amahon lamlhonga chun mi sanga athatnun, chule Gidom geijin hatah-in anung adelun, mi sangni athatnun ahi.
target: As they turned and fled toward the wilderness to the rock of Rimmon, the Israelites cut down five thousand men along the roads. They kept pressing after the Benjamites as far as Gidom and struck down two thousand more.

source: Hitichun chuche nikho-a Benjamin mite athi jat chu chemjam lamthei cheh mi sangsomni le sangnga ahin; amaho abonchauva mihangsan cheh ahiuve.
target: On that day twenty-five thousand Benjamite swordsmen fell, all of them valiant fighters.

source: Ahin mi jagup hochu akiheijun gamthip Rimmon songpi lama chun ajamun, chule Rimmon songpi-a chun lhali aumun ahi.
target: But six hundred of them turned and fled into the wilderness to the rock of Rimmon, where they stayed four months.

source: Chuin Israel miho Benjamin miho chunga achukit uvin, chemjamin athatnun, khopi jouse-a konin amu jouseu mihem hihen, sahem hijongle athat gamun ahi. Chule amahon ahung lhunnao khopi jouse jongchu meijin ahalun ahi.
target: The men of Israel went back to Benjamin and put all the towns to the sword, including the animals and everything else they found. All the towns they came across they set on fire.

source: Tun Israel mihon chu Mizpeh'a akihahselun, Ilah uva khatchan achanu Benjamin mi ji dinga apehthei louding ahi, atiuve.
target: The men of Israel had taken an oath at Mizpah: “Not one of us will give his daughter in marriage to a Benjamite.”

source: Chuin mipi chu Pathen in'a ahungun, Pathen anga nilhah geijin aumun, aw sangtah-in asamuvin, hakan akapmun;
target: The people went to Bethel, where they sat before God until evening, raising their voices and weeping bitterly.

source: Vo Israelte Pakai Pathen, hitobang pihi ipi jeh-a Israel lah-a soh-a, tunikho-a Israel lah-a kona phungkhat lhasam ding hitam? atiuve.
target: “ Lord , God of Israel,” they cried, “why has this happened to Israel? Why should one tribe be missing from Israel today?”

source: Chuin ajingin ahung hitin ahi, miho chu jingpi tah in athouvun, maicham khat asaovin, govam thilto le chamna thilto atoh-un ahi.
target: Early the next day the people built an altar and presented burnt offerings and fellowship offerings.

source: Chuin Israel chaten, Israel phung jouse lah-a kona Pakai henga dinga mipi houkhom ho toh lhontou lou koi umam? atiuve. Ajehchu amahon Mizpeh mun'a Pakai henga hunglou tapou chungchanga kihahselna lentah aneijuva, Amachu thatei tei ding ahi, atiu ahi.
target: Then the Israelites asked, “Who from all the tribes of Israel has failed to assemble before the Lord ?” For they had taken a solemn oath that anyone who failed to assemble before the Lord at Mizpah was to be put to death.

source: Chuin Israel chate chu asopipao Benjamin dingin alung hesoh-un, Tuni hin Israel'a konin phung khat akipai dohtai.
target: Now the Israelites grieved for the tribe of Benjamin, their fellow Israelites. “Today one tribe is cut off from Israel,” they said.

source: Tu-a amoh umnalai ho ji ding chungchanga hi ipi ibol dingu hitam? Eihola Ichanuteu ajidiuvin pepouhite tin Pakai anga kihahselna ineitaovin, atiuve.
target: “How can we provide wives for those who are left, since we have taken an oath by the Lord not to give them any of our daughters in marriage?”

source: Chuin amahon, Pakai henga dinga Mizpeh'a hungtou lou Israel phung khat tou umam? atiuvin ahi. Chuin veovin, Jabesh Gilead'a konin akikhomho umna gebuh'a chun koimacha ahungpouve.
target: Then they asked, “Which one of the tribes of Israel failed to assemble before the Lord at Mizpah?” They discovered that no one from Jabesh Gilead had come to the camp for the assembly.

source: Ajehchu mipi chu akisima ahile, veuvin, Jabesh Gilead'a cheng miho chu khatcha jong aumpon ahi.
target: For when they counted the people, they found that none of the people of Jabesh Gilead were there.

source: Chuin mipi kikhom chun ahangsan dehset cheh mi sangsom le sangni asolun, chule thupeh aneijun, ahenguva, Cheovinlang Jabesh Gilead'a chengho chu numei leh achateuse toh chemhemin gathatnun.
