source: Chule keima lengdinga thao kinu kahi jeng vangin, tuni hin katha alhasam lheh-in ahi; chule hiche miho Zeruiah chapate hi keima dingin akhoh behseh jengun ahi. Pakaiyin thilphalou bolhohi aphatlounao natoh dungjuija alethuh dingu ahi, ati.
target: And today, though I am the anointed king, I am weak, and these sons of Zeruiah are too strong for me. May the Lord repay the evildoer according to his evil deeds!”

source: Chuin Saul chapan Hebron'a Abner athi tai ti ajah phatnin, akhut teni angoilhan, chule Israel pumpi jouse alunggim taovin ahi.
target: When Ish-Bosheth son of Saul heard that Abner had died in Hebron, he lost courage, and all Israel became alarmed.

source: Chule Saul chapan loilah-a gal lamkai mini aneijin: khatpa minchu Baanah ahin, chule khatjopa minchu Rechab ahi, Benjamin phunga Beeroth mi Rimon chapateni ahilhone, (ajehchu Beeroth jonghi Benjamin'a kisim ahi;
target: Now Saul’s son had two men who were leaders of raiding bands. One was named Baanah and the other Rekab; they were sons of Rimmon the Beerothite from the tribe of Benjamin—Beeroth is considered part of Benjamin,

source: Ajehchu Beeroth miho chu Gittaim'a jamlut uva, chule hiche munna chun tunikho geija khopemden ahitaove).
target: because the people of Beeroth fled to Gittaim and have resided there as foreigners to this day.

source: Chule Saul chapa Jonathan'in chapa khat aneijin amachu akengbai ahi. Jezreel'a kona Saul le Jonathan chungchang thu ahungchun amachu kumnga ahitan, ama jenlea pangnu chun amachu apuija ajampi ahi. Chule hitihi hija ahi, amanun mangang tah-a ajampi laitah-a amapa kiseplhu-a, akeng kibai ahi. Chule amapa minchu Mephibosheth ahi.
target: (Jonathan son of Saul had a son who was lame in both feet. He was five years old when the news about Saul and Jonathan came from Jezreel. His nurse picked him up and fled, but as she hurried to leave, he fell and became disabled. His name was Mephibosheth.)

source: Chuin Beeroth mipa Rimmon chapateni Rekab le Baanah chu akipat lhonin, hiche sun nisa noija chun Ishbosheth in'a ahung lhonin, amapa chu suna alupna-a ana lumin ahi.
target: Now Rekab and Baanah, the sons of Rimmon the Beerothite, set out for the house of Ish-Bosheth, and they arrived there in the heat of the day while he was taking his noonday rest.

source: Chuin amani suhlou chang hamding bangin insunga alutlhonin; amapa nahgu nga channa noitah chu asun lhonin: chuin Recab le asopipa Baanah chu ajamdoh lhontan ahi.
target: They went into the inner part of the house as if to get some wheat, and they stabbed him in the stomach. Then Rekab and his brother Baanah slipped away.

source: Ajehchu amani insunga ahunglut lhonchun, amapa alupna dansung alupna-a analumin ahi, chuin amanin amachu avo lhonin, athat lhonin, alu atan lhonin, chule alu chu ahinchoi lhonin jankhovah-a phaicham lampia chun ahin jampi lhonin ahi.
target: They had gone into the house while he was lying on the bed in his bedroom. After they stabbed and killed him, they cut off his head. Taking it with them, they traveled all night by way of the Arabah.

source: Chuin amanin Ishbosheth luchang chu Hebron'a David henga ahinpo lhonin, lengpa henga, Ven, nahinkho lahdinga gopa namelmapa Saul chapa Ishbosheth luchang ahi; ka pakai le ka-lengpa dinga hi tunia Pakaiyin Saul le achilhahte chunga phu nalahpeh ahitai, atilhone.
target: They brought the head of Ish-Bosheth to David at Hebron and said to the king, “Here is the head of Ish-Bosheth son of Saul, your enemy, who tried to kill you. This day the Lord has avenged my lord the king against Saul and his offspring.”

source: Chuin David'in Beeroth mi Rimmon chapateni Recab le asopipa Baanah chu adonbutnin, ajah lhona, Kaki lungdoupi ho-a kona kahinna huhdohpa, hingjing Pakai mina kasei ahi,
target: David answered Rekab and his brother Baanah, the sons of Rimmon the Beerothite, “As surely as the Lord lives, who has delivered me out of every trouble,

source: Mikhatnin kahenga kipana thupha hinlhut dana akingaitoa, Ven, Saul chu athitai atichun; athupoh jeh-a kipaman kapeh dinga kinempa chu keiman kamanin, Ziklag'ah kathat tan ahi.
target: when someone told me, ‘Saul is dead,’ and thought he was bringing good news, I seized him and put him to death in Ziklag. That was the reward I gave him for his news!

source: Achutile migilou hon michonpha khat a-insunga alupna chunga atha chungchanga hi ichana khohcheh-a kibolding hitam? Tu-a hi keiman amapa thisan hi nakhut lhona kangeh-a, leisetna kona kasuhmang lhonlou dingham? ati.
target: How much more—when wicked men have killed an innocent man in his own house and on his own bed—should I not now demand his blood from your hand and rid the earth of you!”

source: Chuin David'in agolhangho chu thu apen ahile, amahon amani chu athatnun, akhutlhon le akenglhon atanbongun, Hebron'a um twikul chung khatna akhai taovin ahi. Ahin amahon Ishbosheth luchang chu alauvin, Hebron mun'a um Abner lhanna chun avuitaove.
target: So David gave an order to his men, and they killed them. They cut off their hands and feet and hung the bodies by the pool in Hebron. But they took the head of Ish-Bosheth and buried it in Abner’s tomb at Hebron.

source: Chuin Israel phung jouse Hebron'a David henga ahungun, ahenga, Ven keihohi nagu le naphe jeng kahiuve.
target: All the tribes of Israel came to David at Hebron and said, “We are your own flesh and blood.

source: Chule masanga Saul keiho chunga lenga anapan laija patna, Israel gamsunga keiho eipuidoh uva le eipuilut uva nahi; chule Pakaiyin nahenga, Ka kelngoi Israelte hi navah ding, chule nangma Israelte chunga gallamkai nahi ding ahi, tin aseijin ahi, atiuve.
target: In the past, while Saul was king over us, you were the one who led Israel on their military campaigns. And the Lord said to you, ‘You will shepherd my people Israel, and you will become their ruler.’ ”

source: Hitichun Israel upaho jouse chu Hebron'a lengpa henga ahungun: chule David lengpan Hebron'a Pakai angsunga amatoh kitepna khat aneipin: chuin amahon David chu Israel pumpi chunga leng dingin thao anu taovin ahi.
target: When all the elders of Israel had come to King David at Hebron, the king made a covenant with them at Hebron before the Lord , and they anointed David king over Israel.

source: David alengchan kipatchun ama kum somthum ahitan, chule kum somli aleng changin ahi.
target: David was thirty years old when he became king, and he reigned forty years.

source: Hebron'a Judah te chunga kum sagile lhagup aleng changin, chule Jerusalem'a chun kum somthum le kumthum Israel le Judah chunga aleng changin ahi.
target: In Hebron he reigned over Judah seven years and six months, and in Jerusalem he reigned over all Israel and Judah thirty-three years.

source: Chuin lengpa le amite chu chuche gama um Jebus mite chenna Jerusalem'a chun acheuvin; amaho chun David henga, Mitcho le elbai nalahdoh masat loule hichea hi nahunglut theilou diu ahi, atiuvin ahi; ajehchu amahon David chu khopi sunga hin hunglut jou ponte, tia anagelu ahi.
target: The king and his men marched to Jerusalem to attack the Jebusites, who lived there. The Jebusites said to David, “You will not get in here; even the blind and the lame can ward you off.” They thought, “David cannot get in here.”

source: Ahijeng vanginla David'in Zion mundet pen chu alatan: hichu David khopi ahitai.
target: Nevertheless, David captured the fortress of Zion—which is the City of David.

source: Chuin hiche nikho chun David'in, Koi hijongle twilama kaltouva, Jebus miho le, David hinna-in adou mitcho le elbai ho gathat penpenpa chu lamkai pipuile gal lamkai hiding ahi, ati. Hijeh-a chu amahon, Mitcho le elbai insunga hunglut theilou ding ahi, atiu ahi.
target: On that day David had said, “Anyone who conquers the Jebusites will have to use the water shaft to reach those ‘lame and blind’ who are David’s enemies.” That is why they say, “The ‘blind and lame’ will not enter the palace.”

source: Hitichun David kulpi sunga chun achengin, chule hichu David khopi asahtai. Chuin David'in Millo'a pat asunglamsea chun kul akaikhum tan ahi.
target: David then took up residence in the fortress and called it the City of David. He built up the area around it, from the terraces inward.

source: Chuin David chu ahung khangtou chehcheh in, janel Pakai Pathen'in aumpin ahi.
target: And he became more and more powerful, because the Lord God Almighty was with him.

source: Chuin Tyre lengpa Hiram'in David henga sottol ho, chule cedar thingho, thingthem bolhole, song kheng themho ahinsolin ahi: chule amahon David dingin in asahpeh uvin ahi.
target: Now Hiram king of Tyre sent envoys to David, along with cedar logs and carpenters and stonemasons, and they built a palace for David.

source: Chuin David chun Pakaiyin Israelte chunga lengdinga atundoh ahichu ahetan; chule alenggam jong chu ami Israelte jal-in achoi lheh jengtan ahi.
target: Then David knew that the Lord had established him as king over Israel and had exalted his kingdom for the sake of his people Israel.

source: Chuin ama Hebron'a kona ahungdoh jouchun, David'in Jerusalem'a konin aji dingle athaikem akipuiben: chule David'a dingin chapate le chanute apenbe nalaijun ahi.
target: After he left Hebron, David took more concubines and wives in Jerusalem, and more sons and daughters were born to him.

source: Chule hichengsehi Jerusalem'a aumsunga pengho achate minchu ahi, Shammuah, Shobab, Nathan le Solomon,
target: These are the names of the children born to him there: Shammua, Shobab, Nathan, Solomon,

source: Chule Ibhar, Elishua, Napheg le Japhia,
target: Ibhar, Elishua, Nepheg, Japhia,

source: Elishama, Eliada, chule Eliphalet ahiuvin ahi.
target: Elishama, Eliada and Eliphelet.

source: Ahin Philistine ten David chu Israelte chunga leng dingin thao anutaove ti ajah phatnun, Philistinte jouse chu David holding chun ahung taovin; chule David'in hichu ajan, kulpidet lamma chun achesuhtan ahi.
target: When the Philistines heard that David had been anointed king over Israel, they went up in full force to search for him, but David heard about it and went down to the stronghold.

source: Philistinte jong chu ahungun Rephaim phaichama chun akithecheh taovin ahi.
target: Now the Philistines had come and spread out in the Valley of Rephaim;

source: Chuin David'in Pakai adongin, Keima Philistinte dou dinga kachetou dingham? Nangman amaho kakhutna neipeh doh dingham? ati. Chuin Pakaiyin David henga, Chetouvin; ijeh inem itile keiman tahsanlelna beihela Philistinte chu nakhutna kapeh dohding ahi, ati.
target: so David inquired of the Lord , “Shall I go and attack the Philistines? Will you deliver them into my hands?” The Lord answered him, “Go, for I will surely deliver the Philistines into your hands.”

source: Chuin David chu Baal-perazima ahungin, chule David'in hilaija chun amaho chu ajouvin, chuin aman, Pakaiyin kamelmate chu kamasanga twi kiphijah bangin asukeh jengtan ahi, ati. Hijeh chun aman hiche munchu Baal-perazim asahtai.
target: So David went to Baal Perazim, and there he defeated them. He said, “As waters break out, the Lord has broken out against my enemies before me.” So that place was called Baal Perazim.

source: Chuin amahon hia chun amilimhou chu adalha taovin ahile, David le aloihon ahalha taovin ahi.
target: The Philistines abandoned their idols there, and David and his men carried them off.

source: Chuin Philistine ho chu ahung kontou kitnun, chule amaho Rephaim phaichama chun akithecheh-un ahi.
target: Once more the Philistines came up and spread out in the Valley of Rephaim;

source: Hijeh chun David'in Pakai adongin ahile, aman, Nangma nakontou louding ahi; amavang nangman amaho nunglama kona nahin velkola, thingtheimi phungho maidon tah-a chu achunguva nachuh ding ahi.
target: so David inquired of the Lord , and he answered, “Do not go straight up, but circle around behind them and attack them in front of the poplar trees.

source: Chule hitiding ahi, nangman thingtheimi phungho chunga mipi kitol gin najah tengle, malam nanoding ahi; ijeh inem itile hiche phat chule Pakai chu Philistine janelho thatgam dinga namasanga cheding ahi, ati.
target: As soon as you hear the sound of marching in the tops of the poplar trees, move quickly, because that will mean the Lord has gone out in front of you to strike the Philistine army.”

source: Chuin David'in jong Pakaiyin athupeh bangchun aboltan; hitichun aman Philistinte chu Geba'a pat Gezer geijin athat tan ahi.
target: So David did as the Lord commanded him, and he struck down the Philistines all the way from Gibeon to Gezer.

source: Chuin David'in Israel mi akilhengdoh sangthum hochu akhom khomin ahi.
target: David again brought together all the able young men of Israel—thirty thousand.

source: Hichun David akipatdoh-in, aumpi jouse toh Juda gam Baale'a konin, Cherubim teni kikah-a um janel ho Pakai minna kikou, Pakai thingkhong chu gapotou dingin ache taovin ahi.
target: He and all his men went to Baalah in Judah to bring up from there the ark of God, which is called by the Name, the name of the Lord Almighty, who is enthroned between the cherubim on the ark.

source: Chuin amahon Pathen thingkhong chu bongkang thah khat chunga akoijun, Gibeah kho-a cheng Abinadab in'a konchun ahin podoh taovin ahi. Hitichun Abinadab chapateni Uzzah le Ahio chun hiche bongkang thah chu ahintol lhonin ahi.
target: They set the ark of God on a new cart and brought it from the house of Abinadab, which was on the hill. Uzzah and Ahio, sons of Abinadab, were guiding the new cart

source: Chule amahon Pathen thingkhong chu Gibeah kho-a Abinadab in'a konin ahinpodoh-un; Pathen thingkhong chutoh ahung kilhonpeh-un, chule Ahio chu Pathen thingkhong masanga chun achen ahi.
target: with the ark of God on it, and Ahio was walking in front of it.

source: Chuin David le Israel insung mijouse chun Pakai masanga chun chahthinga kisem manchah jatchom chomho, selangdah, tumgingtheiho jouse, khongchaho, sumkon bineiho, chule thih khutbeh ho atum gingun ahi.
target: David and all Israel were celebrating with all their might before the Lord , with castanets, harps, lyres, timbrels, sistrums and cymbals.

source: Chuin amaho Nacon pholmun ahunglhun phatnun, Uzzah chun Pathen thingkhong lama chun akhut ajahdoh-in, atuh-in ahi: ajehchu bongchal teni chun hichu athin lhon ahi.
target: When they came to the threshing floor of Nakon, Uzzah reached out and took hold of the ark of God, because the oxen stumbled.

source: Chuin Pakai lunghanna chu Uzzah chunga ahung koujah jengin; chuin Pathen'in athemona jeh-in hikoma chun ajepmin; chule ama Pakai Pathen thingkhong koma chun athitan ahi.
target: The Lord ’s anger burned against Uzzah because of his irreverent act; therefore God struck him down, and he died there beside the ark of God.

source: Chuin Pakai Uzzah chunga achuh jehchun David alung nommo lheh jengtan; hiche mun chu Perezuzzah asah-in, tunigeijin akisah tan ahi.
target: Then David was angry because the Lord ’s wrath had broken out against Uzzah, and to this day that place is called Perez Uzzah.

source: Chuin hicheni chun David'in Pakai akichan, Pakai thingkhong chu kahenga iti hung thei dingham? ati.
target: David was afraid of the Lord that day and said, “How can the ark of the Lord ever come to me?”

source: Hijeh chun David'in Pakai thingkhong chu ahenga David khopi sunga pohlut ding anomtapon; ahinla David'in hichu Gitt mi Obed-edom insunga chun apolut tan ahi.
target: He was not willing to take the ark of the Lord to be with him in the City of David. Instead, he took it to the house of Obed-Edom the Gittite.

source: Chuin Pakai thingkhong chu Gitt mi Obed-edom in'a chun lhathum aumin; chuin Pakaiyin Obed-edom le a-insung pumpi chu phatthei aboh tan ahi.
target: The ark of the Lord remained in the house of Obed-Edom the Gittite for three months, and the Lord blessed him and his entire household.

source: Chuin David lengpa jah-a, Pathen thingkhong jal-in Obed-edom le a-insung pumpi le anei agou jouse phatthei achang tai, ti akiseipeh tan ahi. Hijeh chun David achen, Pathen thingkhong chu Obed-edom in'a konin kipah tah-in David khopi-a ahin potou tan ahi.
target: Now King David was told, “The Lord has blessed the household of Obed-Edom and everything he has, because of the ark of God.” So David went to bring up the ark of God from the house of Obed-Edom to the City of David with rejoicing.

source: Chuin anahitin ahi, Pakai thingkhong puhon kalgup ason jouvun, aman bongchal le gan kivahthaova ganlhainan abolin ahi.
target: When those who were carrying the ark of the Lord had taken six steps, he sacrificed a bull and a fattened calf.

source: Chuin David chu Pakai angsunga chun athanei chasunin alamin; chule David chun tupat ponnem thempu sangkhola atai akigah ahi.
target: Wearing a linen ephod, David was dancing before the Lord with all his might,

source: Hijeh chun David le Israel insung miho jouse chun aw thongjeju le sumkon ginto thon Pakai thingkhong chu ahin putouvun ahi.
target: while he and all Israel were bringing up the ark of the Lord with shouts and the sound of trumpets.

source: Chule Pakai thingkhong chu David khopi sunga ahung lhunto lhonin, Saul chanu Michal'in bangkotna konin ahinven ahile, David lengpa Pakai masanga akhut alea alam chu amutan; amanun alungthimin amuneo lheh-in ahi.
target: As the ark of the Lord was entering the City of David, Michal daughter of Saul watched from a window. And when she saw King David leaping and dancing before the Lord , she despised him in her heart.

source: Chuin amahon Pakai thingkhong chu ahinpolut nun, aumna dinga David'in anasah ponbuh lailung tah-a chun akoitaovin ahi. Chuin David'in Pakai anga govam thilto le chamna thilto abolin ahi.
target: They brought the ark of the Lord and set it in its place inside the tent that David had pitched for it, and David sacrificed burnt offerings and fellowship offerings before the Lord .

source: Chuin David'in athilto, govam thilto le chamna thiltoho achai phatnin, aman mipi hochu Pakai janel minin phatthei aboh tan ahi.
target: After he had finished sacrificing the burnt offerings and fellowship offerings, he blessed the people in the name of the Lord Almighty.

source: Chuin David'in mijouse le Israel mite jouse chu, anumei apasal'in changlhah lum khatcheh le sachan khatcheh, chule lengpitheija kisem changlhah khatcheh ahoppeh'in ahi. Hitichun mijouse chu a-inlam cheh uva achetauvin ahi.
target: Then he gave a loaf of bread, a cake of dates and a cake of raisins to each person in the whole crowd of Israelites, both men and women. And all the people went to their homes.

source: Chuin David chu a-insung miho phatthei bohdingin ahung kiletan ahi. Chuin Saul chanu Michal chu David kimupi dingin ahungdoh-in, ahenga, Tunia Israelte lengpa pannabei mijahmo tah khat asagoh-a aum banga, tunia asoh numei ho mitmu-a asagoh-a aum jengchu iti loupi hitam! ati.
target: When David returned home to bless his household, Michal daughter of Saul came out to meet him and said, “How the king of Israel has distinguished himself today, going around half-naked in full view of the slave girls of his servants as any vulgar fellow would!”

source: Chuin David'in Michal jah-a, Pakai mite Israelte chunga vaihom dinga eitungdohpa, napa le a-insung miho jouse khella eilhengdoh pa Pakai masang ahi; hijeh achu Pakai masanga lamding kahi.
target: David said to Michal, “It was before the Lord , who chose me rather than your father or anyone from his house when he appointed me ruler over the Lord ’s people Israel—I will celebrate before the Lord .

source: Chule hiche sunga kamelse cheh ding, chule kamitmu-a kakisuhnem ding ahi. Nangman nasei soh numei ho chungchanga vang, keima amaho jabola kaum ding ahi, ati.
target: I will become even more undignified than this, and I will be humiliated in my own eyes. But by these slave girls you spoke of, I will be held in honor.”

source: Hijeh chun Saul chanu Michal chun athini geijin cha aneitapon ahi.
target: And Michal daughter of Saul had no children to the day of her death.

source: Chuin ahitin ahi, lengpa insunga atouva, Pakaiyin akimvela amelmaho-a konin choldona apeh phatnin,
target: After the king was settled in his palace and the Lord had given him rest from all his enemies around him,

source: Chutichun lengpan themgao Nathan henga, Tun vetemin, keima Cedar in'a kachengin, ahin Pathen thingkhong chu ponbuh maimai sunga aumin ahi, ati.
target: he said to Nathan the prophet, “Here I am, living in a house of cedar, while the ark of God remains in a tent.”

source: Chuin Nathan'in lengpa henga, Chenlang nalunga umjouse chu gaboltan, ajehchu Pakaiyin na-umpinai, ati.
target: Nathan replied to the king, “Whatever you have in mind, go ahead and do it, for the Lord is with you.”

source: Chuin chuche janchun ahitin ahi, Pakai thu chu Nathan henga ahungin, hitin ati,
target: But that night the word of the Lord came to Nathan, saying:

source: Chenlang kasoh David jah-a, Nangman keima dinga kachenna ding in khat neisahpeh dingham?
target: “Go and tell my servant David, ‘This is what the Lord says: Are you the one to build me a house to dwell in?

source: Keiman Israel chate Egypt gama kona kahin puidoh ni-a pat tuni geijin in'a kachengpon, amavang ponbuh sungle houbuh sungabou kachen ahi.
target: I have not dwelt in a house from the day I brought the Israelites up out of Egypt to this day. I have been moving from place to place with a tent as my dwelling.

source: Keima Israel chateto kana valena mun jouse-a, kami Israelte vahdinga kathupeh Israel phungho henga thu kanaseija, ahenguva, Ipi dinga nanghon keima dinga Cedar thinga in khat neisahpeh louvu ham tia kanasei khah-em?
target: Wherever I have moved with all the Israelites, did I ever say to any of their rulers whom I commanded to shepherd my people Israel, “Why have you not built me a house of cedar?” ’

source: Hijeh-a chu tuahi nangman kasoh David henga hitia hi nasei ding ahi, Janel Pakaiyin hitin aseije, Keiman nangmahi kelngoi lhatna hamhing lah-a kelngoi najuina-a kona kamite Israelte chunga vaihom dinga kalhendoh nahi:
target: “Now then, tell my servant David, ‘This is what the Lord Almighty says: I took you from the pasture, from tending the flock, and appointed you ruler over my people Israel.

source: Chule keiman nachena chana kalhonpin, namitmu-a konin namelmate jouse kasumangin, leiset chunga miminthang ho minkhat bangin namin kathansah tan ahi.
target: I have been with you wherever you have gone, and I have cut off all your enemies from before you. Now I will make your name great, like the names of the greatest men on earth.

source: Hiche chungvuma chu keiman kami Israelte dinga chu munkhat kalhendoh pehding, chule amaho agam mong monguva achenuva, akichon lele tahlou nadinguva kaphudet dingu; chule masanga banga migilou chaten jong asuhgenthei tahloudiu;
target: And I will provide a place for my people Israel and will plant them so that they can have a home of their own and no longer be disturbed. Wicked people will not oppress them anymore, as they did at the beginning

source: Kami Israelte chunga dinga thutan ho kana thupeh laija patna ana chutiu ahin; chule namelmate jouse-a konin kakicholdo sahtan ahi. Chujongle Pakaiyin nahenga na-insung katundoh pehding nahi ati.
target: and have done ever since the time I appointed leaders over my people Israel. I will also give you rest from all your enemies. “ ‘The Lord declares to you that the Lord himself will establish a house for you:

source: Chule nahin nikhoho ahunglhina, nangma napu napate toh nalupkhom tengle, keiman nanunga nachilhah, nangma taijola mong monga peng khat katundoh ding, Chule keiman alenggam kaphudet ding ahi.
target: When your days are over and you rest with your ancestors, I will raise up your offspring to succeed you, your own flesh and blood, and I will establish his kingdom.

source: Ama chun kamina in khat asah ding, chule keiman alenggam chu atonsotna dinga kaphudet ding ahi.
target: He is the one who will build a house for my Name, and I will establish the throne of his kingdom forever.

source: Keima apa kahi ding, chule ama kachapa hiding ahi. Aman khangit louna aneija ahile keiman amachu mihem sehgimna tenggol le mihem chate kajepna-a chu kasehgim ding ahi.
target: I will be his father, and he will be my son. When he does wrong, I will punish him with a rod wielded by men, with floggings inflicted by human hands.

source: Amavang namasanga kona kachondoh Saul'a kona kalahmang banga, kami hepina chu ama-a kona kalahmang louding ahi.
target: But my love will never be taken away from him, as I took it away from Saul, whom I removed from before you.

source: Chule na-insung le nalenggam chu a-itih a dinga namasanga kiphutdet ding; na laltouna jong a-itih-a dinga kiphutdet ding ahi, tin gaseipeh-in ati.
target: Your house and your kingdom will endure forever before me; your throne will be established forever.’ ”

source: Hicheng thuho dungjui le hiche gaothilmu ho dungjui hin Nathan'in David chu aseipeh tan ahi.
target: Nathan reported to David all the words of this entire revelation.

source: Chuin David lengpa chu alutnin, Pakai masanga atouvin, hitin aseije, Vo Pakai Pathen, keima koi kahi ham? chule ka-in chu ipiham hija nangman hichan geija neipuiham?
target: Then King David went in and sat before the Lord , and he said: “Who am I, Sovereign Lord , and what is my family, that you have brought me this far?

source: Chule vo Pakai Pathen, hichehi nangma dinga thil neocha bou ahinalaijin; chule nangman khonungpeh-a nasoh insunga hunglhung ding jong naseijin ahi. Chule Vo Pakai Pathen, hichehi mihem chonna dan ngaimong hinam?
target: And as if this were not enough in your sight, Sovereign Lord , you have also spoken about the future of the house of your servant—and this decree, Sovereign Lord , is for a mere human!

source: Chule David'in nahenga ipi aseibe dingham? Ajehchu Pakai Pathen nangin nasoh hi nahenai.
target: “What more can David say to you? For you know your servant, Sovereign Lord .

source: Ajehchu nathu jal le nangmatah lung ngaito dungjuija, hiche thil loupitahhi nasoh-in ahetthei nadinga nabol ahitai.
target: For the sake of your word and according to your will, you have done this great thing and made it known to your servant.

source: Hijeh chun vo Pakai Pathen, nangma naloupin ahi: ajehchu keihon kanaova kajah dungjuijun nangma tobang aumpon, nangma tailou Pathen dang aumpoi.
target: “How great you are, Sovereign Lord ! There is no one like you, and there is no God but you, as we have heard with our own ears.

source: Chule leiset chunga hi nami Israelte tobanga namkhat Pathen'in nangma-a hidinga Egypt gama kon, namtin le a-pathen hou lah-a kona, namite hiding le namin loupi sah ding, chule nangma dinga thil loupitahho le nagama dinga tijat umtahho boldinga nalhatdoh umkham?
target: And who is like your people Israel—the one nation on earth that God went out to redeem as a people for himself, and to make a name for himself, and to perform great and awesome wonders by driving out nations and their gods from before your people, whom you redeemed from Egypt?

source: Ajehchu nangma tah-in nami Israelte hi a-itih-a namite hidinga nanamdet ahitan: chule Pakai, nangma a-Pathen'u nahung hitai.
target: You have established your people Israel as your very own forever, and you, Lord , have become their God.

source: Chule tun, vo Pakai Pathen, nasoh chungchang le a-insung chung chang thua nasei thuhi a-itih a dingin phutdet ninlang, naseibang chun boltan.
target: “And now, Lord God, keep forever the promise you have made concerning your servant and his house. Do as you promised,

source: Chule Janel Pakai hi Israelte Pathen ahi tin namin hi a-imatih chanin choisangin umhen lang: chule nasoh David insung hi namasanga kiphutdet hen.
target: so that your name will be great forever. Then people will say, ‘The Lord Almighty is God over Israel!’ And the house of your servant David will be established in your sight.

source: Ajehchu nangma Vo janel Pakai le Israel Pathen'in nasoh henga naphong doh-in, Keiman na-insung katundoh ding ahi tin naseije. Hijeh-a chu nasoh hin hiche taona neina dinga hi alungsunga hansana amu ahi.
target: “ Lord Almighty, God of Israel, you have revealed this to your servant, saying, ‘I will build a house for you.’ So your servant has found courage to pray this prayer to you.

source: Chule tun, vo Pakai Pathen, nangma Pathen nahin, chule nathu hohi thutah ahin, chule nangman hiche phatna hi nasoh henga nahahsel in ahi.
target: Sovereign Lord , you are God! Your covenant is trustworthy, and you have promised these good things to your servant.

source: Hijeh chun tun a-itih-a namasanga aumjing nadin, nasoh insung phatthei naboh dinghi nalung lhaina hihen:ajehchu vo Pakai Pathen, nangman hichehi nasei ahitai; chule nangma phatthei bohna-a chun, nasoh insunghi a-itih-in phatthei changjing tahen.
target: Now be pleased to bless the house of your servant, that it may continue forever in your sight; for you, Sovereign Lord , have spoken, and with your blessing the house of your servant will be blessed forever.”

source: Chuin hiche jouchun ahitin ahi, David'in a Philistinte chu asatnin, amaho chu asunemin ahi. Chuin David'in Metheg-ammah chu Philistinte khutna konin aladohtan ahi.
target: In the course of time, David defeated the Philistines and subdued them, and he took Metheg Ammah from the control of the Philistines.

source: Chule aman Moab asatnin, chule amahochu tolla alupsah-in, khaovin aten; thading ho chu golni in aten, chule hinghoi dingho chu golkhat lhingsetnin aten ahi. Chutichun Moab mite chu David soh-in ahung pangun, thilpeh ahinchoi jiuvin ahi.
target: David also defeated the Moabites. He made them lie down on the ground and measured them off with a length of cord. Every two lengths of them were put to death, and the third length was allowed to live. So the Moabites became subject to David and brought him tribute.

source: Chuin David Euphrate luidunga agamgi lelah dinga achea chun, aman Zobah lengpa Rehob chapa Hadadezer jong chu athatnin ahi.
target: Moreover, David defeated Hadadezer son of Rehob, king of Zobah, when he went to restore his monument at the Euphrates River.

source: Chuin David'in amapa-a konchun sakol kangtalai sangkhat le sakol sepai jasagi, chule keng sepai sangsomni ahinlan ahi. Chuin David'in sakol kangkai jouse chu asubaijin, ahinla sakol kangtalai jakhat kaiding vang akhendoh-in ahi.
target: David captured a thousand of his chariots, seven thousand charioteers and twenty thousand foot soldiers. He hamstrung all but a hundred of the chariot horses.

source: Chuin Damascus'a Syria mite chu Zobah lengpa Hadadezer kithopi dingin ahungun ahile, David'in Syria mite chu sangsomni le sangni athatnin ahi.
target: When the Arameans of Damascus came to help Hadadezer king of Zobah, David struck down twenty-two thousand of them.

source: Chuin David'in Syria'a um Damascus'a chun sepai tampi akoitan ahi. Chuin Syria mite chu David soh-in ahung pangun, thilpeh ahinchoi jiuvin ahi. Chule Pakaiyin David chu achenna jouse-ah aveng jingin ahi.
target: He put garrisons in the Aramean kingdom of Damascus, and the Arameans became subject to him and brought tribute. The Lord gave David victory wherever he went.

source: Chuin David'in Hadadezer sohpa khutna um sana lumdal chu alan, Jerusalem'a ahin polut tan ahi.
target: David took the gold shields that belonged to the officers of Hadadezer and brought them to Jerusalem.

source: Chuin Hadadezer khopi Betah le Berothai'a konin, David lengpan sum-eng tamtah ahinpon ahi.
target: From Tebah and Berothai, towns that belonged to Hadadezer, King David took a great quantity of bronze.

source: Hamath lengpa Toi'in David lengpan Hadadezer janel jouse athattai ti ajah phatnin,
target: When Tou king of Hamath heard that David had defeated the entire army of Hadadezer,

source: Hichun aman Hadadezer asatna ajo jehchun, Toi'in ama chibai bohding le phatthei bohdingin achapa Joram chu David henga ahinsolin ahi; ajehchu Hadadezer chu Toi toh anakigal jinga ahi. Chule Joram'in dangka, sana, chule sum-eng kong le belho ahinpon:
target: he sent his son Joram to King David to greet him and congratulate him on his victory in battle over Hadadezer, who had been at war with Tou. Joram brought with him articles of silver, of gold and of bronze.

source: Hicheho chengse chu David'in asuhnem namtin jouse-a kona alah dangka le sana jouse chutoh Pakai henga atohdoh-in ahi.
target: King David dedicated these articles to the Lord , as he had done with the silver and gold from all the nations he had subdued:

source: Hicheho chu Syria'a kon, Moab'a kon, Ammon chate'a kon, Philistinete-a kon, Amalek'a kon, Zobah lengpa Rehob chapa Hadadezera'a kon galthil kichomho ahi.
target: Edom and Moab, the Ammonites and the Philistines, and Amalek. He also dedicated the plunder taken from Hadadezer son of Rehob, king of Zobah.

source: Chuin David'in chi phaicham mun'a Syria mite sangsom le sangget atha-a ahung kinunglekit chun amin athang tan ahi.
target: And David became famous after he returned from striking down eighteen thousand Edomites in the Valley of Salt.

source: Chuin aman Edom'a sepai tampi akoijin, Edom gamsung jouse chun sepai akoisoh keijin, chuin Edom mite jouse David sohte ahung hitaovin ahi. Chule David chu Pakaiyin achena jouse-a avengbit jingin ahi.
target: He put garrisons throughout Edom, and all the Edomites became subject to David. The Lord gave David victory wherever he went.

source: Chuin David'in Israel pumpi chunga vai ahomin; chule David'in amite jouse chunga chun phatah le dihtah-in na atongin ahi.
target: David reigned over all Israel, doing what was just and right for all his people.

source: Chule Zeruiah chapa Joab chun janel chunga vaipo ahin; chule Ahilud chapa Jehoshaphat chu thuching ahin;
target: Joab son of Zeruiah was over the army; Jehoshaphat son of Ahilud was recorder;

source: Ahitub chapa Zadok le Abiathar chapa Ahimelech chu thempu ahilhonin; chule Seraiah chu danthu sun ahin;
target: Zadok son of Ahitub and Ahimelek son of Abiathar were priests; Seraiah was secretary;

source: Jehoiada chapa Benaiah chu Chereth mite le Peleth mite chunga vaihomin apangin; chule David chapate chu vaihom pipun apangun ahi.
target: Benaiah son of Jehoiada was over the Kerethites and Pelethites; and David’s sons were priests.

source: Chuin David'in, Jonathan khohsahna jala hepina kamusah ding Saul insungmi khatbeh akikhendoh umlou ham? ati.
target: David asked, “Is there anyone still left of the house of Saul to whom I can show kindness for Jonathan’s sake?”

source: Chuin Ziba kiti Saul insungmi lah-a soh khat aumin ahi. Chuin amahon amachu David henga akouvun, chuin lengpan ajah-a, Nangma Ziba nahim? ati. Chuin aman, Nasohhi amachu kahinai, ati.
target: Now there was a servant of Saul’s household named Ziba. They summoned him to appear before David, and the king said to him, “Are you Ziba?” “At your service,” he replied.

source: Chuin lengpan ajah-a, Achunga Pathen mihepina kamusah ding Saul insungmi khatbeh umlou ham? ati. Chuin Ziba'in lengpa henga, Jonathan chapa khat aumin, amachu kengbai ahi, ati.
target: The king asked, “Is there no one still alive from the house of Saul to whom I can show God’s kindness?” Ziba answered the king, “There is still a son of Jonathan; he is lame in both feet.”

source: Chuin lengpan ajah-a, Amachu hoilaija umam? ati. Chuin Ziba'in lengpa henga, Ven amachu Lodebar kho-a um Ammiel chapa Machir in'a aumin ahi, ati.
target: “Where is he?” the king asked. Ziba answered, “He is at the house of Makir son of Ammiel in Lo Debar.”

source: Chuin David lengpan mi asolin, Lodebar kho-a um Ammiel chapa Machir in'a konchun agapuidoh tan ahi.
target: So King David had him brought from Lo Debar, from the house of Makir son of Ammiel.

source: Tun Saul chapa, Jonathan chapa Mephibosheth chu David kom ahunglhun phatnin, ama aboh khupmin jana apen ahi. Chuin David'in, Mephibosheth, ati. Chuin aman, ven nasohhi! tin adonbutnin ahi.
target: When Mephibosheth son of Jonathan, the son of Saul, came to David, he bowed down to pay him honor. David said, “Mephibosheth!” “At your service,” he replied.

source: Chuin David'in ajah-a, Kicha hih-in: ajehchu keiman thonlouva napa Jonathan khohsahna jala nangma hepina kamusah ding, chule napu Saul gam sese jong kalepeh kitna, nangma tanglou hela kadokhang chunga changlhah naneh jing ding ahitai, ati.
target: “Don’t be afraid,” David said to him, “for I will surely show you kindness for the sake of your father Jonathan. I will restore to you all the land that belonged to your grandfather Saul, and you will always eat at my table.”

source: Chuin ama akunin, Nasohhi ipi kahia, chule uicha thisa tobang keimahi nei khohsah ham? ati.
target: Mephibosheth bowed down and said, “What is your servant, that you should notice a dead dog like me?”

source: Chuin lengpan Saul sohpa Ziba chu akouvin, ajah-a, Saul neijouse le a-in jouse napakai pa chapahi kapeh ahitai.
target: Then the king summoned Ziba, Saul’s steward, and said to him, “I have given your master’s grandson everything that belonged to Saul and his family.

source: Hijeh-a chu nangma le nachapate, chule nasohten amadinga leiset chu nalhopeh diu, chule napakai pau hin nehding an aneitheina dinga agasoh hochu nahin pohdiu ahi: ahin napakai pao chapa Mephibosheth hin phattina kadokhanga changlhah anehding ahi, ati. Tun Ziba'n chapa somle ngale soh somni aneijin ahi.
target: You and your sons and your servants are to farm the land for him and bring in the crops, so that your master’s grandson may be provided for. And Mephibosheth, grandson of your master, will always eat at my table.” (Now Ziba had fifteen sons and twenty servants.)

source: Hichun Ziba'n lengpa jah-a, Ka pakai lengpan asoh athupeh dungjuija hi nasoh-in kabol ding ahi, ati. Mephibosheth chungchanga, lengpan hitin ati, aman kadokhang chunga chapateho khat banga an anehding ahi.
target: Then Ziba said to the king, “Your servant will do whatever my lord the king commands his servant to do.” So Mephibosheth ate at David’s table like one of the king’s sons.

source: Chule Mephibosheth'in chapa khangdong khat aneijin, amin chu Mica ahi. Chule Ziba insunga cheng jouse chu Mephibosheth soh ahi taovin ahi.
target: Mephibosheth had a young son named Mika, and all the members of Ziba’s household were servants of Mephibosheth.

source: Hitichun Mephibosheth chu Jerusalem'a achengin ahi: ajehchu aman tanglou helin lengpa dokhanga anen; chule ama akeng ni-a baija ahi.
target: And Mephibosheth lived in Jerusalem, because he always ate at the king’s table; he was lame in both feet.

source: Chuin hiche jouchun ahitin ahi, Ammon chateho lengpa chu athitan ahile achapa Hanun chun ama khelin lengvai apotan ahi.
target: In the course of time, the king of the Ammonites died, and his son Hanun succeeded him as king.

source: Chuin David'in, Apan kachunga hepina eimusah banga, keima jong Nahash chapa Hanun chunga hepina kamusah ding ahi, ati. Hitichun David'in apa chungchanga ama lhamon ding chun asohte asoltan ahi. Chuin David soh ho chu Ammon chate gama chun ahunglut taovin ahi.
target: David thought, “I will show kindness to Hanun son of Nahash, just as his father showed kindness to me.” So David sent a delegation to express his sympathy to Hanun concerning his father. When David’s men came to the land of the Ammonites,

source: Chule Ammon chate pipuho chun apakaipao Hanun jah-a, David hin napa ajana jala lhamonsah hohi ahinsol ahi hinte tia nagelem? David hin khopi hi ajotheina dinga akholtoh dingle, avelhi ding joh-a ahinsol hilou ham? atiuve.
target: the Ammonite commanders said to Hanun their lord, “Do you think David is honoring your father by sending envoys to you to express sympathy? Hasn’t David sent them to you only to explore the city and spy it out and overthrow it?”

source: Hijeh chun Hanun'in David soh ho chu amanin, akhamulu akeh langkhat avolhahpeh-in, chule aponchenu chu akimlaitah, ato don laitah-u chu achetanpeh-in; chuin amahochu asolmang tan ahi.
target: So Hanun seized David’s envoys, shaved off half of each man’s beard, cut off their garments at the buttocks, and sent them away.

source: Chuin hichehi David aseipeh phatnun, aman amaho kimupi ding asolin ahi, ajehchu miho chu jahcha lheh jengu ahi: chuin lengpan, Nakhamulu asaodohkit kahsen Jericho-a umunlang, ahung saodoh tengle hung kinunglekit taovin, ati.
target: When David was told about this, he sent messengers to meet the men, for they were greatly humiliated. The king said, “Stay at Jericho till your beards have grown, and then come back.”

source: Chuin Ammon chaten David angsung kidah umtah ahiu amudoh phatnun, Ammon chate chun Bethrehob'a um Syria mite, Zobah'a um Syria mite keng sepai sangsomni, Maakah lengpa-a kon mi sangkhat, chule Ishtob'a kon mi sangsom le sangni athalah-un ahi.
target: When the Ammonites realized that they had become obnoxious to David, they hired twenty thousand Aramean foot soldiers from Beth Rehob and Zobah, as well as the king of Maakah with a thousand men, and also twelve thousand men from Tob.

source: Chuin David'in hichu ajah phatnin, Joab le amihat janelho chu asoltan ahi.
target: On hearing this, David sent Joab out with the entire army of fighting men.

source: Chuin Ammon chate chu ahung kondoh-un, kotpi phung lutna-a chun galsat dingin akigolun: Zobah'a um,Rehob'a um, Ishtob'a um le Maakah'a um Syria mite chu amaho le amaho loujaova aumun ahi.
target: The Ammonites came out and drew up in battle formation at the entrance of their city gate, while the Arameans of Zobah and Rehob and the men of Tob and Maakah were by themselves in the open country.

source: Joab'in galchu anung le ama-a aum amu phatnin, Israel mi lhentum cheh chu alhengdoh-in, amaho chu Syria te toh kisat dingin akigolsah-in:
target: Joab saw that there were battle lines in front of him and behind him; so he selected some of the best troops in Israel and deployed them against the Arameans.

source: Chule adangho sese chu asopipa Abishai khutna Ammon chate toh kisat dinga agoltoh dingin apedoh-in ahi.
target: He put the rest of the men under the command of Abishai his brother and deployed them against the Ammonites.

source: Chuin aman, Syria te chu keija dinga ahat behseh uva ahile, nangman neikithopi ding; ahia Ammon chate chu nanga dinga ahat behseh uva ahile, keima kahunga kahung kithopi ding nahi.
target: Joab said, “If the Arameans are too strong for me, then you are to come to my rescue; but if the Ammonites are too strong for you, then I will come to rescue you.

source: Hangsanun, eiho imiteu dingleh i-Pathen'u khopiho-a dingin pangu hite: chule Pakaiyin amitmu-a pha asah bang bangin bolhen, ati.
target: Be strong, and let us fight bravely for our people and the cities of our God. The Lord will do what is good in his sight.”

source: Chuin Joab le aumpi miho chu Syria mite to kisat dingin galmun anailut taovin ahile, amaho chu amasanga chun ajam taovin ahi.
target: Then Joab and the troops with him advanced to fight the Arameans, and they fled before him.

source: Chuin Ammon chate chun Syria mite jam chu amu phatnun, amaho jong Abishai masanga chun ajamun, khopi sungah aluttaovin ahi. Hitichun Joab chu Ammon chate-a konchun ahung kinunglen, Jerusalem'a ahungtan ahi.
target: When the Ammonites realized that the Arameans were fleeing, they fled before Abishai and went inside the city. So Joab returned from fighting the Ammonites and came to Jerusalem.

source: Chuin Syria miten Israelte masanga agal lel'u chu amuphatnun, amaho akikhom khom taovin ahi.
target: After the Arameans saw that they had been routed by Israel, they regrouped.

source: Chuin Hadadezer'in mi asolin, luipi galla um Syria mite chu agapuidoh-in ahi. Chuin amaho Helam'a ahungun, chule Hadadezer janel gal lamkai Shobach chu amaho masanga achen ahi.
target: Hadadezer had Arameans brought from beyond the Euphrates River; they went to Helam, with Shobak the commander of Hadadezer’s army leading them.

source: Chule hichethu hi David aseipeh phatnun, aman Israelte jouse akhom khomin, Jordan agalkaijun, Helam mun'a ahungun ahi. Chuin Syria mite chu David doudingin amaho le amaho akigol toh-un, ama chutoh akisat taovin ahi.
target: When David was told of this, he gathered all Israel, crossed the Jordan and went to Helam. The Arameans formed their battle lines to meet David and fought against him.

source: Chuin Syriaho chu Israel masanga chun ajam taovin; chule David'in Syria miho sakol kangtalai tolmi jasagi le sakol sepai sangsomli, chule ajanelhou lamkai Shobach jong chu athatnin, hiche mun'a chun athitan ahi.
target: But they fled before Israel, and David killed seven hundred of their charioteers and forty thousand of their foot soldiers. He also struck down Shobak the commander of their army, and he died there.

source: Chuin Hadadezer soh-a um lengho jouse chun Israelte masanga agal lel'u chu amu phatnun, Israelte toh chamna abollun, amaho jenle-in apang taovin ahi. Hijeh chun Syria miten Ammon chateho kithopi kit ding chu akicha taovin ahi.
target: When all the kings who were vassals of Hadadezer saw that they had been routed by Israel, they made peace with the Israelites and became subject to them. So the Arameans were afraid to help the Ammonites anymore.

source: Chuin ahitin ahi, kum ahung kichaina, lengho galkon phat laitah-in, David'in Joab le aumkhompi asote chule Israel mite chu asolin; chuin amahon Ammon chate asumangun, Rabbah khopi aum uvin ahi. Ahinla David Jerusalem'a aum jingin ahi.
target: In the spring, at the time when kings go off to war, David sent Joab out with the king’s men and the whole Israelite army. They destroyed the Ammonites and besieged Rabbah. But David remained in Jerusalem.

source: Chuin nilhah langin ahitin ahi, David chu alupna-a konin athoudoh-in, leng in chunga chun avahle len ahi. Chuin aman in chunga konchun numei khat akisilpet amun, chule hiche numeinu chu vetdinga melhoitah ahi.
target: One evening David got up from his bed and walked around on the roof of the palace. From the roof he saw a woman bathing. The woman was very beautiful,

source: Chuin David'in mi asolin amanu thudol agakholchil sah-in ahi. Chuin mikhatnin, Hichehi Hit mi Uriah inneipi Eliam chanu Bathsheba hilouham? ati.
target: and David sent someone to find out about her. The man said, “She is Bathsheba, the daughter of Eliam and the wife of Uriah the Hittite.”

source: Chuin David'in thupole ho khat asolin, amanu agapuisah tan; chule amanu ahenga ahungin, aman amanu aluppitan ahi; ajehchu amanu chu athen louna-a kona kisuthenga ahin: chuin amanu a-in lama akile kittan ahi.
target: Then David sent messengers to get her. She came to him, and he slept with her. (Now she was purifying herself from her monthly uncleanness.) Then she went back home.

source: Chuin amanun nao avop phatnin, David henga mi asolin, Nao kavoptai, agati sah-e.
target: The woman conceived and sent word to David, saying, “I am pregnant.”

source: Chuin David'in Joab thu athotnin, Hit mi Uriah chu neihin solpeh-in, ati. Chuin Joab'in Uriah chu David henga ahin soltan ahi.
target: So David sent this word to Joab: “Send me Uriah the Hittite.” And Joab sent him to David.

source: Chuin Uriah ahenga ahung phatnin, David'in Joab le mipite chu iti naovem, chule galchu itobanga machal jinga hinam tin adongin ahi.
target: When Uriah came to him, David asked him how Joab was, how the soldiers were and how the war was going.

source: Chuin David'in Uriah jah-a, Na-in lama chesuh inlang, nakeng kisilin, ati. Chuin Uriah chu lengpa in'a konin akipatdoh-in, chule lengpa-a kona nehding thilpeh ho-in anung ajuisuh paijin ahi.
target: Then David said to Uriah, “Go down to your house and wash your feet.” So Uriah left the palace, and a gift from the king was sent after him.

source: Ahivangin Uriah chu lengpa in kotkhah bula chu a-pakaipa sohte chutoh alum denin, a-in lama chun achesuhpon ahi.
target: But Uriah slept at the entrance to the palace with all his master’s servants and did not go down to his house.

source: Chuin amahon Uriah chu a-in lama achetapoi tia David aseipeh phatnun, David'in Uriah jah-a, Nakholjin na-a kona nahung hilouham? ipidinga na-in lama chu chesuh louva nahim? ati.
target: David was told, “Uriah did not go home.” So he asked Uriah, “Haven’t you just come from a military campaign? Why didn’t you go home?”

source: Chuin Uriah chun David henga, Pathen thingkhong le Israel chule Judah pon in'a aumun; chule ka pakaipa Joab le ka pakaipa sohten gamlah-a gebuh akisonun; keima ane dingle adonding, chule kaji toh lumkhom dinga ka-in'a kache dingham? Nangma nahina nalhagao ahinlaisen keiman hiche tobang thil hi bolponge ati.
target: Uriah said to David, “The ark and Israel and Judah are staying in tents, and my commander Joab and my lord’s men are camped in the open country. How could I go to my house to eat and drink and make love to my wife? As surely as you live, I will not do such a thing!”

source: Chuin David'in Uriah henga, Tunin jong hiche mun'a hin umkit tan, chule jing tengle keiman kipatdohsah nange ati. Hijeh chun Uriah chu Jerusalem'a hicheni chun chule ajing geijin aumtan ahi.
target: Then David said to him, “Stay here one more day, and tomorrow I will send you back.” So Uriah remained in Jerusalem that day and the next.

source: Chuin David'in ama akou phatnin, aman ama masanga chun anen adonin, chuin aman ama chu adonkhamsah tan ahi. Chuin nilhah lamin a-pakaipa sohtetoh jalkhuna lum dingin achen, ahin a-inlanga vang achesuh pon ahi.
target: At David’s invitation, he ate and drank with him, and David made him drunk. But in the evening Uriah went out to sleep on his mat among his master’s servants; he did not go home.

source: Chuin jingkah-in ahitin ahi, David'in Joab henga dingin lekha khat asunin, hichu Uriah khutna athottan ahi.
target: In the morning David wrote a letter to Joab and sent it with Uriah.

source: Chuin aman lekha chunga chun asunin, Uriah chu galmun khohpen masanga chun pansah-in, amachu akisuhkhah -a athitheina dingin, ama-a konin kinung chonun, ati.
target: In it he wrote, “Put Uriah out in front where the fighting is fiercest. Then withdraw from him so he will be struck down and die.”

source: Chule ahitin ahi, Joab'in khopi chu aum laijin, Uriah chu galhat miho umna-a ahet munkhatna chun apansah-in ahi.
target: So while Joab had the city under siege, he put Uriah at a place where he knew the strongest defenders were.

source: Chuin khopi sunga um miho chu apotdoh-un, Joab toh akisat taovin ahi: chule hiche mun'a chun David sohte mipi ho lah-a phabep khat alhutaovin; chule Hit mi Uriah jong chu athitai.
target: When the men of the city came out and fought against Joab, some of the men in David’s army fell; moreover, Uriah the Hittite died.

source: Chuin Joab'in gal chung chang thu jouse David gaseipeh dingin mi asoltan;
target: Joab sent David a full account of the battle.

source: Chuin aman thupolepa chu thu apen, Nangman lengpa henga gal umchan thuho jouse nagasei soh tengle,
target: He instructed the messenger: “When you have finished giving the king this account of the battle,

source: Lengpa alunghana, nahenga, Ipidinga kisatpi dinga khopi chu nachuti nailut jengu ham? Banga kona nahin kap dingu chu nanghon nahetlouvu ham?
target: the king’s anger may flare up, and he may ask you, ‘Why did you get so close to the city to fight? Didn’t you know they would shoot arrows from the wall?

source: Jerubesheth chapa Abimelech chu koiham athatna? Banga kona numei khatnin sumheisong halkhat aselhah khumleh ama chu Thebez mun'a thia hilouham? Ipi dinga nangho bang naija nacheu ham? tia asei tengle nangman, Nasoh Hit mi Uriah jong athitai, tia nasei ding ahi, ati.
target: Who killed Abimelek son of Jerub-Besheth? Didn’t a woman drop an upper millstone on him from the wall, so that he died in Thebez? Why did you get so close to the wall?’ If he asks you this, then say to him, ‘Moreover, your servant Uriah the Hittite is dead.’ ”

source: Chuin thupolepa chu achen, Joab'in asol lona jouse chu David henga aseitan ahi.
target: The messenger set out, and when he arrived he told David everything Joab had sent him to say.

source: Chuin thupolepa chun David henga, Tahbeh-in miho chun keiho eihinjou jouvin, chule loujaova keiho lah-a lama ahungpotnun, keihon amaho chu kotpi phung lutna geijin kanung delun ahi.
target: The messenger said to David, “The men overpowered us and came out against us in the open, but we drove them back to the entrance of the city gate.

source: Chuin thalkap hon kulbanga konin nasohte lah ahin kapmun ahile lengpa soh phabep khat athitan, chule nasoh Hit mi Uriah jong chu athitan ahi, ati.
target: Then the archers shot arrows at your servants from the wall, and some of the king’s men died. Moreover, your servant Uriah the Hittite is dead.”

source: Chujouvin David'in thupolepa henga, Nangman Joab henga, Hicheho hin nangma nalungkham sah dahen, ajehchu chemjamin mikhat ahiloule adangkhat athateiji mong ahi: khopi douna-a chun nagalsat hatsah cheh inlang, khopi chu suse-in, tia naseija amachu natilkhou ding ahi, ati.
target: David told the messenger, “Say this to Joab: ‘Don’t let this upset you; the sword devours one as well as another. Press the attack against the city and destroy it.’ Say this to encourage Joab.”

source: Chuin Uriah jinun ajipa Uriah athitai ti ajah phatnin, ajipa pul adoutan ahi.
target: When Uriah’s wife heard that her husband was dead, she mourned for him.

source: Chuin alunghemna akichai phatnin, David'in amanu chu a-in'a agapuilut sah-in, chule amanu chu a-inneipi ahung hitan, chuin ama dingin chapa khat ahinpeh-in ahi. Ahin David thilbol chun Pakai alung lhaisah tapon ahi.
target: After the time of mourning was over, David had her brought to his house, and she became his wife and bore him a son. But the thing David had done displeased the Lord .

source: Chuin Pakaiyin David henga Nathan asolin, chuin ama ahenga ahungin, ajah-a, Khopi khatna hin mini aumin, khatchu ahaovin, khatjohpa chu avaichan ahi.
target: The Lord sent Nathan to David. When he came to him, he said, “There were two men in a certain town, one rich and the other poor.

source: Mihaopa chun kelngoi honle ganchahon tamtah aneijin:
target: The rich man had a very large number of sheep and cattle,

source: Ahinla mivaichapan akichoh-a avah kelngoinou anu khat tilouvin imacha aneipon ahi. Chule hiche kelngoinou amale achate toh thakhatna hungkhang len ahin, chule ama an ngei chu aneh-a, akhontah-a twi adona, ama angsunga lumma, chule amadinga chanu khat tobang hija ahi.
target: but the poor man had nothing except one little ewe lamb he had bought. He raised it, and it grew up with him and his children. It shared his food, drank from his cup and even slept in his arms. It was like a daughter to him.

source: Chuin mihaopa koma chun kholjin vahlekhat ahungin, chuin aman akelngoi honho lah-a khatjeng chajong chu hiche kholjin ahung lhungpa thapeh dingchun aphalpon; ahin mivaichapa kelngoi chu alan, chuin aman ahenga hung mipa ding chun athapehtan ahi, ati.
target: “Now a traveler came to the rich man, but the rich man refrained from taking one of his own sheep or cattle to prepare a meal for the traveler who had come to him. Instead, he took the ewe lamb that belonged to the poor man and prepared it for the one who had come to him.”

source: Hiche mipa chunga chun David lunghana chu akoujah jengin, chuin aman Nathan henga, Hingjing Pakai mina kasei ahi, hitobang thil bolla michu thiteiding ahi:
target: David burned with anger against the man and said to Nathan, “As surely as the Lord lives, the man who did this must die!

source: Chule hitobang abola, khotona anei loujeh-a, kelngoi chu ajatlia aleding ahi, ati.
target: He must pay for that lamb four times over, because he did such a thing and had no pity.”

source: Chuin Natha'in David henga, Hiche mipa chu nangma nahi. Israel Pakai Pathen'in hitin aseije, Keiman nangmahi Israel chunga leng dinga thao kanua, chule Saul khutna kona kahuh doh-a;
target: Then Nathan said to David, “You are the man! This is what the Lord , the God of Israel, says: ‘I anointed you king over Israel, and I delivered you from the hand of Saul.

source: Chule napakai pa insungle ajiteho chu nangma kapeh-a, chule Israel le Judah insung jong nangma kapeh nahin; ahin hiche chu lhombehseh ahia ahile, keiman nangma adang dang jong kapehbe nalai ding ahi.
target: I gave your master’s house to you, and your master’s wives into your arms. I gave you all Israel and Judah. And if all this had been too little, I would have given you even more.

source: Ipidinga nangman amitmua thilphalou bolna dinga Pakai thupeh chu nahsah louva nabol ham? Nangman Hit mi Uriah chu chemjamin nathatnin, a-inneipi chu naji dingin nakipuijin, chule ama Ammon chate chemjamin nathatnin ahi.
target: Why did you despise the word of the Lord by doing what is evil in his eyes? You struck down Uriah the Hittite with the sword and took his wife to be your own. You killed him with the sword of the Ammonites.

source: Hijeh chun tu-a hi na-insunga kona chemjam kiladoh louding ahi; ajehchu nangman nahsahmon neibolin, Hit mipa Uriah inneipi chu najidingin nakipuijin ahi.
target: Now, therefore, the sword will never depart from your house, because you despised me and took the wife of Uriah the Hittite to be your own.’

source: Pakaiyin hitin aseije, Vetan, Keiman nangma douna-a na-insunga thilphalou khat kasodohsah ding, chule najiteho chu namitmu-a kalahpeh-a, amaho chu na-inhengho kapeh ding, chule aman najiteho chu sunchang noija aluppi dingu ahi.
target: “This is what the Lord says: ‘Out of your own household I am going to bring calamity on you. Before your very eyes I will take your wives and give them to one who is close to you, and he will sleep with your wives in broad daylight.

source: Ajehchu nangman hichehi guhthima nabol ahin; ahinla keiman hichehi Israel jouse masangle sunchang noija kabol ding ahi, ati.
target: You did it in secret, but I will do this thing in broad daylight before all Israel.’ ”

source: Chuin David'in Nathan henga, Keima Pakai dounan kachonse tai, ati. Chuin Nathan'in David henga, Pakaiyin jong nachonsetna aladohtai, nangma nathi louding ahi.
target: Then David said to Nathan, “I have sinned against the Lord .” Nathan replied, “The Lord has taken away your sin. You are not going to die.

source: Hijeng jongle hiche nathilbola konahi Pakai melmaten Pathen ataitomna ding uva phat gomkom napeh ahi jeh-in, nangma-a dinga penga nachapa chu thitei ding ahi, ati.
target: But because by doing this you have shown utter contempt for the Lord , the son born to you will die.”

source: Chuin Nathan chu a-in'a dingin akipatdoh tan ahi. Chuin Pakaiyin Uriah inneipin David ahinpeh chapang chu adengin ahile, hanatnin anatan ahi.
target: After Nathan had gone home, the Lord struck the child that Uriah’s wife had borne to David, and he became ill.

source: Chuin David chapang dingchun Pakai henga ataovin; chule David'in an angolin, chuin insunga alutnin, jankhovah-in tolla alumin ahi.
target: David pleaded with God for the child. He fasted and spent the nights lying in sackcloth on the ground.

source: Chuin a-insung upaho akipat doh-un, tolla kona ama gathoudoh dingin ahenga acheuvin ahi: ahinla ama thodoh ding anompon, chule amahotoh anjong anepon ahi.
target: The elders of his household stood beside him to get him up from the ground, but he refused, and he would not eat any food with them.

source: Chuin ahitin ahi, nisagi lhinin chapang chu athitan ahi. Chule David sohte chun naosen athitai tia ama seipeh ding chu akichalheh jengun ahi. Ajehchu amahon, Veuvin, chapang chu ahin laija bon ahenga thu iseijuva ahile, aman ithuseiju anangai lou ahin: chapang chu athi tin seipeh leuhen, khohjo cheh louding ham? atiu ahi.
target: On the seventh day the child died. David’s attendants were afraid to tell him that the child was dead, for they thought, “While the child was still living, he wouldn’t listen to us when we spoke to him. How can we now tell him the child is dead? He may do something desperate.”

source: Ahin David'in asohho kihou lhih chu amu phatnin, David'in naosen chu athi ahi ahetai. Hijeh chun David'in asohte henga, Chapang chu athi hitam? ati. Chuin amahon, Ama athitai, atiuve.
target: David noticed that his attendants were whispering among themselves, and he realized the child was dead. “Is the child dead?” he asked. “Yes,” they replied, “he is dead.”

source: Hichun David tolla konin athoudoh in, akisilin, thao akinun, chuin avon akikhelin, Pakai in'a ahung lutnin, Pathen ahou tan ahi. Chuin a-in lama ahung kilen; chuin aman angaichat phatnin amahon a-angsunga an aluipeh-un ahile aman anetai.
target: Then David got up from the ground. After he had washed, put on lotions and changed his clothes, he went into the house of the Lord and worshiped. Then he went to his own house, and at his request they served him food, and he ate.

source: Chujouvin asohten ahenga, Ipibola hitia hi chona nahim? chapang chu ahinlaisen ama dingin an nangolin nakapmin, ahin chapang chu athi phatnin nathou doh-in an nanen ahi, atiuve.
target: His attendants asked him, “Why are you acting this way? While the child was alive, you fasted and wept, but now that the child is dead, you get up and eat!”

source: Chuin aman, Chapang chu ahinlaijin keiman an kangol-in, kakapmin ahi: ajehchu keiman, Pathen'in eilungsetna chapang chu hunghing maithei ahi kon ija aseithei dingham? kati ahi.
target: He answered, “While the child was still alive, I fasted and wept. I thought, ‘Who knows? The Lord may be gracious to me and let the child live.’

source: Ahinla tun ama athitai, ipidinga keiman an kangol dingham? Keiman ama kapuikit theiham? Keima amakoma kache ding ahin; ahinla ama keikoma hung kilethei louding ahitai, ati.
target: But now that he is dead, why should I go on fasting? Can I bring him back again? I will go to him, but he will not return to me.”

source: Chuin David'in a-inneipi Bathsheba chu alhamonin, chule amanu koma chun achen, aluppin ahi: chuin amanun chapa khat ahingin, amapan amin Solomon asahtai: chule Pakaiyin amachu angailun ahi.
target: Then David comforted his wife Bathsheba, and he went to her and made love to her. She gave birth to a son, and they named him Solomon. The Lord loved him;

source: Chuin aman Nathan themgaopa khutna thu athotnin ahile; aman Pakai jal-in aminchu Jedidiah asahtan ahi.
target: and because the Lord loved him, he sent word through Nathan the prophet to name him Jedidiah.

source: Chuin Joab'in Rabbah-a Ammon chate dounan gal asatnin, chuin leng khopi chu alatan ahi.
target: Meanwhile Joab fought against Rabbah of the Ammonites and captured the royal citadel.

source: Chuin Joab'in thupole ho chu David henga asolin, ahenga, Keiman Rabbah kasatnin, chule twipi khopiho chu kalatai.
target: Joab then sent messengers to David, saying, “I have fought against Rabbah and taken its water supply.

source: Hijeh chun tun mipi adang sese chu khom khomin, chule khopi douna ding chun gebuh kisonun lang, hichu laovin; achutiloule akhopi chu kalah-a kamin kalosah ding ahi, ati.
target: Now muster the rest of the troops and besiege the city and capture it. Otherwise I will take the city, and it will be named after me.”

source: Chuin David'in mipi jouse akhom khomin, Rabbah-a achetauve, chule agasatnun, hichu alataovin ahi.
target: So David mustered the entire army and went to Rabbah, and attacked and captured it.

source: Chuin aman alengpao lallukhuh chu aluchanga konin aladoh-in, hiche agih dan songmantam toh kihal sana talent khat ahin; chuin hichu David luchanga akhuh peh-un ahi. Chuin aman khopi-a thil kichomdoh tamtah ahinpon ahi.
target: David took the crown from their king’s head, and it was placed on his own head. It weighed a talent of gold, and it was set with precious stones. David took a great quantity of plunder from the city

source: Chuin aman chua um mipi ho chu ahinpui doh-in, chule amaho chu thing-at, thih loukai le thih heicha semin apansah-in, chule cheh dengin apansah-in: hitichun aman Ammon miho khopi jouse-a chun abolin ahi. Chuin David le mipi ho chu Jerusalem'a ahungkile taovin ahi.
target: and brought out the people who were there, consigning them to labor with saws and with iron picks and axes, and he made them work at brickmaking. David did this to all the Ammonite towns. Then he and his entire army returned to Jerusalem.

source: Chuin hicheho jouse nunghin ahitin ahi, David chapa Absalom chun Tamar kiti sopi nungah hoitah khat aneijin, chule David chapa Amnon chun amanu chu adeicha lheh jengin ahi.
target: In the course of time, Amnon son of David fell in love with Tamar, the beautiful sister of Absalom son of David.

source: Chule Amnon chu anaonu Tamar jehchun agenthei lheh jengin anatlo tan ahi; ajehchu amanu nungah thengsel ahin; chule Amnon'in amanu chunga thilkhat abolding chu amadingin hahsa asalheh jengin ahi.
target: Amnon became so obsessed with his sister Tamar that he made himself ill. She was a virgin, and it seemed impossible for him to do anything to her.

source: Ahin Amnon'in David sopipa Shimeah chapa Jonadab kiti gol khat aneijin: Jonadab hi mi lungthim themtah khat ahi.
target: Now Amnon had an adviser named Jonadab son of Shimeah, David’s brother. Jonadab was a very shrewd man.

source: Chuin aman ajah-a, Nangma lengpa chapa hija ipidinga ani ania nagon cheh cheh ham? neiseipeh louding ham? ati. Chuin Amnon'in, ajah-a, Keiman kasopipa Absalom naonu Tamar kadeichai, ati.
target: He asked Amnon, “Why do you, the king’s son, look so haggard morning after morning? Won’t you tell me?” Amnon said to him, “I’m in love with Tamar, my brother Absalom’s sister.”

source: Chuin Jonadab'in ajah-a, Najalkhuna luminlang kinatsah-in: chule napa nave-a ahung tengle, ajah-a, Nahenga katao ahi, kasopinu Tamar chu hunghen lang nehding eihung pehen, chule amanu khutna kona kaneh theina dingin kamitmu in nehding eihung sempeh hen, tin seijin, ati.
target: “Go to bed and pretend to be ill,” Jonadab said. “When your father comes to see you, say to him, ‘I would like my sister Tamar to come and give me something to eat. Let her prepare the food in my sight so I may watch her and then eat it from her hand.’ ”

source: Hitichun Amnon alumin, chule akinat sahtan ahi. Chuin lengpa avedinga ahung phatnin, Amnon'in lengpa henga, Nahenga katao ahi, kasopinu Tamar chu hung henlang, akhutna kona kaneh theina dingin kamitmu-a changlhah phengni eihung sempeh hen, ati.
target: So Amnon lay down and pretended to be ill. When the king came to see him, Amnon said to him, “I would like my sister Tamar to come and make some special bread in my sight, so I may eat from her hand.”

source: Hichun David'in in'a Tamar henga mi asolin, ajah-a, Nangma tun na-upa Amnon in'a chenlang, anehding an gagotpeh in, ati.
target: David sent word to Tamar at the palace: “Go to the house of your brother Amnon and prepare some food for him.”

source: Hitichun Tamar chu asopipa Amnon in'a achen ahile, ama analumin ahi. Chuin amanun changbong alan, ameh-in, amitmun changlhah phabep asemin, chuin changlhah chu akangin ahi.
target: So Tamar went to the house of her brother Amnon, who was lying down. She took some dough, kneaded it, made the bread in his sight and baked it.

source: Chuin aman khangbel khat alan, chule hicheho chu a-angsunga asunglhan; ahinla ama nehding anompon ahi. Chuin Amnon'in, Pasal jouse kakoma konin soldoh-in, ati. Chuin amaho amitakip ama koma konin achedoh taovin ahi.
target: Then she took the pan and served him the bread, but he refused to eat. “Send everyone out of here,” Amnon said. So everyone left him.

source: Chuin Amnon'in Tamar henga, Nakhutna kona kaneh thei nadingin, nehding chu indan sunga hinchoi lutnin, ati. Chuin Tamar'in achanglhah semho chu alan, hicheho chu indan sunga a-upa Amnon henga ahinchoitan ahi.
target: Then Amnon said to Tamar, “Bring the food here into my bedroom so I may eat from your hand.” And Tamar took the bread she had prepared and brought it to her brother Amnon in his bedroom.

source: Amanun hicheho chu ama nehdinga ahinchoi phatnin, aman amanu chu amanin, ahenga, Kanaonu, hungin neiluppin, ati.
target: But when she took it to him to eat, he grabbed her and said, “Come to bed with me, my sister.”

source: Chuin amanun adonbutnin, Ahipoi, he-o, pumhatnin neibol hih-in; ajehchu hitobang thil hi Israelte lah-a akibol ngaipoi: hiche ngol hoitah thil hi bolhih-in.
target: “No, my brother!” she said to him. “Don’t force me! Such a thing should not be done in Israel! Don’t do this wicked thing.

source: Chule keiman kajumna hi hoija kachepi ding ham? chule nangma jong Israel sunga mingol khat banga naum ding ahi. Hijeh chun tun, nahenga katao ahi, lengpa henga seijin, ajehchu aman nangma dingin ei-it louding ahi, ati.
target: What about me? Where could I get rid of my disgrace? And what about you? You would be like one of the wicked fools in Israel. Please speak to the king; he will not keep me from being married to you.”

source: Ahivangin aman amanu thusei chu angaipeh pon: amanu sanga hatjoh ahijeh-in, pumhatnin abolin, amanu aluppitan ahi.
target: But he refused to listen to her, and since he was stronger than she, he raped her.

source: Hiche jouchun Amnon'in amanu chu hahotnin ahotan, hitichun aman amanu ahotna chu angailutna sangin alenjotan ahi. Chuin Amnon'in amanu jah-a, Thoudoh inlang chemangtan, ati.
target: Then Amnon hated her with intense hatred. In fact, he hated her more than he had loved her. Amnon said to her, “Get up and get out!”

source: Chuin amanun ajah-a, Hichehi angai ahipoi: hitia dihlou tah-a neisol mang hi kachunga nathilbol khatjo sanga chu phaloujo ahi, ati. Ahinla aman amanu thusei chu angaipeh pon ahi.
target: “No!” she said to him. “Sending me away would be a greater wrong than what you have already done to me.” But he refused to listen to her.

source: Hichun aman ama jenlea pang asohpa chu akouvin, ajah uva, Hiche numei nuhi kakoma konin kaidoh inlang, amanu nunga kot kamun, ati.
target: He called his personal servant and said, “Get this woman out of my sight and bolt the door after her.”

source: Chule amanu chun sangkhol jatchom choma pol khat aki-ah ahi: ajehchu hitobang sangkhol chu leng chanu nungahthengho von ahi. Chujouvin asohpa chun amanu chu ahinpui doh-in, amanu nunga kotchu akamtan ahi.
target: So his servant put her out and bolted the door after her. She was wearing an ornate robe, for this was the kind of garment the virgin daughters of the king wore.

source: Chuin Tamar'in aluchunga vut akinun, chule amanun asangkhol jatchom choma polchu abotkeh-in, alujanga akhut akoijin, kap pumin achemang tan ahi.
target: Tamar put ashes on her head and tore the ornate robe she was wearing. She put her hands on her head and went away, weeping aloud as she went.

source: Chuin asopipa Absalom'in amanu jah-a, Nasopipa Amnon chun naum khompi ham? Ahinla tun, kasopinu lung mongin umin: ama nasopipa ahi; hiche thilhi lungnat nan neihih-in, ati. Hitichun Tamar chu asopipa Absalom in'a chun thomhao tah-in aumtan ahi.
target: Her brother Absalom said to her, “Has that Amnon, your brother, been with you? Be quiet for now, my sister; he is your brother. Don’t take this thing to heart.” And Tamar lived in her brother Absalom’s house, a desolate woman.

source: Ahinla David lengpan hicheho jousehi ajah phatnin, ama alunghang lheh jengin ahi.
target: When King David heard all this, he was furious.

source: Chule Absalom'in asopipa Amnon henga ase jong apha jong imacha aseipon ahi. Ahin Amon'in asopinu Tamar pumhatna abol jeh chun, Absalom'in Amnon chu ahon ahi.
target: And Absalom never said a word to Amnon, either good or bad; he hated Amnon because he had disgraced his sister Tamar.

source: Chuin kumni lhingset jouvin ahitin ahi, Absalom'in Ephraim koma um Baal-hazor mun'a kelngoimul avouvin: chule Absalom'in lengchapaho jouse chu akouvin ahi.
target: Two years later, when Absalom’s sheepshearers were at Baal Hazor near the border of Ephraim, he invited all the king’s sons to come there.

source: Chuin Absalom chu lengpa henga ahungin, Tun vetemin, nasoh hin kelngoimul kavo ding ahin; katao ahi, lengpa hu nasoh hito lhonin cheohite, ati.
target: Absalom went to the king and said, “Your servant has had shearers come. Will the king and his attendants please join me?”

source: Chuin lengpan Absalom henga, Ahipoi, kachapa, tun eiho ibonun chepou hite, achuti loule nanga dingin pohgih hikhao vinge, ati. Chuin aman amachu angeh kitnin, ahivangin ama cheding anompon, phatthei aboh jotan ahi.
target: “No, my son,” the king replied. “All of us should not go; we would only be a burden to you.” Although Absalom urged him, he still refused to go but gave him his blessing.

source: Hichun Absalom'in, Chuti ahilou dingle, nahenga katao ahi, kasopipa Amnon hi keihotoh lhonkhom hen, ati. Chuin lengpan ajah-a, Ipidinga amachu nangma toh lhonkhom dingham? ati.
target: Then Absalom said, “If not, please let my brother Amnon come with us.” The king asked him, “Why should he go with you?”

source: Ahinla Absalom'in angeh teiteijin ahile, aman Amnon le lengpa chapateho jouse chu amatoh alhonkhom sahtan ahi.
target: But Absalom urged him, so he sent with him Amnon and the rest of the king’s sons.

source: Tun Absalom'in asohho chu thu apeh-a, hitia asei ahi, Amnon lungthim chu ju-a akipasah tengleh nanghon melchih-un, chule keiman naheng uva, Amnon chu thatnun; kati tengle, amachu thatnun, kicha hih-un: keiman nangho kathupeh nahiu hilouham? hangsanun lang hatnun, ati.
target: Absalom ordered his men, “Listen! When Amnon is in high spirits from drinking wine and I say to you, ‘Strike Amnon down,’ then kill him. Don’t be afraid. Haven’t I given you this order? Be strong and brave.”

source: Chuin Absalom soh ho chun Absalom'in athupeh bangu chun Amnon chunga abol taovin ahi. Chuphatnin lengpa chapateho jouse akipat doh-un, amitakip asangan chunga atoudoh-un, ajam taovin ahi.
target: So Absalom’s men did to Amnon what Absalom had ordered. Then all the king’s sons got up, mounted their mules and fled.

source: Chuin ahitin ahi, amaho lampia achepetnun, Absalom'in lengpa chapate jouse athat gamin, amaho khatcha jong ahingdoh aumpoi, tithu David heng ahung lhungtan ahi.
target: While they were on their way, the report came to David: “Absalom has struck down all the king’s sons; not one of them is left.”

source: Hichun lengpa akipat doh-in, aponsil abotkeh-in, tolla alumin; chule asohte jousenjong aponsilu abotkeh-un akoma adingun ahi.
target: The king stood up, tore his clothes and lay down on the ground; and all his attendants stood by with their clothes torn.

source: Chuin David sopipa Shimeah chapa Jonadab'in adonbutnin, Ka pakai amahon lengpa chapate khangthah jouse atha sohkeijin ngaito hih-in, ajehchu Amnon sehseh bou athin ahi. Ajehchu aman asopinu Tamar pumhatna anabol ni-a patna, Absalom thupeh dungjuija hichehi hung kigong pana ahitai.
target: But Jonadab son of Shimeah, David’s brother, said, “My lord should not think that they killed all the princes; only Amnon is dead. This has been Absalom’s express intention ever since the day Amnon raped his sister Tamar.

source: Hijeh chun tun ka pakai lengpan lengchapate jouse thia ahi tin nalungin ngaito hih-in: ajehchu Amnon sehseh bou thi ahi, ati.
target: My lord the king should not be concerned about the report that all the king’s sons are dead. Only Amnon is dead.”

source: Hichun Absalom ajamtan ahi. Chuin gollhang khongah-a pangpa chu akhoda-a, avetna ahile, veuvin, anunglam molpang lampia chu mitamtah ahung amun ahi.
target: Meanwhile, Absalom had fled. Now the man standing watch looked up and saw many people on the road west of him, coming down the side of the hill. The watchman went and told the king, “I see men in the direction of Horonaim, on the side of the hill.”

source: Chuin Jonadab'in lengpa henga, Ven, Lengpa chapate ahunguve: nasoh-in asei bangbang chu ahi, ati.
target: Jonadab said to the king, “See, the king’s sons have come; it has happened just as your servant said.”

source: Chuin ahitin ahi, aman thu asei joujou chun, veuvin, lengpa chapate ahung lhungun, chuin awsang tah-in akapmun ahi: chule lengpa le asohte jong hakan akap taovin ahi.
target: As he finished speaking, the king’s sons came in, wailing loudly. The king, too, and all his attendants wept very bitterly.

source: Ahinla Absalom chu ajam mangin, Geshur lengpa Ammihud chapa Talmai henga achetan ahi. Chuin David chu achapa jeh-in niseh-in alunghemin ahi.
target: Absalom fled and went to Talmai son of Ammihud, the king of Geshur. But King David mourned many days for his son.

source: Hitichun Absalom ajamin, Geshur'a achen, chua chun kumthum aumin ahi.
target: After Absalom fled and went to Geshur, he stayed there three years.

source: Chule David lengpa hinna chu Absalom henga achenom lheh jengin ahi. Ajehchu ama Amnon thi chung changa ana lungmonga ahitai.
target: And King David longed to go to Absalom, for he was consoled concerning Amnon’s death.

source: Tun Zeruiah chapa Joab'in lengpa lungthim chu Absalom heng lama aume ti ahetan ahi.
target: Joab son of Zeruiah knew that the king’s heart longed for Absalom.

source: Chuin Joab'in Tekoah'a mi asolin, chuche-a um numei chingtah khat agapuisah-in, amanu henga chun, Nahenga katao ahi, alunghem khat bangin uminlang lunghemna von kivonin, chule thao jong kinu hih-in, ahin phatsottah thi-op numei khat bangin umin.
target: So Joab sent someone to Tekoa and had a wise woman brought from there. He said to her, “Pretend you are in mourning. Dress in mourning clothes, and don’t use any cosmetic lotions. Act like a woman who has spent many days grieving for the dead.

source: Chutengle lengpa henga hungin lang, ahenga hitobanghin seijin, ati. Hitichun Joab'in amanu kamsunga aseiding thuho chu akoipehtan ahi.
target: Then go to the king and speak these words to him.” And Joab put the words in her mouth.

source: Chuin Tekoah numei nun lengpa henga thu aseichun, amai tolla asulutnin, jana apen, lengpa henga, Vo lengpa, neikithopin, ati.
target: When the woman from Tekoa went to the king, she fell with her face to the ground to pay him honor, and she said, “Help me, Your Majesty!”

source: Chuin lengpan amanu jah-a, Ipin nasuh genthei ham? ati. Chuin amanun adonbutnin, Tahbeh-in keima meithai kahin, ka-inneipu chu thia ahitai.
target: The king asked her, “What is troubling you?” She said, “I am a widow; my husband is dead.

source: Chule nasohnu hin chapa ni aneijin, chuin amani gamlah-a akidel lhonin, koimacha aphel khending aumpon, khatpan khatjopa chu avon, athattan ahi.
target: I your servant had two sons. They got into a fight with each other in the field, and no one was there to separate them. One struck the other and killed him.

source: Chule, ven, insung pumpihi nasohnu doudin akipatdoh taovin, chule amahon, Asopipa thatpa chu asopipa athajeh-a katha theina diuvin neipedoh un; chule agou lodingpa jongchu kasuh mangdiu ahi, atiuve. Chule chutia chu akidalha-a kamei-am chu asuhmitnuva, kapasal chu min neilou le, leichunga chilhah himhim neilouva akoi dingu ahi, ati.
target: Now the whole clan has risen up against your servant; they say, ‘Hand over the one who struck his brother down, so that we may put him to death for the life of his brother whom he killed; then we will get rid of the heir as well.’ They would put out the only burning coal I have left, leaving my husband neither name nor descendant on the face of the earth.”

source: Chuin lengpan numeinu jah-a, Na-in lama chetan, keiman nangma chung chang thu hinhetsah nange, ati.
target: The king said to the woman, “Go home, and I will issue an order in your behalf.”
