source: Chuin Tekoah numeinu chun lengpa henga, Ka pakai, O lengpa, hiche khangitlouna chu keimale kapa insunga chuhen: chule lengpa le alaltouna vang themonabei hihen, ati.
target: But the woman from Tekoa said to him, “Let my lord the king pardon me and my family, and let the king and his throne be without guilt.”

source: Chuin lengpan aseijin, koi hijongle nahenga ikhat seija aumle, amachu kahenga hinpuijin, chule aman avela natohkhah kit louding ahitai, ati.
target: The king replied, “If anyone says anything to you, bring them to me, and they will not bother you again.”

source: Hichun amanun, Nahenga katao ahi, lengpan Pakai na Pathen hejingin lang, thisan phulapan asuhmangbe louna dingin phalna pehih-in; achuti loule kachapa sumang getnunte, ati. Chuin aman, Hingjing Pakai mina kasei ahi, nachapa samjang khatcha jong tolla lhalou ding ahi, ati.
target: She said, “Then let the king invoke the Lord his God to prevent the avenger of blood from adding to the destruction, so that my son will not be destroyed.” “As surely as the Lord lives,” he said, “not one hair of your son’s head will fall to the ground.”

source: Hitichun amanun, Ka pakai ka-lengpa jah-a nasoh in thukhat seijinge, ati. Chuin aman, Seijin, ati.
target: Then the woman said, “Let your servant speak a word to my lord the king.” “Speak,” he replied.

source: Chuin numeinu chun, Chuti ahile ipidinga nangman Pathen mite douna hitobang thil chu nagelham? ajehchu lengpan anomangpa chu in'a apuilut kitloujeh-a, lengpan hichehi themona nei khat thusei banga nasei ahi.
target: The woman said, “Why then have you devised a thing like this against the people of God? When the king says this, does he not convict himself, for the king has not brought back his banished son?

source: Ajehchu eiho ithi teitei dingu ahin, tolla twi kisunglha kithaldoh kit theilou tobang ihi dingu ahi. Ahijeng vangin Pathen'in hinkho alamang pon; amavang aman anodoh hochu ama-a kona akipaimang lou nadingun lampi asemin ahi.
target: Like water spilled on the ground, which cannot be recovered, so we must die. But that is not what God desires; rather, he devises ways so that a banished person does not remain banished from him.

source: Hijeh-a chu, tu-a mipihon eikichatsah jeh uva, keima hiche seidinga hi ka pakai lengpa henga hunga kahi. Chule nasohnu hin, Ijemtia lengpan asohnu taona hi asanpeh khatle, tun lengpa koma thu gaseijinge.
target: “And now I have come to say this to my lord the king because the people have made me afraid. Your servant thought, ‘I will speak to the king; perhaps he will grant his servant’s request.

source: Ajehchu lengpan eingaipeh intin, asohnu hi Pathen gouloa kona keima le kachapa suhmang dingpa khutna konin eilhatdoh inte, kati ahi.
target: Perhaps the king will agree to deliver his servant from the hand of the man who is trying to cut off both me and my son from God’s inheritance.’

source: Chule nasohnun, Tu-a hi ka pakai lengpa thusei chu lhamona hiding ahi: ajehchu ka pakai leng hi aphale ase sepkhen na-a Pathen vantil tobang hija ahi. Hijeh chun na Pakai na Pathen'in naumpi hen, ati.
target: “And now your servant says, ‘May the word of my lord the king secure my inheritance, for my lord the king is like an angel of God in discerning good and evil. May the Lord your God be with you.’ ”

source: Chuphatnin lengpan numeinu chu adonbutnin; Nahenga katao ahi, keiman nangma kadoh dingho hi im hih-in, ati. Chuin amanun, Tun ka pakai lengpan seijin, ati.
target: Then the king said to the woman, “Don’t keep from me the answer to what I am going to ask you.” “Let my lord the king speak,” the woman said.

source: Chuin lengpan, Hicheng jousehi Joab to kikhut jopna naneijam? ati. Chuin numei nun adonbutnin, Ka pakai lengpa hinna pana kasei ahi, ka pakai lengpan nathuseidoh hohi koimachan jetlam ahiloule veilama aheikon theilou ahi. Ajehchu nasoh Joab'in eisola, hiche thuho jousehi nasohnu kama akoi ahi.
target: The king asked, “Isn’t the hand of Joab with you in all this?” The woman answered, “As surely as you live, my lord the king, no one can turn to the right or to the left from anything my lord the king says. Yes, it was your servant Joab who instructed me to do this and who put all these words into the mouth of your servant.

source: Kivaihom danho akikhel nadinga nasoh Joab'in hichehi abol ahi; Pakai vantil chihna bangin, leiset thil umjouse hetna dingin, ka pakai hi achingin ahi, ati.
target: Your servant Joab did this to change the present situation. My lord has wisdom like that of an angel of God—he knows everything that happens in the land.”

source: Chuin lengpan Joab henga, Ven, tun hichehi kaboltan ahi: hijeh chun chenlang, gollhang Absalom chu gapuijin, ati.
target: The king said to Joab, “Very well, I will do it. Go, bring back the young man Absalom.”

source: Chuin Joab aboh khupmin, tolla amai asulutnin, lengpa henga kipathu aseije: chule Joab'in, Tuni hin ka pakai vo lengpa, lengpan asohpa ngaichat asuh bulhitna konhin, nasoh keima namitmun lungsetna kachange ti kahetan ahi, ati.
target: Joab fell with his face to the ground to pay him honor, and he blessed the king. Joab said, “Today your servant knows that he has found favor in your eyes, my lord the king, because the king has granted his servant’s request.”

source: Hitichun Joab akipatdoh-in, Geshur'a achen, Absalom chu Jerusalem'a ahin puitan ahi.
target: Then Joab went to Geshur and brought Absalom back to Jerusalem.

source: Chuin lengpan, A-in lama kihei henglang, kamai muda hen, ati. Hitichun Absalom chu a-in lama akile heijin, lengpa mai chu amutapon ahi.
target: But the king said, “He must go to his own house; he must not see my face.” So Absalom went to his own house and did not see the face of the king.

source: Ahinla Israelte lah-a chun Absalom banga amel hoina pachat ding koimacha aumtapon ahi. Akengtoa pat aluchanga lallukhuh geijin ama achun nolna aumpon ahi.
target: In all Israel there was not a man so highly praised for his handsome appearance as Absalom. From the top of his head to the sole of his foot there was no blemish in him.

source: Chule aman asam avolhah tengle (ajehchu kumlhun sehle avolhahji ahi: ajehchu achunga asam chu agihjin, hijeh-a chu avolhahji ahi:) asam chu atejin, lengpa thiltena dungjuijin shekel jani aphajin ahi.
target: Whenever he cut the hair of his head—he used to cut his hair once a year because it became too heavy for him—he would weigh it, and its weight was two hundred shekels by the royal standard.

source: Chule Absalom'a dingin chapa thumle, chanu khat apengin, achanu min chu Tamar ahi. Amanu chu numei melhoi tah ahi.
target: Three sons and a daughter were born to Absalom. His daughter’s name was Tamar, and she became a beautiful woman.

source: Hitichun Absalom chu kumni lhingset Jerusalam'a achengin, ahinla lengpa mai amupon ahi.
target: Absalom lived two years in Jerusalem without seeing the king’s face.

source: Hijeh chun Absalom'in lengpa henga soldingin Joab agakou sah-in; ahinla ama amahenga ahungpon ahi. Chuin aman aniveinan akouding asolkitnin, ahung dehpon ahi.
target: Then Absalom sent for Joab in order to send him to the king, but Joab refused to come to him. So he sent a second time, but he refused to come.

source: Hijeh chun aman asohte henga, Veuvin, Joab lou khu kei lou komcha-a um ahin, chule aman hilaija chun sakol chang aneijin ahi; cheovinlang meija gahalun, ati. Chuin Absalom sohte chun louchu meijin ahaltaovin ahi.
target: Then he said to his servants, “Look, Joab’s field is next to mine, and he has barley there. Go and set it on fire.” So Absalom’s servants set the field on fire.

source: Chuin Joab akipatdoh-in, Absalom henga a-in'a chun ahungin, ajah-a, Ipidinga nasohten kalou chu meija ahalu ham? ati.
target: Then Joab did go to Absalom’s house, and he said to him, “Why have your servants set my field on fire?”

source: Chuin Absalom'in Joab chu adonbutnin, Ven, lengpa henga, Ipidinga keima Geshur'a kona hunga kahim? tuchan hin chukoma umleng keija dinga phajo ahi: tia seidinga kasol theina dinga hikoma hungin tia nangma kou dinga mi kahinsol ahi; hijeh chun tun lengpa maicha neimusah-un, chule kachunga khangit louna auma ahile, aman eithat jenghen, ati.
target: Absalom said to Joab, “Look, I sent word to you and said, ‘Come here so I can send you to the king to ask, “Why have I come from Geshur? It would be better for me if I were still there!” ’ Now then, I want to see the king’s face, and if I am guilty of anything, let him put me to death.”

source: Hijeh chun Joab lengpa henga ahungin, ahenga aseitai. Chuin aman Absalom akou phatnin, ama lengpa henga ahungin, lengpa angsunga tolla aboh khupmin: chuin lengpan Absalom chu achoptan ahi.
target: So Joab went to the king and told him this. Then the king summoned Absalom, and he came in and bowed down with his face to the ground before the king. And the king kissed Absalom.

source: Chuin hiche jouchun ahitin ahi, Absalom'in ama dingin sakol kangtalai ho le sakol ho, chule amasanga lhaiding mi somnga akigot tan ahi.
target: In the course of time, Absalom provided himself with a chariot and horses and with fifty men to run ahead of him.

source: Chule Absalom matah-in athoudoh jin, kotpi phungkom lampia chun anadingjin ahi: chule ahitin ahi, mi khattouvin boina aneija, lengpa henga athu tansah dinga ahung teng, Absalom'in ama chu aheng lama akoulutjin, chule ahenga chun, Hoikom khopi-a kon nahim? atijin, chule amachun, Nasohhi Israel phungho lah-a hiche phung chu kahi, atijin ahi.
target: He would get up early and stand by the side of the road leading to the city gate. Whenever anyone came with a complaint to be placed before the king for a decision, Absalom would call out to him, “What town are you from?” He would answer, “Your servant is from one of the tribes of Israel.”

source: Chuteng Absalom'in ajah-a chun, Ven, nathuho hi aphan adih-e; ahinla nathu ngailha dinga mopohna apeh koima aumpoi, atijin ahi.
target: Then Absalom would say to him, “Look, your claims are valid and proper, but there is no representative of the king to hear you.”

source: Hicheng tilou jongchun Absalom'in, Kaden keima gamsunga thutan dinga eikisem hitavele, chutile kiheh nading ahiloule boina neijouse kahenga hunguntin, chuteng keiman amaho them anachan ji tadinga! tin aseibejin ahi.
target: And Absalom would add, “If only I were appointed judge in the land! Then everyone who has a complaint or case could come to me and I would see that they receive justice.”

source: Chule ahitijin ahi, mi khattou chibai boh dinga akom anai tengleh, aman akhut alhangdoh jin, amapa chu atuh-in, achopjin ahi.
target: Also, whenever anyone approached him to bow down before him, Absalom would reach out his hand, take hold of him and kiss him.

source: Hitobanghin Absalom'in lengpa henga athu tansah dinga hunga Israelte jouse chu anabolsoh keijin ahi. Hitichun Absalom'in Israel miho lungthim chu agumang sohtan ahi.
target: Absalom behaved in this way toward all the Israelites who came to the king asking for justice, and so he stole the hearts of the people of Israel.

source: Chuin kum somli jouvin ahitin ahi, Absalom'in lengpa henga, Nahenga katao ahi, Pakai henga kitepnaho gasubulhit dingin Hebron'a neisolin.
target: At the end of four years, Absalom said to the king, “Let me go to Hebron and fulfill a vow I made to the Lord .

source: Ajehchu Syria gam Geshur'a kana umlaijin nasohhin kitepna khat kana neijin, Pakaiyin Jerusalem'a eipuilut kitna ahile, Pakai kajen ding ahi, tia kanasei ahi, ati.
target: While your servant was living at Geshur in Aram, I made this vow: ‘If the Lord takes me back to Jerusalem, I will worship the Lord in Hebron.’ ”

source: Chuin lengpan ajah-a, Lung mongin chen, ati. Hitichun ama akipatdoh-in, Hebron'a achetai.
target: The king said to him, “Go in peace.” So he went to Hebron.

source: Ahinla Absalom'in Israel phungho jouse lah-a guhthimin mi asolin, ajah uva, Nanghon sumkon gin najah jah tengule, Absalom'in Hebron'a vai ahomtai, nati dingu ahi, ati.
target: Then Absalom sent secret messengers throughout the tribes of Israel to say, “As soon as you hear the sound of the trumpets, then say, ‘Absalom is king in Hebron.’ ”

source: Chuin Jerusalem'a kona kikoudoh mi jani chu Absalom toh alhonun; amaho imacha gellouva cheu ahin, imacha ahet louvu ahi.
target: Two hundred men from Jerusalem had accompanied Absalom. They had been invited as guests and went quite innocently, knowing nothing about the matter.

source: Chuin Absalom'in David dinga thumopma pang Gilon mi Ahithophel chu ama khopi Gilon'a ganlhaina thilto abol laitah-in agakou sah-in ahi. Chule galguh chu ahatlheh jengin ahi; ajehchu Absalom dingin mi atamcheh cheh jengtan ahi.
target: While Absalom was offering sacrifices, he also sent for Ahithophel the Gilonite, David’s counselor, to come from Giloh, his hometown. And so the conspiracy gained strength, and Absalom’s following kept on increasing.

source: Chuin David henga thupole khat ahungin, Israelte jouse lungthim chu Absalom lamma akaitaove, ati.
target: A messenger came and told David, “The hearts of the people of Israel are with Absalom.”

source: Chuin Davidn'in Jerusalem'a amato umkhom asohte jouse henga, Kipatdoh-un, jamtaohite; ajehchu eiho Absalom'a kona ihoidoh loudiu ahi. Potdoh dingin mangang un, achutiloule aman hetman louvin eihin delkhum diu, chule eiho chunga thilphalou ahin lhutna, khopi hi chemjam'a asat ding ahi, ati.
target: Then David said to all his officials who were with him in Jerusalem, “Come! We must flee, or none of us will escape from Absalom. We must leave immediately, or he will move quickly to overtake us and bring ruin on us and put the city to the sword.”

source: Chuin lengpa soh ho chun lengpa henga, Ven, nasohte hi ipihile ka pakai lengpan boldinga eithupeh chanu boldinga kigosa dema um kahiuve, atiuve.
target: The king’s officials answered him, “Your servants are ready to do whatever our lord the king chooses.”

source: Chuin lengpa apotdoh-in, chule a-insung miho jouse chun anung ajuijun ahi. Chuin lengpan inngah dingin athaikem numei som adalhan ahi.
target: The king set out, with his entire household following him; but he left ten concubines to take care of the palace.

source: Chule lengpa apotdoh-in, mipi jousen anung ajuijun, mun gamlatah khatna aumtaovin ahi.
target: So the king set out, with all the people following him, and they halted at the edge of the city.

source: Chuin asohho jouse chu amato akilhonun, chule Gath'a kona anung hinjui Cherth mite, Palet mite, chule Git mite mi jagup chu lengpa masanga acheuvin ahi.
target: All his men marched past him, along with all the Kerethites and Pelethites; and all the six hundred Gittites who had accompanied him from Gath marched before the king.

source: Chuin lengpan Gitmi Ittai jah-a, Ipidinga nangjong keihohitoh nalhon ham? Naumna lama kile kitnin lang, lengpa toh gaum khomin. Ajehchu nangma gamchommi nahin, chule nagam sunga kona kinodoh jong nahi.
target: The king said to Ittai the Gittite, “Why should you come along with us? Go back and stay with King Absalom. You are a foreigner, an exile from your homeland.

source: Chule nangma janhi vela bou hung nahin, tunia keima kachena thei thei na-a che ding kahin, iti nangma keiho toh lhonna kachesuh kachetou sah ding ham? nangma kilekittan, chule nasopi ho hi kipuijin: hepina le thutah-in naumpi jinghen, ati.
target: You came only yesterday. And today shall I make you wander about with us, when I do not know where I am going? Go back, and take your people with you. May the Lord show you kindness and faithfulness.”

source: Chuin Ittai'in lengpa adonbutnin, ajah-a, Hingjing Pakai min le ka pakai lengpa min pana kasei ahi, thonlouva hoikom mun hijongle ka pakai lengpa umna-a chu thina hihen, hinna hile, hichelai mun ngeija chu nasoh hi kaumding ahi, ati.
target: But Ittai replied to the king, “As surely as the Lord lives, and as my lord the king lives, wherever my lord the king may be, whether it means life or death, there will your servant be.”

source: Chuin David'in Ittai jah-a, Chenlang galkaitan, ati. Chuin Git mi Ittai chu amite jousele aumkhompi chapang neoho jouse chutoh agalkai taovin ahi.
target: David said to Ittai, “Go ahead, march on.” So Ittai the Gittite marched on with all his men and the families that were with him.

source: Chuin gam pumpi chu awsang tah-in akapmun, chule mipihochu agalkai taovin ahi. Chule lengpa amatah jong Kedron vachadung chu agalkaijin, chuin miho jouse chu gamthip jotna lampi langa chun agalkai taovin ahi.
target: The whole countryside wept aloud as all the people passed by. The king also crossed the Kidron Valley, and all the people moved on toward the wilderness.

source: Chule veuvin, Zadok le ama koma um Levi hon jong Pathen kitepna thingkhong apouvin ahi. Chuin amahon Pathen kitepna thingkhong chu angaovin; chule mipi ho jouse khopi-a kona apotdoh kahseuvin Abiathar chu achetouvin ahi.
target: Zadok was there, too, and all the Levites who were with him were carrying the ark of the covenant of God. They set down the ark of God, and Abiathar offered sacrifices until all the people had finished leaving the city.

source: Chuin lengpan Zadok hengah, Pathen thingkhong chu khopi-a nungpoh kitnin: ijemtia Pakai mitmu-a lungsetna kachana ahile, aman eihin lepui kitna, anai-a hiche hile aumna mun chu eimusah kitding ahi.
target: Then the king said to Zadok, “Take the ark of God back into the city. If I find favor in the Lord ’s eyes, he will bring me back and let me see it and his dwelling place again.

source: Ahinla aman, Nachunga lunglhaina kaneipoi atia ahile; ven, hikoma kaume, aman kachunga pha asah bangbang chun bolhen, ati.
target: But if he says, ‘I am not pleased with you,’ then I am ready; let him do to me whatever seems good to him.”

source: Chuin lengpan Zadok thempupa henga, Nangma mitvah nei nahi louham? Nangma to umkhom nachapateni, nachapa Ahimaaz le Abiathar chapa Jonathan toh lung mongin khopi sunga kiletaovin.
target: The king also said to Zadok the priest, “Do you understand? Go back to the city with my blessing. Take your son Ahimaaz with you, and also Abiathar’s son Jonathan. You and Abiathar return with your two sons.

source: Ven nangma-a kona thu ahung kahse-a keiman gamthip phaichama kaum ding ahi, ati.
target: I will wait at the fords in the wilderness until word comes from you to inform me.”

source: Hijeh chun Zadok le Abiathar chun Pathen thingkhong chu Jerusalem'a apokit lhonnin; chule hikoma chun amani aum lhontan ahi.
target: So Zadok and Abiathar took the ark of God back to Jerusalem and stayed there.

source: Chuin David chu olive molsang kaltouna-a chun achetouvin, chule akap pum pumin achetouvin, alu akhu khumin, akeng keuvin lam ajotnin ahi: chule akoma um mipi jouse amitakipmin alu akhu khumun, kap pumin achetouvun ahi.
target: But David continued up the Mount of Olives, weeping as he went; his head was covered and he was barefoot. All the people with him covered their heads too and were weeping as they went up.

source: Chuin mikhatnin David jah-a, Ahithophel chu Absalom galguh bolho lah-a ajaove, tin aseipeh-in ahi. Chuin David'in, Vo Pakai, nahenga katao ahi, Ahithophel thumopna chu ngolnan heidoh peh-in, ati.
target: Now David had been told, “Ahithophel is among the conspirators with Absalom.” So David prayed, “ Lord , turn Ahithophel’s counsel into foolishness.”

source: Chuin ahitin ahi, David a-Pathen houna mun molchung ahunglhun phatnin, veuvin, Arch mi Hushai chu sangkhol chol kibotkeh le aluchanga leiset nat pumin ama kimupi ding chun ahungin ahi.
target: When David arrived at the summit, where people used to worship God, Hushai the Arkite was there to meet him, his robe torn and dust on his head.

source: David'in ama henga, Nangma keima toh lhon lehen, keima dinga pohgih nahi ding ahi:
target: David said to him, “If you go with me, you will be a burden to me.

source: Ahinla nangma khopi-a nakile-a, Absalom henga, Vo lengpa, keima nasoh hinge; hichan geija napa soh-a kana um bangin, tunjong nangma soh hingkate, tia nagaseija ahile: nangman keima dingin Ahithophel thumop chu neijopeh ding ahi.
target: But if you return to the city and say to Absalom, ‘Your Majesty, I will be your servant; I was your father’s servant in the past, but now I will be your servant,’ then you can help me by frustrating Ahithophel’s advice.

source: Chule nangman nangma to pangkhom dinga Zadok le Abiathar thempu teni nanei hilouham? Hijeh-a chu hitiding ahi, Ipi hile nangman lengpa in'a kona najah chanchu, Zadok le Abiathar thempupa naseipeh ding ahi.
target: Won’t the priests Zadok and Abiathar be there with you? Tell them anything you hear in the king’s palace.

source: Ven, hikoma chun amani chutoh achapateniu Zadok chapa Ahimaaz le Abiathar chapa Jonathan aumlhone; chule nangman najah takip chu amani-a kona kakoma nahin thotding ahi, ati.
target: Their two sons, Ahimaaz son of Zadok and Jonathan son of Abiathar, are there with them. Send them to me with anything you hear.”

source: Hitichun David lengpa golpa Hushai chu khopi sunga ahungin, chule Absalom chu Jerusalem'a ahunglut tan ahi.
target: So Hushai, David’s confidant, arrived at Jerusalem as Absalom was entering the city.

source: Chuin David'in molsang chungvum phabep akhel nungin, veuvin, Mephibosheth sohpa Ziba'in sangan ni apho pumle achunga chanlhah pheng jani, lengpithei gop boh jakhat, chule nipilai theiga jat jakhat, chule ju haikhat toh ana kimupin ahi.
target: When David had gone a short distance beyond the summit, there was Ziba, the steward of Mephibosheth, waiting to meet him. He had a string of donkeys saddled and loaded with two hundred loaves of bread, a hundred cakes of raisins, a hundred cakes of figs and a skin of wine.

source: Chuin lengpan Ziba jah-a, Hiche nabolhi ipi vetsahna ham? ati. Chuin Ziba'n, Sanganho hi lengpa insung mite touna ding ahin, chule changlhah leh nipilai theigahohi gollhangho nehding ahin, chule juhi gamthipma lhasamho donding ahi, ati.
target: The king asked Ziba, “Why have you brought these?” Ziba answered, “The donkeys are for the king’s household to ride on, the bread and fruit are for the men to eat, and the wine is to refresh those who become exhausted in the wilderness.”

source: Chuin lengpan, Chuti ahile, napakai pa chapa lah-em? ati. Chuin Ziba'n lengpa henga, Ven, ama Jerusalem'a aume: ijeh inem itile aman, Tunia Israel insungin kapa lenggam eilosah dingu ahi, ati.
target: The king then asked, “Where is your master’s grandson?” Ziba said to him, “He is staying in Jerusalem, because he thinks, ‘Today the Israelites will restore to me my grandfather’s kingdom.’ ”

source: Hiche phatchun lengpan Ziba henga, Ven, Mephibosheth nei jouse chu nangma-a ahitai, ati. Chuin Ziba'n, namitmu-a lungsetna kachan theina dinga, ka pakai, vo lengpa, nahenga katao ahi, ati.
target: Then the king said to Ziba, “All that belonged to Mephibosheth is now yours.” “I humbly bow,” Ziba said. “May I find favor in your eyes, my lord the king.”

source: Chuin David lengpa Bahurima ahung phatnin, veuvin, chua konchun Gera chapa Shimei kiti Saul insungmi khat ahungdoh-in ahi. Ama ahung potdoh-in, alamjot toh gaosap ahin koppeh-in ahi.
target: As King David approached Bahurim, a man from the same clan as Saul’s family came out from there. His name was Shimei son of Gera, and he cursed as he came out.

source: Chuin aman David le, David lengpa sohte jouse chu songin ahin sepmin: chule miho jousele mihat ho jouse jet le veija aumun ahi.
target: He pelted David and all the king’s officials with stones, though all the troops and the special guard were on David’s right and left.

source: Chule Shimei'in agaosap laijin hitin aseijin ahi, Hung doh-in, hung doh-in, nangma thisan sopa le Belial mipa :
target: As he cursed, Shimei said, “Get out, get out, you murderer, you scoundrel!

source: Akhela navaihom, Saul le a-insung pumpi thisan chu Pakaiyin nachunga ahinle lhunsah ahin; chule Pakaiyin lenggam chu nachapa Absalom khutna apehdoh ahitai: chule ven, nangma thisanso hat nahi jeh-a, nathemmona chu nachunga chua ahitai, ati.
target: The Lord has repaid you for all the blood you shed in the household of Saul, in whose place you have reigned. The Lord has given the kingdom into the hands of your son Absalom. You have come to ruin because you are a murderer!”

source: Chuphatnin Zeruiah chapa Abishai'in lengpa henga, Ipidinga hiche uicha thisa hin ka pakai lengpa hi agaosap ham? nahenga katao ahi, galkaijing ting, alu galange, ati.
target: Then Abishai son of Zeruiah said to the king, “Why should this dead dog curse my lord the king? Let me go over and cut off his head.”

source: Chuin lengpan, Nangho Zeruiah chapate, nangho le kei ikibahnao ipi umam? Eigaosap hen, ajehchu Pakaiyin ahenga, David khu gaosapmin, ati ahi. Chuti ahile, Ipidinga nangin hiti ahi nabol ham? tia aseidinga chu koiham? ati.
target: But the king said, “What does this have to do with you, you sons of Zeruiah? If he is cursing because the Lord said to him, ‘Curse David,’ who can ask, ‘Why do you do this?’ ”

source: Chuin David'in Abishai le asohte jouse henga, veuvin, ka-oisunga kona hungdoh kachapa jengin kahinna lahdinga ahola ahile; tu-a hi hiche Benjamin miten ichan geija ahol dingu ham? Limsah hih-un, agaosap nom chanin gaosaphen; ajehchu Pakaiyin asol ahi.
target: David then said to Abishai and all his officials, “My son, my own flesh and blood, is trying to kill me. How much more, then, this Benjamite! Leave him alone; let him curse, for the Lord has told him to.

source: Chuti henlang hile Pakaiyin kagen theina hinve intin, tunia aman eisapset nahi Pakaiyin aphalama eilethuhpeh ding ahi, ati.
target: It may be that the Lord will look upon my misery and restore to me his covenant blessing instead of his curse today.”

source: Chule David le amiho chu lampia ache laijun, Shimei chu molpanga chun ama dontah-a achen, achepum chun agaosapmin, chule songin asepmin leivui athekhumin ahi.
target: So David and his men continued along the road while Shimei was going along the hillside opposite him, cursing as he went and throwing stones at him and showering him with dirt.

source: Chuin lengpa le aumkhompi mihochun alel taovin; hijeh chun amaho hia chun akicholdo taove.
target: The king and all the people with him arrived at their destination exhausted. And there he refreshed himself.

source: Chuin Absalom le Israel mite jouse chu Jerusalem'a ahungun, chule ama Ahithophel toh ahi.
target: Meanwhile, Absalom and all the men of Israel came to Jerusalem, and Ahithophel was with him.

source: Chuin ahitin ahi, David golpa Arch mi Hushai chu Absalom henga ahung phatnin, Hushai'in Absalom henga, Pathen'in lengpa huhhing hen, Pathen'in lengpa huhhing hen, ati.
target: Then Hushai the Arkite, David’s confidant, went to Absalom and said to him, “Long live the king! Long live the king!”

source: Chuin Absalom'in Hushai henga, Hichehi nagolpa nahepina ham? ipidinga nagolpatoh lhonlou nahim? ati.
target: Absalom said to Hushai, “So this is the love you show your friend? If he’s your friend, why didn’t you go with him?”

source: Chuin Hushai'in Absalom henga, Ahipoi, Pakai le hiche mite, chule Israel mipi ho jousen alhen paova chu kahi ding, chule keima ama toh kaumding ahi.
target: Hushai said to Absalom, “No, the one chosen by the Lord , by these people, and by all the men of Israel—his I will be, and I will remain with him.

source: Chujongle, keiman koi kajen dingham? Achapa chu kajen ding hilouham? Napa kajen banga chu nangma kajending ahi, ati.
target: Furthermore, whom should I serve? Should I not serve the son? Just as I served your father, so I will serve you.”

source: Chuphat chun Absalom'in Ahithophel henga, Ipi kabol dinguham neithumop uvin, ati.
target: Absalom said to Ahithophel, “Give us your advice. What should we do?”

source: Chuin Ahithophel'in Absalom henga, Napan inngah dinga akoi athaikemho henga chun chen; chule Israel mipi ho jousen nangma napa-a dinga kidah umtah nahichu ajahdiu: chutengle nangma toh umho jouse khuttha chu hatdoh ding ahi, ati.
target: Ahithophel answered, “Sleep with your father’s concubines whom he left to take care of the palace. Then all Israel will hear that you have made yourself obnoxious to your father, and the hands of everyone with you will be more resolute.”

source: Hitichun amahon Absalom dingin in chunga chun pon inkhat asongun, chuin Absalom chu Israel miho jouse mitmun apa thaikem ho henga aluttan ahi.
target: So they pitched a tent for Absalom on the roof, and he slept with his father’s concubines in the sight of all Israel.

source: Chule Ahithophel thumop, hiche nikho laija Ahithophel anathumopho chu, mikhatnin Pathen athudop banga ana gelu ahi. David le Absalom dinga jong Ahithophel thumop ho jouse chu hitobang chu anahija ahi.
target: Now in those days the advice Ahithophel gave was like that of one who inquires of God. That was how both David and Absalom regarded all of Ahithophel’s advice.

source: Hicheng tilou chun Ahithophel'in Absalom henga, Tun keima mi sangsom le sangni lhendoh ingting, tujan mama hin kipatdoh ingting, David ganungdel inge:
target: Ahithophel said to Absalom, “I would choose twelve thousand men and set out tonight in pursuit of David.

source: Chule ama athachola akhuttha alhompet tahle achunga kachuh ding, kasuh kichat ding: chutengle aumpi miho jouse chu jam mang untin, keiman lengpa bouchu katha ding ahi.
target: I would attack him while he is weary and weak. I would strike him with terror, and then all the people with him will flee. I would strike down only the king

source: Chule mipi jouse chu nahenga kahin lepuiding ahi. Nangman naholpa tailou adang jouse ahung kilekit teng, mijouse chu lung mong diu ahi, ati.
target: and bring all the people back to you. The death of the man you seek will mean the return of all; all the people will be unharmed.”

source: Chule akisei chun Absalom le Israel upaho jouse chu alunglhaisah lheh-in ahi.
target: This plan seemed good to Absalom and to all the elders of Israel.

source: Chujouvin Absalom'in, Tun Arch mipa Hushai jongchu kouvun, chule eihon ama thusei jongchu ngaiju hite, ati.
target: But Absalom said, “Summon also Hushai the Arkite, so we can hear what he has to say as well.”

source: Chuin Hushai chu Absalom henga ahung phatchun, Absalom'in akihoupin, Ahithophel'in hitihin aseije: aman asei bangahi iboldiu ham? Ahilouva ahile, nangman hinseijin, ati.
target: When Hushai came to him, Absalom said, “Ahithophel has given this advice. Should we do what he says? If not, give us your opinion.”

source: Chuin Hushai'in Absalom henga, Ahithophel thumop hi tuphatna dingin aphapoi.
target: Hushai replied to Absalom, “The advice Ahithophel has given is not good this time.

source: Hushai'in aseiben, Ajehchu nangman napale amiho chu gal hat ahiu, chule vompi gamlah-a anou kilahpeh banga alungsung uva lungsa ahiu nahen ahi; chule napahi galsat mi ahin, miho lah-a jong gehlou ding ahi.
target: You know your father and his men; they are fighters, and as fierce as a wild bear robbed of her cubs. Besides, your father is an experienced fighter; he will not spend the night with the troops.

source: Ven, amahi tu-a leiko khat sung, ahiloule munchom dang khatna kisel ding ahi: chule hung hitiding ahi, amaho lah-a themkhat ahung lhuh masah tengule, hiche jaho jouse chun, Absalom nungjui miho lah-a kitha chapna aumtai atidiu ahi.
target: Even now, he is hidden in a cave or some other place. If he should attack your troops first, whoever hears about it will say, ‘There has been a slaughter among the troops who follow Absalom.’

source: Chutengle mihangsan tah, alungchang keipi lungchang tobang jong chu junlha ding ahi: ajehchu Israelte jousen napa chu mihat ahi ahetnu ahin, chule aumkhompi miho chu mihangsan jeng ahiuve.
target: Then even the bravest soldier, whose heart is like the heart of a lion, will melt with fear, for all Israel knows that your father is a fighter and that those with him are brave.

source: Hijeh chun Dan'a pat Beersheba geija Israelte jouse luipikama neldi jat banga nahenga nakhop khoma, chule nangmatah chu gala nakon ding chu kathumop nahi.
target: “So I advise you: Let all Israel, from Dan to Beersheba—as numerous as the sand on the seashore—be gathered to you, with you yourself leading them into battle.

source: Hiti achu eiho ama kimunathei ding mun'a chu ihungdiu, chule daitwi tolla alhah banga eiho ama chunga ichuh jeng dingu ahi. Chule amale aumpi miho jouse khatcha jong kidalha louding ahi.
target: Then we will attack him wherever he may be found, and we will fall on him as dew settles on the ground. Neither he nor any of his men will be left alive.

source: Hicheng chungchona chu, ama khopi sung khat touva alutna ahile, Israelte jousen hiche khopi lama chu khao ahinchoidiu, chule khopi chu song halkhat cha akimulou kahse-a vadung sunga ikailut dingu ahi, ati.
target: If he withdraws into a city, then all Israel will bring ropes to that city, and we will drag it down to the valley until not so much as a pebble is left.”

source: Chuin Absalom le Israel mipi jouse chun, Arch mipa Hushai thumop hi Ahithophel thumop sangin aphajoi, atiuvin ahi. Ajehchu Pakaiyin Absalom chunga thilphalou ahinlhun sahna dinga, Pakaiyin Ahithophel thumop phaho jona dinga tohgon ananeisa ahitai.
target: Absalom and all the men of Israel said, “The advice of Hushai the Arkite is better than that of Ahithophel.” For the Lord had determined to frustrate the good advice of Ahithophel in order to bring disaster on Absalom.

source: Hichun Hushai'in Zadok le Abiathar thempupa henga, Hiti khati hin Ahithophel'in Absalom le Israel upaho athumopmin; hiti tihin keiman kathumop in ahi.
target: Hushai told Zadok and Abiathar, the priests, “Ahithophel has advised Absalom and the elders of Israel to do such and such, but I have advised them to do so and so.

source: Hijeh chun tun gangtah-in solin lang, David henga, Tujan gamthip phaicham ho-a chun gehhihhen, ahinla mangang tah-in galkaijin; achutiloule lengpa le aumpi miho jouse chu val lhuma umkha diu ahi, tin gaseisah-in, ati.
target: Now send a message at once and tell David, ‘Do not spend the night at the fords in the wilderness; cross over without fail, or the king and all the people with him will be swallowed up.’ ”

source: Tun Jonathan le Ahimaaz chu khopisung ahunglut lhon akimulouna dingin Enrogel'a aumlhonin ahi: chuin soh numei khat achen amani agaseipeh-in; chuin amani ache lhonin David lengpa agaseipeh lhontan ahi.
target: Jonathan and Ahimaaz were staying at En Rogel. A female servant was to go and inform them, and they were to go and tell King David, for they could not risk being seen entering the city.

source: Ahijeng vangin pasal chapang khatnin amaho chu anamun, Absalom chu aseipehtan ahi. Ahin amani mangang tah-in achemang lhonin, chuin Bahurim'a ahongsunga twikul neikhat in'a ahung lhonin; hia chun akumlha lhontan ahi.
target: But a young man saw them and told Absalom. So the two of them left at once and went to the house of a man in Bahurim. He had a well in his courtyard, and they climbed down into it.

source: Chuin numeinu chun twikul kamchu asingin, chuin achunga chun chang aphouvin ahile, hichu akihedoh pon ahi.
target: His wife took a covering and spread it out over the opening of the well and scattered grain over it. No one knew anything about it.

source: Chuin Absalom sohte numeinu in'a ahung phatnun, ahenga, Ahimaaz le Jonathan chu hoilama umham? atiuve. Chuin numei nun ajah uvah, Amani vachadung galkailhon tante, ati. Chuin amahon aholmo phatnun Jerusalem'a ahungkile taovin ahi.
target: When Absalom’s men came to the woman at the house, they asked, “Where are Ahimaaz and Jonathan?” The woman answered them, “They crossed over the brook.” The men searched but found no one, so they returned to Jerusalem.

source: Chuin ahitin ahi, amaho chedoh nungin, amani twikul'a konin ahungdoh lhonin, achelhonin David lengpa henga agaseipeh lhonin, ajah-a, Kipatdoh inlang mangang tah-in twi chu galkaijin; ajehchu Ahithophel'in nangma douna-a hitia hi athumop ahitai, atilhonne.
target: After they had gone, the two climbed out of the well and went to inform King David. They said to him, “Set out and cross the river at once; Ahithophel has advised such and such against you.”

source: Hichun David le aumkhompi miho jouse chu akipat doh-un, Jordan agalkaijun: jingkho vah-in amaho Jordan galkailou khatcha aumtapouvin ahi.
target: So David and all the people with him set out and crossed the Jordan. By daybreak, no one was left who had not crossed the Jordan.

source: Chuin Ahithophel'in athumop akijuilou amuphatnin, asangan pho kigotnin, akipatdoh-in, akhopi a-in lama achen, a-insung asemtupmin, chuin amale ama akikhailih-in, athin, apa lhanna akivuitan ahi.
target: When Ahithophel saw that his advice had not been followed, he saddled his donkey and set out for his house in his hometown. He put his house in order and then hanged himself. So he died and was buried in his father’s tomb.

source: Hichun David Mahanaim'a ahung lhungin ahi. Chule Absalom le aumpi Israel mite jouse chu Jordan agalkai taovin ahi.
target: David went to Mahanaim, and Absalom crossed the Jordan with all the men of Israel.

source: Chuin Absalom'in Joab khelin Amasa chu janel lamkaijin apansahtai: Hiche Amasa kitipa hi chu Joab nu Zeruiah sopinu Nasah chanu Abigail galuppi pa Israel mi Jithra kitipa chapa ahi.
target: Absalom had appointed Amasa over the army in place of Joab. Amasa was the son of Jether, an Ishmaelite who had married Abigail, the daughter of Nahash and sister of Zeruiah the mother of Joab.

source: Hitichun Israel le Absalom'in Gilead gama chun pon in akison taovin ahi.
target: The Israelites and Absalom camped in the land of Gilead.

source: Chuin ahitin ahi, David Mahanaim ahunglhun phatnin, Ammon mi Rabbah kho-a cheng Nahash chapa Shobi le, Lodebar kho-a cheng Ammiel chapa Machir toh, Rogelim kho-a cheng Gilead mi Barzillai'in,
target: When David came to Mahanaim, Shobi son of Nahash from Rabbah of the Ammonites, and Makir son of Ammiel from Lo Debar, and Barzillai the Gileadite from Rogelim

source: Jalkhunho, twikhonho, leibelho, suhlou chang, sakolchang, changbong, changkanpoh, bepaiho, bechim, belheng kikangho,
target: brought bedding and bowls and articles of pottery. They also brought wheat and barley, flour and roasted grain, beans and lentils,

source: Chule khoiju, bongnoi thao, kelngoi le bongnoihaho chu David le aumpi miho nehdingin ahinpouvin ahi: ajehchu amahon, Mipi hi gamthipma gilkel, thachol le dangchah-a umu ahi, atiuve.
target: honey and curds, sheep, and cheese from cows’ milk for David and his people to eat. For they said, “The people have become exhausted and hungry and thirsty in the wilderness.”

source: Chuin David'in aumkhopi miho chu asimin, chuin aman sangkhat chung lamkai le jakhat chunga lamkai ding alhengdoh-in ahi.
target: David mustered the men who were with him and appointed over them commanders of thousands and commanders of hundreds.

source: Chule David'in mipi hopthum-a hopkhat chu Joab khut noija asoldoh-in, hopthum-a hopkhat chu Zeruiah chapa Joab sopipa Zeruiah chapa Abishai khut noija asoldoh-in, chule hopthum-a hopkhat chu Git mi Ittai khut noija chun asoldoh-in ahi. Chuin lengpan mipi ho henga, Keima tahjong thonlouva nang hotoh kalhonkhom ding ahi, ati.
target: David sent out his troops, a third under the command of Joab, a third under Joab’s brother Abishai son of Zeruiah, and a third under Ittai the Gittite. The king told the troops, “I myself will surely march out with you.”

source: Ahinla mipin adonbutnun, Nangma nakondoh louding ahi: ajehchu keiho jamta leoveng, amahon keiho gelkhoh-a einei loudiu; chule keiho akehkhat thijong leoveng, amahon keiho gelkhoh-a einei loudiu ahi. Ahinla tun nangma keiho sangsom toh kibang nahi: hijeh-a chu nangman tu-a khopi sunga naum hi phajo ahi, atiuve.
target: But the men said, “You must not go out; if we are forced to flee, they won’t care about us. Even if half of us die, they won’t care; but you are worth ten thousand of us. It would be better now for you to give us support from the city.”

source: Chuin lengpan ajah uva, Nanghon aphapen dinga nagelu chu kabol ding ahi, ati. Chuin lengpa kotpi phung koma chun adingin, mipi jouse chu jakhat cheng le sangkhat chengin ahungdoh-un ahi.
target: The king answered, “I will do whatever seems best to you.” So the king stood beside the gate while all his men marched out in units of hundreds and of thousands.

source: Chuin lengpan Joab, Abishai chule Ittai chu thu apen, ajah uva, Keima ding ngaitonan gollhangpa, Absalom ngeichu lungneng tah-in hindemun, ati. Chule miho jouse chun lengpan Absalom chung changa ja lamkaiho athupeh chu ajaovin ahi.
target: The king commanded Joab, Abishai and Ittai, “Be gentle with the young man Absalom for my sake.” And all the troops heard the king giving orders concerning Absalom to each of the commanders.

source: Hitichun mipi chu gamlah-a Israelte doudin achedoh taovin ahi. Chuin gal chu Ephraim gammanga kisat uva ahi;
target: David’s army marched out of the city to fight Israel, and the battle took place in the forest of Ephraim.

source: Hiche mun'a chun Israel mipi ho chu David sohte masanga akithat chap taovin, chule hiche nikho chun mi sangsomni athin ahi.
target: There Israel’s troops were routed by David’s men, and the casualties that day were great—twenty thousand men.

source: Ajehchu gal chu gamsung jouse-a akithechan soh-a ahitan: chule hiche nikho chun chemjam'a kithat sangin, gammang lah-a ohlih atamjouvin ahi.
target: The battle spread out over the whole countryside, and the forest swallowed up more men that day than the sword.

source: Chuin Absalom'in David sohte chu atohkha tan ahi. Chuin Absalom chu sangan chung khatna touva ahin, chule sangan chu gangpi lentah abah kibom noija chun achen ahile, alu chu gangpi-a chun a-ohdentan; chuin ama vanle lei kikah-a akikhai denin; anoija um sangan chu achemang tan ahi.
target: Now Absalom happened to meet David’s men. He was riding his mule, and as the mule went under the thick branches of a large oak, Absalom’s hair got caught in the tree. He was left hanging in midair, while the mule he was riding kept on going.

source: Chuin mikhatnin hichu amun, Joab jah-a, Ven, keiman Absalom gangpi phunga akikhai kamun ahi, ati.
target: When one of the men saw what had happened, he told Joab, “I just saw Absalom hanging in an oak tree.”

source: Chuin Joab'in aseipehpa henga, Ven, nangman ama namu ahin, ipidinga amachu tolla satlhalou nahim? chutile keiman nangma dangka Shekel somleh konggah khat nape tadinga, ati.
target: Joab said to the man who had told him this, “What! You saw him? Why didn’t you strike him to the ground right there? Then I would have had to give you ten shekels of silver and a warrior’s belt.”

source: Chuin mipa chun Joab henga, Keiman dangka Shekel sangkhat kakhutna kasan ding hijongleh, keiman lengpa chapa dounan kakhut kalha louding ahi; ajehchu keiho jah tah-in lengpa nangma le Abishai chule Ittai nathu peh-un, Gollhang Absalom chu koimachan natohkhah louna dingun chingtheijun, ati.
target: But the man replied, “Even if a thousand shekels were weighed out into my hands, I would not lay a hand on the king’s son. In our hearing the king commanded you and Abishai and Ittai, ‘Protect the young man Absalom for my sake.’

source: Achuti louva ahile kahinkho douna-a dihlou tah-a na katohding ahi: ajehchu lengpa-a kona ki-ima imacha aumpon, nangmatah ngeijong keima douva nahung panding ahi, ati.
target: And if I had put my life in jeopardy—and nothing is hidden from the king—you would have kept your distance from me.”

source: Hichun Joab'in, Keima nangma toh hitihin umthei ponge, ati. Chuin aman akhutna tengcha thum alan, Gangpi thing lah-a ahinga ana umnalai Absalom alungchang chu asun pailetnin ahi.
target: Joab said, “I’m not going to wait like this for you.” So he took three javelins in his hand and plunged them into Absalom’s heart while Absalom was still alive in the oak tree.

source: Chuin Joab galmanchah po-a pang gollhang mi somho chun Absalom chu a-umkimvelun, avouvin, athat taovin ahi.
target: And ten of Joab’s armor-bearers surrounded Absalom, struck him and killed him.

source: Chuin Joab'in sumkon amutnin ahile, mipi chu Israelte anungdel naova konin ahungkile taovin ahi; ajehchu Joab'in mipi chu akhamtang ahitai.
target: Then Joab sounded the trumpet, and the troops stopped pursuing Israel, for Joab halted them.

source: Chuin amahon Absalom chu alauvin, gammang lah kotong lentah khat aseplutnun, chule achunga songlhuh lentah-in aseuvin ahi. Chuin Israelte chu amitakip ama ama ponbuh lam cheh-a ajamtaovin ahi.
target: They took Absalom, threw him into a big pit in the forest and piled up a large heap of rocks over him. Meanwhile, all the Israelites fled to their homes.

source: Tun Absalom'in ahinlaijin lengpa phaichama chun amadingin khompi khat anatung doh-in ahi. Ajehchu aman, keiman kamin geldoh jingna dinga koiding chapa kaneipoi, ati: chuin aman khompi chu ama-min aputsah-in ahi. Chule hichu tunigeijin Absalom mun tin akisahtai.
target: During his lifetime Absalom had taken a pillar and erected it in the King’s Valley as a monument to himself, for he thought, “I have no son to carry on the memory of my name.” He named the pillar after himself, and it is called Absalom’s Monument to this day.

source: Chujouvin Zadok chapa Ahimaaz'in, Tun keima lhaijing kating, Pakaiyin melmaho chunga iti phu analah hitam, lengpa koma athu hi galhut inge, ati.
target: Now Ahimaaz son of Zadok said, “Let me run and take the news to the king that the Lord has vindicated him by delivering him from the hand of his enemies.”

source: Chuin Joab'in ahenga, Tunia hi nangman thu napoh theilou ding, amavang nidang tengle napoh ding ahi. Tunia vanghi nangman thu napoh louding ahi, ajehchu lengpa chapa thia ahi, ati.
target: “You are not the one to take the news today,” Joab told him. “You may take the news another time, but you must not do so today, because the king’s son is dead.”

source: Chujouvin Joab'in Cushi henga, Chenlang nathilmu hi lengpa gaseipehtan, ati. Chuin Cushi chu Joab anga akunin, alhaijeltan ahi.
target: Then Joab said to a Cushite, “Go, tell the king what you have seen.” The Cushite bowed down before Joab and ran off.

source: Hichun Zadok chapa Ahimaaz chun Joab henga aseikitnin, Ahile hitante, nahenga katao ahi, Cushi nunga chun lhaijing kate, ati. Chuin Joab'in, Kachapa, athupoh ding umlouva ipi dinga lhaiding nakigot jengham? ati.
target: Ahimaaz son of Zadok again said to Joab, “Come what may, please let me run behind the Cushite.” But Joab replied, “My son, why do you want to go? You don’t have any news that will bring you a reward.”

source: Ahinla aman, Ahile hitante, lhaijeng inge, ati. Hichun aman ajah-a, Lhaitan, ati. Hichun Ahimaaz chu phaicham lampia chun alhaijin Cushi chu akhelpatan ahi.
target: He said, “Come what may, I want to run.” So Joab said, “Run!” Then Ahimaaz ran by way of the plain and outran the Cushite.

source: Chule David chu kotpi teni kikah-a chu touva ahi. Chuin khongahpa chu kotpi phung bang chunga chun akaldoh-in, akhodah in ahile, veuvin, mikhat achanga hunglhai amun ahi.
target: While David was sitting between the inner and outer gates, the watchman went up to the roof of the gateway by the wall. As he looked out, he saw a man running alone.

source: Chuin khongahpa chun asamin, lengpa henga aseipehtan ahi. Chuin lengpan, Ama achang ahile, akama thu ahinpoh hinte, ati. Chuin ama kintah-in ahunglhaijin ahungnai chehcheh-in ahi.
target: The watchman called out to the king and reported it. The king said, “If he is alone, he must have good news.” And the runner came closer and closer.

source: Chuin khongahpa chun michom dang khat hunglhaija amukitnin: chuin khongahpa chun kotngahpachu akouvin, ahenga, Ven, michom dang khat jong ahunglhaije, ati. Chuin lengpan amajong thu ahinpoh ahi, ati.
target: Then the watchman saw another runner, and he called down to the gatekeeper, “Look, another man running alone!” The king said, “He must be bringing good news, too.”

source: Chuin khongahpan, Keiman ahunglhai masapenpa chu Zadok chapa Ahimaaz lhai danin kahen ahi, ati. Chuin lengpan, Amachu mipha ahin, chule thupha toh hungtha ahi, ati.
target: The watchman said, “It seems to me that the first one runs like Ahimaaz son of Zadok.” “He’s a good man,” the king said. “He comes with good news.”

source: Chuin Ahimaaz'in ahin samin, lengpa henga, Imajouse aphasoh keinai, ati. Chuin aman lengpa masang tolla chun amai asulutnin, Ka pakai lengpa douna akhut lamho jouse pedoh-a Pakai na Pathen chu nunnom hen, ati.
target: Then Ahimaaz called out to the king, “All is well!” He bowed down before the king with his face to the ground and said, “Praise be to the Lord your God! He has delivered up those who lifted their hands against my lord the king.”

source: Chuin lengpan ajah-a, Gollhang Absalom chu hoidoh nam? ati. Chuin Ahimaaz'in adonbutnin, Joab'in lengpa sohpa le nasoh keima eisol lhonchun, keiman mipi boilah lah chu kamun, ahinla hichu ipi ahi kahepoi, ati.
target: The king asked, “Is the young man Absalom safe?” Ahimaaz answered, “I saw great confusion just as Joab was about to send the king’s servant and me, your servant, but I don’t know what it was.”

source: Chuin lengpan ajah-a, Kikhindoh inlang, hikoma hin dingin, ati. Chuin ama akikhindoh-in, ading thimbeh-in ahi.
target: The king said, “Stand aside and wait here.” So he stepped aside and stood there.

source: Chuin veuvin, Cushi ahung lhungin; chule Cushi'n, ka Pakai lengpa thu kahinpoi; ijeh inem itile nangma doudinga kipatdoh ho jouse chunga tuni hin Pakaiyin phu alatai, ati.
target: Then the Cushite arrived and said, “My lord the king, hear the good news! The Lord has vindicated you today by delivering you from the hand of all who rose up against you.”

source: Chuin lengpan Cushi henga, Gollhang Absalom chu hoidoh nam? ati. Chuin Cushi'n adonbutnin, Ka pakai lengpa melmaho jouse, chule nangma suhkhah nadinga nangma douna kipatdoh jouse chu gollhangpa chutoh bangcheh hen, ati.
target: The king asked the Cushite, “Is the young man Absalom safe?” The Cushite replied, “May the enemies of my lord the king and all who rise up to harm you be like that young man.”

source: Chuin lengpa chu alung analheh jengtan, kotpi phunga dan chunga chun akaldoh-in, akaptan ahi: chuin aman achepumin, Ohe! kachapa Absalom! kachapa, kachapa Absalom! Pathen'in nangma khela eithisah joh hile ong! ohe Absalom, kachapa, kachapa, atin ahi.
target: The king was shaken. He went up to the room over the gateway and wept. As he went, he said: “O my son Absalom! My son, my son Absalom! If only I had died instead of you—O Absalom, my son, my son!”

source: Chuin Joab henga, Ven, lengpa chu Absalom dingin akapmin, alunghemin ahi tin aseipeh-un ahi.
target: Joab was told, “The king is weeping and mourning for Absalom.”

source: Chule hiche nikho-a galjona chu mijouse dingin lunghemna asohtan ahi. Ajehchu mipi jousen, Lengpa ichan geija achapa dinga lung gentheija hitam, tia kisei chu ajauvin ahi.
target: And for the whole army the victory that day was turned into mourning, because on that day the troops heard it said, “The king is grieving for his son.”

source: Chule galmuna kona ajamdoh jeh-a jahchatah-a umho bangin, hiche nikho chun mipi ho chu guhthim chan khopi sunga chun ahung lutnun ahi.
target: The men stole into the city that day as men steal in who are ashamed when they flee from battle.

source: Ahivangin lengpan amai akikhun, awsang tah-in, Vo kachapa Absalom! vo Absalom kachapa, kachapa, tin akapmin ahi.
target: The king covered his face and cried aloud, “O my son Absalom! O Absalom, my son, my son!”

source: Chuin Joab chu lengpa in'a ahunglutnin, ajah-a, Nangman tunikho hin nangma hinkho, nachapate hinkho, nachanute hinkho, najite hinkho, nathaikem ho hinkho huhdoh-a nasohte jouse maihi najumson;
target: Then Joab went into the house to the king and said, “Today you have humiliated all your men, who have just saved your life and the lives of your sons and daughters and the lives of your wives and concubines.

source: Hiche-a hin nangman namelmate nangailun, naloi nagol ho nahotbolin ahi. Ajehchu tuni hin nangman leng chapate le soh ho hi ija naselouna naphongdoh tan: tuni hin Absalom chu hing henlang, keiho jousehi thileuveng nakipah ding ahi ti kamudohtai.
target: You love those who hate you and hate those who love you. You have made it clear today that the commanders and their men mean nothing to you. I see that you would be pleased if Absalom were alive today and all of us were dead.

source: Hijeh chun tun kipatdoh-in, chedoh-in lang nasohte henga lungmona thu gaseijin: ajehchu Pakai mina kihahsel kahi, napotdoh louva ahile, tujan apat khatcha jong nangma toh umlou ding ahitai: chule hichu nakhangdon laija patna tuni geija nachunga thilse anachuho sanga khohjo ding ahi, ati.
target: Now go out and encourage your men. I swear by the Lord that if you don’t go out, not a man will be left with you by nightfall. This will be worse for you than all the calamities that have come on you from your youth till now.”

source: Hichun lengpa akipatdoh-in, kotpi phunga chun atoutan ahi. Chuin amahon mipi ho jouse henga chun, Veuvin; lengpa chu kotpi phunga atoutai, atiuve. Chuin mipi chu lengpa masanga ahungun ahi: ajehchu Israelte amitakip ama ama pon-in lam cheh-a jamu ahitai.
target: So the king got up and took his seat in the gateway. When the men were told, “The king is sitting in the gateway,” they all came before him. Meanwhile, the Israelites had fled to their homes.

source: Chuin Israel phung jouse lah-a mipi ho chu akiphinun, Lengpan imelmateu khutna konin eihuhdoh-un; chule Philistinte khutna konin eihuhdoh-un; chule tun ama Absalom jeh-in gamsunga konin ajamdoh tai.
target: Throughout the tribes of Israel, all the people were arguing among themselves, saying, “The king delivered us from the hand of our enemies; he is the one who rescued us from the hand of the Philistines. But now he has fled the country to escape from Absalom;

source: Chule ichunguva dinga thao inupao Absalom chu galmuna athitan ahi. Hijeh chun tun ipidinga lengpa lepuikit nadinga thu changkhat beh nasei daoham? atiuve.
target: and Absalom, whom we anointed to rule over us, has died in battle. So why do you say nothing about bringing the king back?”

source: Chuin David lengpan Zadok le Abiathar thempu henga mi asolin, ajah-a, Judah upaho henga hitin aseijin, Israelte thusei chu lengpa le a-insung ngei tah-a hunglhung tai ti namu nunguva, ipidinga nanghon lengpa a-in'a lepui kitnadinga anunung pena napan uham?
target: King David sent this message to Zadok and Abiathar, the priests: “Ask the elders of Judah, ‘Why should you be the last to bring the king back to his palace, since what is being said throughout Israel has reached the king at his quarters?

source: Nangho kasopite nahiuvin, kaguhole kaphe nahiuve. Chuti ahile ipidinga nangho lengpa lepuina dinga anunungpen nahiu ham?
target: You are my relatives, my own flesh and blood. So why should you be the last to bring back the king?’

source: Chule nanghon Amasa henga, Nangma kagule kaphe nahilouham? Nangma kamasang Joab khela janel gallamkai nahijom jing louva ahile, Pathen'in kachunga hitichun, chule akhohjo cheh-in eibolhen, ati.
target: And say to Amasa, ‘Are you not my own flesh and blood? May God deal with me, be it ever so severely, if you are not the commander of my army for life in place of Joab.’ ”

source: Chuin aman mikhat lungsung bangin Judah miho jouse lungsung chu asunemin; hitichun amahon lengpa henga thu athotnun, Nangmale nasohteho hungkile taovin, atiuvin ahi.
target: He won over the hearts of the men of Judah so that they were all of one mind. They sent word to the king, “Return, you and all your men.”

source: Hitichun lengpa ahungkilen, Jordan ahung lhungtan ahi. Chuin Judah chu lengpa kimutopi ding le Jordan galkaipi dingin Gilgal'a ahungtan ahi.
target: Then the king returned and went as far as the Jordan. Now the men of Judah had come to Gilgal to go out and meet the king and bring him across the Jordan.

source: Chuin Bahurim'a um Benjamin mi Gera chapa Shimei chu Judah miho toh David lengpa kimutopi dingin mangang tah-in ahungsuh-in ahi.
target: Shimei son of Gera, the Benjamite from Bahurim, hurried down with the men of Judah to meet King David.

source: Chule ama chu Benjamin mi sangkhat to ahin, Saul insungmi sohpa Ziba le achapa somlenga toh, chule asoh somni toh ahiuvin: chuin amaho chu lengpa masanga chun Jordan agalkaijun ahi.
target: With him were a thousand Benjamites, along with Ziba, the steward of Saul’s household, and his fifteen sons and twenty servants. They rushed to the Jordan, where the king was.

source: Chuin amaho lengpa insungmi le aman boldinga pha-a agel chu boldingin kongneo khatna agalkaijun ahi. Chuin ama Jordan ahung galkai kaijin, Gera chapa Shimei chu lengpa masanga abohkhup jengin;
target: They crossed at the ford to take the king’s household over and to do whatever he wished. When Shimei son of Gera crossed the Jordan, he fell prostrate before the king

source: Chule lengpa henga, Ka pakaiyin khangitlouna chu keija simhih-in, chule ka pakai lengpan Jerusalem adalhah ni-a nasoh kanachonvalna jong chu geldoh danlang, lengpan nalunga jong vophih beh-in.
target: and said to him, “May my lord not hold me guilty. Do not remember how your servant did wrong on the day my lord the king left Jerusalem. May the king put it out of his mind.

source: Ajehchu nasoh hin chonse kahi ti kakihetne: hijeh chun ven, tunia hi Joseph insung miholah-a ka pakai lengpa kimutopi dinga hungsuh masapen kahi, ati.
target: For I your servant know that I have sinned, but today I have come here as the first from the tribes of Joseph to come down and meet my lord the king.”

source: Ahivangin Zeruiah chapa Abishai'in adonbutnun, aman Pakai thaonusa agaosap jeh-a Shimei chu thading hilouham? ati.
target: Then Abishai son of Zeruiah said, “Shouldn’t Shimei be put to death for this? He cursed the Lord ’s anointed.”

source: Chuin David'in, Nangho Zeruiah chapate, nangho le keima ipi ikibahnao uma, tunia hi keima douva napan uham? Tunia Israel sunga mi kithat ding ham? tunia hi keiman Israelte chunga leng kahihi kahet louva nabolu ham? ati.
target: David replied, “What does this have to do with you, you sons of Zeruiah? What right do you have to interfere? Should anyone be put to death in Israel today? Don’t I know that today I am king over Israel?”

source: Hijeh chun lengpan Shimei jah-a, Nangma nathilou ding ahi ati. Chuin lengpa amahenga akiteptan ahi.
target: So the king said to Shimei, “You shall not die.” And the king promised him on oath.

source: Chuin Saul chapa Mephibosheth chu lengpa kimupi dingin ahungsuh-in, chule aman lengpa akipatdoh ni-a pat lungmonga ahungkit nikho tokah-a hi akeng jong asillou, akhamul jong apolou, avonho jong asoplou ahi.
target: Mephibosheth, Saul’s grandson, also went down to meet the king. He had not taken care of his feet or trimmed his mustache or washed his clothes from the day the king left until the day he returned safely.

source: Chuin ahitin ahi, ama Jerusalem'a lengpa kimutopi dinga ahung chun lengpan ahenga, Mephibosheth ipidinga keima toh kilhonlou nahim? ati.
target: When he came from Jerusalem to meet the king, the king asked him, “Why didn’t you go with me, Mephibosheth?”

source: Chuin aman adonbutnin, Ka pakai, vo kalengpa, nasohhi kengbai kahi jeh-in keima, Achunga katouva lengpa henga kache theina dingin sangan chu kigotninge kati ahi; hinlah kasohpan eijoulhep ahi
target: He said, “My lord the king, since I your servant am lame, I said, ‘I will have my donkey saddled and will ride on it, so I can go with the king.’ But Ziba my servant betrayed me.

source: Chule aman nasohhi ka pakai lengpa henga eihehsen ahi; ahinla ka pakai lengpa hi Pathen vantil tobang ahi. Hijeh chun namitmu-a pha masah dungjuijin boltan.
target: And he has slandered your servant to my lord the king. My lord the king is like an angel of God; so do whatever you wish.

source: Ajehchu kapa insung pumpiho ka pakai lengpa masanga athisa ahitan, hijongle nangman nasohhi nangma dokhanga neho lah-a napan sah-in ahi. Hijeh chun lengpa henga taokitna dinga ipi thaneina kaneijem? ati.
target: All my grandfather’s descendants deserved nothing but death from my lord the king, but you gave your servant a place among those who eat at your table. So what right do I have to make any more appeals to the king?”

source: Chuin lengpan ahenga, Ipidinga nangman nathu chu nasei nahlai ham? Keiman, Nang le Ziba gam chu kihomlhontan tin kanaseije, ati.
target: The king said to him, “Why say more? I order you and Ziba to divide the land.”

source: Chuin Mephibosheth'in lengpa henga, Ka pakai lengpa lungmonga a-in'a hung kilekit ahitah jeh-in, abonin aman kilahtahen, ati.
target: Mephibosheth said to the king, “Let him take everything, now that my lord the king has returned home safely.”

source: Chuin Gilead mi Barzillai chu Rogelim'a konin ahungsuh-in chuin, Jordan gal gei gathah dingin, lengpa toh Jordan agalkai lhonin ahi.
target: Barzillai the Gileadite also came down from Rogelim to cross the Jordan with the king and to send him on his way from there.

source: Tun Barzillai chu mi kum upatah ahitan, kum somget ahitai. Chule aman lengpa Mahanaim'a aumlaija chu nehding ana khan ahi; ajehchu ama mihao tah ahi.
target: Now Barzillai was very old, eighty years of age. He had provided for the king during his stay in Mahanaim, for he was a very wealthy man.

source: Chuin lengpan Barzillai henga, Kakoma hungin lang, Jerusalem'a kakoma na-umlaisen keiman navah nange, ati.
target: The king said to Barzillai, “Cross over with me and stay with me in Jerusalem, and I will provide for you.”

source: Chuin Barzillai'in lengpa henga, Keima itih chanpi kahin nahlai ding hija, lengpa toh Jerusalem'a kachetou dingham?
target: But Barzillai answered the king, “How many more years will I live, that I should go up to Jerusalem with the king?

source: Tuhin keima kum somget kahitai. Chule keiman apha le ase kalhengkhen thei ding ham? Nasoh hin kaneh dingle kadon ding chu atwi atam kahetthei ding hinam? Numei lasathem le pasal lasathem ho lasah awgin chu kajah thei nalaiding hinam? chuti ahile ipi dinga nasohhi ka pakai lengpa dinga pohgih kibe nabep kahiding ham?
target: I am now eighty years old. Can I tell the difference between what is enjoyable and what is not? Can your servant taste what he eats and drinks? Can I still hear the voices of male and female singers? Why should your servant be an added burden to my lord the king?

source: Nasoh hi lengpa toh Jordan gal themkhat chebeding kahi: ipidinga hitobang thilpeh-a hi lengpan neilethuh got ham?
target: Your servant will cross over the Jordan with the king for a short distance, but why should the king reward me in this way?

source: Nahenga katao ahi, nasohhi kakhopia kathi-a kanule kapa lhanna kakivui theina dingin, neinungsol tan. Ahinla ven, nasoh Chimham hi; amahi ka pakai lengpa toh lhonhen lang, nangman apha hidinga kilom nasah dungjuijin achunga hin boltan, ati.
target: Let your servant return, that I may die in my own town near the tomb of my father and mother. But here is your servant Kimham. Let him cross over with my lord the king. Do for him whatever you wish.”

source: Chuin lengpan adonbutnin, Chimham hi keimatoh kilhon ding ahin, chule keima ama chunga hi apha hidinga kilom kasah dungjuija kabolding ahi. Chule ipi hitajongle keima-a kona nangaichat chu kabolpeh ding nahi, ati.
target: The king said, “Kimham shall cross over with me, and I will do for him whatever you wish. And anything you desire from me I will do for you.”

source: Chuin mijouse Jordan agalkai taovin ahi. Chuin lengpa ahung galkai phatnin, lengpan Barzillai chu achopmin, chule phatthei aboh-in; chuin ama aumna lama akile kittan ahi.
target: So all the people crossed the Jordan, and then the king crossed over. The king kissed Barzillai and bid him farewell, and Barzillai returned to his home.

source: Chujouvin lengpa Gilgal'a achen, chule Chimham chu amatoh alhonin ahi. Chuin Judah mijouse le Israel mipi akehkhat chun lengpa ahin puijun ahi.
target: When the king crossed over to Gilgal, Kimham crossed with him. All the troops of Judah and half the troops of Israel had taken the king over.

source: Chuin veuvin, Israel mipi ho jouse chu lengpa henga ahungun, lengpa jah-a, Ipidinga Judah mi kasopi hon nangma naguh manguva, lengpa le a-insungmi chule David'in aumpi miho jouse chu apui galkaiju ham? atiuve.
target: Soon all the men of Israel were coming to the king and saying to him, “Why did our brothers, the men of Judah, steal the king away and bring him and his household across the Jordan, together with all his men?”

source: Chuin Judah miho jouse chun Israel miho chu adonbutnun, Lengpa hi kakinaipiu ka-insungmiu ahijeh ahi. Chuti ahile ipidinga nangho hiche jeh-a hi lunghanga nahiuvem? Lengpa chohsa ne-a kahiuvem? ahiloule aman keiho thilpeh eipeh khah uvem? atiuve.
target: All the men of Judah answered the men of Israel, “We did this because the king is closely related to us. Why are you angry about it? Have we eaten any of the king’s provisions? Have we taken anything for ourselves?”

source: Chuin Israel miho chun Judah miho chu adonbutnun, Keihon lengpa-a chansom kaneijun, chule keihon nangho sangin David'a thaneina kaneijouvin ahi. Chuti ahile ipidinga lengpa galepui kitna dinga keiho thuhil chu masajo ahi chu i-sah louva bol nahiuvem? tiuve. Ahinla Judah miho thusei chu Israel miho thusei sangin ahatjon ahi.
target: Then the men of Israel answered the men of Judah, “We have ten shares in the king; so we have a greater claim on David than you have. Why then do you treat us with contempt? Weren’t we the first to speak of bringing back our king?” But the men of Judah pressed their claims even more forcefully than the men of Israel.

source: Chuin Benjamin Bikhri chapa Sheba kiti boinasem mikhat ana umin ahi. Chuin aman sumkon amutnin, Eihon David'a chan ineipouve, chule Jesse chapa-a konin jong goulo ding ineipouve: Vo Israel, naponbuh cheh uva chetaovin, ati.
target: Now a troublemaker named Sheba son of Bikri, a Benjamite, happened to be there. He sounded the trumpet and shouted, “We have no share in David, no part in Jesse’s son! Every man to his tent, Israel!”

source: Hitichun Israel mite jousen David adalhaovin, chuin Bikhri chapa Sheba chu ajuitaovin ahi. Ahivangin Jordan'a pat Jerusalem geija Judah mite vangchu alengpaova dingin apangdetnun ahi.
target: So all the men of Israel deserted David to follow Sheba son of Bikri. But the men of Judah stayed by their king all the way from the Jordan to Jerusalem.

source: Chuin David Jerusalem'a a-in ahung lhungin, chuin lengpan a-inngah dinga adalhah, numei thaikem somho chu insung dan khatna akoijin, avah-in, ahin amaho koma chun alut tapon ahi. Hitichun amaho chu athi nikho geijun khakhumin aumun, meithai bangin ahing taovin ahi.
target: When David returned to his palace in Jerusalem, he took the ten concubines he had left to take care of the palace and put them in a house under guard. He provided for them but had no sexual relations with them. They were kept in confinement till the day of their death, living as widows.

source: Chujouvin lengpan Amasa henga, Nithum sungin Judah mite neikhop khompeh inlang, chule nangma tahjong umin, ati.
target: Then the king said to Amasa, “Summon the men of Judah to come to me within three days, and be here yourself.”

source: Hijeh chun Amasa chu Judah mite khom dingin achen: ahinla David'in atepeh phat sangchun ahung geijotan ahi.
target: But when Amasa went to summon Judah, he took longer than the time the king had set for him.

source: Chuin David'in Abishai henga, Tu-a hi Bikhri chapa Sheba hin Absalom'in eibolnao sanga khohjo cheh-a eiboldiu hitam? Napakai sohte kipuijin lang ama chu nungdelin, achuti loule khopi kul kikai khum khat kimuntin, eihoa konin sohcha getninte, ati.
target: David said to Abishai, “Now Sheba son of Bikri will do us more harm than Absalom did. Take your master’s men and pursue him, or he will find fortified cities and escape from us.”

source: Chule ama nunga chun Joab miho, Chereth mite, Peleth mite le mihat ho jouse acheuvin; chuin amaho Bikhri chapa Sheba nung del dingin Jerusalem'a konin akipat doh-un ahi.
target: So Joab’s men and the Kerethites and Pelethites and all the mighty warriors went out under the command of Abishai. They marched out from Jerusalem to pursue Sheba son of Bikri.

source: Amaho Gibeon mun songpilen phunga aumlaijun, Amasa chu amasanguva ahungin ahi. Tun Joab chu galvon'a kivon ahin, chule chu-a chu konggah um, chule akonga chu chemjam apaija kiheng kikhaija ahi; chuin ama malama achea ahile hichu ahung kitanglhan ahi.
target: While they were at the great rock in Gibeon, Amasa came to meet them. Joab was wearing his military tunic, and strapped over it at his waist was a belt with a dagger in its sheath. As he stepped forward, it dropped out of its sheath.

source: Chuin Joab'in Amasa henga, Kasopi pa, nadam hinam? ati. Chuin Joab'in Amasa chop dingin akhut jetlama akhamulin amanin ahi.
target: Joab said to Amasa, “How are you, my brother?” Then Joab took Amasa by the beard with his right hand to kiss him.

source: Ahivangin Amasa chun Joab'in akhutna chemjam achoi chu ahepon ahi. Chuin aman hichea chun a-oipoh asut peh-in ahile, agil tolla alonglhan, avelin asunkit tapon; chuin ama athitan ahi. Hitichun Joab le sopipa Abishai chun Bikhri chapa Sheba chu anungdel lhontan ahi.
target: Amasa was not on his guard against the dagger in Joab’s hand, and Joab plunged it into his belly, and his intestines spilled out on the ground. Without being stabbed again, Amasa died. Then Joab and his brother Abishai pursued Sheba son of Bikri.

source: Chule Joab miho khat chu Amasa koma adingin, Joab khohsah jouse le, David langa pang jouse chu Joab nunga cheohen, ati.
target: One of Joab’s men stood beside Amasa and said, “Whoever favors Joab, and whoever is for David, let him follow Joab!”

source: Chuin Amasa chu lamlhong lailunga athin achupmin ahi. Chuin mipa chun mipi adinden chu amuphatnin, Amasa chu lamlhonga konin gamlah-a achondoh-in, chule akom hinhopa jouse adin dennu chu amuphatnin, ama chu ponkhat akhukhumin ahi.
target: Amasa lay wallowing in his blood in the middle of the road, and the man saw that all the troops came to a halt there. When he realized that everyone who came up to Amasa stopped, he dragged him from the road into a field and threw a garment over him.

source: Ama lamlhonga akichondoh phatnin, mijouse Bikhri chapa Sheba nung del dingin Joab nunga acheuvin ahi.
target: After Amasa had been removed from the road, everyone went on with Joab to pursue Sheba son of Bikri.

source: Chule ama Abel gei le Beth-maachah geijin Israel phung jouse henga le Ber mite jouse henga achen ahi. Chuin amaho akikho khomun ama nung ajuitaove.
target: Sheba passed through all the tribes of Israel to Abel Beth Maakah and through the entire region of the Bikrites, who gathered together and followed him.

source: Chuin amaho ahungun amaho chu Beth-maachah'a um Abel mun'a chun aumkolun, chule amahon khopi dounan leibang asepmun, chule hichu kiselna leiko-a dinga ahin: Joab toh umkhom mipi jouse chun kulbang chu suhchim dingin asusepan ataovin ahi.
target: All the troops with Joab came and besieged Sheba in Abel Beth Maakah. They built a siege ramp up to the city, and it stood against the outer fortifications. While they were battering the wall to bring it down,

source: Hichun khopi-a konchun numei chingtah khatnin ahin samin, Ngaijun, ngaijun; Joab henga katao ahi, nangma toh kakihou theina din, hilam hin naijin, ati.
target: a wise woman called from the city, “Listen! Listen! Tell Joab to come here so I can speak to him.”

source: Chuin amapa amanu henga ahungnai phatnin, numeinu chun ahenga, Nangma Joab nahim? ati. Chuin aman adonbutnin, Keima ama chu kahi, ati. Hichun amanun ajah-a, Nasohnu thusei ho hi ngaijin, ati. Chuin aman Kangaije, atin adonbutnin ahi.
target: He went toward her, and she asked, “Are you Joab?” “I am,” he answered. She said, “Listen to what your servant has to say.” “I’m listening,” he said.

source: Hichun amanun, Masanglai chun min, Amahon thonlouva Abel kho-a thumop adoh teidiu ahi, tin anasei jiuvin: chule hitichun thu chu achai jiuvin ahi.
target: She continued, “Long ago they used to say, ‘Get your answer at Abel,’ and that settled it.

source: Keima Israel sunga chamna deile tahsan ho lah-a khat kahi. Nangman khopi khat le Israel minu khat suhmangdin naholin ahi. Ipidinga nangman Pakai goulo chu naval lhum ding ham? ati.
target: We are the peaceful and faithful in Israel. You are trying to destroy a city that is a mother in Israel. Why do you want to swallow up the Lord ’s inheritance?”

source: Chuin Joab'in adonbutnin, Keiman kaval lhum ding ahiloule kasuhmang ding chu keija konin gamlahen, keija konin gamlahen.
target: “Far be it from me!” Joab replied, “Far be it from me to swallow up or destroy!

source: Athu chu chuti ahipoi: ahin Ephraim molsana kon mikhat Bikhri chapa amin Sheba chun David lengpa dounan akhut alamin ahi. Ama changseh chu hinpe doh-un, chule keiman khopi hi dalhatange, ati. Chuin numei nun Joab henga, Ven aluchang chu bang chunga kona kahin selhahpeh ding nahi, ati.
target: That is not the case. A man named Sheba son of Bikri, from the hill country of Ephraim, has lifted up his hand against the king, against David. Hand over this one man, and I’ll withdraw from the city.” The woman said to Joab, “His head will be thrown to you from the wall.”

source: Hichun numeinu chu chingtheitah in mipi ho jouse henga chun achen ahi. Chuin amahon Bikhri chapa Sheba chu alu atanun, Joab henga asepdoh taovin ahi. Chuin aman sumkon amutnin, chuin amaho khopi-a konin ama ama pon-in cheh-a akile taovin ahi. Chuin Joab lengpa henga Jerusalem'a ahung kiletan ahi.
target: Then the woman went to all the people with her wise advice, and they cut off the head of Sheba son of Bikri and threw it to Joab. So he sounded the trumpet, and his men dispersed from the city, each returning to his home. And Joab went back to the king in Jerusalem.

source: Tun Joab chu Israel janel chunga ahin: chule Jehoiada chapa Benaiah chu Chereth mite le Peleth mite chunga ahi.
target: Joab was over Israel’s entire army; Benaiah son of Jehoiada was over the Kerethites and Pelethites;

source: Chule Adoram chu kaidong pipu ahin; chule Ahilud chapa Jehoshaphat chu thuching ahi.
target: Adoniram was in charge of forced labor; Jehoshaphat son of Ahilud was recorder;

source: Chule Sheva chu danthusun ahin; chule Zadok le Abiathar chu thempu ahilhone.
target: Sheva was secretary; Zadok and Abiathar were priests;

source: Chule Jair mi Ira chu David dinga vaihom pipu ahi.
target: and Ira the Jairite was David’s priest.

source: Chujouvin David nikho laichun akum kum-in kum thum kel alhan ahile, David'in Pakai chu adongin ahi. Chuin Pakaiyin, Hichehi Saul le thisanso hat a-insung mite jeh ahi, ajehchu aman Gibeon mite chu ana thatnin ahi, tin adonbutne.
target: During the reign of David, there was a famine for three successive years; so David sought the face of the Lord . The Lord said, “It is on account of Saul and his blood-stained house; it is because he put the Gibeonites to death.”

source: Chuin lengpan Gibeon mite chu akouvin, ajah uva hitin ati; (tun Gibeon mite hi Israel chate ahipouvin, amavang Amor mite amoh ho ahiuve; chule Israel chate chu ahenguva ana kihahselu ahi: ahin Saul'in Israel le Judah chate-a dinga atompan nalama thadinga anahol ahi).
target: The king summoned the Gibeonites and spoke to them. (Now the Gibeonites were not a part of Israel but were survivors of the Amorites; the Israelites had sworn to spare them, but Saul in his zeal for Israel and Judah had tried to annihilate them.)

source: Hijeh chun David'in Gibeon mite henga, Nangho dinga ipi kabolpeh diuham? chule Pakai goulo hohi phatthei nabohna diuva, ipi-a longlhena kabol dingham? ati.
target: David asked the Gibeonites, “What shall I do for you? How shall I make atonement so that you will bless the Lord ’s inheritance?”

source: Chuin Gibeon mihon ajah-a, Keihon Saul ahiloule a-insunga kon sana dangka kadeipouvin, chule keiho-a dinga jong Israel sunga mi khatcha natha louding ahi, atiuve. Chuin aman, Nanghon nasei seiju chu kabolpeh ding nahiuve, ati.
target: The Gibeonites answered him, “We have no right to demand silver or gold from Saul or his family, nor do we have the right to put anyone in Israel to death.” “What do you want me to do for you?” David asked.

source: Chuin amahon lengpa chu adonbutnun, Israel gamsung munkhat cha-a jong kaum louna diuva suhmang dingle thagam dinga eigopao thudola,
target: They answered the king, “As for the man who destroyed us and plotted against us so that we have been decimated and have no place anywhere in Israel,

source: Achapate pasal sagi chu keiho eikipedoh-uhen, chule keihon amaho chu Pakai henga, Pakaiyin analhen Saul umna Gibeah'a chun khaisang uvinge atiuve. Chuin lengpan, Amahochu kapeh dingu nahiuve, ati.
target: let seven of his male descendants be given to us to be killed and their bodies exposed before the Lord at Gibeah of Saul—the Lord ’s chosen one.” So the king said, “I will give them to you.”

source: Ahinla lengpan Saul chapa Jonathan chapa Mephibosheth chu Pakai hahselna amaho kah, David le Saul chapa Jonathan kah-a aumjeh chun akhendoh-in ahi.
target: The king spared Mephibosheth son of Jonathan, the son of Saul, because of the oath before the Lord between David and Jonathan son of Saul.

source: Hijeh chun lengpan Aiah chanu Rizpah'in Saul'a dinga ahinpeh achapateni Armoni le Mephibosheth le, Meholath mi Barzillai chapa Adriel dinga ahin Saul chanu Michal chapa ngaho chu alan,
target: But the king took Armoni and Mephibosheth, the two sons of Aiah’s daughter Rizpah, whom she had borne to Saul, together with the five sons of Saul’s daughter Merab, whom she had borne to Adriel son of Barzillai the Meholathite.

source: Chuin aman amaho chu Gibeoh miho khutna apedoh-in, chule amahon amaho chu Pakai masanga lhang chunga akhaijun ahi. Chuin amaho abonchauvin mi sagi chu chang-at nikho masapen, sakolchang ki-at tillin thakhatnin athat taovin ahi.
target: He handed them over to the Gibeonites, who killed them and exposed their bodies on a hill before the Lord . All seven of them fell together; they were put to death during the first days of the harvest, just as the barley harvest was beginning.

source: Chuin Aiah chanu Rizpah'in khaodip pon khat alan, chang-at kipatna pat van'a kona hicheho chunga twi ahung chuh tokahse-a ding chun amanu-a dingin songpi chunga aphan; chule sunle chungleng vachaho, chule janteng gamlah-a gamsaho chu achunguva achuh sahpon ahi.
target: Rizpah daughter of Aiah took sackcloth and spread it out for herself on a rock. From the beginning of the harvest till the rain poured down from the heavens on the bodies, she did not let the birds touch them by day or the wild animals by night.

source: Chuin Saul thaikemnu Aiah chanu Rizpah'in athilbol chu David aseipeh taovin ahi.
target: When David was told what Aiah’s daughter Rizpah, Saul’s concubine, had done,

source: Chuin David achen, Saul le achapa Jonathan guho chu Jabesh-gilead mite koma konin agalan; hiche guho chu Philistine miten Gilbao mun'a Saul athajou uva, Beth-shan kholaija akhai naova kona ana guhdoh-u ahi.
